items.statement: FY27 capex expected at INR1,500 crores, FY28 at INR2,000 crores, FY29 at INR1,500 crores, including Northeast but excluding land for Kutch and Nagore.

items.quote: Total for FY27 in 12 months period we expect a total capex of about INR1,500 crores and thereafter next year slightly higher at INR 2,000 crores and then again 1,500.

items.statement: Fuel cost per Kcal to rise from 1.65 to 1.8-1.85 in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: I think see, major is contributor is going to be fuel cost, so from 1.65 to maybe it can touch even about 1.8 plus or even 1.85 times.

items.statement: Packaging cost to increase by INR3.5-4 per bag in Q2 FY27 due to higher granule prices.
items.quote: So that is also going up and the impact of that, you know, to my calculation, initial calculation is about on bag itself is about, you know, INR3.5 to INR4 per bag.

items.statement: Maintains target of 30 million tons capacity by FY30.
items.quote: No, we are maintaining that. So, we are on track and on track of achieving 30 million tons by 2030.

items.statement: Net debt to EBITDA to not exceed 2.5-2.75x, may touch 2.75x near FY29-30.

items.statement: Non-cement revenue expected to reach INR800 crores plus by end of FY27.
items.quote: This year, so last year it was INR613, crores so perhaps I think we'll be around INR800 crores plus types, this is what I think our estimation is.

items.statement: Solar power project to be implemented in 8-9 months, benefits from Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
items.quote: The we expect this to take about eight to nine months for the project to get implemented. So the real benefit will start flowing from the fag end of the fourth quarter.

items.statement: Renewable energy share at 49% last quarter, plans to increase in 6-8 months.
items.quote: last quarter we have renewable energy 49%, right? So whatever energy we consume 49% is our renewable energy and that includes solar, wind and WHRS, right?

items.statement: SPV for 42 MW solar power with INR20 crores investment, payback less than two years.
items.quote: Yes, this SPV we have taken about captive power route for having these 42 megawatts of the solar power in SPV in which we are likely to invest about INR20 crores and that will give us a payback of less than two years.

items.statement: Northeast expansion on track, 1.5 million ton initially, details next quarter.
items.quote: And parallelly, also we have a plan to put up of course initially 1.5 million ton in Northeast. For that also we have started activities, of course plant land and then getting all those clearances before identifying locations for grinding stations.

items.statement: Durg expansion capex INR3000 crores, INR400 crores spent so far.
items.quote: Durg it does include Durg because out of 5000 capex which the number we have given we are talking of about INR3000 crores for Durg and INR1500 crores for Northeast.

items.statement: Clinker utilization at 95% last quarter.
items.quote: Clinker utilization, 95% I suppose last quarter. Just see that. Yes, 95%.

items.statement: Pet coke mix at 16% in Q1 FY27, up from 14% in previous quarter.
items.quote: Okay, so pet coke was last quarter 16%. And if you compare that with earlier quarter it was 14.

items.statement: Household penetration for key brands remains in mid-50s annually, indicating significant headroom
items.quote: if you look at the actual penetration numbers, they are still in the mid -50s across. And that clearly indicates that there is a significant headroom

items.statement: Premium portfolio contribution grew from 11% to 14%, growing ~500 bps ahead of overall growth
items.quote: If you look at our premium portfolio, the contribution has grown rapidly from 11% to 14%. More importantly, the growth in this part of the portfolio is well, well ahead of our overall growth. So, the premium part is growing by close to 500 bps ahead of overall growth

items.statement: Invested over Rs 64 billion in last 5 years; added new MAGGI line (Rs 170 Cr) and Munch line (Rs 225 Cr) in last calendar year
items.quote: if you look at the last five years, we have invested more than 64 billion. In the last one calendar year, w e started a new MAGGI line with close to Rs.170 Crores plus investment, a new Munch line where again we invested close to Rs.225 Crores

items.statement: Cost savings accelerated to 2.6% in 2025 (vs normal 1.8-1.9%), further accelerating this year
items.quote: if you look at our cost saving programs it is really accelerated. In a normal year, we would be around 1.8 to 1.9%, we have really stepped up, we have gone to 2.6% in 2025 a nd this year we are further accelerating on that

items.statement: Facing cost inflation in energy, packaging, oil, shipping disruptions, and currency volatility
items.quote: There are some costs which are going up of things like energy, packaging, oil, shipping disruptions, there is volatility in the currency

items.statement: Pet food gaining market share in cat food category; cat food growing strongly; dog/cat population ~50:50 in metros
items.quote: the cat food is we gain market share in that category and it is a category that is growing now, and where we are growing actually, also very strongly

items.statement: Drools is only a financial investment by Nestlé global; no operational synergy with Purina
items.quote: Drools is just a financial investment, which the Nestlé worldwide group has done, so I do not have any specific comments on Drools per se. It is just a financial investment

items.statement: No forward-looking projections or numbers given; secular short-to-medium term growth opportunity remains strong.
items.quote: I think, to start with, I am not getting into forward-looking projections or numbers.

items.statement: Will maintain margins in line with past track record, not chasing growth at cost of margin.
items.quote: we are not chasing growth at the cost of margin. We will deliver and maintain our margin in line with our past track record.

items.statement: Efficiency programs support holding margins; accelerated savings reinvested behind brands.
items.quote: our efficiency programs are here to tell on how we hold those margins.

items.statement: Price points remain critical for penetration; company will not flex pricing to protect penetration opportunity.
items.quote: if we keep on sort of flexing the pricing, we will lose out on the penetration opportunity.

items.statement: Rural contribution still half of peers; rural growing faster than urban, long runway ahead.
items.quote: We still have half of what some of our peer group companies are.

items.statement: CERELAC ZAS (zero added sucrose) launched; both ZAS and regular range have traction.
items.quote: we launched a ZAS version , which is zero added Sucrose. Now across the entire CERELAC range, moms have a choice of using ZAS or the sugar within the permissible limit.

items.statement: Coffee delivered 20 quarters of double-digit growth; KITKAT ran out of capacity, adding more.
items.quote: I spoke about coffee, 20 quarters of double-digit growth, so it is not just a confectionery thing.

items.statement: KITKAT capacity constraints being addressed with additional capacity investment.
items.quote: Ye s, we did run out of capacity , we are putting in more capacity , but the growth we are seeing is equally strong.

items.statement: Nutrition portfolio saw good volume growth last quarter; confident of continued volume growth.
items.quote: We saw good volume growth in this part of the business. And I see no reason for that to change in the future also.

items.statement: Parent portfolio brands being leveraged: Pops, Delight, ready-to-drink cold coffee, Purina Friskies, NESPRESSO.
items.quote: We spoke about Pops and Delight and r eady-to-drink cold coffee, the Vietnamese coffee.

items.statement: M&A not a focus; bulk of medium-term growth to come organically from current categories.
items.quote: bulk of our focus on growth in the medium term, I believe we have the headroom to do it through our current categories.

items.statement: Concerned about rising costs and macro challenges, but team resilience gives confidence.
items.quote: while we are concerned about some of the rising costs and the challenges, I think the last one year clearly gives me the confidence that my team has the resilience to work around it

items.statement: Ad spend trend to continue but not at 40% every quarter due to base catching up.
items.quote: At this point, we have not I would say the trend would continue. Would it be 40% every quarter? Obviously not because of the base catching.

items.statement: E-commerce/q-commerce focus on gaining share ahead of market rather than absolute growth.
items.quote: I am happy to report on most of our brands , we are growing ahead of the market wherever players share that data.

items.statement: Maintains FY27 revenue guidance of INR1,450-1,500 crores and 12% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: Yes. We had projected a margin of 12% EBITDA over this INR1,500 crores. So quarter 1 has been 9%. We hope to recover the rest in the 3 quarters that are to come to average out 12%. We are still maintaining that.

items.statement: Garment division expects about INR100 crores per quarter for next three quarters, ~INR375-380 crores for the year.
items.quote: And overall, the order book is very healthy. So we are expecting in garments probably a INR100 crores quarter for the next 3 quarters, which will take us close to what we were expecting around INR375 crores, INR380 crores to finish plus whatever export incentives, etc.

items.statement: Plans INR140 crores capex this year, already sanctioned, in fabric, garment and common infrastructure.
items.quote: So we are actually thinking of making investments, which we continue to make. This year, we will be investing another about INR140 crores is planned and already sanctioned.

items.statement: Plans 20-25% capacity expansion in garment and 20% in fabric in FY28.
items.quote: I mean in general, we are looking at an expansion next year of about 20%, 25% in garment and an expansion of about 20%. I'm talking now '27-'28 FY.

items.statement: Surat facility restart planned with ~INR50 crores fresh investment for INR200 crores additional revenue.
items.value: INR50 crores investment, INR200 crores revenue
items.quote: So when we will look at restarting Surat, we would look at it in a way of investing fresh into Surat and completely making a modern plant with new machinery. And that would give us additional runway to grow the business an additional INR200 crores with an approximate investment of about INR50 crores.

items.statement: Segment EBITDA targets: fabric 12-14%, garment 8-10%, yarn 8-10%, consolidated 12%.
items.quote: Right now if you get to the segment-wise margins, more or less, we expect the margins in the Fabric business to be about between 12% to 14% EBITDA and in the Garment business between, say, 8% to 10%. And our yarn business is also somewhere between 8% to 10%. And our consolidated EBITDA target is at about 12%.

items.statement: Fabric order book strong with orders up to November end.
items.quote: Our fabric order book position is also quite good and is showing almost orders up to November end.

items.statement: Demand for fabric and garment healthy for next two quarters, meeting or surpassing projections.
items.quote: And I think, yes, the demand is definitely looking good for both, I can say, for both fabric and garment, at least for the next 2 quarters is looking very healthy and meeting our projections or somewhat slightly surpassing our projections.

items.statement: Increasing share of value-added fabrics like bi-stretch, wool blends to improve realizations.
items.quote: We have been consciously increasing the share of premium product categories such as our bi-stretch fabrics, both in poly viscose and poly-rich blends, wool blends, in our portfolio.

items.statement: Garment export share to rise from 60% toward 70% by year end, improving earnings.
items.quote: But I wouldn't be surprised at the end of the year if we're even inching towards 70% of export.

items.statement: Jacket volumes expected at 800,000-900,000 this year vs 600,000 average, 70,000-75,000 per month.
items.quote: This year, we expect to close between 800,000 to 900,000 jackets. We will probably be averaging between 70,000 to 75,000 jackets a month.

items.statement: Q1 impacted by labor shortage in spinning and delayed garment dispatches; issues now largely eased.
items.quote: The major reason for the top line not increasing has been the labor availability in the first quarter in our spinning business and some dispatches being held back in the garment.

items.statement: Surat SEZ debonding expected complete in 3-5 months, facility operational by April 2027.
items.quote: And we expect that these remaining 2 parts should get done within the next 3 months, hopefully, and definitely within the next 4 to 5 months. So we're hoping that we should have the facility for use in DTA by November or December and operational for start in, let's say, April of '27.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at small single-digit; Dahej plant revenue guided at Rs 65 cr for full year
items.quote: We are looking at a small single-digit growth, I would say. Yes.

items.statement: Dahej plant EBITDA expected negative Rs 4-5 cr in FY27; breakeven difficult
items.quote: EBITDA, breakeven appears to be difficult. They are trying hard, but I think it is difficult. That will be in the range of around negative Rs. 4 crore-Rs. 5 crore.

items.statement: Nagpur capex spend of Rs 100 cr+ in FY27-28; Dahej capex to be communicated later
items.quote: You see, in terms of this Nagpur, the CAPEX would be around Rs. 100 crore plus. Dahej will communicate it later.

items.statement: Bayer products (Iprovalicarb, Triadimenol) acquired for global markets; customers established in some markets, distribution setup ongoing in others
items.quote: We have acquired Iprovalicarb and its variants and Triadimenol and its variants from Bayer for global markets. As we speak, we have already established some customers in various markets and already business started with them.

items.statement: New product introductions benchmarked at minimum 20% margin; 9(3) patented and nutrition products command significantly higher, often more than double
items.quote: We benchmark a healthy 20% margin minimum for any new introduction, but mostly 9(3) and nutrition would have significantly higher, more than double sometimes.

items.statement: Price hikes attempted in April-June to offset raw material/logistics costs but could not sustain; prices declined from May, further in July
items.quote: Price hike happened in the month of June. It could not sustain. From May, it started declining. In June, significant decline in many molecules. In July it further declined.

items.statement: Q1 impacted by 40% rain shortfall in June (15% by July-end); delayed sowing, resowing in Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, Maharashtra; Q2 remains difficult with large parts of country still rainfall deficit
items.quote: In the month of June, we had 40% shortfall in the rain, and by the end of July, it came down to 15% shortfall. Even 1% shortfall in the rainfall impacts the sowing areas and the overall growth of the crops.

items.statement: Five new product launches planned: one Liquid Fertilizer, three Fungicides, one Herbicide; Innovation Turnover Index 13.89% last year, 11.56% from last 3 years' launches
items.quote: We are pleased to inform you that in the upcoming months, we are planning to launch five new products consisting of one Liquid Fertilizer, three Fungicides, and one Herbicide.

items.statement: GST notice on molecule categorization; company confident of winning as per 5% fertilizer circular; hearing date pending
items.quote: Now these molecules are categorized under that category of fertilizer. Currently, as per the circular, it is 5%. We are sure we will win the case, absolutely. There's no doubt about it.

items.statement: Final dividend of 100% (Rs 2 per share) approved at AGM; buyback of 5 lakh shares at Rs 1,400/share (Rs 70 cr) completed

items.statement: Bayer product revenue in India nominal in Q1; major turnover from Iprovalicarb expected in September (Q2) for grape season
items.quote: It's a product for grapes. Grape season starts in the 2nd Quarter. Major turnover will come from Bayer products Iprovalicarb in the month of September.

items.quote: Out of three products, we have already introduced two, and one more is in the pipeline to be introduced pretty soon. Probably by August end, we will be launching the third one also.

items.statement: Targets revenue of Rs 900-950 crore in FY28 and Rs 1,000-1,050 crore in FY29 with current capacity.
items.quote: So, I would say '27-'28 is when we would target 900-950 and then '27-'28 with 1,000-1,050, 2029.

items.statement: Expects ESSEKAN premium PP yarn revenue of about Rs 10 crore this year with 20-25% EBITDA margin.
items.quote: So, ESSEKAN, we are expecting the revenue of about Rs. 10 crore rupees this year, which should be at an EBITDA level 20 %-25%, which is significantly higher than what we are doing.

items.statement: Aims to reach Rs 100 crore revenue in ESSEKAN within four years.
items.quote: The ultimate aim is to reach Rs. 100 crores in the next four years in Essekan.

items.statement: FIBC capacity expansion of up to 6,000 MT over five years on track; adding 1,200 tons annually.
items.quote: As informed earlier, the capacity expansion of FIBC to further add up to 6,000 metric tons per annum over the next five years is on track.

items.statement: Non-woven fabric facility on track for commissioning by Q3 FY27; revenues to start then.
items.quote: The Company remains on track to commission the non -woven fabric facility by Q3 of 2026 -'27.

items.statement: Plans new Rs 40 crore term loan for new project; long-term debt to rise to ~Rs 74 crore by year-end.
items.quote: And by the yearend, it will be near about Rs. 74 crores because the Rs. 40 crore new term loan we will take from here for the new project that we are making.

items.statement: Expects to sustain current EBITDA margin level; no exact guidance given.
items.quote: I would not be able to give a very exact guidance on it at the moment, but we should be able to continue the level that we are at.

items.statement: Raw material price increases and decreases are passed on to customers, with possible lag.
items.quote: So, in our business, mostly whatever the raw material increase and decrease is either ways, we are able to pass it on to the customers.

items.statement: Demand visibility remains about four weeks due to cautious customer procurement at high prices.

items.quote: In Q1 FY '27, we did 52% of FIBC, 20% of Fabric, 12% of Small Bags, 8% of Multifilament Yarns and others contributed abou t 8%.

items.quote: What we are able to save annually is about close to Rs. 3 crores to Rs. 5 crores a year is what we are able to save annually.

items.quote: So, in non-woven, we were expecting between 15% to 20% IRR and a ROCE of above 20%.

items.quote: The estimated cash flow potential pretax and post debt on ongoing projects, upcoming projects and other revenues is estimated to about INR3,380 crores over the life cycle of the project.

items.statement: Q1FY27 EBITDA margin 29%, PAT margin 14%

items.statement: Residential demand healthy with structural shift to lifestyle/premium; commercial demand driven by GCCs and data centers
items.quote: Speaking about the residential market, we've witnessed to see a structural shift, although over this entire quarter, we've seen lifestyle and premium development seeing good demand coming across all sectors.

items.statement: Q1FY27 sales value INR146 crores, 43,000+ sq ft sold, collections INR173 crores
items.quote: Ajmera Realty delivered steady start to FY27, reporting sales value of INR146 crores with a sales active area of about 43,000 plus square feet sold out and collections being at around INR173 crores for the quarter.

items.statement: Kanjurmarg land conversion targeted in 2-3 months before December deadline; strategic tie-up talks ongoing
items.quote: So we are working very aggressively on the land conversion process. But yes, it's a regulatory process, which we've involved the government as well as the other processes which we need to do. So we are working on that. Hopefully, our target is we should be able to achieve that very soon, hopefully, in the next 2 to 3 m

items.statement: Boutique office Phase 1 launch increased to 8-8.5 lakh sq ft (INR3,600 crores GDV) from earlier 4-5 lakh sq ft plan
items.quote: Earlier, we were doing about 4-5 lakh square feet of office space launch. Now we are going to do about 8 to 8.5 lakh square feet of office space launch. And that is why we are seeing this larger number coming.

items.statement: Received INR89 crores from asset monetization out of INR330 crores guided; further stake sale sealed in July 2026 to be reported in Q2
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that in this quarter, we have received an INR89 crores towards our share of investment and profit from a property sale out of the INR330 crores, which we had mentioned in our potential cash flows, which are coming.

items.statement: Debt reduced by INR57 crores to INR680 crores; debt-equity 0.47x; weighted average cost of debt 11.01%
items.quote: On the back of the strong collection and asset monetization, we have reduced our debt by INR57 crores in this particular quarter from INR737 crores, which stood at around 31st March 2026 to INR680 crores as on 30th June 2026. As a result, we achieved a debt equity ratio of 0.47x as on 30th June 2026.

items.statement: Debt-equity guidance FY27 1x but expect lower levered position with asset monetization
items.quote: But yes, there would be about a quarter or two whereby this kind of a situation are going to be there. And that's the reason we gave the guidance of FY27 to 1x, but with this asset monetization and another also absolutely sealed out kind of a thing, we are now seeing a much lower levered position as we go forward kind

items.statement: Ajmera Vann luxury project sales subdued this FY due to excavation stage; expect traction when superstructure progresses next year
items.quote: We will see subdued sales this financial year for this project. But over the time and next year when the progress of the superstructure is happening, we will start seeing traction coming in a faster way.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margin above 30% in near term and 40% long-term.
items.quote: we remain confident of progressing towards an EBITDA margin above 30% in the near term and towards our long-term benchmark of 40%.

items.statement: Targets Courtyard occupancy 80-85% and ADR 6,800-8,500 over next two financial years.
items.quote: we would like to maintain the 80% to 85% levels across the next 2 financial years. But ADR is something that we'd like to pick up from about that late 6,800 to 8,500 in the next 2 financial years.

items.statement: Courtyard ADR could reach 9,000-9,500 by FY28 due to limited supply.
items.quote: I wouldn't be surprised if we are closer to the 9,000-9,500 mark by FY28.

items.statement: Hyderabad ADR expected to grow 10-12% annually.
items.quote: Hyderabad is some -- is one of the markets where you can expect a 10% to 12% growth in ADRs.

items.statement: Phase 2 renovation to complete by December (Q3 FY27).
items.quote: we're expecting to finish this by December of this of this financial year. So, third quarter.

items.statement: Greenfield Courtyard at Madhapur: total project cost INR120-130 crores, 180-200 keys.
items.value: INR120 to INR130 crores; 180 to 200 keys
items.quote: the total project cost will be around INR120 to INR130 crores, the total project cost, and we look to build about 180 to 200 seats.

items.statement: Greenfield construction to start Q4 FY27, operational by FY29-2030.
items.quote: Expecting fourth quarter to start.

items.statement: Convention center offline causes ~INR10 crores EBITDA displacement in FY27.
items.quote: in terms of displacement, it's close to about INR10 crores in combination of the kind of business that you're losing through the convention and the rooms that comes with it.

items.statement: Confident of crossing 30% EBITDA margin this year, targeting 40% after full renovation.
items.quote: all the other quarters put together, we will easily cross that 30% EBITDA margin, and we are looking -- once we have the complete renovated product, we'll be looking to hit that 40% margin, as I already promised.

items.statement: Renovated rooms achieve ~30% higher ADR (~INR9,000 vs INR6,700-6,800).
items.quote: there's almost a 30% delta. The ADRs for the renovated inventory, I mean, the newer rooms, is closer to 9,000 versus the 6,700-6,800 mark that you see at a consolidated level.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 demand strong; expects to beat previous year's quarters despite renovation.
items.quote: Q2 is pretty strong. It is coming back well and I think everybody has come to terms that this war is not something that is going to -- it's in anybody's hands to stop anytime soon or when it's going to stop.

items.statement: Shifting mix from corporate to higher-paying retail/groups; F&B 40-45% of revenue, rooms 50-55%.
items.quote: about 40% to 45% of overall F&B, which includes your banqueting and your restaurants, there is about 50%-55% kind of contributes from the rooms.

items.statement: Rights issue of INR107 crores to reduce promoter stake below 75% and repay debt.
items.quote: we're just repaying the debt and to keep the limit open for the Greenfield project or any other future expansion.

items.statement: War impacted foreign demand in Q1; no permanent business loss from convention center closure.
items.quote: we also witnessed a war where a lot of the foreign demand dropped in the country. So, that is where you see the drop in ADR.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at Rs 700-800 crore, Rs 180 crore deployed in Q1; capex intensity to reduce significantly from next year
items.quote: In line with our earlier guidance, FY27 CAPEX remains on track within the Rs. 700 to 800 crore range, with about Rs 180 crores already deployed in Q1FY27.

items.statement: Zone 4 project delayed 3-6 months due to labour constraints and war issues; phased commissioning in FY27, ramp-up over FY28-29
items.quote: Barring the 3-6 months delay due to labour constraints and war related issues, our Zone 4 project expansion continues to progress. The project is being commissioned in a phased manner this year, FY27, with ramp-up expected over FY28 and FY29.

items.statement: Augene JV (50-50 with Superform) commissioning in Q2 FY27; steady-state revenue projected at Rs 300-400 crore; consolidates at PAT level
items.quote: We had projected INR300 crore to INR400 crore. I think we will maintain that range for the joint venture to start with.

items.quote: So volumes on energy business were down 17% on a quarter-on-quarter basis and on non-energy business, they were down by 7% on a quarter-on-quarter basis. On an overall organization level, they were roughly 12% down on quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA Rs 385 crore (+79% YoY) aided by inventory/forex gains (~Rs 50-60 crore); underlying run-rate lower
items.quote: The FX and inventory gains are difficult to estimate correctly, but I think the impact could be anywhere in the range of INR 50 crore to INR 60 crores.

items.statement: NCB chain pricing improved due to China VAT removal; part of gain structural, part raw-material linked; deltas managed in absolute terms
items.quote: NCB chain, the China's VAT removal led to changing of the pricing regime for the products in the entire value chain. So you will definitely see volatility linked to raw materials as the raw material softens in future, pricing, of course, will get corrected to some extent. But there is some element which is also linked

items.statement: West Asia conflict cut regional revenue share from 15% to 2%; volumes redirected; inventory/forex volatility risk remains high

items.statement: Augene JV seeing order book traction; Zone 4 has 25-30 products targeted by FY28, 5-10 in FY27; customer qualifications largely done
items.quote: I think by FY28, we are talking about anywhere in the range of 25 to 30 products. Within this year, we are looking at anywhere between 5 to 10 products.

I think in the imported raw materials, which is where we tend to have 1 to 1.5 months of inventory ideally in stock or over waters, which is where this price fluctuation sometimes could impact us

items.quote: We are prepared to raise debt because if my CBG plants starts, we need money there as well. And we are a zero-debt company. So, we can always raise debt, yes.

items.statement: International operations expected to cross INR1,000 crores revenue and ~INR120 crores EBITDA in FY27
items.quote: Overall, if you see, last year, we did around INR800 crores, INR850 crores with both the operations combined. This year, we are very confident of crossing INR1,000 crores and an EBITDA of, say, around INR120-odd crores.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA grew 13% YoY to INR68 crores; margin pressure from raw material volatility and foam mix shift
items.quote: On a standalone basis, revenue grew by 20% year-on-year to INR761 crores, while EBITDA grew by 13% to reach INR68 crores.

items.statement: Foam grew 26% value, 4% volume vs mattress 15% value, 6% volume; foam growth pulled gross margins down but was cash accretive
items.quote: Foam witnessed higher growth than mattresses, which pulled gross margins down. However, this growth was cash accretive and supported better EBITDA generation.

items.statement: Kurlon integration 96-97% complete; 75-80% synergies realized; remaining INR40 crores synergy from machine installation to fully reflect in Q3
items.quote: So, as I mentioned last time, there is only INR 40 crores worth of synergy that is outstanding. And this also I mentioned last quarter that the machine has already come. It is under installation. Maybe some impact you see during this quarter, but full impact would be visible in quarter 3.

items.statement: Furlenco subscriber base +36%, revenue +38%, EBITDA +65% YoY; operating profit ~INR9 crores/quarter; deferred tax assets caused Q4 PAT spike
items.quote: On Furlenco, the business continues to do well and is deepening its presence in newer cities. Its acquired subscriber base has grown by 36%, while revenue rose by 38%, and the EBITDA grew by 65% year-on-year.

items.statement: Staqo (IT) revenue +67% YoY, EBITDA 28-30%; Presence 360 ERP users crossed 3.2 lakh
items.quote: Our IT business, Staqo, also continues to evolve and grow exceptionally well. It registered a revenue growth of 67% in quarter 1 FY27 over last year while maintaining a healthy EBITDA run rate of around 28% to 30%.

items.statement: U2O network expanded to nearly 10,000 dealers; revenue +81% YoY, volume +19%; driven by 5-6 inch mattress portfolio expansion
items.quote: Our U2O, that is the unorganized to organized business, has now expanded to nearly 10,000 dealers across the country. This vast and growing network helped us clock 81% year-on-year growth with volumes growing by 19%.

items.statement: E-commerce Brand.com +69% YoY, platforms +19%; category +30% value, +23% volume; launched sofa beds under Sleepwell/Kurlon brands
items.quote: Sales on our websites, which we call as Brand.com, grew by 69% year-on-year basis, while sales on platforms grew by 19% year-on-year. The category registered an overall year-on-year growth of 30% in Q1 FY27 with volumes growing by 23%.

items.statement: Expects FY27 blended revenue growth ~13% and EBITDA growth ~16%.
items.quote: Blended, we are expecting about a 13% overall revenue growth, about a 16% EBITDA growth.

items.statement: Non-MF revenue to grow at least 20% in FY27, possibly 22-23%.
items.quote: So we believe that for the year, overall blended non-MF revenue will certainly be 20%. If you're lucky, it could come at 22%, 23%.

items.statement: MF revenue targeted to grow at least 12% in FY27.
items.quote: MF revenue, we would like it to grow at least 12%.

items.statement: Confident of 1% margin expansion, may reach 1.5%.
items.quote: We will still say that 1% we are very confident of, we may get to 1.5%.

items.statement: Non-MF margin to improve to 16-17% for the year from 13% in Q1.
items.quote: But I think our outlook for the year, we said will be 16% to 17% given that KRA will recover and the losses in a few other businesses will come down as the year progresses.

items.statement: Re-architecture project total cost INR500 crores, with INR290 crores capex; INR123 crores spent so far.
items.quote: From a re-arch perspective, we expect to spend -- the overall project cost, as we have said, is around INR500 crores. We have so far spent INR123 crores on this and part of it is capex, part of it is opex.

items.statement: Additional INR80 crores re-arch capex to be capitalized in FY27.
items.quote: So in the rest of the year, we will expect that at least another INR80 crores will get capitalized.

items.statement: Yields stable; annual yield decline expected 2.5-3%.
items.quote: You will see that play out, but you've said historically that you should see 2.5% to 3% annually. My guess is that's perhaps the number you'll end up seeing when we speak to you in May.

items.statement: Employee cost growth targeted around 5% year-on-year.
items.quote: So to answer your question, it is end of the year, year-on-year, your cost increase should be around 5% for employees.

items.statement: Overall cost increase target less than 10% for next 2-3 years.
items.quote: So, to answer your question, we will keep our cost increase down to less than 10% overall across all the heads of expense for the next two, three years.

items.statement: Headcount to reduce 4-5% in FY27, with 2-3% already down.
items.quote: We'll give you that number, and that number is expected to have a 4% to 5% down impact in the financial year, which has already started from 1st April onwards. We are about 2%, 3% down already.

items.statement: SIF segment accumulated over INR12,000 crores AUM and ~50,000 investors.
items.quote: So, it's accumulated to about just in excess of INR12,000 crores now, almost 50,000 investors.

items.statement: Payments business grew ~70% year-on-year, driven by cards.
items.quote: Pay, of course, did the best, grew just short of 70% year-on-year, largely riding on cards.

items.statement: Guiding for 10-12% revenue growth in FY27, skewed towards H2, and sustaining EBITDA margins in 30-32% range
items.quote: We are guiding for revenue growth of 10% to 12% in FY '27 with growth skewed towards H2 FY '27. We also remain confident of sustaining EBITDA margins in the 30% to 32% range.

items.statement: Capex of INR85 cr in Q1 FY27; expect ~INR540 cr for full FY27
items.quote: Our capex for the quarter stood at INR85 crores. We expect to incur a capex of approximately INR540 crores in FY '27.

items.statement: Management sees 60% gross margin as sustainable; EBITDA margin could reach 34% if war-related raw material risks don't worsen
items.quote: Yes. Like you said, a quarter here, a quarter there, but yes, I think we can hold.

items.statement: Non-GPL business grew 26.5% YoY (20% cc) driven by volume (+21-22%) with slight price decline (-1-2%); broad-based across geographies
items.quote: Our non-GPL business delivered strong growth of 26.5% year -on-year, driven by successful new product launches and strong demand across all geographies.

items.statement: Geopolitical war situation creating raw material cost volatility; conservative margin guidance (30-32%) despite potential for 34%
items.quote: The issue is this war situation, and what it's doing to raw material prices. So we need to be a little bit cautious. There's no point giving you a higher guidance and then not delivering.

items.statement: Solvent recovery improvement of 5-10% via membrane tech; but wide product basket limits full mitigation
items.quote: We might improve by about 5% to 10% there on recovery. We can't recover everything, okay?

items.statement: High-potent API pipeline: 29 products ($82B TAM); 13 validated, 7 advanced, 9 in lab; commercialization starts end CY27 (FY28)
items.quote: Our high- potent API portfolio continues to advance with 29 products in the active grid, representing a total addressable market of $82 billion. Of these 13 products have been validated, 7 are in advanced stages of development and the remaining 9 products are progressing through lab development stages.

items.statement: R&D spend at 3.7% of sales in Q1; targeting steady-state ~4%; focused on new API, second-gen processes, some CDMO support
items.quote: So we should sort of end up at a steady state of around 4%.

items.statement: Debt-free with INR880 cr cash/equivalents; strong FCF of INR90 cr in Q1; actively evaluating synergistic acquisitions (API-plus) but not for capacity
items.quote: We generated a strong free cash flow of INR90 crores, leading to cash and cash equivalents including short -term investments of INR880 crores as of 30th June 2026. We continue to remain a debt -free company.

name: Aptus Value Housing Finance India Ltd

items.statement: Plan to expand Nykaa Now quick commerce to over 25 cities by end of FY27 and cater to a meaningful percentage of orders within 60 minutes
items.quote: In terms of expansion, we plan to be in over 25 cities by the end of FY27 and cater to a meaningful percentage of our orders coming through the Nykaa Now fulfillment model, which means within 60 minutes.

items.statement: Added 160 new brand partners in Q1 FY27, total brand partners now 10,000+ across beauty and lifestyle
items.quote: In fact, almost 160 were added in this quarter alone. And many important ones amongst those were brands like Rare Beauty, SK-II, Birkenstock in Fashion, as well as Debenhams.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded 196 bps YoY to 8.5% in Q1 FY27 driven by scale and marketing efficiency
items.quote: EBITDA growth of 68% Y-o-Y, which is a 196 basis points margin expansion on a Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Beauty vertical EBITDA margin improved 130 bps YoY to 10.3% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: delivering a very healthy EBITDA margin of 10.3%, which is 130 basis points higher than Q1 of FY26.

items.statement: Fashion vertical achieved profitability in Q1 FY27 with 627 bps YoY EBITDA margin improvement, marketing efficiency improved 534 bps to 22.9%
items.quote: It has been a profitable quarter overall, which means the 627 basis points year -on-year improvement versus the same quarter last year. And underlying this across line items in the P&L, we've seen improvement, but worth calling out 2 of the line items which have changed most meaningfully. On the marketing side, marketi

items.statement: Beauty platform visits grew 22% YoY to nearly 0.5 billion in Q1 FY27, annual unique transacting customers crossed 20 million
items.quote: You can see that on the penetration side, we have increased the number of visits to our platform to close to 0.5 billion in Q1 FY27, which is a 22% growth year-over-year. And the number of annual unique transacting customers on the platform has now crossed 20 million.

items.statement: Acquired 51% stake in Aminu, a premium dermocosmetic skincare brand with INR 19 crore net revenue in FY26, to fill premium skincare gap and add R&D capabilities
items.quote: We are acquiring 51% today. The remaining 49% will be acquired over the next few years as per terms that we've set out in the documents.

items.statement: Fulfillment expenses increased 42 bps due to infrastructure expansion and one-off impact of new labor code
items.quote: Fulfillment expenses increased by 42 basis points as we continue to invest in infrastructure expansion, which is leading to O2D efficiencies. The increased fulfillment expenses, incidentally, were offset by a like improvement in marketing efficiency of 42 basis points.

items.statement: Superstore GMV growth to normalize from Q3; on track for 35%+ CAGR guidance by FY2030.
items.quote: Firstly, the GST impact will start normalizing from Q3 onwards. So you will see very close numbers between NSV growth and GMV growth.

items.statement: Fashion vertical retains 3 to 3.5x growth guidance over 4-5 years.
items.quote: Firstly, just anchoring to the long term, we still guide to what we shared in the Investor Day just a couple of weeks ago, which is 3 to 3.5x growth over a 4- to 5-year period, and we still retain that.

items.statement: Nykaa Now not expected to dilute EBITDA margins; seen as accretive from LTV perspective.
items.quote: So our early read is that we don't think this will be dilutive if at all.

items.statement: Fulfillment cost per order higher for Nykaa Now, offset by higher purchase frequency and stable AOV.
items.quote: But again, the benefit is the increase in frequency of purchase, and the average order value staying consistent. I think these things are all offsetting some of that increase in fulfillment.

items.statement: No differential pricing on Nykaa Now versus mainline; discounts are brand-funded, not retailer-funded.
items.quote: So currently, there is no differential pricing on Nykaa Now versus the mainline.

items.statement: Nykaa Now driving incremental demand in low-penetration personal care categories like face washes and cleansers.
items.quote: So things like low ASP face washes and cleansers and bath gels, et cetera. So those are also pure incremental business for us because those are categories in which historically Nykaa never had a big role to play.

items.statement: Festive demand benefit expected to accrue mostly in Q3, with some possibly in Q4.
items.quote: I think if there are dates that are being pushed into Q4, then some of that benefit might accrue in Q4 as well. But to me, it seems most of the dates are falling in Q3.

items.statement: Fashion to remain predominantly marketplace; inventory-based business small and Nike D2C partnerships selective.
items.quote: Partnerships such as the Nike D2C partnerships will also be selective in nature. So it will be predominantly a marketplace business.

items.statement: Nike partnership has two parts: standard marketplace listing and end-to-end D2C platform operation by Nykaa Fashion.
items.quote: The second is where we completely end-to-end operate their D2C customer platforms, which is across web and app.

items.statement: Nike D2C arrangement is retailer-like with commission and service fees, protected against inventory.
items.quote: Yes. But I think, Abhijeet, what they may be looking for is it's like a retailer -like arrangement where we get commission-like numbers and some other service numbers based on the sales that we achieve. And we are protected against inventory.

items.statement: Beauty AOV growth sustainable on repeat customer AOV and rising per capita consumption.
items.quote: I think the average order value moving in the right direction is definitely our base case at this point in time.

items.statement: Fashion TAM seen at $65-100 million consumers over 5 years; no price filter applied.
items.quote: So yes, we believe that somewhere between $65 million and $100 million will be the relevant TAM for Nykaa.

items.statement: No plans to open fashion stores; focus remains on digital build-out with partners.
items.quote: On the second one, not for now. I mean, we are focused on just building out digitally with partners. So not for the moment.

items.statement: Fixed asset turnover improved to 10.7x in June 2026; ROCE at 26.8% annualized.
items.quote: Fixed asset turnover, as we can see, has improved to 10.7x as of quarter-end June '26 versus 9.9x in FY26.

items.statement: Total order book stands at INR 2,654 crores including negotiated orders; international order book at INR 39 crores
items.quote: Our order book stands at INR2,654 crores, including orders negotiated, providing a healthy revenue visibility over the coming years.

items.statement: Expect INR 2,000 crores of fresh order inflows during FY27 over and above orders already received and negotiated
items.quote: We also remain confident of securing around INR2,000 crores of fresh order inflows during FY '27 over and above the orders already received and negotiated.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR 150-200 crores minimum over next 2 years for infrastructure, clean rooms, integration facilities and production lines
items.quote: INR150 crores to INR200 crores minimum -- definietly based on the requirements.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 27% impacted by high employee costs and product mix changes; confident of achieving full year targeted margins
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR31.4 crores with an EBITDA margin of 27%. Margins during the quarter were impacted by high employee costs associated with capability expansion and changes in the product mix.

items.statement: Transitioning products from development to complete system solutions, expanding addressable market and enabling participation in higher-value programs
items.quote: A key milestone for us has been the successful transition of several products from the development stage to complete system solutions. This significantly expands our addressable market and enables us to participate in larger and higher-value programs.

items.statement: Initial traction in drone and counter-drone business with orders received; expect this to become important growth driver as demand for indigenous unmanned solutions increases
items.quote: Another encouraging development during the quarter was the initial traction in our drone and counter drone business, where we have started receiving orders. We believe that this business will become an important growth driver as demand for indigenous unmanned and counter UAVs solutions continue to increase.

items.statement: Additional investments in AI-driven initiatives, computer servers and IT infrastructure planned over next 1-2 years
items.quote: today, we're also investing a lot of server money because of AI. There are a lot of investments also happening in computer servers, IT infrastructure to support the AI-driven initiatives that the company has taken up very seriously.

items.statement: BrahMos seeker commercial orders expected this financial year after qualification completion; delays possible but products are ready
items.quote: We expect this will happen this year, this financial year. But the approvals and qualifications will take time. Products are ready. As soon as the qualification is completed in right time, I think the contract should happen or even quality itself, that should happen.

items.statement: Copper pass-through lag remains 3 to 6 months; company wants to reduce it.
items.quote: See, copper, the lag is still on 3 to 6 months.

items.statement: 7% copper inflation lag sitting in current quarter results versus 17% in preceding quarter.
items.quote: So, right now, if you see just look at the quarter-on-quarter, there is increase of 7%. So we still have a lag of the delta of 7% which is sitting in the current results, unlike 17% in the preceding quarter.

items.statement: Some price hikes due from March quarter pending, will flow into September quarter.
items.quote: Yes, that's right. Some of the customers are there.

items.statement: Majority of customers on 3-month copper pass-through basis, barring a few.
items.quote: Majority of our customers are on a 3-month basis, barring few.

items.statement: Minimum wage hikes of 30-40% in NCR fully reflected in Q1 results.
items.quote: So as we mentioned, the increase is quite significant, which has which has absorbed in the current quarter result in terms of significant wages, because in the NCR region only we have seen an increase of 30% to 40% in the in the wages.

items.statement: Constructive discussions ongoing with customers to recover minimum wage cost increases; no timeline.
items.quote: Nobody can predict exactly the timeline, but our endeavor would be to reach an agreement with the customers as soon as possible.

items.statement: EVs contributed 8.5% of Q1 FY27 revenues.
items.quote: Contribution from EVs continues to be strong, with 8.5% of our revenues coming from EVs in Q1.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 37% in Q1, of which 7% from copper inflation, rest from volume, content, premiumization.
items.quote: So out of the total 37% growth, 7% is on account of the copper inflation, and the remaining is on account of, volume growth, content increase, premiumization, our presence on the new model launches by the OEMs.

items.statement: Greenfield plants at break-even with run rate around INR450 crores, same as previous quarter.
items.quote: Have a run rate of around INR450 crores in the previous quarter. We maintain the same level of revenue and the break-even point at this quarter as well.

items.statement: Current year budgeted capex to be funded from internal accruals.
items.quote: The current what we have budgeted for this current year, the capex, we will do from the internal accruals.

items.statement: New expansion plans may be announced in coming quarters based on customer forecasts.
items.quote: And as I said that in the next quarters, you can hear from us that what are the new expansion plans for MSWIL.

items.statement: Greenfields to merge into regular business and deliver same margins over time; ROCE target above 40%.
items.quote: So yes, and that's right, that after some time, they have to merge into your regular business and they will give the same margin. But as Mr. Mittal said that we are a ROCE-focused company, idea is to have it more than 40%, and we all committed to that, and we have shown that in the past also -- in the past years also.

items.statement: Other state governments may also raise minimum wages; impact uncertain.
items.quote: So as we speak, we are hearing something from the other state as well, but nothing has concluded so far. So it's very difficult to anticipate that how the other governments would...

items.statement: CEM and CRAMS to contribute 70%+ of revenue in next couple of years.
items.quote: we have a clear line of sight to these two models contributing 70+ of our -- percentage of our revenue in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Core specialty and CRAMS plus CEM business delivering 25-30% compounding growth.
items.quote: Our core specialty and CRAMS plus CEM business is delivering 25% to 30% compounding growth you have come to expect.

items.statement: FY27 capex expected INR3,000-3,500 million, mainly for Site 5 and new R&D site.
items.quote: The capex expected for FY27 is expected to be between INR3,000 million to INR3,500 million.

items.statement: Magnum Site 5 total investment INR2,200-2,300 crores; Phase 1 online, Phase 2 by FY2030.
items.quote: The total investment is in the order of INR2,200 crores to INR2,300 crores. Phase 2, FY 2030.

items.statement: CEM business runs at EBITDA margins of 28-30%.
items.quote: CEM runs at EBITDA margins north of 28% to 30%, so every point of mix that shifts towards this model makes our earnings both larger and more resilient.

items.statement: LSM to contribute only 35% of total top line in few years.
items.quote: still the LSM product line business segment is important to us, even though it will contribute only 35% of our total top line in the few years to come.

items.statement: New LSM products from Magnum Site 5 to start contributing to revenue in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: Magnum, that is our Site 5, which is at Panoli, began commercial sales of the new LSM products during this quarter. And we expect them to start contributing to our revenue in Quarter 2 of financial year 2027.

items.statement: First three new LSM products priced at $30-40 per kilo.
items.quote: This is the first set of three new LSM products across pharmaceutical, agrochemicals, and material science sector, priced roughly at $30 to $40 per kilo range.

items.statement: Semiconductor materials: starting capacity 400 tons, to grow 3x by 2030; average price ~$50/kg.
items.quote: We are starting with capacities of 400 tons at this point of time, which is supposedly going to grow 3x by 2030. That’s what we are looking at. So that’s the size of the business. The average product value is approximately $50 a kilo.

items.statement: Semiconductor large stream at Site 5: 45 tons/month in 3 streams, online end of September.
items.quote: the big stream, that is a large stream of semiconductors coming on site 5, that is Magnum Site, which is located in Panoli, whereby we’ll come out with 45 tons per month capabilities split it into 3 streams of 15 tons each. And that is going to be online in end of September.

items.statement: Dow collaboration: exclusive multi-year research program for silicones; potential $1B India market.
items.quote: It is an exclusive multi-year program with all research and pilot plant scale-up activities to be carried out at Aether’s facilities of R&D and pilot plant in Surat, Gujarat.

items.statement: Dow program is multiyear; application testing and commercialization a few years away.
items.quote: It's a multiyear research program. And so, you're talking about a few years, until we get into the application testing and commercialization and the manufacturing as long as it works out.

items.statement: Top risks: safety in chemical industry and ability to execute expansions.
items.quote: The problem -- the potential problems and the challenges I have always maintained in the chemical industry is safety. And so that remains the foremost concern of the company, safe chemical processes. And the second one, especially now for companies like us in India is our ability to execute, right?

items.statement: R&D expansion: new facility with ~15 labs and ~160 fume hoods on track for FY2028.
items.quote: A much larger R&D facility, as you know, with around 15 new labs and close to 160 cumulative fume hoods, is on track for commissioning in FY 2028.

items.statement: Bromine volume run rate expected to exit FY27 at 20,000-25,000 tons annualized.
items.quote: we expect to exit the year at the 20,000 to 25,000 tons run rate

items.statement: Salt volumes expected to normalize from Q3 FY27 after highway construction completes.
items.quote: For the balance of FY27, we expect salt volumes to normalize from Q3 as the highway work completes.

items.statement: SOP full-year target of 9,000-10,000 tons maintained.
items.quote: for the full year, our target is to do a 9,000 to 10,000 tons, and we still remain very confident about able to develop through that throughput

items.statement: Bromine realizations expected to remain firm near INR300 per kg.
items.quote: Realizations are broadly up and we expect them to largely remain firm near the INR300 per kg level.

items.statement: Semiconductor capex of USD249 million; 60-65% in FY27, balance 40-45% in FY28.
items.quote: the capex for semicon which was USD249 million. 15% to 20% of that has already been incurred

items.statement: Semiconductor project targeted for commercial start of production in 24-27 months.
items.quote: our target is to kind of get this done in 24 to 27 months. And we are on -- we're executing to that schedule

items.statement: Brine field phase one expansion mostly complete; commissioning may be preponed to post-monsoon.
items.quote: We have completed most of phase one and we are optimistic that we actually be able to pre -pone commissioning of phase one to post the monsoons.

items.statement: Derivatives business Acume turned EBITDA positive at INR19 million in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Acume delivered an EBITDA of INR19 million this quarter against a EBITDA loss of INR27 million in Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Logistics cost increase expected to normalize, improving profitability from Q3 FY27.
items.quote: they should be reflecting our numbers by in Q3 and should help us first improve profitability and then secure more demand as well

items.statement: Bromine landed prices in China declined 30-40% in past 12 weeks; company aims to hold price increases.
items.quote: Landed prices in China, for example, have declined by 30% to 40% in the past 12 weeks.

items.statement: Sea freight costs increased 30-35%, impacting landed cost to East and South Asia customers.
items.quote: sea freight costs have also increased by 30% to 35%, impacting our landed cost to customers in East and South Asia

items.statement: Bromine and derivatives demand firm across most geographies; flame retardants, oilfield, energy storage healthy.
items.quote: bromine and bromine derivatives demand has remained firm, firm across most geographies

items.statement: Derivatives mix shifting to higher-value organic products; NPBR volumes rose to 350 tons from 25-30 tons.
items.quote: We've also had an increase in PBR volumes, which last year, for example, where same quarter last year, we won 25, 30 tons. This quarter has been on 350 tons for the quarter

items.statement: Launch pipeline for FY27 across MMR projects estimated at GDV of INR 8,000 crores plus.
items.quote: Altogether, these projects should be an estimated GDV of about INR 8,000 crores plus as was guided by us earlier.

items.statement: Operating cash flow guidance of INR 1,000 crores for the year remains intact.
items.quote: INR 1,000 crores guidance remains intact, yes.

items.statement: Plotted development expected to contribute INR 500-750 crores presales and INR 150-200 crores margin annually.
items.quote: I'm looking at this as INR 500 crores to INR 750 crores year-on-year in terms of presales with a margin of exceeding INR 150 crores to INR 200 crores year-on-year.

items.statement: Gross debt-to-equity guidance of 0.75:1; net debt expected to turn positive over time.
items.quote: And we have said that our gross debt to the equity will be 0.75:1. Now we are still at 0.3:1.

items.statement: Margin profile expected to improve quarter-by-quarter, in sync with guidance.
items.quote: Margin profile, I would like to summarize it like that the margin profile will continue to improve quarter-by-quarter.

items.statement: About 95% of legacy completed-method projects to be recognized in current year; 98% POC from next year.
items.quote: We expect a substantial portion of that, almost 95% of that to be recognized during the current year only.

items.statement: Current year revenue mix: 40% from completed method, 60% from percentage of completion method.
items.quote: About 40% of our revenue in the current year comes from those projects which are under completion method and 60% comes from the projects which are under the POC method.

items.statement: Legacy projects to contribute 15% of current year revenue; 85% from current projects.
items.quote: In the current year, of the total revenue profile, we are expecting 15% of the revenue to be contributed by the legacy projects and 85% to be recognized from the current projects.

items.statement: Construction spends rose 26% YoY to INR 299 crores in Q1 FY27 from INR 238 crores.
items.quote: Our construction spends have increased from INR 238 crores in FY26 Q1 to INR 299 crores in Q1 of FY27, 26% growth year-on-year on quarterly basis.

items.statement: Land and approval investment rose 54% YoY to INR 232 crores in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Our land and approval investment in projects has increased to INR 232 crores compared to INR 151 crores in Q1 FY26. This is a 54% year-on-year growth, pointing towards more launches taking place now.

items.statement: Added 2 new projects in Q1 FY27 with combined estimated GDV of INR 547 crores.
items.quote: To drive future growth, the company added 2 new projects to its portfolio during the quarter, having the estimated GDV of INR 547 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 21.3% from 10.1% YoY.
items.quote: EBITDA margins expanded to 21.3% from 10.1% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Focus remains on premium and super premium segments; luxury pipeline retained.
items.quote: But yes, our focus will always be more on the premium and super premium category.

items.statement: Interest rate hikes seen as having insignificant impact on margins and limited demand impact.
items.quote: So should there be a situation that there is some small hike in the interest rates, I will say that it will have insignificant impact on the margin profile.

items.statement: Targets 25-30% loan book growth, secured lending ~55% of portfolio, NIM ~8%, ROE ~15% by FY28
items.quote: We are aiming for a loan book growth of 25% to 30% , with the secured lending comprising ~55% of the portfolio, maintaining NIM of around 8% and delivering a ROE of ~15% by FY28.

items.statement: JLG portfolio to remain around 25% of gross loan book over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So, our idea is to remain almost in the same range, around 25% or so , overall, if you look at JLG part over a period of next 2 to 3 years also, so, around 25% is what we expect our JLG portfolio will be.

items.statement: JLG and Micro Banking portfolio growth targeted at 15-20%
