items.quote: So, yeah, it will remain same at present is around 70%. So, what we ar e estimating, it will be around, say, 68% to -- between 71% that we are anticipating.

items.statement: 100% raw material and forex pass-through to OEM customers with 2-3 month lag
items.quote: Yes. We have a all major customers are OEMs, so we have pass-through mechanisms along with forex and like that.

items.statement: Energy 49%, Motion Control 24%, Industrial Equipment 19%, Others 7%; Exports 78% (NA 52%, Asia 27%, India 17%, EU/UK 3%)
items.quote: For the quarter ended June 30th of 2026, energy contributed around 49% of the revenue base, motion control and automation contributed around 24%, industrial equipment systems contributed around 19%, and other diversified industrial application contributed around 7%.

items.statement: Defense/aerospace revenue starting in FY27 (6.9% of Q1 revenue), scaling over 1-3 years as FA approvals complete
items.quote: So, if you see our last year's others was a less and like Q1, our others has been increased. So, it has been start showing into that other areas in the revenue. So, now it is a 6.9%. So, what I mean to say, some revenue at the FA level and some level it has been already start showing into the our revenue models. So, we

items.statement: Geographic concentration risk: NA 55-60% of order book; targeting 10-20% shift to Middle East/Europe
items.quote: And in terms of the geography -wise, yes, North America is still around 55 % to 60%. So, that will be around, we are working on the -- as per our strategies, we are working on the balancing that our geographical risk, that so for that our Middle East and our Europe regions, that is growing in the good way. So, that wil

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 233 from 294; targeting further 10-20% improvement
items.quote: So, in the working capital, you can just we are seeing in terms of -- in this range, and we are we are working on to improve another 10% to 20% in the range of to improve the working capital.

items.statement: Current capacity supports INR800-900 cr revenue; new capex adds similar capacity incrementally
items.quote: So, roughly around you can say like INR800 crores to INR900 crores roughly we can do from the existing. And the similar size of the building in terms of the square feet, in terms of the land, we are also investing into the new capex.

items.statement: ROCE target >20% on new capex; asset turnover 2-2.5x
items.quote: See, if you see our asset turnover ratios and similar like that, so it is around 2.25 around 2 to 2.5 in between. And in terms of ROCE it should be more than 20 and similar like that.

items.statement: Management maintains jewellery EBIT margin center of gravity at ~11% (plus/minus) and double-digit value growth target; no change to prior guidance.
items.quote: In the Investor Day and prior, we have said that more of 11% being the center of gravity for jewellery business margin, we would be around that plus/minus something can happen.

items.statement: Normalized Tanishq/Mia/Zoya EBIT margin for Q1 FY27 is 10.9% after removing customs duty gain and MTM gain.
items.quote: The normalized margin considering both custom duty gain and MTM gain, the normalized EBIT margin for our Tanishq Mia Zoya business would be 10.9%, the number for this quarter.

items.statement: Customs duty increase (6% to 15%) yielded ₹407 cr consolidated gain in Q1 (₹386 cr Tanishq/Mia/Zoya, ₹21 cr CaratLane); gains to realize over next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: We had during this quarter, gains on account of customs duty rate increase from 6% to 15%. While these gains will be realized as the inventory gets sold over the next couple of quarters, but in this quarter, we had overall at a consolidated level realization of ₹407 crores.

items.statement: Accounting MTM gain from gold procurement added 75-80 bps to jewellery division EBIT in Q1; expected to reverse over next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: On account of those price divergence, we have accounting MTM in the inventory, which is -- which caused 75 to 80 basis point jewellery division EBIT upward. So jewellery division has the benefit of that. And we believe that these are likely to reverse in the coming quarters.

items.statement: May demand softness due to PM announcement, customs duty change, and Adhik Maas recovered in June; no spillover into Q2 expected.
items.quote: We believe that it was a deferment and we saw things pick up in June. What we lost in May, perhaps we gained back in the month of June.

items.statement: Buyer growth 5% in Q1; stable or mildly rising gold prices support positive sentiment and buyer growth.
items.quote: See if gold rates stay stable, we always see that sentiments are positive and people come back and they don't sit on the fence.

items.statement: Damas core business loss-making due to war-related footfall and ticket size decline in Middle East; rest of international portfolio at 5-6% EBIT margin.
items.quote: Given the current situation of war, I think purchasing jewellery in Dubai and Saudi and other countries is the last priority for anyone there. So the footfall has fallen down. Ticket sizes have fallen down.

items.statement: Committed to double-digit healthy value growth in jewellery to achieve FY30 goals; all growth levers (regionalization, studded, retail transformation, sub-₹50k/₹1L buyer growth) remain intact.
items.quote: We are committed to a double-digit healthy growth in value in the jewellery business. So that's the only way we'll get to our committed FY 30 goals that we've said.

items.statement: Natural diamond prices stable at retail for both solitaires and small diamonds; lab-grown vs natural narrative has subsided.
items.quote: Natural diamond prices. Yes, we have seen more stability perhaps in the pricing, both of solitaires as well as small diamonds.

items.statement: Medium-term EBITDA margin target range of 14% to 16% maintained; near-term focus on absolute EBITDA growth over margin percentage
items.quote: Our primary focus will remain on driving EBITDA growth while progressing towards our medium-term EBITDA margin target range of 14% to 16%.

items.statement: Near-zero channel inventory for VIDA (2-3 days) and depleted ICE scooter stocks indicate strong pent-up demand; capacity additions being absorbed immediately
items.quote: We have pretty much nil channel inventory. It's 2 to 3 days depending on region to region. So whatever we are supplying and shipping is actually retailed immediately.

items.statement: Industry 2W volumes grew 14% YoY in Q1 (ICE +11%, EV +67%); July retail growth 28% YoY; H2 growth positive but lower YoY due to high base; full-year industry targeting double-digit growth
items.quote: 2-wheeler industry volumes grew 14% year-on-year in terms of VAHAN or retail sales, of which 11% was growth in ICE and 67% was in EV.

items.statement: Mix benefit of 8% from shift to EV, scooters, premium, global; scooter dispatches nearly doubled YoY; EV wholesale +151% YoY; global business +63% YoY; parts & accessories +30% YoY
items.quote: This top line expansion was driven by premiumization across our portfolio, driven by a shift in mix towards EV, scooters and premium variants, contributing a mix benefit of 8% with the rest coming from calibrated price increase.

items.statement: PLI benefit INR 48 cr in Q1 covering 60% of EV portfolio; 100% PLI compliance expected by Dec 2026; EV revenue ~5% of total (INR 660 cr); EV EBITDA loss narrowed from INR 50k to 40k per unit QoQ
items.quote: On the PLI front, I'm pleased to share that around 60% of our EV portfolio is now PLI certified, and we expect 100% of our portfolio to be PLI compliant by December 2026.

items.statement: New premium motorcycle launches (XPulse 421, XMR 250) in next 12 months; some refreshes before festive; EV motorcycles (Ubex, VXZ) from next year; GPC 2.0 parts capacity expansion with INR 750 cr capex
items.quote: In the next 12 months, you'll see many more coming up. Market will be fully lined up with these models. You'll see a few starting from this festive itself and going up to next few quarters as well.

items.statement: Target to collect Rs. 380 crores from legacy government receivables in remaining nine months of FY27
items.quote: remainder of nine months minimum, and this I am talking minimum, target is Rs. 380 crores will come from that in total

items.statement: Biochar plant started recently; revenue impact expected from next fiscal year
items.quote: You will start seeing because project has recently started any impact on numbers from the next fiscal

items.statement: Hi-Tech margin fell to 14.4% from 16.6% YoY due to unabsorbed fixed costs; expect recovery in H2
items.quote: Hi-Tech division delivered about a 14.4% margin versus similar period at 16.6, so approximately 2% reduction

items.statement: Plastic division margin improved to 11% from 10% YoY
items.quote: plastic, in fact, improved by about a percent or so from 10 to 11

items.statement: Agro-Processing margin declined by 3% YoY due to seasonality
items.quote: Agro-Processing also came down by 3%

items.statement: July revenue growth positive vs Q1; August-September outlook good; institutional pipe demand strong
items.quote: We have registered already positive revenue growth in July as against April to June, significant revenue growth here

items.statement: One large Pune water supply project remains with triple-digit billing pending; other projects 98-99% complete with Rs. 40-50 crores left
items.quote: total billing left is about approximately closer to Rs. 40-50 crores only

items.statement: Government receivables >180 days total ~Rs. 1,100 crores (Rs. 300 crores project EPC + Rs. 800-900 crores state subsidy orders)
items.quote: about Rs. 1100 crores is about 180 days

items.statement: FY27 order inflow guided at INR 22,000-25,000 crore, revenue growth 8-10%, EBITDA margin 8.5-9%
items.quote: The order inflow for this financial year is a band INR 22,000 crores to INR25,000 crores. I repeat, INR 22,000 crores to INR 25,000 crores; revenue growth of 8% to 10% and EBITDA margin in the range of 8.5% to 9%.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 81,214 crore as of June 30, 2026, with Q1 inflows of INR 3,889 crore
items.quote: As of 30th June ' 26, our order book stands at INR 81,214 crores. During the quarter, we have booked new orders worth INR 3,889 crores, mainly from our Buildings and Water & Railways divisions.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 9.4% in Q1 FY27 from 8.8% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: The EBITDA margin for the quarter stands at 9.4% on a consol basis as against 8.8% in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Capex guidance maintained at INR 500 crore for FY27; INR 170 crore spent in Q1
items.quote: Yes. Guidance remains the same for the CAPEX, INR 500 crores, whatever we have given.

items.statement: Prospective bid pipeline of INR 2.5 lakh crore as of Q1 FY27; all INR 81,000 crore order book executable
items.quote: The prospective pipeline of projects is about INR 2.5 lakh crore as of 1st Quarter.

items.statement: Ken-Betwa project facing land acquisition protests 20-30 km from site; no material impact on execution currently
items.quote: Yes, we have seen all these media reports, and we understand that the local administration is in touch with the agitators, and the issues are slowly getting resolved.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt increased to INR 3,513 crore due to INR 1,461 crore smart meter project debt; standalone net debt INR 2,008 crore
items.quote: Out of 3,500, it is 1,461 is the smart meter debt.

items.statement: Smart meter CAPEX to complete by March 2027; O&M revenue ~INR 1 crore per 1 lakh meters; 45% of 7-8 million meters installed
items.quote: We are expecting that all the smart meter projects, either at Maharashtra or Bihar, will be completed by March '27. By that time, the CAPEX part will be over. Then we will have the O&M revenue, which will be consistent and on a regular basis, it will be accruing to the organization.

items.statement: JJM outstanding INR 2,771 crore; collected INR 610 crore in Q1 and INR 413 crore in July; expect substantial completion in FY27
items.quote: The overall JJM projects, including the surface water and the groundwater, the total is INR 2,771 crores is the UBR. The amount collected during the 1st Quarter against this is INR 610 crores.

items.statement: Standalone debt expected to remain flat at ~INR 2,250 crore by March 2027 depending on JJM collections
items.quote: Yes, more or less. It will be the same number.

items.statement: Order book mix: Buildings 28%, Transportation 20%, Electrical T&D 16%, Mining 16%, Water & Railways 14%, Irrigation 6%
items.quote: The broad components of this order book as of the end of the 1st Quarter is the Buildings division stands at INR 22,357 crores, which is about 28% of the total order book. The Transportation division has an order book of INR 16,344 crores, which is about 20% of our order book. The Electrical T&D stands at INR 13,312 cr

items.statement: Expect all remaining quarters to be similar or better than Q1 FY27 performance
items.quote: We expect all quarters to be similar or better than this.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 8% in Q1 FY27 from 7.4% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved to 8% compared with 7.4% in Q4 FY26 and 6.9% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Gross profit margin expanded to 39.8% in Q1 FY27 from 37.4% in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Gross profit margins expanding to 39.8% from 37.4% supported by favorable product realization, better inventory management and efficient raw material utilization.

items.statement: PET food-grade chip project (50,000 MT/yr) to complete trials in Q4 FY27, commercial production in Q1 FY28
items.quote: This project is on ground in reality. So, we have the civil construction on. We have placed orders for all critical machines and project is likely to be completed in fourth quarter of this year for trials and commercial production may happen in quarter one of next financial year.

items.statement: Knitting capacity expansion from 650 to 900 tons/month including 150 tons printing, benefits from Q3 FY27
items.quote: Currently we have capacity of 650 tons. So, after this expansion probably we will be touching around 900 tons per month. So, in 900 tons, 150 tons will be printing, which is not there as of now.

items.statement: Denim garmenting JV approved, Phase 1 up to 5 lakh pieces/month, RSWM majority stake
items.quote: In the first phase, we may go up to 5 lakh pieces per month, which may further be added in two more phases in the coming period. So, this is in line with what we have been discussing in last 4-5 investor call meetings that we see potential in garmenting and downstream expansion from RSWM.

items.statement: Power cost reduction target ₹40 Cr for FY27 at same utilization, renewable share reached ~60% in Q1
items.quote: I think that should give us advantage to the tune of 40 crores for the year. The rest overall number will depend on if we increase more units and add more spindles or add more machines.

items.statement: Polyester fiber prices rose ~30% in March 2026, impacting April-June volumes
items.quote: The prices for polyester fiber went up as high as to the tune of 30%. So, thereby, uncertainty did prevail in terms of buying from customers.

items.statement: Domestic demand healthy and less volatile; export demand softer sequentially but in line with expectations
items.quote: Demand within India remained healthy across several customer segments supported by stable consumption and improved order execution. Export demand, while relatively softer on a sequential basis remained in line with expectations.

items.statement: Graphene fiber development with Birla Cellulose progressing, expect commercial traction within FY27
items.quote: I expect within this financial year we should get it rolling.

items.statement: Geopolitical issues (West Asia conflict), crude volatility, and US tariff developments creating supply chain and cost uncertainties
items.quote: Geopolitical developments including the West Asia conflict contributed to supply chain disruptions and volatilities in energy costs as well. Elevated crude oil prices have influenced input costs for synthetic yarn particularly.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand across power generation, mining, railways; exports challenged by geopolitics
items.quote: For the domestic market, we see from an end market perspective, power generation growth to be pretty strong. We have seen that in this quarter. I am basing my optimism based on the orders we are generating today.

items.statement: Data center inquiries show strong momentum with visibility into next 2 years
items.quote: The data center inquiries as they had picked up in the last few quarters, the momentum continues, very strong momentum on the data center side. And our execution has also been strong.

items.statement: One price hike taken at start of Q2; commodity inflation unprecedented, freight costs rising
items.quote: We have taken one, and we will continue seeing how the market adjusts to this price increase and then see how best to manage the cost inflation and the price increases going forward.

items.statement: Margins unlikely to return to historic highs soon due to unprecedented commodity inflation
items.quote: I will not be able to say whether we will hit historic highs or not, because these are unprecedented times in terms of commodity increases and inflation coming at the same time.

items.statement: Utilization at 70-75%; capex in line with recent years for existing plants
items.quote: Our utilization level is between 70% to 75%. So it has been consistently going up. And the capital investment is in line with what we have been doing in the last few years in our existing plants.

items.statement: Data centers contributed 40% of domestic power gen revenue in Q1 FY27 vs 23% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Data centers out of this, in this particular quarter, was 40% of overall power generation revenue.

items.statement: Related party transaction approvals for exports are for current year only, purely anticipatory
items.quote: This is purely in anticipation, Jonas, just as a prudent governance practice and order books don't get built this early in the year, they get built 2 to 3 months in advance only.

items.statement: West Asia crisis impacting Middle East exports; orders not bunching up for later delivery
items.quote: Whatever we are not able to fulfill the market in the Gulf will try and fulfill with whatever availability they have from their own region. These orders do not stay that long.

items.statement: Distribution business has potential for 20% growth this year and next few years
items.quote: DBU business absolutely has the potential to grow at 20% growth over this year and the next few years as well.

items.statement: BESS demonstrator installed at Phaltan rebuild center; close to getting orders
items.quote: We have already installed the BESS at one of our own plants, our own rebuild center in Phaltan. We have installed this BESS as a demonstrator and we are getting our customers to see and experience that.

items.statement: High horsepower export sales INR 296 cr in Q1 FY27, up 16% YoY and 37% QoQ
items.quote: High-horsepower exports at INR296 crores are a 16% increase over last year and 37% increase over last quarter.

items.statement: Rail segment growing on power cars and diesel-electric tower cars; hotel load converter acceptance good
items.quote: Rail has been growing good order board and good execution from our end. So largely, the applications where we have been getting orders are power cars and diesel electric tower cars.

items.statement: Royalty rates standardized to 4% from previous 1-8% range; proportion of sales increased to 2.5% in FY26
items.quote: Actually, we had some different royalty percentages for different services, which used to range between 1% to 8%. We have standardized it to 4%. That's all.

items.statement: Crude tanker order book at 27%, VLGC at 35%, product tankers at 20-21%, bulk carriers at 14%
items.quote: The order book now for crude tankers is at 27%. The order book for VLGCs is currently at 35%, which is a huge number for product tankers continues to be at about 20%, 21%, while bulk carriers are at about 14%, having picked up from about 10% to 12%.

items.statement: Invested INR 1,200 crores last year and INR 300 crores in Q1 FY27 on fleet modernization; additional INR 250-300 crores invested in July
items.quote: Last year, we invested about INR 1,200 crores in changing the fleet mix. So, we have invested INR 1,200 crores. This year, in the first quarter, we invested INR 300 crores in doing those transactions. Last month, already, we have invested between INR 250 crores and INR 300 crores.

items.statement: No fixed annual capex budget; replacement decisions ship-specific based on age and tradability, typically before 20-25 years
items.quote: No, we look at it more ship specific. We have a guiding idea because we know the ships, how they're aging and where we would ideally like to do certain things. But as you can imagine, if the markets change, we do change the way we stick to that plan.

items.statement: Eco-ship fuel savings up to 20-25% vs pre-2013 vessels, translating to $1,000-$2,500/day earnings improvement
items.quote: If you compare the ship built in the 2020s compared to what was built prior to 2013, fuel savings could be up to maybe 20%, 25%. And then depending on the size of the ship, it can translate from $1,000 to maybe even $2,000, $2,500 per day on the earnings.

items.statement: Structural trade shifts uncertain; Russian refinery attacks and Venezuela sanctions creating temporary dislocations, not necessarily permanent
items.quote: But it's not quite a structural. It just has happened. The refineries are down. There is a shortage of that diesel export from Russia, which has to be made up by other refineries. And that is not structural at all. It is a temporary phase.

items.statement: Treasury strategy: no US Treasury holdings; USD balances in bank, INR in debt funds/bank deposits
items.quote: We don't hold any cash in U.S. treasuries. Our money sits in the bank. We have some dollar balances, which just sit in the bank. Our rupee balances are invested in debt funds or bank deposits typically.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 revenue guidance of over INR2,500 crores with EBITDA margin range of 25% plus/minus 2%
items.quote: Accordingly, we reaffirm our guidance of achieving over INR2,500 crores in revenue for FY27 while maintaining EBITDA margin in the range of 25% plus/minus 2%.

items.statement: Medium-term target of 15-20% revenue CAGR and reaching INR3,500 crores in 3-4 years
items.quote: Over the medium term, we continue to target 15% to 20% revenue CAGR, supported by capacity expansion, increasing contribution from value-added products and backward integration through the TPU project.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin hit record 30.3% (up 544 bps YoY); management expects sustainable margins at 27-28% but maintains conservative guidance
items.quote: EBITDA increased 56% year-on-year to INR192 crores with EBITDA margin expanding by 544 basis points to a record of 30.30%, crossing the 30% milestone for the first time in company's history.

items.statement: TPU backward integration expected to add 1.5-2% margin expansion in FY28
items.quote: Yes. So we have given a guidance of 1.5% to 2% after this line comes into stream, of course, for FY28.

items.statement: Architectural films now >25% of revenue (up from 5%), Sun Control 55% and PPF 20% in Q1 FY27; shift to high-end IR rejection and architectural driving margin expansion
items.quote: If you really see like from 5% revenue percentage of architectural today stands more than 25%. So such kind of high-end products always lead to good margins.

items.statement: Healthy demand across Sun Control and PPF segments; strong export markets and India momentum; Middle East demand big but supply chain impacted by war
items.quote: Demand remained healthy across our key specialty segments, particularly Sun Control Films and Paint Protection Films, supported by improving demand across our key export markets and continued momentum in India.

items.statement: PPF old line at ~100% utilization, new line at ~60% (impacted by shipping delays); SCF new line peak revenue potential INR500-550 crores
items.quote: PPF old line is running almost 100% and the new one is running at the rate of roughly 60%. We lost some volume last quarter because of some delays in the shipping.

items.statement: Company debt-free with INR850 crores cash/liquid investments; evaluating inorganic growth and further capex for manufacturing reliability
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to remain one of our greatest strength despite investing over INR700 crores towards strategic expansions over the past few years, the company remains debt-free with a healthy cash and liquid investment balance of INR850 crores.

items.statement: Raw material correlation only 10-12% due to backward integration; cost increases passed on to customers after negotiation
items.quote: See, raw material on our consumer products, there is like the real impact. If I say correlation, if I talk, it's only 10% to 12%, direct correlation with the top end raw material, right?

items.statement: DGTR recommended antidumping duty on TPU-based PPF imports from China, creating level playing field for domestic manufacturers
items.quote: Another important development during the quarter has been DGTR's recommendation for antidumping duty on TPU-based paint protection film imports from China. We believe this represents an important step towards creating a more level playing field for domestic manufacturers.

items.statement: Expect raw material inflation of ~8% sequentially in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Based on the current outlook, we expect raw material inflation of about 8% sequentially into Q2.

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 FY27 capex was INR 650 crore; full-year capex expected to exceed INR 3,000 crore
items.quote: The full CapEx for Q1 was INR 650 crores at a consol level.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 11.7% in Q1 FY27, down 150 bps YoY due to RM cost pressures
items.quote: The consolidated revenue for the quarter stood at INR 74 billion with an EBITDA margin of 11.7%, down about 150 basis points year-on-year, primarily on account of RM cost pressures.

items.statement: India: 7-9% price hikes implemented in Q1 (staggered); need 15-16% total; further 1-2% hikes announced for July and August
items.quote: What was implemented and that also in a staggered manner through the quarter was about 7% to 9%. Further price increases into Q2 have already been announced.

items.statement: Europe: RM basket up 8% in Q1; need ~10% price hikes for Q1+Q2; only 3-4% implemented so far
items.quote: Europe, the price increases total for Q1, Q2 needed is about 10-odd percent. As of now, only 3% - 4% has been implemented.

items.statement: India demand healthy across categories; July off to strong start; expect momentum to carry into Q2
items.quote: Looking ahead, demand remains healthy across categories and channels. July already delivered a strong start, providing confidence that the momentum will carry into Q2.

items.statement: India volume growth: Replacement 13%, OEM 10%, Exports 15% YoY in Q1; all double-digit except TBB
items.quote: Replacement was 13% OEM was 10% and exports was 15%. So fairly in a narrow range, but all in double digits.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation in West Asia creating raw material, energy and logistics cost volatility
items.quote: The geopolitical situation in West Asia continued to create headwinds in select international markets, leading to heightened uncertainty and cost volatility across raw materials, energy and logistics costs.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt ~INR 1,700 crore; net debt/EBITDA 0.4x; expect ratio to rise slightly in FY27 as net borrower
items.quote: Absolute net debt just a minute. was about INR 1,700 plus crores.

items.statement: India Operations revenue INR 54.6B (+15.6% YoY, +4.3% QoQ); EBITDA margin 12% vs 13.6% YoY
items.quote: The revenue for the quarter was INR 54.6 billion, representing a healthy growth of 15.6% Y-o-Y and 4.3% sequentially.

items.statement: Europe Operations revenue EUR 147M (+0.5% YoY); EBITDA margin 8.9% vs 10.8% YoY due to Enschede transition costs
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter was EUR147 million, up 0.5% Y-o-Y. The EBITDA for the quarter stood at EUR13 million, a margin of 8.9%, lower than the previous year 10.8%.

items.statement: Raw material prices Q1 FY27: Natural rubber INR 225/kg, Synthetic rubber INR 250/kg, Carbon black INR 125/kg, Steel cord INR 165/kg; expect NR avg INR 260+ in Q2
items.quote: rubber this quarter was at INR 225, synthetic rubber, INR 250, carbon black, INR 125 and steel cord, INR 165.

items.statement: MIBK, MIBC, acetophenone commissioning in August; multipurpose agrochemical intermediates facility within Q2 FY27
items.quote: MIBK as well as MIBC will be commissioned along with acetophenone in August itself, and the rest of them will be commissioned within Q2.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 21% in Q1 FY27 from 11% YoY and 18% QoQ; Phenolics EBIT margin 24%, AI EBIT margin 8%
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded to 21% compared to 18% in previous quarter and 11% in Q1 FY26. Margin expansion was supported by higher operating leverage, favorable product mix, backward integration benefits, improved manufacturing efficiencies and continued cost discipline.

items.statement: Ammonia-to-amines integration chain completed; no longer just nitration company but nitrogen company that nitrates
items.quote: One of the most strategic and significant developments over the last few quarters has been the successful completion and stabilization of our ammonia-to-amines integration chain. This gives me the opportunity to say that we're no longer a nitration company that buys nitric acid. We're now a nitrogen company that nitrat

items.statement: AI segment 33% YoY revenue growth driven by improving domestic demand, better product mix, export market strengthening
items.quote: Performance was driven by improving domestic demand, a better product mix and increasing synergies from our recent backward integration and growing contribution from other commissioned manufacturing assets.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments and pricing volatility may continue; raw material cost pressure in AI for certain products
items.quote: While geopolitical developments and pricing volatility may continue to influence the operating environment, Deepak today is significantly stronger, significantly more integrated and significantly more diversified.

items.statement: Debt for INR 11,500 crore project fully tied up at competitive rates; peak debt estimated INR 8,000-8,500 crore including working capital; debt-to-equity to stay below 1x
items.quote: So today, at this INR 11,500 crore what we are having against that, we are borrowing around INR 6,800 crore plus working capital, whatever is required, in the business at the peak. So that would be somewhere around INR 8,000 crore to INR 8,500 crore. But debt-to-equity ratio will be very, very comfortable. It will not

items.statement: Polycarbonate project targeting H2 FY28-29 commissioning; BPA plant a few months later; aligned with PDH propylene supply
items.quote: I would anticipate that we would target H2 for our polycarbonate commissioning. And we would target BPA, which would be commissioned maybe a couple of months after that.

items.statement: Competitive raw material procurement across ammonia, toluene, benzene, propylene, hydrogen; propylene from PDH to further improve competitiveness
items.quote: Whether it is ammonia, whether it is toluene, whether it is benzene or propylene or hydrogen, I think it would be a reasonable assumption to make that we would be absolutely competitive compared to anybody else in the country and perhaps competitive enough compared to anybody else on a global basis as well.

items.statement: Flow chemistry platform reduces reaction time from 16-18 hours to 45-52 seconds; commercial scale-up expected next financial year
items.quote: One product that we're making currently in a batch or in a semi batch, it takes us about 16 to 18 hours from feedstock to finished product. This gets completed in roughly between 45 to 52 seconds.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target >30% YoY, EBITDA margin ~6%, PAT margin 3.5-4%
items.quote: Based on the current demand environment and our execution roadmap, we remain confident of delivering more than 30% revenue in the current financial year '27 along with the EBITDA margin of around 6% and a profit after tax in the range of 3.5 % to 4%.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds: INR100cr working capital, INR50cr Nakoda CP plant, INR23cr debt repayment, INR22cr solar plant
items.quote: The board has approved the allotment of 16.84 crores equity shares at an issue price of INR11.86 per share, raising INR199.75 crores with net proceeds of approximately INR194.90 crores available for deployment towards our strategic growth initiatives.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 3.24% impacted by raw material volatility; expect gross margins >25% and EBITDA 6% for FY27
items.quote: We are very confident that we will be able to achieve our gross margins over 25% and maintain the same so that we can achieve our EBITDA levels.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions caused crude/PTA/MEG volatility and freight cost spikes; raw material prices not yet at pre-war levels
items.quote: Due to the geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and US, there was a sharp increase in the crude oil prices, which resulted in significant volatility in our raw material, such as PTA and MEG, along with elevated freight and logistics costs.

items.statement: No tax losses or unabsorbed depreciation available; all settled during NCLT process
items.quote: No, no, it was everything was used up and we had cleared the balance sheet. When the liabilities were written off, in that everything was settled.

items.statement: Expect margin pressure in short term due to elevated costs from war; will pass on some but not all cost increases
items.quote: So, in the short term, margins are likely to be impacted.

items.statement: Taken 7-10% price hikes in non-household segments; household cooler segment hikes pending; further hikes depend on war duration and cost normalization
items.quote: In the other segment, we have taken 7% to 10% of a price hike. And in others, we will be taking hikes in the days to come.

items.statement: Mexico expects significant growth in summer FY27 after two consecutive mild summers; USA growth continues if summer remains robust; China momentum to continue on export orders
items.quote: So, we hope and we expect that the summer of '27, statistically, it will be almost impossible for it to be a mild summer. It should be certainly a fairly robust summer, and the sales should grow significantly.

items.statement: Middle East exports still affected by geopolitical issues; other regions face high shipping costs impacting buyer sentiment and demand
items.quote: So, the Middle East, which was primarily impacted, continues to remain affected.

items.statement: BISP (Beyond India Summer Products) contributed ₹560 crore (48% of consolidated TTM revenue) and ₹179 crore (23% of standalone TTM revenue)
items.quote: BISP segment i.e. Beyond India Summer Products i.e. the sales, product wise or segment wise, not dependent upon Indian summer, constituted about ₹560 crore on a consol basis in trailing 12 months i.e. almost 48% reinforcing our strategic derisking and diversification from Indian summer.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin improved to 49.8% and EBITDA margin to 12.6% in Q1 FY27 despite commodity pressure and inventory overhang
items.quote: we have marginally increased the gross margin percentage to 49.8% , while EBITDA margin percentage to 12.6%.

items.statement: Geopolitical war and shipping disruptions causing elevated costs and export headwinds; Middle East exports remain affected
items.quote: it all depends on how long the war lasts and when the costs begin to normalize.

items.statement: Interim dividend of ₹1 per share (face value ₹2) announced, total payout ~₹7 crore
items.quote: For June '26 quarter, the Board of Directors had announced interim dividend of ₹1 per share on a face value of ₹2 with a total payout of about ₹7 crore.

items.statement: Standalone ROCE at 164% and consolidated ROCE at 67% after capital rationalization from CTPL impairment; treasury at ₹345 crore after repaying ₹225 crore Australia loans
items.quote: core capital employed on standalone is ₹73 crore versus ₹136 crore, translating into ROCE percentage of 164, while return on net worth at 22% and treasury stands at ₹345 crore versus ₹363 crore.

items.statement: Q1 domestic sales grew 15% despite inventory overhang; no inventory overhang at trade or company level as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: domestic sales i.e. India revenue grew by 15%, despite huge inventory overhang before the summer and importantly all different segments of modern trade grew in excess of 100%.

items.statement: Australia strategy: no new capital deployment, no new product introductions, just optimizing existing operations
items.quote: First and foremost, our strategy is not to deploy any additional capital and whatever best can be done without deploying any additional capital in our Australian business.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 PAT guidance of INR200-220 crores, representing 34-48% growth over FY26
items.quote: we remain confident of delivering our FY '27 profit after tax guidance of INR200 crores to INR220 crores, representing the healthy growth of 34% to 48% over FY '26

items.statement: Board authorized INR190 crores additional investments, bringing FY27 total new projects to INR340 crores; including carryforward, total capex ~INR500 crores
items.quote: The Board has authorized additional investments towards new expansion projects of INR190 crores, bringing the total for FY '27 to INR340 crores. This is in addition to the INR150 crores worth of projects carried forward from FY '26

items.statement: Signed projects totaling ~INR340 crores in FY27; expect to commercialize capacities exceeding INR500 crores during FY27
items.quote: we have already signed on various projects totaling to around INR340 crores in this financial year. Including these investments and the projects already under implementation, we expect to commercialize manufacturing capacities exceeding INR500 crores during FY '27

items.statement: Footwear business faced INR6 crores impact in Q1 from higher raw material costs and revised wage rates; expect progressive mitigation and margin recovery
items.quote: The quarter numbers were impacted due to cost pressure faced in our footwear business arising from higher raw material costs and revised wage rates, which totaling to around INR6 crores impact for Q1 FY '27

items.statement: Most contracts have pass-through mechanism for labor code changes and inflation; footwear contracts fixed 6-8 months advance, no mid-season pass-through
items.quote: most of our contracts other than shoes, we have a pass -through mechanism. And as a result, whether it is the changes in the labor code or whether it is the changes in the inflationary aspect of Middle East crisis, et cetera, we've been able to successfully pass on those costs

items.statement: Capex allocation: F&B INR210 crores (5 units), Ice Cream INR80 crores (Panipat), HPC INR50 crores (Lucknow); beverages and ice cream highlighted as major growth avenues
items.quote: Food and beverages, INR210 crores at Coimbatore, Mysuru, Goa, Aurangabad and Hyderabad plant. Ice Cream, INR80 crores at Panipat; Home and Personal Care, INR50 crores at Lucknow

items.statement: FY27 revenue target to cross INR15,000 crores with high-teens EBITDA growth, aspiring for 20% EBITDA growth
items.quote: We are confident of achieving high-teens EBITDA growth and aspire to touch 20% EBITDA growth during this year. We expect India to deliver high single-digit volume growth and international business to deliver mid-teens constant currency growth.

items.statement: International business targeting mid-teens constant currency growth for FY27
items.quote: We expect India to deliver high single-digit volume growth and international business to deliver mid-teens constant currency growth.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 40 bps YoY to 20.7% in Q1 FY27; full-year EBITDA margin expansion guided at 140-150 bps
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved 40 basis points year-on-year to 20.7%.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 30 bps YoY in Q1 FY27; management aims to hold gross margin percentage for full year despite mixed input cost trends
items.quote: Gross margin expanded 30 basis points year-on-year, led by softer copra prices, a favourable channel and portfolio mix.

items.statement: Copra prices expected to remain range-bound at 30-35% below last year's peak; crude and vegetable oils showing upward bias with higher input costs expected in Q2
items.quote: Copra prices have corrected meaningfully. While it has seen some upward bias recently, we expect prices to be range bound at around 35% lower than the last year's peak levels. On the other side, crude and vegetable oils continue to exhibit an upward bias. And consequently, we expect input costs to be relatively higher

items.statement: Domestic demand remains healthy with India delivering 11% volume growth in Q1; over 96% of business gaining or sustaining market share
items.quote: The India business delivered one of the strongest quarters in recent years with 11% volume growth and revenue growth of 21%.

items.statement: A&P spend grew 25% in Q1 FY27 as company invests significantly behind brands, innovations and consumer salience
items.quote: Advertising and sales promotion expenses grew substantially at 25% as we continue to invest significantly behind our brands to strengthen their long-term equity, support innovation, some of the big innovations we have launched this quarter, and drive consumer salience.

items.statement: Tax rate guidance: ~18% for FY27 and 19-20% for FY28 at consolidated level
items.quote: Yes. So this year, tax this quarter, it was about 17.5%. I think from a full year perspective, you can take a guidance of about 18% for FY27 and maybe about 19% to 20% for FY28.

items.statement: Reiterated FY27 guidance of 9-11% revenue growth with EBITDA margin expansion of 50-100 bps over FY26
items.value: 9-11% revenue growth; 50-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: On the outlook front, we reiterate our FY '27 guidance of 9% to 11% revenue growth with EBITDA margin expansion of 50 to 100 basis points over FY '26.

items.statement: Mid-to-long-term target of 12-15% growth and INR 5,000-5,500 crore revenue by FY30
items.quote: Looking further ahead, we remain confident in our journey towards achieving 12% to 15% growth in mid - to long-term as we continue to scale our digital platforms across geographies, brands and channels.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded to 11% from 9.2% in Q1 FY26; gross margin at 67%
items.quote: EBITDA came in at INR102 crores, up 37% year-on-year with EBITDA margin at 11%, a strong improvement from 9.2% in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Macro volatility (wars, oil prices) cited as reason for conservative FY30 guidance; US discretionary spending weak due to fuel/grocery inflation
items.quote: The macroeconomic environment is very volatile. It keeps on changing with how the world is moving towards different war, oil prices up and down. So considering all in our mind, we have kept our number like that.

items.statement: Music vertical revenue growth guidance maintained at 20-23% YoY for FY27
items.quote: If I have to look at on a full year basis, we maintain our guidance of the music vertical growing between 20% to 23% year-on-year.

items.statement: Annual music EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 60-65%
items.quote: For the music vertical, we maintain our medium-term guidance of 20% to 23% revenue growth and an annual music EBITDA margin guidance of 60% to 65%.

items.statement: New music content spend expected at Rs 300-350 crore for FY27, mostly committed
items.quote: Our spend on new music content this year is expected to be anything between Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 350 crores. Most of that is already committed.

items.statement: 60% of FY26 music revenue came from post-2000 releases, 45% from post-2020 releases
items.quote: In FY'26, 60% of all music revenue at Saregama came from music released post 2000. I'm repeating . 60% of the revenue in last financial year came from music of the 21st century.

items.statement: Paid streaming penetration in India at 3% vs 67% in Sweden, 57% in US; target 100M subscribers at Rs 100/month if free content curtailed
items.quote: We believe in Indian market, if the subscription is priced correctly, which means closer to Rs. 100 and if the supply of free content somewhere are curtailed, we should not have a problem touching 100 million paid subscription mark pretty soon.

items.statement: Major album pipeline includes Love & War (Jan), Rajinikanth's Dharman, Paradise, Naagzilla, Bhansali-Tiger Shroff film, Arjan Dhillon album in Q2
items.quote: Big albums lined up including Love and War, which is coming out in January, Rajinikanth's Dharman, which is a Kamal Haasan's Company's production; Telegu Cinema's most awaited film Paradise; Dharma's film with Kartik Aaryan called Naagzilla and another Bhansali Productions film with Tiger Shroff are some of the albums

items.statement: Music EBITDA margin dipped 1% YoY due to Artiste Management mix shift (lower margin, zero investment)
items.quote: If you see the segmental results that people have declared, you will see Artiste Management piece is also growing. And Artiste Management is always a lower margin. It takes zero investments. Artiste Management part of the revenue is always a lower margin part.

items.statement: Video/films business being wound down consciously; revenue to decline over next 3-4 quarters as existing films cleared
items.quote: We have shared with you after our Bhansali acquisition that we are taking a conscious call to wind down our films business and make all our investments through the Bhansali Productions channel, which means the film segment revenue is eventually going to come down.

items.statement: Pocket Aces reached breakeven in FY26, expected to turn profitable in FY27
items.quote: Pocket Aces reached breakeven in financial year '26 and is now moving towards profitability. This year, we should be seeing further building on the profitability of Pocket Aces.

items.statement: Artiste Management represents 309 artists with 440M+ followers; revenue run-rate ~Rs 40 cr/quarter, margins ~10% with scope to improve
items.quote: At the end of this quarter, we represent 309 artists with more than 440 million follower and subscriber base for these artists on Instagram and YouTube combined.

items.statement: Live Events expanding: 23 Carvaan Live shows, 22 devotional shows, 48 standard packs in Q1; Ilaiyaraaja US tour underway, Arjan Dhillon US tour in Sept, Diljit India tour tentative Q3
items.quote: 23 such shows were produced in quarter 1. We further built up our devotional format with 22 shows featuring Manoj Muntashir, Backstage Siblings and Jaya Kishori during the quarter. We also staged 48 standard packs during this quarter.

items.statement: AI music video creation cost as low as Rs 70,000; AI teams created for content generation and process optimization, impact expected by year-end
items.quote: The cost of a music video, if it is done through AI can be Rs. 70,000 also. So the numbers are that small at this moment.

items.statement: Expect to exceed full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance significantly; EBITDA and volume growth may exceed slightly; cash conversion may be squeezed
items.quote: We remain firmly on track to deliver our guidance for the full year with the confidence to exceed the same in select areas.

items.statement: Will certainly exceed revenue growth guidance; EBITDA may exceed double-digit growth target slightly; volume growth may meet or slightly exceed
items.quote: We'll certainly exceed it on revenue growth pretty significantly. On EBITDA, we may exceed by a little bit the original number that we had set of double-digit EBITDA growth may go up a little bit.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin target 22-26% even in weak quarters; expect recovery to normative margins by H2 FY27 after Q1 hit from LPG, kerosene, LABSA cost spikes
items.quote: Our target is to be in this 22% to 26% kind of margin for India even in a weak quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 19% in Q1 FY27; India gross margin fell sharply due to 3x cost inflation in LPG, kerosene, LABSA
items.quote: At a consolidated level, revenues grew 19% year-on-year with underlying volume growth of 9%. EBITDA grew 14% with margins at 19%.

items.statement: Took ~5% weighted average price increase in India in Q1; may take similar increase in Q2; pricing calibrated to volatile crude-linked commodity costs
items.quote: We've taken up prices by about 5%. We probably will still take up a little bit more, but you see we have to be prudent because now costs have come down again.

items.statement: Consolidated underlying volume growth 9% in Q1 FY27; confident of reaching consistent double-digit volume growth in a few quarters
items.quote: This quarter, consolidated underlying volume growth reached 9%, supported by increasingly broad-based momentum across geographies and categories.

items.statement: Speedboats (Fab, GK Incense, Godrej Air, new entries) growing strongly; launched Godrej Rizz in liquid dishwash (INR2,500-3,000 cr category growing double-digits)
items.quote: We are pleased to announce the launch of Godrej Rizz, our entry into liquid dishwash. Liquid dishwash is a INR2,500 crores to INR3,000 crore category, which is growing in strong double digits.

items.statement: GAUM constant currency growth ~25% in Q1; mid-to-high teens growth sustainable for rest of FY27; FMCG now ~50% of GAUM revenue, driving 75% of growth
items.quote: I think for FY27, rest of the year, possibly so. I would say in the longer term, you may or may not get 17% volume growth may not be what we may sustainably get even with FMCG growth.

items.statement: El Nino impact: India HI weak in H1, better in H2; Indonesia HI positive; palm crop risk later; geographically diversified sourcing provides resilience
items.quote: We remain mindful that El Nino conditions can heighten weather volatility across our key markets with the potential to disrupt agricultural output and rural demand.

items.statement: Committed INR500 cr to pet care business; expanded from Tamil Nadu to rest of South India after achieving product-market fit
items.quote: I think the important thing is that when we launched the pet care business, we committed INR500 crores of capital to pet care.

items.statement: Indonesia 10% growth in Q1 driven by slower base, stepped-up air care media, El Nino benefit; Stellar business showing faster growth
items.quote: I think there are 3 things. One is Indonesia is sitting on a slightly slower base. And even last year, we were unduly worried about the volumes because the second thing is that our air business, we have significantly stepped-up media on our air business there.

items.statement: LPG price spiked from INR60/kg to INR190/kg (3x) in Q1; now back to INR90/kg; Q2 consumption still impacted, full normalization by Q3
items.quote: LPG before the war was INR60 a kilo. At the peak of the war, it went to INR190. I think our average consumption was about maybe, I don't know, a little lower than that, and it's now back to INR90 a kilo.

items.statement: Board approved INR90 crore capex for advanced materials adoption capacity funded through internal accruals
items.quote: The Board has approved a new capex of INR90 crores funded through internal accruals towards setting up adoption capacities for our advanced materials business.

items.statement: Phase 2 cGMP4 capex of INR125 crore initiated for CDMO business, expected to operationalize by Q4 FY27
items.quote: In addition to the capex in the advanced materials, we have initiated in our CDMO business, Phase 2 cGMP 4 capex of INR125 crores funded through internal accruals, expected to operationalize by Q4 FY '27.

items.statement: Renewable energy project of INR15.73 crore for 14.9 MW hybrid captive power to meet >60% energy needs
items.quote: A renewable energy project, an investment of INR15.73 crores in a group captive hybrid renewable project for 14.9 megawatts of renewable power supports our sustainability and decarbonization goals.

items.statement: CDMO cGMP4 capex (INR288 crore) targeting 3x asset turn by FY29
items.quote: On the INR288 crores, we've talked of an asset turn of 3x, and I think we've said that by FY '29, if I remember correctly.

items.statement: CDMO revenue target of $100 million for FY27 remains on track
items.quote: Yes, the $100 million is very much on track.

items.statement: HFC pricing environment remains constructive supported by favorable demand-supply dynamics
items.quote: The pricing environment of HFCs remain constructive, supported by favorable demand supply dynamics.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals facing pricing pressure in LatAm market but offset by patented molecules and productivity gains
items.quote: While volume growth is recovering, pricing pressure continues to remain, particularly in the LatAm market, which is already well supplied.

items.statement: Long-term R32 demand to double over decade while quota-driven supply shrinks by half
items.quote: We all know that over a decade, the demand for 32 is going to double, while the supply -- quota-driven supply is going to sort of shrink to half.

items.statement: Advanced materials vertical targeting data centers, electronics, semiconductors, defense with 12+ products in pipeline, 5 lab-approved
items.quote: This vertical will focus on niche sort of applications in high-growth sectors, mainly data centers, electronics, defense and semiconductors.

items.statement: Expect meaningful acceleration in biosimilars revenue in H2 FY27 driven by new launches and expanded insulin capacity
items.quote: Q1 performance was broadly in line with our expectations, and we expect momentum to build progressively through the year with meaningful acceleration in the second half of FY'27.

items.statement: Syngene expects single-digit revenue degrowth in rupee terms for full FY27 with EBITDA margins returning to mid-20s
items.quote: While revenues are expected to decline in the first half, performance should improve in the second half, resulting in a single-digit revenue degrowth in rupee terms for the full year and EBITDA margins back to mid-20s.

items.statement: Biosimilars EBITDA margin at 25% in Q1 FY27; management targets mid-20s margin normalized from last year's 27%
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR728 crores, representing a growth of 10% year-on-year and this translates into an EBITDA margin of 25%

items.statement: Generics EBITDA margin improved to 7% in Q1 FY27, up 250 bps QoQ driven by volumes and operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA margin at 7% improved more than 250 basis points over Q4FY'26, driven by higher volumes and operating leverage.

items.statement: Strong demand for insulin franchise globally; Malaysia facility second line approved by EMA and supplying from Q2 FY27
items.quote: We achieved a significant manufacturing milestone with EMA approval for the second drug product line at our Malaysia insulin facility. Supplies from this line have started and should pick up further from Q2 FY'27.

items.statement: Five key biosimilar products (Aflibercept, Denosumab, Aspart, Ustekinumab, Bevacizumab) to drive H2 FY27 growth
items.quote: These five products will drive growth. We have been contracting for some of these products in recent days.

items.statement: No plans to increase capex for new US manufacturing facilities; will pursue partnerships instead
items.quote: No, I don't believe that we will be increasing our capex in establishing new facilities or capacities in the US. We will look at it through partnerships, if required.

items.statement: US tariff risk on generics/biosimilars currently low as existing law exempts them; legislation change required
items.quote: Right now, the law states within the United States, generics and biosimilars are exempt. So, legislation would have to be passed and redone.

items.statement: Net debt increased INR1,100 crore QoQ due to inventory build for H2 scale-up; free cash flow prioritized for debt reduction
items.quote: The increase in inventory, working capital is largely in inventory, and that's basically we are getting ready for the second-half scale-up in both biosimilars and generics.

items.statement: Generics profitability improved via API pricing premium, R&D portfolio optimization, and opex reduction
items.quote: The improvement that you're seeing in the Generics profitability is because of three things. One is some of the premium on API products, pricing premium; secondly, optimization of the R&D portfolio; and thirdly, opex.

items.statement: Active payer contracting underway for July-September window to secure FY28 market access for key biosimilars
items.quote: You know that July to September is the window when most of these payor negotiations finalize for full year for the following calendar year, and I think what I can tell you at this point in time is we are in a good place to have those conversations.

items.statement: Biosimilars R&D investment at 7% of revenue in Q1 FY27; generics API to formulation split at 60:40
items.quote: R&D investments for the quarter stood at 7% of revenues.

items.statement: Target new product launch every year in US or Europe through end of decade
items.quote: The focus has always been to see that we have a new product launch either in the US or in Europe every year from here on till the end of the decade.

items.quote: I think at this point of time, what we are saying is that let's maintain -- I mean, rather than giving a very clear outlook, I mean, what we are saying is we will maintain or we'll better the numbers what we have done for Q1.

items.quote: Raw material prices, geopolitics and global demand are outside our control, and we take nothing for granted.

items.quote: Critical minerals are something we are interested in because it's certainly adjacent to our skill set. We have looked at a couple of blocks but have unfortunately not been successful in the bid.
