items.quote: Once there is no major change, we can with the low CapEx and hardly any working capital requirement, debt free, we don't see any major shift in the dividend payout policy.

items.statement: Current order book stands at ₹13,596 crore comprising 11 projects and 44 marine platforms, down from above ₹15,000 crore for the first time in 10 years due to strong execution.
items.quote: Our current order book stands at ₹13,596 crore and this comprises mostly of shipbuilding orders with shipbuilding divisions contributing to ₹13,296 crore and the other two divisions, the engineering and the engine divisions, contribute to the balance of the order book.

items.statement: Non-defense share of shipbuilding order book risen to 25% from 2% historically; executing research vessels, export ferries, dredger, multipurpose vessels, and platform support vessels.
items.quote: There was a period when 98% of the shipbuilding order book was comprised of defence orders, but now the split, the breakup has been different, mostly because we have been executing the research ship projects for various ministries, and of course the export orders.

items.statement: Capacity expansion from 28 to 32 concurrent platforms by end CY2026 via brownfield; greenfield yards at Raichak and Gujarat to raise capacity to 43 platforms including large commercial vessels (Aframax, VLGC).
items.quote: We intend, with the creation of these two facilities, the capacity constraint will be completely obliterated, and we will have the capability to build 43 platforms, and the 11 platforms, 11 types of platforms, that means from 32 to 43 platforms, there will be large vessels of Aframax and VLGC type.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 PAT up 44% YoY to ₹173 crore; EPS up 44% to ₹15.09; revenue from operations up 39% to ₹1,815 crore.
items.quote: The profit after tax has moved up by 44% from ₹ 120 crore to ₹173 crore during this period and the earnings per share has increased by 44% from ₹10.49 to ₹ 15.09.

items.statement: Employee cost may rise 15-20% due to upcoming pay commission; already factored into projections.
items.quote: Our anticipation is that it could be of similar range 15-20% which is normal in every pay commission. We don't see any abnormality, and we have already factored those in our, let us say, future projections and calculations.

items.statement: Execution momentum to continue in FY27; major projects P-17A (₹4,519 cr left) and ASW SWC (₹1,815 cr left) nearing completion, supporting near-term revenue.
items.quote: The current quarter's performance will be able to replicate in the coming quarters too.

items.statement: Next Generation Destroyer (NGD) RFP not expected before FY29 (DAC approval pending, 1.5-2 years to RFP after DAC).
items.quote: I do not expect the RFP to come out for NGD till FY29, because currently we are in FY27. Considering, depending upon the priority that Navy has got, even if a DAC approval is taken in the current financial year, it could take about a year-and-a-half for the RFP to come out.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance maintained at 12-15% for FY27
items.quote: No. We will stick to our guidance on growth going forward.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 11-13% for FY27
items.quote: Our guidance is 11% to 13% kind of operating margin.

items.statement: Q1 capex of INR 40-42 crore spent on Bhuj plant second tranche; full year plan unchanged
items.quote: For this quarter, around INR 40 crores, INR 42 crores has been spent, and that has primarily been on the completion of second tranche of Bhuj plant takeover.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin at 13%, up 600 bps YoY driven by product mix and pricing
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 77 crores, a growth of 93% Y-o-Y, while margins stood at 13%, registering a 600 basis point growth.

items.statement: Plumbing share increased vs agri; CPVC/PPR/PP contribution improved vs PVC
items.quote: So one is agri versus building material and second is PVC versus CPVC, PP, PPR. So both product mix improvements at a segmental and at a polymer level has helped as far as gross margin is concerned.

items.statement: Channel restocking resumed in June-July after April destocking; MIP provides price floor
items.quote: In June and July, we saw better stocking from channel partners, which is more reflective of the secondary demand or the last mile demand.

items.statement: CPVC price hikes being passed on in phased manner over 1-2 weeks
items.quote: I think we are passing it on in a phase-wise manner. So usually, we give 1 to 2 weeks to the channel.

items.statement: Inventory days at 100 vs 65-75 guidance due to supply insecurity and volume miss; expects correction by Q2 end
items.quote: We should see immediate correction in inventory. This is not a structural thing. We will be back to our stated guidance by end of September quarter.

items.statement: Bathware revenue INR 13 crore, EBITDA loss INR 5 crore in Q1; expects INR 25 crore quarterly run rate by Q3
items.quote: In the December quarter, we should be doing INR 25 crores, which will be very close to break even.

items.statement: Capacity utilization at 52-53%; 12-15% volume growth would take it to ~60%
items.quote: As of now, we are at around 52% - 53% kind of utilization. And what we have guided is 13% to 15% of growth in this year, which translates to, if the capacity is static, then we will reach to around 60% of utilization.

items.statement: Targeting industry-leading volume growth via network expansion, digitization, new products
items.quote: We are confident that more long-term initiatives like network expansion and digitizing of value chain, new product innovation. These are going to be the levers of sustainable growth going forward.

items.statement: DECILO PP drainage pipes launched at Haridwar; installed in residential, hospitals, hotels
items.quote: We have developed our polypropylene-based drainage system, DECILO, which is designed to deliver superior performance across these parameters.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 lowest quarter; expect improvement in Q2 FY27 and YoY growth from H2 FY27
items.quote: As we had indicated in our previous earnings call, Q1 of this year would be our lowest quarter ever, and that is how the quarter has played out. From here onwards, we expect improvement in Q2FY27 and the return to year-on-year growth from the second half.

items.statement: Sequential improvement in Q2 FY27; YoY comparability by end of H1; YoY growth from H2 FY27
items.quote: The recovery phasing outlined by Umang is in line with our financial framework. We expect sequential improvement in Q2FY27and movement towards the year-on-year comparability by end of the first half and a return on year-on-year growth from the second half.

items.statement: Margin recovery weighted to H2 FY27; pace depends on revenue conversion, mix, utilization, milestones
items.quote: Given the unusually low operating base inQ1FY27, margin recovery will be weighted towards the second half of the year. The pace of improvement will depend on the revenue conversion, business mix, utilization, and delivery against the operating milestones discussed today.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target closer to previous year level in FY27; acceleration from FY28 onwards
items.quote: So Foram we should be looking at a number which will be closer to previous year margin percentage for the current year. And we should thereafter start accelerating from FY28 onwards.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex approximately INR 598 million
items.quote: Capital expenditure during the quarter was approximately INR598 million as we continue to invest in capabilities required for future growth.

items.statement: Robust API order book supporting outlook for the year
items.quote: These were largely timing-related factors, and importantly, the underlying demand remains healthy, with a robust API order book supporting our outlook for the year.

items.statement: Restocking order secured for one commercial molecule; delivery visibility for Q4 FY27 and FY28
items.quote: For one commercial molecule that faced destocking last year, we have now received the restocking order, providing meaningful delivery visibility for Q4 FY27 and FY28.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 71.5% in Q1 FY27 vs 73% in Q1 FY26; decline due to mix and lower high-margin Pharma CDMO contribution
items.quote: Consolidated gross margin was at 71.5% compared with 73% in Q1 FY26. The decline primarily reflected the product mix and the lower contribution from the high-margin Pharma CDMO business.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA INR 92 million (2.2% margin); standalone EBITDA INR 332 million (9.2% margin)
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA was at INR92 million, representing a margin of 2.2%. The reduction reflects the lower revenue base, negative operating leverage, and the impact of subsidiary consolidation. It is important to look at the components of the consolidated performance. The standalone business generated a revenue of INR3,599

items.statement: Pharma CDMO RFQ pipeline strengthening with Phase 3 KSM commercial supply inquiries from large pharma and Western CDMOs
items.quote: Our RFQ pipeline continued to strengthen during the quarter, supported by many Phase 3 KSM commercial supply inquiries from a large pharma company, along with additional commercial and late-stage inquiries from all the large pharmaceutical customers and Western CDMOs.

items.statement: Biotech funding environment influencing timing of customer decisions and FTE renewals at NJ Bio
items.quote: We remain watchful of the biotech funding environment, which continues to influence the timing of customer decisions and FTE renewals.

items.statement: Sapala reported 2.5x revenue growth in Q1 FY27; supply commenced on specialized nucleic acid building blocks program
items.quote: In oligonucleotide segment, under Sapala, supply commenced on the specialized nucleic acid building blocks program during Q1FY27. As a result, Sapala reported 2.5x revenue growth in Q1.

items.statement: USFDA inspection of Pashamylaram facility (Jul 27-Aug 5, 2026) resulted in Form 483 with five observations; none relate to data integrity
items.quote: I also want to add that we have just announced that USFDA has completed an inspection of our Pashamylaram facility, which was conducted from 27th July to 5th August, 2026. Following this, we received a Form 483 with five observations. None of them relate to data integrity.

items.statement: Expects gross margin to improve by at least 1% YoY in FY27 and settle between 40-42% over next 2-3 years
items.quote: We are very confident of the current margin levels, and we are also confident of improving from here. We hope that on a year-on-year basis, there is some headroom, and we will be able to improve at least 1% on gross margin year-on-year.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 14-15% in next 2-3 years from current 11.2%
items.quote: On the EBITDA margins, yes, that is where the endeavor is. We believe that we'll be able to grow at least a percentage even on the margin side year-on-year, which will ultimately in the range, in the next two to three years, we should be in the range of 14-15%.

items.statement: Expects export contribution (including IKEA) to reach 15% of revenue in next two years from ~12% currently
items.quote: As of last year, we had about 12% contribution to the revenue. As the company grows, we believe even in spite of the growth overall as a company, our export contribution in the next two years, that is the current and the next year, should get to 15%.

items.statement: Targets 500 standalone Pigeon exclusive outlets by end of 2027; added 17 stores in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Further, we added 17 new stores under franchise model during the quarter, reinforcing our retail expansion strategy and advancing our long-term objective of establishing 500 standalone Pigeon exclusive outlets by the year end 2027.

items.statement: Expects Induction Cooktop contribution to stabilize at 20%+ of full year FY27 revenue
items.quote: We are confident of this, contribution from Induction Cooktop to be in the range of, at least 20% and a little above that as we progress over the year.

items.statement: Targets non-induction categories to grow at nearly 20% consistently
items.quote: Our endeavor is to actually take the non-induction growth to nearly 20% if possible, if you are able to do everything right.

items.statement: Expects Q2 FY27 to be as strong as Q1 with growth over high base of last year
items.quote: Historically, the Q2 is the strongest and we will continue to be there. Obviously, because the Q1 was stronger, the Q2 has to be in line with that. It may not be exactly at the same rate of growth of Q1, but definitely there is a very strong demand, that we are witnessing. So we believe that the Q2 will be as strong.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin expanded 127 bps YoY to 39.6%; EBITDA margin expanded 71 bps YoY to 11.2%
items.quote: Gross profit for the quarter stood at INR190.4 crores versus INR130.4 crores in Q1 FY26, a growth of 46% year-on-year. Despite ongoing supply chain challenges and elevated raw material costs. Also, gross margins expanded by 127 basis points year-on-year

items.statement: Increased domestic prices and export realizations to pass through input cost inflation; follows cost-plus model
items.quote: We have increased our prices for the domestic market. We also are, there's a favorable situation even in our exports. They have corrected their buying prices upwards to address the input cost.

items.statement: Induction Cooktop demand remains structurally higher than pre-war levels; expects annualized 2x growth vs last year
items.quote: On an annualized basis, we still believe that we will be a 2x of last year.

items.statement: Premiumization driving mix shift: stainless steel pressure cookers growing faster than aluminium; retail channel grew 86% YoY
items.quote: We have grown higher in our stainless steel pressure cooker versus our aluminium pressure cooker, which also means, I mean, it's the product mix which is contributing.

items.statement: IKEA supplies to begin in Q2 FY27; IKEA deemed export business expected to be 5-6% of revenue at full scale
items.quote: In this quarter, Q2 is when, IKEA business is starting.

items.statement: Chimney category revamped with BLDC motors; expects substantial growth from internal manufacturing and own retail
items.quote: What we have done is actually revamped the entire range from normal AC motors to BLDC motors, all but one. So that makes us extremely, current and in fact ahead of many of our competitors. And given that we've got our own retail also to drive this, we are very confident that the Chimney business is going to grow quite

items.statement: Committed to reaching 300 restaurants by FY27 with disciplined, calibrated pace
items.quote: We are committed to reaching 300 restaurants by FY27, and we'll build our portfolio from there.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR140 crores: INR120 crores for new outlets, INR20 crores for maintenance and ancillary
items.quote: We guided previously capex for full year would be around INR140 crores of which INR120 crores to the new outlet openings and INR20 crores towards the maintenance capex and our ancillary capex.

items.statement: 15 restaurants under construction to operationalize through Q2 and Q3 FY27
items.quote: As of today, we have 15 restaurants that are under construction, and these will operationalize through Q2 and Q3 of this financial year.

items.statement: Pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin improved to 8.1% in Q1 FY27, up 350 bps YoY and 260 bps QoQ
items.quote: Pre-Ind AS adjusted operating EBITDA margin for Q1 came in at 8.1%, which was around 350 basis points higher than Q1 of last year.

items.statement: Mature restaurant operating margin reached 16.2% in Q1 FY27, up 290 bps YoY
items.quote: Q1 FY27 matured portfolio Pre-Ind AS restaurant operating margin came in at 16.2%. This was again around 290 basis points higher than Q1 of last year.

items.statement: No price increase taken in Q1 FY27; growth entirely volume-led with average per cover spend reflecting mix changes
items.quote: Our growth continues to be entirely volume led. We have not taken any price increase during Q1, and our average per coverage spend continues to reflect changes in business segment mix.

items.statement: Consolidated same-store sales growth 28.7% in Q1 FY27; dine-in transaction volumes up 63.5% YoY
items.quote: Consolidated same-store sales growth for the quarter was 28.7%. Consolidated revenue grew 43.4% year-on-year to INR426 crores. Dine-in transaction volumes increased by 63.5%.

items.statement: Barbeque Nation India TAM revised to 600 restaurants from earlier 400-450; Big Buffet format enabling Tier 3/4 expansion
items.quote: Overall, if I look at the dynamics that we have with respect to the metro markets, the Tier 1 markets and the Tier 2, Tier 3 markets, I think at the current scale, the brand, which is Barbeque Nation India can take it up to around 600-odd restaurants.

items.statement: Net debt increased marginally to INR106 crores from INR102 crores due to capex investment
items.quote: Our net debt position has moved marginally up from INR102 crores at the end of FY26 to INR106 crores at the end of Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Same-store sales growth expected to moderate in FY27 due to stronger comparatives, not demand change
items.quote: We are conscious that the same-store sales growth will moderate as we move through FY27. This again, is more mathematics than our comment on demand.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin in 66-67% range; India gross margin improved 130 bps sequentially, International softer
items.quote: I think the current levels of around 66% -67% range is a good operating band and we would expect to move directionally from here over time.

items.statement: Monthly active users on digital platform grew ~60% YoY to 1.4 million; captive channels contribute 65% of dine-in transactions
items.quote: Our monthly active users on our digital platform have grown to approximately 1.4 million, which is up by almost 60% year-on-year. Our captive digital ecosystem contributes to 65% of overall Barbeque India dine-in transactions.

items.statement: Targets export contribution of 14%-15% of consolidated revenue by FY28
items.quote: We continue to focus on scaling our export business and remain committed to achieving export contribution of 14%-15% of consolidated revenue by FY28.

items.statement: New SJS Decoplast facility in Pune adds Rs 200-250 crore revenue capacity; commercial operations commenced August 2026
items.quote: This new capacity will add close to about 200 crs to 250 crs of additional revenue.

items.statement: Cover glass and display plant equipment on order; supplies expected from Q2 FY28
items.quote: Equipment is on order. It will be shipped and installed. And sales out of this new plant will come in Q2 of next year. This is what is for FY28.

items.statement: Q1FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 239 bps YoY to 30%; adjusted PAT margin 19.3% excluding one-time gain
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 799.6 mn, reflecting a year-on-year increase of 36.2%, with EBITDA margin expanding by 239 bps to 30%.

items.statement: Input cost impact ~0.5-0.6% on profitability; pass-through to customers typically with 1-2 quarter lag
items.quote: That would be somewhere between 0.5% to 0.6%.

items.statement: Automotive business grew 32.4% YoY vs industry 21.7% in Q1FY27; PV segment up 45.4%, 2W up 19.5%
items.quote: During the quarter, our automotive business registered a year-on-year growth of 32.4%, significantly ahead of the 21.7% growth recorded by the combined passenger vehicle and two-wheeler industry.

items.statement: New generation products contributed ~24% of consolidated revenue in Q1FY27
items.quote: New generation products contributed approximately 24% of consolidated revenue during Q1FY27.

items.statement: Non-compete with Walter Pack Spain expires January 2027; currently restricts competing for BMW/Mercedes globally
items.quote: We have an agreement with Walter Pack Spain on non-compete till January of 2027. At that point in time, we will take a call what we need to do.

items.statement: Board approved wholly-owned subsidiary for cover glass and display business; R&D centre received DSIR recognition
items.quote: The Board has approved setting up a wholly-owned subsidiary for the cover glass and display business. Further reinforcing our commitment to innovation, our in-house R&D Centre received recognition from the Department of Science and Industrial Research, DSIR, the Government of India.

items.statement: Aims to double SJS Decoplast sales in next 3-4 years; display market opportunity Rs 5,000-7,000 crore by 2030, targeting 10% share
items.quote: Our estimate is it could grow be as large as maybe Rs. 5,000 crs. So, that is, and what I said earlier, 5,000 crs to maybe 7,000 crs. And what I said earlier is our aspiration is to be at least 10% of the market by 2030.

items.statement: Exclusivity with BOE for four-wheeler displays; Pricol partnership limited to two-wheelers
items.quote: They are only for two-wheelers. We have exclusivity for four-wheelers.

items.statement: Priority remains fresh business growth over margin expansion; P1 target is fresh business growth.
items.quote: From a 3-year targeting perspective, internally, when we have set targets for our business, like, of course, there are detailed targets, but the P1 target is fresh business growth.

items.statement: Hired 5,000 people gross in Q1 FY27 despite it being seasonally weak quarter, indicating investment in growth.
items.quote: We hired, at a gross level, 5,000 people in Q1. That explains to you how much we are trying to reduce cost. Because most of those 5,000 will not be productive in Q1, for sure.

items.statement: Paisabazaar contribution margin at 41%, operating break-even achieved in Q1.
items.quote: Paisabazaar business has just broken even on the operating basis. On the contribution side, it's 41%.

items.statement: Targeting mid-double-digit revenue growth for FY27, split between ASP and volume growth
items.quote: we are looking at a mid-double-digit growth as an overall annualized impact of a business. Closely split between ASP and volume.

items.statement: Expecting high single-digit volume growth and 6-7% ASP growth from Q2 onwards for FY27
items.quote: we will be close to double-digit. We cannot promise a double-digit volume growth, but it will be high single digits for sure, right? It will be a combination of both ASP and volume growth that will lead us to mid-double-digit overall growth

items.statement: Confident of delivering full-year EBITDA margin of 17-19% for FY27
items.quote: Absolutely, Umang. Yes, we are 100% confident of delivering that. There is no reason not to deliver the margin.

items.statement: Implemented 8% MRP increase across key categories effective April 1, 2025, resulting in ~5% underlying ASP increase in core Stuck-On category
items.quote: During the quarter, we implemented MRP increases of approximately 8% across key product categories, resulting in an underlying ASP increase of around 5% in our core Stuck-On category.

items.statement: RM inflation fully absorbed by 8% price hike; no further hikes planned, benefit expected to flow back to P&L as market stabilizes
items.quote: RM inflation has been fully absorbed. And in fact as the volatility subsides we believe that and we will not be obviously taking the MRP increases correction again.

items.statement: Broad-based growth across channels, categories, geographies; strong momentum in women, kids, sneakers, school shoes
items.quote: Growth was broad-based across channels, categories and geographies, with particularly encouraging momentum in our women and kids' portfolio.

items.statement: School shoes revenue grew ~50% YoY, moved from DIP to Stuck-On (margin-accretive), contributed ~40% of volume growth in Q1
items.quote: We have moved this entire business from DIP to Stuck-On, which has a much better ASP and is a margin-accretive category versus DIP.

items.statement: Sneaker portfolio targeting ~30% growth in FY27; contributed 12-13% of volumes in Q1
items.quote: We are looking at a close to 30% growth on this category. And we are investing and our product launches as well as the category growth are in sync with that.

items.statement: Record orders received at largest-ever distributor meet, giving strong visibility for festive season
items.quote: strengthened our partner ecosystem through one of our largest ever distributor meets, where we have received record orders giving us a very good visibility of the upcoming festive season.

items.statement: Temporary ASP dilution of ~4.5% in Q1 from Walmart accounting change (2.5%) and school shoes mix shift (2%); both normalize from Q2
items.quote: combined just these two factors have had about a 4.5% to 5% impact on our growth which are temporary factors effective only to this quarter.

items.statement: Elan by Campus launched in neo-casual segment (Rs 1,899-2,599); selling in 100-110 own stores + online; initial response extremely positive
items.quote: Elan is almost a two-month-old launch now, and it is doing extremely well. It is selling currently in about 100 or 110 of our own stores, as well as actively selling on Amazon, Myntra, and our own brand.com.

items.statement: Franchise model fully transitioned to SOR (158 stores); franchisee ROI 18-30%; company controls inventory & discounting
items.quote: we have completely converted into a SOR model. So, about another 2%, 2.5% of revenue growth has been tapered off there.

items.statement: Management guides 18-20% revenue growth for FY27, with festive Q3 expected to be strong and West Bengal stores adding revenue by year-end.
items.quote: we can look at a good 18% to 20% kind of revenue growth. That should be very easily achievable.

items.statement: CFO guides full-year FY27 gross margin at 15-15.5%, noting Q1's 17.2% was inflated by cooling product mix and temporary price escalation benefits in IT products.
items.quote: It will be about 15% to 15.5%.

items.statement: CFO guides post-Ind AS EBITDA margin for FY27 at 7.5-8%, calling 9% too optimistic given current trends.
items.quote: Around 8% that's a -- I mean 7.5% to 8% is easily achievable, looking at the current trend.

items.statement: West Bengal entry planned with 5 stores operational by Diwali FY27 and 10-12 stores by end of Q4 FY27; targeting 30 stores in Kolkata over next 24 months.
items.quote: 5 stores will be operational by Diwali. And by 31st of March, by end of Q4 FY27, we should be operational by 10 to 12 stores.

items.statement: Strong demand across categories; AC volumes up significantly (26-27k units vs 20k last year), same-store sales growth 34.2%, South cluster revenue grew 40%, North cluster grew 29%.
items.quote: Our SSSG remains exceptionally strong at 34.2%, reflecting healthy underlying consumer demand and effective execution across our network.

items.statement: Interest cost for FY27 expected to be ~INR 10 crores lower than FY26's INR 150 crores due to reduced borrowings.
items.quote: it will be in the same range like last year. I mean about INR10 crores will be less.

items.statement: Bengal cluster expected to have faster payback than North despite being 1/3 the size of NCR; organized retail headroom seen similar to early North entry.
items.quote: I feel that the turnaround or the payback period would be sooner here compared to what we're seeing in the North for us.

items.statement: Successfully negotiated price revisions with OEMs; benefits to fully reflect from Q2 FY27 onwards
items.quote: We have now successfully negotiated price revisions with OEMs and benefits from these revisions are expected to fully reflect in our P&L from Quarter 2 onwards.

items.statement: Commissioned 4,000-ton forging press line and 7,200 MT machining capacity in Q1 FY27; total forging capacity 152,000 MT, machining 75,200 MT
items.quote: We also added capacity during the quarter by commissioning another 4,000-ton forging press line, adding 4,000 tons of forging capacity. Besides this, 7,200 metric tons of additional machining capacity has been added during the quarter.

items.statement: 18,000-ton vertical upsetter line under commissioning; trials from Q3 FY27, operational from Q4 FY27
items.quote: Yes, we probably start adding from Q4 of this financial year. It is already under commissioning right now, and our trials will start from Q3 onwards.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 275 bps YoY to 31.3%, marking 4th consecutive quarter above 30%; confident of sustaining 30%+ margins going forward
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 275 basis points year-on-year to 31.3%. This marks the 4th consecutive quarter in which we have delivered an EBITDA margin in excess of 30%.

items.statement: Machining contribution increased to 90% in Q1 FY27 from 88% in Q1 FY26; industrial and passenger vehicle mix rising
items.quote: Machining contribution increased to 90% in Q1 FY27 compared with 88% in Q1 FY 26. Furthermore, one of the key strategic developments for our business has been continued diversification of our revenue mix, as reflected in the increasing contribution from industrial and passenger vehicles.

items.statement: Export freight costs rose from $2,000 to $6,000 per container; ~75% pass-through, expecting 15-20% incremental cost hit
items.quote: You're right, the cost of, you know, container has gone up from roughly from USD2,000 to almost USD6,000, and a large part of it, the contract that we have, it's kind of a pass-through, or it is around 75% pass-through.

items.statement: Target industrial revenue to double in 3-4 years; passenger vehicle to reach 12-15% of revenue; combined industrial + PV to contribute 45-50% of revenue
items.quote: We can safely say that, you know, industrial skills will grow from these levels, will double from these levels in next three years to four years. Also, the PV, we should be looking at 12% to 15% of our revenues. Both the sectors put together should be contributing around 45%, 50% to our revenues.

items.statement: Growth capex of Rs.350-400 crores annually expected to be funded primarily from internal accruals; may use bridge loans for LCs
items.quote: As of now, it looks like that we should be able to fund this growth on our own. Cash flows look very strong and the accruals will be even stronger going forward. So yes, we are also -- maybe there is some bridge loan for a year or so for opening up some letter of credit, but most of this will be funded from our own acc

items.statement: Open to inorganic acquisitions/JVs in energy and aerospace for technology and approvals; cautious on valuations in farm/CV segments
items.quote: We are quite like open for this and searching for it on especially on the energy and aerospace side where we are new in entering, and also the technology and approval process takes a lot of time. So we are open for that and are seeing an opportunity in that sector.

items.statement: Expect similar growth trend in Q2 FY27 but price increase speed to halve, potentially reducing growth delta
items.quote: Q2 also similar trend will be there. The only correction will happen on the speed of the price increase. Price increase speed should be half. So, that much detrimental growth could happen.

items.statement: Targeting over US$100 million revenue from semiconductor JV within next three years
items.quote: we are targeting in next three years maximum, we are targeting a revenue of more than US$100 million under the JV.

items.statement: Plan to hire 50+ local engineers over next two years for semiconductor JV with Japanese design expert training
items.quote: It also includes direct skill transfer from Japanese design expert who will train our engineers backing our 50 plus local engineering hires over next two years.

items.statement: Good pipeline of AI data center projects for next three quarters, currently participating in smaller component supplies
items.quote: there is a good pipeline of these projects, which will continue to be there for next three quarters at least.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 3.38%, PAT margin 2.05%; gross margin impacted by higher PES share and accounting change
items.quote: EBITDA grew 55% to INR 173 crores and EBITDA margins at 3.38%. Profit after tax surged 69% to INR 105 crores delivering a PAT margin of 2.05%.

items.statement: 30-35% of Q1 FY27 60% growth from price increases, 5-10% from new products/brands, 20-25% from volume growth
items.quote: broadly speaking, 30%-35% has come from the price increase. 5% to 10% has come because of addition of new products and new brands. And the balance 20%-25% has come by increasing the quantity.

items.statement: Commercial segment strong with preponed buying; consumer segment facing affordability pressure due to 2x laptop price increase
items.quote: consumer there is still slowdown because of the affordability. The laptop prices, for example, has already become 2x as compared to the last year. But for commercial applications, they don't have an option. So, they continue to buy.

items.statement: Semiconductor revenue grew 70% YoY in Q1; VDA Infosolutions acquisition adds ~5% to revenue portfolio from integrated services
items.quote: our semiconductor revenue has already crossed 70% of the entire year's revenue that we did last year. So, there is significant momentum on that side as well.

items.statement: Supply constraints on entry-level laptops (~50% shortage); tracking component shortages weekly as orange alert
items.quote: entry level laptops, there is almost 50% shortage. But if I go for medium and premium notebooks, if we are able to accept the price, then so far availability is not a concern.

items.statement: Acquired 67% stake in VDA Infosolutions (FY26 revenue Rs 850 crores) for forward integration into enterprise services
items.quote: strategic acquisition of 67% stake in the first year. Our core objective is to improve our capabilities in terms of design, pre-sales, post-sales, and managed services.

items.statement: Formed JV with Restar Corporation (74:26) for advanced image sensing solutions in industrial/automotive applications
items.quote: announcing a joint venture with Restar Corporation. It is a leading Japanese semiconductor and technology company, structured a 74% Rashi and 26% Restar focused on advanced image sensing solutions for industrial and automotive applications.

items.statement: Working capital days improved to 56 days despite 62% revenue growth; inventory days 55, debtor days 41, creditor days 40
items.quote: Inventory days tightened to 55 days, debtors' days stood at 41, creditors' days stood at 40, and overall working capital days improved year-on-year to 56 days.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of Rs 1,500 crores plus for FY27 with EBITDA margin above 19%
items.quote: As we have told earlier, you know, we remain fully committed, fully committed for our top line of Rs. 1.500 crores plus and EBIDTA margin of more than 19%. 100% without any doubt in that.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 2,428 crores as of 30 June 2026 providing strong revenue visibility
items.quote: with a strong order book of Rs. 2,428 crores as of 30 June 2026, which gives us strong revenue visibility and a healthy project pipeline across key segments.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance of more than Rs 2,000 crores for FY27, with Rs 700 crores already booked in Q1
items.quote: Your first question, definitely yes, it may increase also. But your first question is absolutely inline, we are likely to get more than 2000 crores worth of inflow in this particular year.

items.statement: Anjar facility utilization at 60-65% in FY27, targeting 100% by end of FY28; no expansion planned for Thailand facility
items.quote: Sir, Whatever we have planned in this particular year, we shall be doing it. But, you know, in that also, we should be reaching at around maybe around 60% to 65% of our available capacities. And our plan is that by the end of next year, we should be utilizing almost 100% of the available capacity at Anjar.

items.statement: Healthy demand across power, oil & gas, process industries domestically and overseas; multi-year opportunity from India's capex cycle and global energy/infrastructure pickup
items.quote: Overall demand, visibility across our core end markets, particularly power, oil and gas, and process industries in India and overseas remains healthy and a strong order pipeline gives us confidence in delivering profitable growth.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 16.9% vs 16% YoY; improvement driven by capacity utilization, operating leverage, seamless pipe contribution; confident of >19% full year
items.quote: Operating EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 49.7 crores with a margin of 16.9% compared with 16% in Q1FY26 and it is up by 38.7% year-on-year.

items.statement: Rs 25 crore dispatches deferred to Q2 due to Middle East situation affecting oil & gas export customers; material ready at company end
items.quote: Around Rs. 25 crores of dispatches scheduled for Q1 got pushed into Q2 primarily on the oil and gas side, where a few of our export customers deferred take-offs given the situation in the Middle East.

items.statement: Thailand facility revenue target Rs 170-200 crores (vs Rs 130 crore FY26); facility fully booked for 3 years; no expansion planned
items.quote: Sir, as we have been telling, last year we did around Rs. 130 crores, and the intention is that we have to keep that unit busy and target to achieve anything between Rs. 170 crores to Rs. 200 crores.

items.statement: Anjar facility peak revenue potential Rs 1,500 crores by FY28-29
items.quote: So, our plan is around Rs. 1,500 crores from Anjar facility only and by '28-29, we should be able to do it.

items.statement: BHEL order pipeline: Rs 200 crore last quarter, more tenders in preparation expected this quarter; L&T orders awarded, more discussing; JSW, Hindustan Energy discussions ongoing
items.quote: Last quarter also we got around Rs. 200 crores worth of order and few more tenders are in the preparation stage. We expect that those tenders should be in the market maybe in this quarter itself and they may get finalized in the next quarter.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 17-19%
items.quote: We have given the guidance of EBITDA margin of 17% to 19% year-on-year and which we maintaining for current year and for even for the next year.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 20-25%
items.quote: 20% to 25% guidance we always maintain, and we try to achieve that. So we are as of now quite sure we will be achieving or crossing that.

items.statement: New Wada land acquisition: 10.15 acres, ~INR40-45 cr capex planned for next FY
items.quote: A broadly INR40 crores something, INR40 crores to INR45 crores something will be there as a capex plan, which we will plan in the next year once we have a complete hold or ownership of this particular land parcel.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 16.51%, expected to improve with Chennai utilization and revenue scale
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at around INR12 crores, up 28% year-on-year, with EBITDA margins at 16.51%.

items.statement: Pricing stable; 10-20% cost advantage vs European peers; raw material pass-through with lag
items.quote: I think pricings are stable, and we are still able to offer between 10% to 20% saving to our customer, maintaining our margins. And for the price increases which are happening on account of raw material particularly and some other heads, we are also getting the pass-through with some lag effects from the customer.

items.statement: Strong order booking growth ~40% YoY; first bulk electrolyzer order secured
items.quote: We delivered robust order booking growth of approximately 40% year-on-year, providing greater visibility for the quarters ahead. We also secured our first bulk commercial order from one of the India's leading electrolyzer manufacturer.

items.statement: New products contribute 30-35% of order book; offshore wind fasteners targeting 10% of fastener sales by FY27 end
items.quote: I think totally newly launched products contribute about 30% to 35% of the order book, which includes bolts which we have started manufacturing in Chennai. This also includes smart fasteners again which we entered into the global market in offshore wind sector.

items.statement: Chennai Phase 2 mezzanine (10k sq ft) completing Q2; Phase 1 utilization 70-80% in Q1, targeting 80-90% in Q2
items.quote: Q1 Phase 1 capacity utilization is almost 70%-80%, and we are seeing in Q2, we should be touching 80%-90% of Phase 1. By the time we are working on the Phase 2 capacity, which should be there partly in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Chennai facility EBITDA parity with Wada expected by Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28 at 70-80% utilization
items.quote: Like, once we complete the Phase 2 and start utilizing approximately 70% to 80%, which should happen in Q4, so maybe in Q4 or next year Q1.

items.statement: Forward forex cover reduced from 70% to 40% due to euro volatility; rupee weakening bias
items.quote: Now we have reduced it to 40% of the total collection, primary because of the huge volatility in the foreign currency, especially as far as euro is concerned.

items.statement: KPMG working capital study initiated July; report expected Q2; action plan and targets by Q3
items.quote: They started this study in July, and we are expecting report by August end or this quarter, and based on that report, we will be planning the actions and targets in quarter 3.

items.statement: Wind turbine fasteners ~25-26% of Q1 sales; offshore wind fastener ramp-up to 10% of fastener sales by FY27 end
items.quote: I think in totality, wind turbine fastener contribution in total sales of quarter one will be approximately 25%-26% approximately.

items.statement: Maintains True North target of INR 3,000 cr EBITDA by FY30 with minimal dilution and return to pre-TruBridge net debt
items.quote: we are continuing to maintain our True North objective of getting to at least INR3,000 crores in EBITDA by fiscal year '30

items.statement: Aspires to grow legacy IKS revenue >12% constant currency; TruBridge growth outlook TBD after 2-3 quarters
items.quote: we will aspire to continue to grow that $388 million book of business at 12% which is the legacy IKS business

items.statement: Targets blended EBITDA margin back to early-to-mid 30s% over next couple years from pro forma ~26-27% post-TruBridge
items.quote: getting back to our early-to-mid 30% EBITDA margins after our pro forma drop post-consolidation of TruBridge initially to, you know, the 26%-27% range

items.statement: Integration costs ~INR 20 cr in Q1 FY27; expect similar range in Q2 FY27
items.quote: We do expect a little bit of integration expenses going into the next quarter as well. It's likely to remain in a similar range

items.statement: Won significant land-and-expand deals: large California health system (Epic migration), national musculoskeletal leader (RCM), expanded Advocate Health (top-5 US system) and StrideCare (vascular)
items.quote: Happy to announce that we've had a couple of very significant wins in that land-and-expansion strategy over the last couple of quarters

items.statement: Headcount grew 4.2% YoY (12,300 to 12,889) vs 12% CC revenue growth demonstrating non-linearity; 1,900 clinical, 600 tech, 60 sales
items.quote: our headcount has gone in June '25, we were at 12,300 people; in June '26, we are at 12,889 people, which is basically a growth of 4.2% in people versus 12% constant currency growth in revenue

items.statement: Maintains mid-teens revenue growth target for FY27 despite Q1 impact from West Asia crisis; expects to make up lost revenue in H2
items.quote: We have tried to maintain a like-to-like growth of mid-teens in that mid-teens range. We will be able to do that and that's why if you look at it our top line increased by 5% but as I mentioned earlier we saw a INR14 crores impact in terms of cancellations of business in our books.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of INR500 crores; INR53 crores spent in Q1, balance ~INR350 crores to be spent over next three quarters
items.quote: In the first quarter, we have spent around INR45 crores towards CWIP and renovation of INR3.5 crores and for the new restaurant Project Grain around INR4 crores. So put together is around INR53 crores and the balance amount will be spent over next three quarters.

items.statement: Total development pipeline capex of INR3,600 crores for ~1,700 keys by FY30; INR400 crores deployed by FY26, funding mix 60% debt / 40% internal accruals
items.quote: Our development pipeline entails a total Capex of approximately INR3,600 crores to build out ~1,700 upcoming keys by FY30 taking our portfolio from 1,600 keys to 3,300 keys. Of this, around INR400 crores had already been deployed by FY26.

items.statement: Luxury/upper-upscale mix to rise from 14% to 31% by FY29 and 38% by FY31 via Grand Hyatt, InterContinental, JW Marriott, Ritz-Carlton additions
items.quote: This will lift our luxury and upper upscale mix from 14% today to 31% by FY29 and 38% by FY31, positioning BHVL in the segment with the strongest pricing power and demand-supply mismatch.

items.statement: Portfolio ADR target above INR7,500 to offset GST impact; Q1 FY27 ADR at INR7,241 (+7% YoY); Kochi Courtyard expects minimum 10% ADR growth this year
items.quote: We had also mentioned we are doing our best to push the entire portfolio and each hotel above that INR7,500 so that that GST impact can also be negated.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 34.8% (+9% YoY EBITDA); GST 2.0 impact of 1.6% on margin; finance cost fell >50% to INR8.7 crores driving 140% PAT growth
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA increased by 9% year-on-year to INR46 crores with EBITDA margin at 34.8%. GST 2.0 had an impact of 1.6% on the EBITDA margin during the quarter.

items.statement: Courtyard by Marriott Chennai WTC (45 keys) to launch Q3 FY27; expects starting ADR INR9,000 and stabilized occupancy ~80%
items.quote: We do expect a minimum of a INR9,000 as a starting ADR and then we expect that to grow in the coming months. This is one hotel that we expect to stabilize quickly and should be continuously occupied through the week so we see stabilized occupancies at about 80%.

items.statement: Grand Hyatt launch delayed from FY28 due to approvals; JW Marriott Chennai and Trivandrum hotel targeting commissioning by 2030
items.quote: We had mentioned that there would be a slight delay in the Grand Hyatt which we had originally slated for FY28 but there is going to be a slight delay in the Grand Hyatt because we're waiting a few approvals there.

items.statement: Under discussion for hotel acquisition using IPO proceeds; hopes to conclude transaction in FY27 subject to due diligence
items.quote: Yes, we're under discussion. We're hoping to conclude a transaction in FY27. But it is subject to due diligence.

items.statement: Bangalore hotels: focus on maintaining occupancy while driving ADR growth over next three quarters; portfolio occupancy stable at 76% with 5 of 9 hotels above 80%
items.quote: Our focus over here is to maintain our occupancy now and focus on positioning only. We do see the market becoming stronger as months go by and we will have an increase in ADR over the coming three quarters.

items.statement: Net cash position INR108 crores as of June 30, 2026 after INR468.1 crores debt repayment from IPO proceeds; effectively no institutional debt
items.quote: As of 30th June 2026, we had a net cash position of INR108 crores reflecting the continued strengthening of our balance sheet. On debt and deleveraging post-IPO, we deployed INR468.1 crores of the proceeds towards debt repayment which has left us with effectively no institutional debt on our book.

items.statement: FY27 steel volume target of 1.2 million tonnes reaffirmed with 20% YoY growth expected
items.quote: We remain on course for our 1.2-million-ton steel volume target for FY27.

items.statement: FY27 non-steel revenue growth target of 25% YoY reaffirmed
items.quote: Going forward, we are confident of meeting our projections given in the last quarter, 20% growth in steel volumes and 25% in non-steel.

items.statement: Medium-term target of 4% EBITDA margin with 20% steel and 25% non-steel volume growth
items.quote: Yes, I think our target would be in the medium term to go to around 4% EBITDA and maintain our 20% volume growth for steel and 25% for non-steel.

items.statement: Added 3 fulfillment centers in Q1 FY27; plan to add 5 more in coming quarters
items.quote: We have added three fulfillment centers in Q1 and we have plans to add around five more in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 3.26%; normalized for Rs 10 cr inventory loss would be ~3.8%; steady-state target 3.5%+
items.quote: I think that resulted in erosion of around 10 odd crores, which I think if I factored that in, we would have obviously been at a much another 0.5% bps would have probably gone up in the EBITDA, EBITDA, which means we would have been around 3.8 or so.

items.statement: Steady-state EBITDA margin target of 3.5%+ for remainder of FY27
items.quote: Ideally, yes. And steady state, we are looking at 3.5% kind of EBITDA margin as we go forward.

items.statement: Steel demand recovery visible from June-July; industry activity points to recovery from Q2 FY27
items.quote: Industry activity in the past month points to a recovery in steel demand from Q2 and with prices now stabilizing, the operating backdrop for the remainder of FY27 looks distinctly better.

items.statement: Non-steel growth driven by 32% YoY growth in fittings & sanitaryware; tiles stabilizing; UPVC roofing gaining traction
items.quote: Our performance for the quarter was driven by a 32% growth in fittings and sanitary ware, our largest product category.

items.statement: Inventory losses of Rs 10 cr in Q1 due to steel price correction in May-June; Q4 FY26 had Rs 15 cr inventory gain
items.quote: I think that resulted in erosion of around 10 odd crores, which I think if I factored that in, we would have obviously been at a much another 0.5% bps would have probably gone up in the EBITDA.

items.statement: Target to reach 2 million tonnes steel volume in ~4 years with geographic expansion and market share gains
items.quote: And our target would be around 4 years to achieve the 2 MT target.

items.statement: Focus on value-added steel products (cut-to-length) and expanding private label products in retail
items.quote: One is we are working on infrastructure addition where we can focus on value-added products in steel. So, this would be more cut to length and more products which customers would help us increase our customer base with OEMs.

items.statement: Acquisitions on the table if suitable opportunities found
items.quote: Definitely on the table. If we find any suitable acquisitions, definitely it will be there.

items.statement: Target to sustain EBITDA margins between 37% and 38% for pharma, food and nutrition business
items.quote: supported by an increasing contribution from differentiated and value-added products. This performance was delivered despite continued geopolitical uncertainty and volatile raw material markets. As these conditions gradually normalize, we believe our international business remains well-positioned to continue growing wh

items.statement: Phosphate portfolio demand exceeds current manufacturing capacity, providing strong visibility for balance of FY27
items.quote: customer demand for our phosphate portfolio continues to exceed our current manufacturing capacity, providing us with excellent visibility for the balance of the financial year and reinforcing our confidence in the sustainability of this growth.

items.statement: Core specialty ingredients business (ex-NSS) maintained mid-30s EBITDA margin despite LPG supply disruption
items.quote: the specialty number that you see is inclusive of NSS. The business without NSS still was in the mid-30s in terms of margin profile. NSS has had a tough, challenging quarter, and that has kind of dragged down the profitability to the 26% level.

items.statement: Target steady-state asset turns of 2.7x-3x for battery and greenfield facilities at scale
items.quote: I would say for battery at scale and greenfield at scale, I would say closer to between 2.7 x and closer to 3x is where we would be the asset turns would sit.

items.statement: Specialty ingredients core business demand healthy; LPG supply shortage caused temporary production constraints in April-May, now normalized
items.quote: It is important to highlight that this was purely a supply-side constraint rather than a demand issue. Customer demand remained healthy throughout the quarter, our order pipeline continues to strengthen, and production has now normalized. As a result, we expect this business to return to its historical growth trajector

items.statement: Optimum capacity utilization target of 70-75% depending on product mix
items.quote: Optimum utilization is between 70% and 75% depending on the product mix that we are running.

items.statement: Targeting ~70% capacity utilization in FY27 and EBITDA margin ~17% by FY28
items.quote: We are targeting to hit a margin of about 17%. By FY28.

items.statement: Core garment EBITDA margin turned positive at 3.4% in Q1 FY27 vs negative last year; targeting pre-tariff levels
items.quote: Our core EBITDA margin i.e. the garment business alone excluding our other income, turned positive at about 3.4% against a marginally negative number in the same quarter last year

items.statement: Expect demand in India to strengthen substantially to absorb planned capacity expansion to 38 lakh pieces
items.quote: We see demand going up in India substantially to be able to use up these capacities that we plan.

items.statement: Offered price discounts to US customers to share tariff burden and retain volumes; margins took a hit
items.quote: We had to partner with our U.S. customers on prices, on discounts. This is in order to hedge the increase in cost so that they don't have to pass too much of a cost on to the end consumer as well.

items.statement: Expanding into women's bottoms, outerwear and athleisure to supplement premium men's bottomwear; not moving away from core
items.quote: We aren't looking to move away. We are intending to supplement our capabilities. Women's wear is an obvious easy entry because a women's wear bottom and a men's wear bottom aren't too different in terms of product.

items.statement: MOU with Sri Lankan contract manufacturer as contingency for adverse US tariffs; evaluating own plants in Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Nepal for geographic diversification
items.quote: We have got an MOU with a Sri Lankan contract manufacturer that helps you change the country of origin. So, if something were to happen on goods made in India, we can offer our customers goods made in Sri Lanka as well.

items.statement: Target to collect minimum Rs. 380 crores from legacy government receivables in remaining nine months of FY27
items.quote: remainder of nine months minimum, and this I am talking minimum, target is Rs. 380 crores will come from that in total

items.statement: Biochar plant recently started; revenue impact expected from next fiscal year
items.quote: You will start seeing because project has recently started any impact on numbers from the next fiscal

items.statement: Hi-Tech margin fell to 14.4% from 16.6% YoY due to unabsorbed fixed costs; plastic improved to 11% from 10%; Agro-Processing down 3%
items.quote: Hi-Tech division delivered about a 14.4% margin versus similar period at 16.6, so approximately 2% reduction, and plastic, in fact, improved by about a percent or so from 10 to 11, and Agro-Processing also came down by 3%

items.statement: July revenue already positive vs April-June; August-September look good; institutional large-diameter pipe negotiations indicate surplus demand
items.quote: We have registered already positive revenue growth in July as against April to June, significant revenue growth here. And August and September also seem to be good

items.statement: One large Pune water supply project with triple-digit billing remaining; other projects only Rs. 40-50 crores left
items.quote: In the other projects apart from the one project in Pune, I think total billing left is about approximately closer to Rs. 40-50 crores only

items.statement: Expect to cover Q1 EBITDA margin reduction in second half; full-year profitability better than last year
items.quote: we believe we should be able to catch up in the second half of the current fiscal year to cover what is lost

items.statement: Targets 8-10% top-line growth for FY27 and FY28, assuming industry grows 6-7%
items.quote: you can assume from all the businesses put together, we are looking at between 8% to 10% growth, quarter-on-quarter. That is the number we are looking.

items.statement: Lighting solutions margin temporarily hit by legacy professional lighting contracts; expects return to double-digit EBIT in a quarter or two
items.quote: once we are off this legacy project, we will go back to double-digit margins in overall lighting.

items.statement: Cost inflation 6-12% across categories; managed via selective price hikes and savings; no major further price increases needed for rest of year at this stage
items.quote: it is as high as 13% in some categories, coolers were the highest in terms of cost, like, yes. So, it is anyway between 6% to about 11%-12%. And most of that, between pricing and savings, we have managed to sail through

items.statement: Consumer products returned to growth (1.7% YoY) after multiple declining quarters; non-summer categories and Morphy Richards grew double-digit; fans declined due to supply issues
items.quote: consumer products growing at 1.7% after a decline for multiple quarters

items.statement: BLDC fan contribution 30-35% industry-wide; company under-indexed but growing faster; premiumization driving margin improvement
items.quote: the estimates which we have on BLDC vary between 30% to 35%. We are slightly under-indexed versus the industry, but it is growing much faster and we will be in our rightful share as we progress.

items.statement: Wires business progress better than expected; will play significant role in lighting segment going forward
items.quote: in wires, our progress is better than what we were expecting. And that gives us confidence that it can play a significant role moving forward to our business.

items.statement: No major capex guidance given; focus on brand investment and distribution expansion (direct dealers in South/West, e-commerce, quick commerce)
items.quote: we are equally mindful about our counter share and the focus is on that also. The second piece was on e-commerce. E-commerce contributes to approximately 15%.

items.statement: Commodity price volatility remains a risk; legacy professional lighting contracts pressuring margins temporarily; fan supply chain issues (gas, PCB) largely resolved
items.quote: the external environment continues to remain volatile. And we will assess the impacts before taking any pricing decisions.

items.statement: Working capital hovering at 50-60 days; inventory slightly up due to seasonal stocking; Q1 operating cash flow negative due to Morphy Richards acquisition tax payments
items.quote: it is largely hovering around between 50-60 days. So, that's the larger trend. And we see some buildup to happen because of the seasonal business.

items.statement: FY27 DI+CIP volume guidance lowered to ~575,000 tons from earlier 650,000-700,000 tons due to slower JJM fund releases
items.quote: So, Sir, we had erstwhile indicated the volume of I think 650,000 tons to 700,000 tons. But due to the slower initial release of JJM, we are expecting to reach a quantity of around 575,000 tons.

items.statement: Export mix target 22-25% of total volumes for FY27, with 60-70% focused on Europe/UK and rest on Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia
items.quote: And we are expecting that at the end of the year, we will be exporting around between 22% to 25% of our total volumes.

items.statement: Current executable order book ~300,000 tons (~5 months), ~50% from JJM; Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, UP, Rajasthan most active
items.quote: So, we have a total order book of around 3 lakh tons, which works out to around five months. So, JJM, this order book, JJM would be around close to 50%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 9.5% in Q1 FY27; targeting 12-13% by Q3/Q4 FY27 on cost optimization and volume recovery
items.quote: Going forward, I think Q3 FY'27, Q4FY'27, we should be hitting EBITDA number of 12% to 13%.

items.statement: DI pipe net realization improved to ~Rs 55,000/ton in Q1 FY27 from ~Rs 50,500/ton in Q4 FY26; management sees rock-bottom pricing behind
items.quote: These are net realizations of around Rs. 50,500 per ton for Q4 FY'26and in Q1 FY'27 is around Rs. 55,000 per ton.

items.statement: Target DI pipe revenue share down from ~85% to ~55% in 4-5 years via valves (double revenue to Rs 800-1,000 cr), paints (Rs 800-1,000 cr in 5 yrs), ferroalloys, railway rubber
items.quote: From today, it's around 85% and in the next four to five years, you will go to around 55% or so.

items.statement: T.I.S. Italy: FY27 revenue target EUR 42-45 mn (vs EUR 38 mn avg last yr), EBITDA margin 14-15%, PAT ~8%; Q1 FY27 revenue EUR 10 mn, EBITDA margin 13%
items.quote: Sir, by the end of this financial year, we are expecting, as mentioned, it was going to be 20% above last year's average of around EUR 38 million. So, we should be, hopefully, we'll reach a number of EUR 42 million to 45 million in revenue.

items.statement: Long-term FY30-31 target: Revenue Rs 7,000-8,000 cr, EBITDA margin 13-13.5%
items.quote: I am very certain that we can look at a growth of revenue to around Rs. 7,000-8,000 crores with EBITDA level of 13%-13.5% by FY30 & FY31.

items.statement: Saudi anti-dumping duty impact minimal: Saudi sales only 2-3% of total, expected to drop to 1.5%, easily diverted to other GCC/Africa markets
items.quote: The total sales of Electrosteel Castings to Saudi Arabia was to a total of, it is about 2% to 3% of our sales. So, that is a quantity that can be diverted to other markets pretty easily.

items.statement: Term debt Rs 340 cr, scheduled to reduce to Rs 230 cr; net debt Rs 876 cr (Jun 2026) down ~Rs 1,100 cr in FY26; Rs 700 cr cash available for bolt-on acquisitions
items.quote: We have around Rs. 700 crores of capital on our books which we are ready to invest.

items.statement: Valves: India facility operational by end FY27; target 40-45% Asia contribution in 3-4 yrs; Q1 FY27 valve revenue grew 18% YoY
items.quote: We also expect our valves manufacturing facility in India to commence operations by the end of this financial year, supporting future growth and improving profitability.

items.statement: Railway rubber components: Board approval taken; registration 4-6 months; additional equipment under installation (3 months); leverages existing gasket plant in Andhra Pradesh
items.quote: So, possibly, it will take four to six months time for us to get it registered.

items.statement: Price increases taken in April and May partly covered war-led and regulatory inflation but not fully, impacting margins
items.quote: We were able to take up in April and May pricing, which partly covered the war-led inflation and the regulatory inflation, but not fully, like I said, thereby impacting margins.

items.statement: Invested INR 245 crores in Pune plant for four-door premium refrigerator (Luxuriem) production
items.quote: We are extremely proud that this entire thing is made in India, thought through by India, executed by India, and it's rolling off our Pune lines where we've invested INR 245 crores on this technology.

items.statement: War-driven crude oil and forex volatility, regulatory cost burden (energy norms, e-waste), and inability to fully pass costs to consumers due to competitive dynamics
items.quote: The companies have not been able to recover the impact of the combined war and regulatory impact through pricing because of industry competitive dynamics, and that obviously impacts the numbers of margins.

items.statement: Management declined to provide full-year revenue growth guidance due to unpredictable commodity costs, forex, and demand environment.
items.quote: The let's say the accuracy of anything that I say would be close to zero. So, all I can tell you is to all our shareholders, we are focusing really hard on making sure the hard-fought gains we have on market shares don't go away.

items.statement: EBITDA margin squeezed 377 bps YoY to 4.6% in Q1 FY27 due to unprecedented commodity inflation, currency depreciation >10%, and regulatory costs.
items.quote: The EBITDA came in at INR 120 crores at 4.6%, and we saw squeeze of margins, wherein EBITDA margin squeezed by 377 basis points.

items.statement: Multiple price increases taken in Q1 FY27 were insufficient to fully offset commodity, forex, and regulatory cost increases, resulting in net under-recovery.
items.quote: We took a couple of price increases in the quarter, but then the price increases were not sufficient enough to mitigate the 100% of all the cost increase, which was like of a very different magnitude which we saw in the quarter, and as a result of this, there was a net under-recovery.

items.statement: JAS quarter (Q2 FY27) expected to be financially tough due to seasonally weak refrigerator/AC volumes while commodity costs and forex remain high.
items.quote: I think it is going to be a tough quarter financially in JAS. My suspicion is it'll be tough for the entire industry, because everybody is more or less in the same boat.

items.statement: E-waste provision accruals ongoing for ~18 months; resolution with government/industry/recyclers needed to release margin pressure.
items.quote: E-waste is something that needs to be sorted out between the government and the industry and the recyclers, and I hope we have some kind of solution soon. It's been a very long time. It's been like what, 18 months since we've been accruing the higher amount.

items.statement: Energy efficiency regulatory changes for refrigerators/ACs occur every 3 years (last Jan 2026, next expected Jan 2029), costing crores; India standards already among world's highest.
items.quote: Technically speaking, if '26 January is the refrigerator one now, as per the calendar, the next one should be '29 January. So, other than that, we know we don't have, we don't expect anything else.

items.statement: No fixed capex budget for FY27; investments driven by project ROI not budget constraints. Base run-rate capex ~INR 100+ crores plus new product/automation projects.
items.quote: The base ongoing capex is about 100 plus, we keep investing based on specific initiatives, innovations, automations, etc.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization ~70-75%; no immediate large capacity capex needed for next 6-12 months. Front-load washer capacity sufficient with headroom (not yet on 3 shifts).
items.quote: Our capacity on an annual basis across all products is about 70%, 75% utilization. So, there is no immediate requirement to put a large capex, immediate, I mean, the short-term, let's say, next 6 months, 12 months, to a large capacity capex.

items.statement: Premium portfolio (front-load washers, air conditioners) performed well, supporting revenue growth via higher ASPs.
items.quote: In line with our strategy of premiumization, our premium portfolio, which is the front load washing machine and the air con business, has done pretty well, and which also aids, given that these are high-value products and higher ASP products, aids in the top-line growth.

items.statement: Elica subsidiary delivered 26% revenue growth and 22% PBT growth in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: The highlight on a consolidated basis is the our Elica business. That continues its robust performance and delivered a double-digit 26% revenue growth and a PBT growth of 22%.

items.statement: Industry refrigerator/washer volumes grew mid-single digits in Q1 FY27; Whirlpool gained double-digit basis point market share in both categories.
items.quote: Our industry, which is the refrigerators and washers, multi-brand outlets volume grew in mid-single digits, which also helped us. But that was not the only factor which drove our top-line. On top of the industry growth, our market share also grew, and we grew market share in double basis points across both the categori

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 5.1% in Q1 FY27, down ~300+ bps YoY, similar squeeze drivers as standalone.
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, we saw a similar margin squeeze of about 300 plus basis points.

items.statement: Took price hikes in April and May 2026; full reflection expected in Q2 FY27 (July-September)
items.quote: we have taken up prices in April and May, as I said before. I'm not going to say exactly what the numbers are, but we have taken up prices two consecutive months because we had to. And it was not fully reflected in April, May, June, but it will be fully reflected in July, August, September and beyond.

items.statement: Gross margin compression driven primarily by war-related commodity/forex impact (larger) and energy regulation charges on refrigerator/AC business (about half of war impact)
items.quote: in the order of magnitude, the war impact was much higher. So, and then half of it, if the war impact was x, probably half of it or a little less than that was the energy regulations impact, which impacted the overall gross margins

items.statement: Refrigerator and washing machine market grew only 4-5% in Q1 FY27; Whirlpool gained 30-35 bps market share
items.quote: the market itself hardly grew, so the mathematics, as you rightly pointed out, the market grew about 4%-5% across refrigerators and washers. And our market share, as I told you, grew about 30-35 basis points.

items.statement: Elica kitchen appliances delivering strong double-digit growth; pricing near fully covering cost increases; expect continued strong growth but may invest 200bps margin for growth
items.quote: We expect to see strong growth coming out of Elica, obviously always strong double-digit growth. We do expect that we will have to invest some of the margins into that. But even if we were to invest some of the margins, like say a couple of hundred basis points, we still think that it will be a significantly higher mar

items.statement: Commodity and forex outlook uncertain; unable to comment but hope resolution within FY27
items.quote: the impact of commodity pricing, excuse me, commodity and forex, this is anybody's guess, you know, your guess is as good as mine. We all pray and hope that this gets resolved soon for the good of the world, and frankly, also for the good of industry. And that is something that we are absolutely unable to make a commen

items.statement: Services agreement with Whirlpool Corporation continues until March 2029 at arm's length cost-plus margins; continuation beyond March 2029 at Whirlpool Corp's discretion
items.quote: There's an agreement as a part of the transaction, we've agreed with the Whirlpool Corporation that these services will continue until March '29. So, that's what is the agreement, which is also in the public domain. We've made disclosures because it is a related party transaction, and the margins are on arm's length ba

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guided at high single-digit with EBITDA margins around 25%
items.value: high single-digit revenue growth; EBITDA margin ~25%
items.quote: We would like to reiterate our earlier guidance of high single-digit revenue growth for the organization with EBITDA margins of around 25% during the year.

items.statement: U.S. business expected at USD 1.1-1.2 billion for FY27, returning to growth trajectory from FY28
items.quote: For the full year, we expect the U.S. business to be in the USD 1.1 billion to USD 1.2 billion range, aided by growth in base business, our injectable launches, and contribution from Pegfilgrastim offsetting the additional competition in products like Mirabegron and Tolvaptan during the year.

items.statement: Quarterly U.S. revenue expected at USD 250-280 million for next few quarters due to competition
items.quote: We expect revenues to be anywhere between USD 250 million to USD 280 million a quarter over the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: R&D spend at 7.4% of sales in Q1FY27, full-year expected around 8%
items.quote: For the full-year, R&D is expected to be around 8%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 30% in Q1FY27, full-year guided around 25% due to U.S. competition and cost inflation
items.quote: For the full year, as indicated by Vinita, we expect EBITDA margins to be around the 25% mark.

items.statement: Chronic share in India increased to 67% from 65% in FY26, target 70% in 5 years
items.quote: The Chronic segment accounts for around 67% of our portfolio, up from around 65% in FY26, and we have set ourselves a target to increase the share to 70% in the next five years.

items.statement: India innovative proprietary products target one-third of revenue in 10 years
items.quote: We have set ourselves a target of novel proprietary products contributing one third of our India revenues in the next 10-year timeframe.

items.statement: India core prescription business grew 15.1% YoY at 1.1x IPM, volume growth 6.1%
items.quote: During the quarter, the India business recorded sales of INR 2,380 crores, growing 13.9% YoY. I would like to highlight that the core prescription business grew 15.1% YoY as against IPM growth of 13.5%, translating to 1.1x IPM growth.

items.statement: Emerging Markets grew 52% YoY led by Brazil 117% growth in local currency
items.quote: Emerging Markets delivered an impressive 52% YoY growth, led by Brazil, South Africa, and Philippines. Brazil continued the strong momentum of the last four quarters, growing 117% YoY in local currency during Q1.

items.statement: Other Developed Markets grew 48% YoY, Europe 83% YoY, targeting 10-20% growth over next couple years
items.quote: We are looking at potentially double-digit growth, in some years., higher than others, but anywhere between 10% to 20% over the next couple of years.

items.statement: U.S. competition intensifying on Mirabegron and Tolvaptan with 4-player market expected for Tolvaptan
items.quote: In Q1, you don't have any additional competition on Tolvaptan. And from Q2 onwards, you will start seeing the impact of Apotex and Teva. We also expect in September, we could potentially have one more entrant. We expect to be a four-player market with Tolvaptan.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions causing cost inflation impacting margins from Q2 onwards
items.quote: the impact of price increases that we have seen in the recent past; post the cost increase that is because of the geopolitical tensions around.

items.statement: Pegfilgrastim launch in H2 FY27, multiple respiratory and injectable launches in FY27-28 including 10 exclusive FTFs, 5 biosimilars, 2-3 505(b)(2)s over 3 years
items.quote: In the next three years, we expect to launch 50 plus products in the U.S. with 10 exclusive first-to-files, five biosimilars, as well as two to three 505(b)(2)s.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 20-24% range; no change despite recent strong performance
items.quote: And I think, of course, our range is known to you, which is 20% to 24%. And therefore, from this high, which you have seen in this quarter, could it moderate a little bit?
