items.statement: VAM consumption cost at $1,370 in Q1 vs $924 YoY and $800 in Q4; price hikes of 2-12% taken across C&B categories, phased through quarter
items.quote: VAM consumption in the quarter was at $1,370 as compared to last year $924 and the fourth quarter was in the $800 range. However, total costs below gross margin increased slower than the revenue growth. The total cost increase was 14.5%.

items.statement: Demand holding well across categories; no price elasticity impact seen despite double-digit price hikes; C&B UVG at 12.5% in Q1
items.quote: I can tell you very, very categorically that the demand is holding quite well. So I think we are not seeing any kind of concern on demand at the moment at all. I think demand is holding well. And in our judgment, the trend is positive and in the right direction.

items.statement: Core businesses growing at 1-2x GDP; growth businesses (Dr. Fixit, Roff, Projects) accelerating at 2-4x GDP; UnoFin seeing green shoots in commercial/high-end residential
items.quote: I think for our growth businesses, particularly Dr. Fixit, Roff, even our projects business, if you look at Pidilite Projects Group and others. Some of our other growth businesses, we are seeing accelerated momentum. I'm saying so that's good news. We are in the range of 2x to 4x, but we are seeing accelerated momentum

items.statement: Tile adhesive penetration only 25-30% in India; Roff growing faster than market (1.5-2x); Nio Pro expanding from 1 to 4 plants; UnoFin early stage with architect acceptance
items.quote: See, just to give you a sense, the penetration of tile adhesives in India is still not more than 25%, at best 30%. So, the room for growth exists for all players. We can only confirm that we are growing fastest amongst all the players, which means we are gaining share in a fast-growing category.

items.statement: VAM prices highly volatile ($800 to near $2,000 back down); crude volatility unprecedented; geopolitical issues impacting exports
items.quote: So it's far more dynamic than maybe we've seen in the past, maybe we have seen it once or twice. But even there, the fluctuation is, I think, quite unique. And as you know, is a little bit decoupled from directly crude as well. So I think there are multiple other factors which are sort of driving some of these things.

items.statement: Expanding plant network for tile adhesives (Nio Pro from 1 to 4 plants); investing in automation for quality consistency; building trained applicator ecosystem for waterproofing
items.quote: Our biggest strength today, which is sort of known also, and I would reiterate, is our wide plant network, which we are expanding. Number two, consistent quality. We are investing in our plants in a manner that the quality consistency improves. These products are susceptible to product inconsistency. And therefore, if

name: Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilizers & Chemicals Ltd

items.statement: Management refuses to provide Q2 realization guidance citing market volatility and policy against guidance
items.quote: We do not recall, gentlemen, having given any guidance of such nature.

items.statement: Dahej coal-based steam/power plant saving INR30,000-40,000 per metric ton of TDI at current gas-coal delta
items.quote: But currently, we are likely to save around INR30,000 to INR40,000 per metric ton of TDI because of the current prices of gas and coal.

items.statement: Inventory built up to June 30 liquidated ~15% by end July; realizations mixed with recent price improvement
items.quote: The inventory, which was built up to 30 of June is liquidated to extent of around 15% by the end of July.

items.statement: TDI production expected at last FY level (~57,000 tonnes); plants restarted Aug 1 after Q1 viability shutdowns
items.quote: See, basically it is our expectation of the TGU production to more less at the same level as that of last FY.

items.statement: Fertilizer segment profit rose ~INR60 crore to INR85 crore (urea INR48 cr, ANP INR12 cr); chemicals main profit driver
items.quote: As far as segment results are concerned, the results in case of fertilizer has further iterated by around INR60 crores or so from around INR24 crores to INR85 crores.

items.statement: Oil prices down from Q1 peak in July-August but Middle East crisis unresolved; gas prices volatile, availability not affecting operations
items.quote: And slowly and slowly in the month of July and August, it has started coming down. Only point is that still the Middle East crisis has not resolved.

items.statement: War escalation/de-escalation causing viability issues, realization and input cost volatility; plants shut for cost economics in Q1
items.quote: Overall, during the quarter 1, it has been the situation of escalation and deescalation as far as war is concerned. And that has a ripple effect on the business as well, in terms of, at times, viability issues, at times, realizations, which have gone up.

items.statement: MoU with GMDC for underground coal gasification; studies ongoing, announcement expected soon
items.quote: GNFC has proposed the Memorandum of Understanding with GMDC. This is for the underground coal gasification.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents ~INR4,000 crore held across G-Sec, GSFS and bank deposits
items.quote: Around INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: (n)Code Solutions size ~INR100 crore; management working on digitization/AI expansion plan by year-end
items.quote: The size is around INR100 crores as of now, okay? And management is working on the plan for increasing the presence in the digitization, AI, etcetera.

items.statement: Exited Q1 FY27 with mid-teens revenue growth; demand environment strong but no formal full-year guidance given
items.quote: we actually exited the quarter in double digits kind of mid-teens number

items.statement: Input cost inflation (LPG/PNG, palm oil, sugar, milk) persists; mitigated only ~half via shrinkflation; ad spends ahead of sales growth; confident of managing volume-value-margin triangle
items.quote: I think at best, we have been able to mitigate half of the inflation through price increases. The other half, we have not been able to.

items.statement: Pricing growth ~1% in Q1 via shrinkflation; expect additional 1.5-2% pricing impact in coming quarters
items.quote: if the overall impact was 1%, you will probably see maybe another 1.5% to 2% coming in

items.statement: Croissant business doubled to ~INR 200 cr ARR growing 30%+; margin accretive to company average; non-biscuit portfolio (cake, rusk, wafers, dairy) grew double digits
items.quote: if you're quoting a number of INR 100 crores ARR, I think you should just double it and it's growing at 30% plus. And the overall margin that we are making in Croissant is kind of equal or slightly accretive to the company margin.

items.statement: International business mixed: Middle East & North America headwinds; Africa (Kenya) strong; new head appointed; expect return to growth track from Q2
items.quote: we are expecting that our international business from this quarter will be back on a growth track

items.statement: Investing in alternate fuels (biomass) to reduce LPG/PNG dependency; packaging cost optimization and renewable energy expansion underway
items.quote: how do we work better with alternate fuels so that the impact that we have on the LPG, PNG can be reduced a bit in a project which is on

items.statement: Volume growth ~9% in Q1 (tonnage basis); GT channel recovery: key states growing, other states 1.3x faster; e-commerce/Q-commerce 80-85% of e-com, growing healthy double digits
items.quote: the volume growth that we had for the quarter was close to 9%, which in any respect is a good volume growth

items.statement: PLI incentive not booked in FY26 or Q1 FY27 due to missing threshold growth; no P&L impact expected
items.quote: we didn't book any PLI incentive even in '25-'26. And nor have we booked anything in the current year because we have not been able to achieve the threshold growth

items.statement: Health/protein platform development underway; will address at platform level not single product; both core indulgent and health portfolios to grow in parallel
items.quote: protein is a part of the health platform. And we believe that if we have to address these problems and opportunities, we have to address them at a platform level and not a single product level

items.statement: Market share gains across biscuit categories sequentially post dual pricing end; focused interventions, media, sales sharpness driving recovery
items.quote: we see that there is sales market share gain across a large number of biscuit categories on a sequential basis, which we are seeing, and we are positive

items.statement: Core business revenue growth target of 16-20% CAGR for next few years under Greaves.Next strategy
items.quote: In the Greaves.Next strategy, which we launched a few quarters ago, we called out that our aim is to grow on a 16% to 20% CAGR for the next few years. So we stick by that.

items.statement: Commodity cost inflation impact ~1.5% on margins; price increases lagging; full pass-through expected by Q3
items.quote: 1.5% is what you can attribute to the additional investments. That is where rent -- what we see on the inflation side has been partially only mitigated by the price increase.

items.statement: Commodity price increases (platinum, aluminum, steel, fuel) due to West Asia geopolitical developments pressuring margins
items.quote: Second, commodity prices increased during the quarter, particularly following the geopolitical developments in West Asia. This has resulted in higher input costs across the industry and for most of our businesses.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA margin improved to 26.1%, up 1,420 bps YoY; consolidated EBITDA margin was 22%.
items.quote: EBITDA margins for quarter 1 FY27 improved to 26.1%, an increase in 1,420 basis points.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 demand dropped 15-25% YoY due to price volatility impacting non-OEM/unorganized sector more than OEM.
items.quote: whatever dip we saw is in line with whatever dip has been across the segment essentially across both the segments for that -- for this particular quarter, which would be to the order of 15% to 20% essentially or maybe 25%.

items.statement: Management expects demand to normalize and return to prior growth levels once geopolitical volatility subsides, but cannot predict timing.
items.quote: if things normalize, we do obviously anticipate that the demand will definitely pick up to the tune of what has happened earlier, and we will still return back to the growth levels that we anticipate in the business.

items.statement: ABS expansion (50kt) on track for completion in FY27; SAN merchant sales will continue unaffected.
items.quote: As far as our ABS expansion is concerned, like I mentioned in our investor presentation, it is online, and we do expect it to be completed accordingly.

items.statement: Commissioning timing within FY27 (Q3 vs Q4) not specified due to brownfield complexity and safety priorities.
items.quote: in our chemical plant, where we are talking about a 50,000 tonne kind of an expansion, Q3 and Q4 distinction is fairly precise. So you keep it broad. I would still say this financial year.

items.statement: Styrene monomer sourcing shifted from Middle East due to Strait of Hormuz disruption; lead times 10-15 days longer, inventory slightly higher.
items.quote: some of our styrene monomer specifically used to come from the Strait, which is no longer an option, so -- at least in the current climate. We do believe it will normalize, but it may take some time.

items.statement: Raw material prices highly volatile: styrene $1,100-1,400 (from $1,000 pre-war), butadiene down from $2,500+ peak, acrylonitrile $1,400-1,600.
items.quote: If you look at styrene monomer before the war, it was around $1,000. It went up to almost $1,600, $1,700. It came down to about $1,200 and has moved between $1,100 and $1,400 since then.

items.statement: No volume guidance given for FY27 due to unpredictable geopolitical environment and demand volatility.
items.quote: If someone is to tell me exactly what will happen in the geopolitical environment and the scenario, I can give a very precise volume guidance, but I don't think anyone can do that.

items.statement: Capital allocation philosophy unchanged: fund capex, maintain ratios, return excess cash to shareholders.
items.quote: we obviously try to find the best use for our capital and the most judicious use. So we don't believe that the company typically doesn't hold on to too much of capital if it doesn't utilize it.

items.statement: Auto sector demand impact muted; appliance sector impact greater. Channel inventory destocking occurring but underlying demand expected to recover.
items.quote: In auto, I think the effect has been muted. It is not that significant. But across the board, I would not say there has been no impact. There has been some impact.

items.statement: Polystyrene expansion will be pursued when business case is clear; current priority is ABS expansion.
items.quote: we, as a priority right now, have decided to go ahead with the ABS expansion as we have mentioned. With regards to polystyrene, as and when we have more information, we will definitely share with all our investors.

items.statement: Expects to continue momentum of last two quarters and exceed internal targets for FY27; no specific revenue or margin targets disclosed
items.quote: we hope to continue the momentum of the last 2 quarters and continue to go beyond our internal targets as far as performance is concerned

items.statement: Board approved new greenfield designer board plant near Hyderabad with estimated capital outlay of Rs. 167 crores
items.quote: During the quarter, the Board has approved the establishment of a greenfield designer board manufacturing facilities in Hyderabad with an estimated capital outlay of Rs. 167 crores

items.statement: Nellore Boards plant on track for commissioning by Q4 FY27; Hyderabad plant approved yesterday; total known capex of ~Rs. 500 crores allocated over next couple of years
items.quote: over the next couple of years, there is close to INR 500 crores of capex that have been allocated to known named programs and projects

items.statement: Parador order book up over 10% year-on-year; pipeline indicates strong recovery in H2
items.quote: The order book is healthy. It is up over 10% over last year, and the pipeline indicates a strong recovery in H2

items.quote: On a standalone basis, revenue increased by 10% year-on-year to Rs. 824 crores, while EBITDA rose by nearly 70% to Rs. 97 crores. EBITDA margins expanded by over 420 basis points

items.statement: Roofs segment EBITDA margin expanded 390 bps to 18.2%; Walls margin expanded 270 bps to 10.2%; Pipes margin expanded 660 bps
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved by 390 basis points to 18.2%, supported by stronger realization, improved volume sales and favourable operating leverage

items.statement: Pipes business navigated sharp resin price swings (60% rise in March, 30% decline in April); disciplined pricing and procurement efficiencies drove 660 bps margin expansion despite 11% revenue decline
items.quote: Despite these headwinds, EBITDA margins expanded by 660 basis points, driven by an improved product mix, procurement efficiencies and disciplined pricing actions

items.statement: Pipes demand expected to improve in Q2 with government interventions stabilizing PVC resin prices; anticipate moderate growth in seasonally weak Q2
items.quote: With government interventions facilitating stabilization in PVC resin price, we expect demand conditions to improve and anticipate moderate growth during the seasonally weak quarter 2

items.statement: Parador revenue mix shifting: commercial channel and new markets (US, India, UK, Middle East) to grow from <5% to ~20% of portfolio over next couple of years, adding EUR 20-30M revenue
items.quote: there is line of sight of adding a good 20 million, 30 million on last year's revenue base. That would push the share of these 2 components to about 20% in the portfolio

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainties persist; raw material, freight, currency markets volatile; labour costs trending upward; Parador impacted by Middle East conflict and SAP migration costs
items.quote: Geopolitical uncertainties continue to persist. Raw material, freight and currency market remain volatile and in addition, labour costs are showing an upward trend

items.statement: Debt-to-equity ratio at 0.68x as of June 30, well within manageable range; borrowings reduced by ~Rs. 100 crores in Q1 from Rs. 852 crores to Rs. 758 crores; no comment on rights issue
items.quote: our debt-to-equity ratio as on 30th June is 0.68x, which is well within our manageable range

items.statement: Parador BCG cost-out program: diagnostic complete, design underway, implementation ~4 months; first P&L impact visible by end of Q2, full impact by Q4 FY27; targeting 300-400 bps EBITDA uplift
items.quote: Our expectation is, at a conservative level that should deliver at least 300 to 400 basis point uplift on the EBITDA side

items.statement: Working capital reduced ~Rs. 100 crores YoY through fibre inventory reduction and 30% receivables reduction; CFO confirms sustainability
items.quote: Through targeted initiatives across receivable, inventories and sourcing, we reduced approximately Rs. 100 crores of working capital on a year-on-year basis

items.statement: Parador one-off costs of ~EUR 1 million in Q1 (SAP migration, front-loaded maintenance); expected to normalize in H2
items.quote: Together, these 2 will account for about EUR 1 million

items.statement: Open order book stands at Rs 365 crore, mostly to be executed in FY27 with some spillover to next year
items.quote: We have open orders of 365 crores, that is the orders which we have received, and the open part of that amount which is yet pending for dispatch. It should be dispatched during this year, or in the near future, over one or two years.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 78% YoY to Rs 48.98 crore driven by product launches, import substitution and international certifications
items.quote: We have an in-house R&D centre, and we launch many products year on year, and we do not compromise on price for competition. A good industry, good products, good product life cycles and good registrations; all of this mix is driving the good growth of Axis Solutions.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted: Industrial Engineering & Systems 59% (vs 28.6%), Water 26% (vs 55.8%), Automation & Digitalisation 15% (vs 15.6%)
items.quote: Revenue from automation and digitalisation in the current year is almost 15%. Last year, it was almost the same at 15.6%. From water, in the current year we earned 26%, and in last year it was 55.8%. From industrial engineering and systems, in the current year it is 59%, where last year it was 28.6%.

items.statement: No fundraising decided yet; must first meet minimum public shareholding (MPS) compliance before any NSE listing
items.quote: Right now, we have not decided anything about the instrument, or about the amount, or about the dilution. So, once it is decided by the board, only then will we be able to announce something on the BSE.

items.statement: Recurring MRO/AMC revenue is 5-6% of total and expected to rise significantly within 1-2 years
items.quote: Around 5% to 6% of the total revenue is in MRO, and it is gradually increasing. Given the type of orders we are receiving, within a very short span of time, during one or two years, you will find a really very good amount of increase in MRO.

items.statement: Opex annualized run rate near FY27 guidance of INR 490 crores; Q1 opex of INR 119 crores to be broadly maintained through Q4
items.quote: In line with our strategic alignment plan, our quarterly operating expenses have now reduced to approximately INR 119 crores from INR 217 crores in Q4'FY26. This represents an annualized run rate near our FY27 guidance of about INR 490 crores of opex.

items.statement: Portfolio yield rose 63 bps QoQ to 18.1% due to mix shift to Emerging Market (18.5%) and GROx (26%)
items.quote: Crucially, portfolio yield rose to 18.1%. Now this was up 63 bps quarter-over-quarter as the mix shifted to high-yield Emerging Markets and GROx.

items.statement: Emerging Market LAP AUM grew 9% QoQ to INR 3,896 crores; GROx AUM grew 32% QoQ to INR 3,003 crores; combined 46% of total AUM vs 32% in Dec'25
items.quote: Together, Emerging Market LAP and Embedded Merchant Finance now have AUM of approximately INR 6,899 crores and represents 46% of our total AUM compared to 32% in December '25.

items.statement: Target Emerging Market and GROx to reach 85% of AUM by FY29; cost reduction of INR 220 crores annualized in place
items.quote: The duo will scale to 85% of our AUM by FY29. The operating cost reset has been substantially completed. Our plan to take out approximately INR 220 crores of annualized operating cost is already in place.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance of 1.5%-2% for Emerging Market LAP maintained; total credit cost contained at 1.7% of average AUM in Q1
items.quote: And so, we are holding for the EM LAP, we are holding the 1.5% to 2% credit cost guidance that you have given? Shachindra Nath: Yes. Yes, that's true.

items.statement: Confident of funding growth without incremental equity through FY29; leverage at 3.6x; liquidity INR 1,864 crores; 66% borrowings beyond 3 years
items.quote: Basis this strategy, we are confident that UGRO can achieve its planned growth without incremental equity through FY29.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing improved 41 bps YoY to 10.14%; 7th consecutive quarterly improvement; incremental long-term borrowing at ~9.8%
items.quote: Our cost of borrowing was down 41 bps year-over-year and stood at 10.14%. This is our 7th consecutive quarterly improvement on our cost of borrowing.

items.statement: Emerging Market branch productivity rose to INR 62 lakhs/branch/month (mature branches INR 81 lakhs); GROx disbursing >60,000 loans/month to 3.4 lakh active customers
items.quote: Blended monthly productivity across the network increased from approximately INR 48 lakhs per branch during FY26 to INR 62 lakhs per branch per month in Q1'FY27. Branches older than 12 months are already producing approximately INR 81 lakhs per month.

items.statement: Merger with NCLT expected to complete by March 2027 (end of FY27), converting DiGiSPICE into pure-play listed fintech Spice Money
items.quote: we are hoping that by March 2027, which is by the close of this financial year. We will effectively DiGiSPICE Technologies will convert into Spice Money as a pure play listed fintech.

items.statement: Targeting 50%+ of gross margin from financial product distribution and credit segments within five years, up from ~20-25% currently
items.quote: what we hope from five years down the line to see is that 50% or more of our margin will be coming from these two segments.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth 14-16% YoY, EBITDA growth 25-30% YoY
items.quote: We believe that the momentum will accelerate even further in H2 FY27, with full-year growth expectations in the range of approximately 14% to 16%, with strong growth in pharma and marginal growth in crop, and EBITDA growth in the range of 25%-30%.

items.statement: Pharma CAGR 18-19% post FDA clearance, potentially faster
items.quote: I think pharma will be 18% to 19% CAGR going forward and maybe even faster. If some of the approvals ramp up and some of the NCE filings that are pending, if they ramp up, the growth could be even faster in the next few years.

items.statement: Animal Health revenue target Rs 400 cr+ by FY30 with 20%+ EBITDA margin
items.quote: We still remain confident of growing this business to Rs. 400 crores plus by FY30, as indicated earlier, making it an increasingly meaningful contributor to our overall portfolio.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex Rs 45 cr focused on debottlenecking, regulatory upgrades, new capacities
items.quote: Capital expenditure during the quarter stood at Rs. 45 crores, focused on de-bottlenecking, regulatory upgrades and building new capacities.

items.statement: Rs 900 cr invested over 4 years (Rs 300 cr maintenance, Rs 600 cr growth)
items.quote: Over the last 4 years, we have invested approximately Rs. 900 crores in capital expenditure. Rs. 300 crores of this was allocated towards maintenance CAPEX which is approximately Rs. 75 crores per year across our 6 sites. The balance Rs. 600 crores was invested in growth CAPEX

items.statement: Crop pricing under pressure from China oversupply; raw material/energy costs up Rs 7-8 cr in Q1
items.quote: In our quarter one number itself, we got impacted by almost 7 crores to 8 crores of raw material increase in our crop division because of raw material energy prices, which impacted our EBITDA in this one quarter itself.

items.statement: Net debt reduced from Rs 815 cr (FY24) to Rs 685 cr (FY26); debt/equity 0.53
items.quote: Despite undertaking significant investment over the last several years and navigating a challenging business environment, we have reduced our net debt from approximately Rs. 815 crores in FY24 to Rs. 685 crores by the end of FY26, with our debt-to-equity ratio now being 0.53.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 18-20%
items.quote: we remain confident of sustaining our growth momentum and maintaining our FY27 revenue growth guidance of 18% to 20%

items.statement: FY27 capex planned at INR 43 crore for Faucetware expansion, manufacturing efficiencies, digital and infrastructure
items.quote: For FY27, we have planned a capital expenditure outlay of approximately INR 43 crore. The investments will primarily be directed towards our Faucetware brownfield capacity expansion, manufacturing efficiencies, digital initiatives, and strengthening our operational infrastructure.

items.statement: Cumulative price increases of ~12% in Sanitaryware and ~16% in Faucetware implemented in March and May 2026, well absorbed by market
items.quote: Following the pricing revisions undertaken during March and May 2026, cumulative price increases now stand at approximately 12% in Sanitaryware and 16% in Faucetware. We are pleased to note that these pricing actions have been well-absorbed by the market.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Sanitaryware 47%, Faucetware 40%, Tiles 11%, Wellness 2%; Premium 44%, Mid 37%, Entry 19%
items.quote: The revenue mix for the quarter was broadly as follows: Sanitaryware accounted for 47%, Faucetware 40%, tiles 11%, and wellness 2% of the total revenue. On a Y-o-Y basis, sanitaryware revenue grew by 14%, Faucetware by 25%, tiles by 22%, and Wellness declined by 7%.

items.statement: Greenfield sanitaryware expansion (INR 130-150 cr) under review; decision by year-end if demand sustains; 18-month execution timeline
items.quote: We will review the greenfield expansion also. So by the end of this year, if we expect that the demand will continue in a similar fashion, accordingly we will take the necessary decision. Once the decision with respect to the construction of this greenfield project is taken, the project will take around 18 months from

items.statement: Brand building budget INR 85 crore for FY27 across TV, digital, social, on-ground; new campaign with Kriti Sanon launched
items.quote: During FY27, we plan to invest approximately INR 85 crore towards brand-building and marketing initiatives. These initiatives will span television, digital, social media and on-ground activations to further strengthen consumer engagement and enhance brand visibility.

items.statement: Dealer Management System extended to retailer loyalty program for better secondary sales visibility, inventory tracking, channel engagement
items.quote: One of the key developments during the quarter has been the extension of our 'Dealer Management System' (DMS) to the retailer loyalty program, marking another important milestone in Cera's digital transformation journey.

items.statement: One-time wage settlement impact INR 6.3 cr (Sep'25-Mar'26) + INR 3 cr (Q1); full year impact INR 18.3 cr; quarterly run rate ~INR 72 cr ex-one-time
items.quote: INR 6.3 crore was the effect which has come in for the previous period because the last wage agreement had ended in the month of September '25. Since we are giving the effect on a retrospective basis, it will be INR 6.3 crore from the period of September '25 to March '26, which has been given effect in the current quar

items.statement: Senator stores target 50 by end FY27 (from 35); Polipluz/ Senator targets unchanged but evaluated over longer horizon
items.quote: We have given a guidance that we will be going up from 35 to something like 50 stores by the end of the current year. We are in line with that. We will continue to scale up these stores, and we should end up with something like 50 by the end of the current financial year.

items.statement: Faucetware brownfield expansion to complete by Q4 FY27; current utilization 96%, can exceed 100%; no material availability issues expected
items.quote: Before 4Q, it is not possible because we have already undertaken the expansion. We should be expecting that increased capacity to come into effect from the fourth quarter. Before that, in Q2 and Q3, it is not possible. But we do not anticipate any challenges in respect of material availability because both the in-house

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue guided at INR 2,600 crores with EBITDA margin 10-11% and PAT margin 5-6%
items.quote: Overall, our outlook for FY27 remains unchanged. We continue to expect consolidated revenues in the range of INR2,600 crores, and within this, we expect the ethanol business to contribute revenue of about INR1,700 to INR1,800 crores, supported by supplies of approximately 22 crores liters during this year and additiona

items.statement: Ethanol business FY27 revenue guided at INR 1,700-1,800 crores with 22 crore liters supply target
items.quote: We continue to expect consolidated revenues in the range of INR2,600 crores, and within this, we expect the ethanol business to contribute revenue of about INR1,700 to INR1,800 crores, supported by supplies of approximately 22 crores liters during this year and additional allocations as received.

items.statement: Current ethanol order book at 19 crore liters with 2 crore liters unofficially announced, confident of meeting 21-22 crore liters FY27 target
items.quote: So, we have already received orders of 19 crores liters. And another 2 crores liters has almost been announced unofficially. We are awaiting for the purchase orders for the same. Once we receive that from the OMCs, we will announce it to the stock exchange. So, by this financial year-end, we are very confident that we

items.statement: Major capex phase complete; FY27 focused on debottlenecking ethanol plants to 100-110% utilization; major expansion in specialty chemicals from FY28
items.quote: The majority of our recent capital expenditure is now behind us, and FY27 is focused on maximizing returns from these investments. Accordingly, our priorities remain improving capacity utilization, reducing working capital intensity, strengthening cash flows, and maintaining a prudent leverage profile.

items.statement: Ethanol capacity debottlenecking to achieve 100-110% utilization by FY28; major expansion in specialty chemicals from FY28
items.quote: For the ethanol business, we will be looking at increasing the capacity by about 15% to 20% from existing capacity utilization. And try to achieve 100% to 110% of our existing capacity utilization by debottlenecking both the plants. So, definitely by FY28, we should be looking at 100% to 110% of our capacity utilizatio

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 14.2% vs 6.5% YoY; full year guided at 10-11% due to seasonal Q2 pressure from higher grain prices
items.quote: Q1 was definitely a very, very good quarter for us. Everything was very much in the favor for the company. The raw material prices were very conducive in both ethanol plants, Assam as well as Madhya Pradesh. In the DDGS, prices were at all-time highs. So, it was an exceptional quarter.

items.statement: Grain processing FY27 revenue guided at INR 800 crores with EBITDA margin ~5%, improvement from prior year
items.quote: So, right now, I mean, definitely we are expecting to achieve a revenue of about INR800 crores from this segment with an EBITDA of about 5%.

items.statement: Raw material mix: 40% FCI rice (mandatory), 50% maize, 10% DDGS/broken rice; FCI rice availability since March 2025 improved margins
items.quote: So, in ethanol, 40% is FCI rice, which is mandatory by the government, and about balance 50% is about maize, and 10% is DDGS, the broken rice.

items.statement: Maize prices currently INR 23-25/kg across 4 plants; stocking limited to 40-45 days due to 3,000 tons/day processing volume
items.quote: So, currently, the maize prices differ in different regions. If I talk about an average, the prices would be between INR23 to INR25 between our 4 plants. So, yes, like right now, Assam is about INR23, Muzaffarnagar is INR23, Gujarat is INR24, MP is INR25.

items.statement: Government committed to E20 blending (achieved), E30 by 2030 announced; ethanol export talks ongoing with neighboring countries and Japan/Indonesia
items.quote: India has already achieved the E20 blending milestone ahead of schedule, and the industry is now preparing for higher blending levels over the coming years. We continue to believe this creates a structurally favorable demand environment for efficient, integrated ethanol producers such as Gulshan Polyols.

items.statement: E30 blending timeline may be delayed 6-12 months due to social media protests; E20 is irreversible
items.quote: The increasing blending beyond 20% may be delayed by 6 months to 1 year until these unnecessary social media noise settles down. But E20 is definitely here to stay.

items.statement: Next growth phase from FY28: specialty and import-substitute chemicals in grain processing segment; products under evaluation, R&D ongoing
items.quote: As we have shared earlier, beginning in FY28, we intend to expand into specialty and import-substitute chemicals. Our objective is to build businesses with strong entry barriers, lower cyclicality, and higher value addition. The products are currently under evaluation, and once finalized, we will share details with all

items.statement: On-site plant at Trident expected operational by end of FY27, adding incremental revenue
items.quote: I would also like to add that our on-site plant at Trident should also be operational by the end of this financial year. That will definitely generate some additional revenue.

items.statement: Management projects high single-digit revenue growth for FY27, maintaining prior guidance despite market softness from geopolitical uncertainty.
items.quote: So, we have projected a high single-digit growth in our guidance. We are maintaining that. There is still a degree of softness in the market because of the war and the uncertainties.

items.statement: Targets INR 3,000 crores revenue in 3-year window (from current ~INR 2,000 crores) via organic and inorganic growth.
items.quote: Yes. So, we are looking at about a 3-year window of about INR 3,000-odd crores. We are about INR 2,000 crores right now roughly. So, we are looking at roughly in that range.

items.statement: Expects ~0.5% EBITDA margin improvement in FY27, targeting closer to 20% for the full year.
items.quote: So, across the board, we are at about 19-odd percent EBITDA margin. We are looking at about, roughly 0.5% improvement in this financial year. So, we should be hitting closer to 20% this financial year.

items.statement: Will sustain AI R&D investment at INR 40-50 crores for FY27; next year's budget undecided due to rapid AI evolution.
items.quote: We will keep it at approximately the same level because right now, there's a lot happening in that space, and we need to keep abreast with what's happening with latest technology, plus we are investing in the platform that we are building.

items.statement: AI-led deals constitute ~60% of wins in current fiscal year, driving higher conversion rates.
items.quote: If you look at the current financial year, about 60% of the deals we won have been AI-led or largely AI-driven. So, we see a good conversion ratio there.

items.statement: Strong traction for AI platforms (KAi underwriting, KAiSDLC, KAiBRE, SuperCX) with legacy modernization projects compressing timelines from years to months.
items.quote: We are seeing a good traction we are getting on the KAi underwriting solution and the KAiSDLC and KAiBRE solutions. These are for enterprise modernization. We have kicked off some projects in that space already.

items.statement: First customer booked for AI underwriting product; more deals expected soon in insurance sector across India, US, and Europe.
items.quote: We have started booking. We've got the first customer. We'll have a few more very soon.

items.statement: Actively evaluating M&A targets; no matured conversations to disclose. Cash position of INR 710 crores (pre-TNQTech payout).
items.quote: We are in dialogue with some companies from an M&A point of view. And no conversation has matured to the level that we need to sort of report it, but we are in dialogue with some companies.

items.statement: Deal sizes increasing but shifting to shorter-tenure transformation projects (3-9 months) vs traditional 3-5 year annuity deals.
items.quote: So, actually, our deal sizes are going up. It's just that they're not the annuity types. The deal size have actually gone up. But margins are where they are.

items.statement: No major shift in customer spending patterns across verticals/geographies; clients experimenting more with AI/automation but overall softness persists.
items.quote: No major changes. They are flirting more with the AI space. So, they are investing more on automation. But outside of that, there's no really pattern shift other than some degree of softness that we see.

items.statement: Board approved preferential issue in HT Media and Digicontent to retire 30-50% of debt, improve EPS and credit rating; priced per SEBI formula at INR 24.7
items.quote: Once the preferential capital comes in, the money will be used to retire the debt. At least 30 % to 50% of the debt will be retired, which will definitely be accretive to the EPS and long-term interest coverage ratio, our credit rating and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Preferential issue chosen over rights issue for faster execution (2-3 months), certainty of fundraising, and no under-subscription risk
items.quote: Preferential issue is a slightly shorter process. There is greater certainty of fundraising because there was a quantum that was being targeted to reduce the debt.

items.statement: Print EBITDA margin at 13% in Q1 FY27; management says it can be used as baseline for modelling if newsprint prices don't worsen
items.quote: So by and large, in your modelling, you can use that, but I told you what the imponderables are.

items.statement: Newsprint prices peaked at $650-700/metric ton, expected to plateau then decline; weak rupee adds cost pressure; no forward hedging available
items.quote: We believe that the prices have peaked and should plateau at this level before they start coming down. But obviously, as a commodity, no one can predict, that's our best estimate.

items.statement: Print ad revenue growth of 15% driven substantially by yield/pricing improvements; government ad rates increased in Nov 2025 after seven years
items.quote: A substantial part of that revenue growth of 15% is driven by our pricing. Of course, Government gave a price increase in November last year, but that was after seven years.

items.statement: Commercial print ad volumes held steady; government ad revenue grew on both volume and pricing; circulation steady with no drastic copy or price changes
items.quote: We have seen commercial revenues holding from a volume perspective. We have had a benefit of yield improvement there.

items.statement: Digital revenue down 28% YoY as portfolio deliberately reset to leaner, profitable offerings; Radio revenue flat after surrendering non-viable licenses
items.quote: Digital revenue moderated during the quarter as we deliberately reset the portfolio around leaner, more focused offerings with the intent of driving sustainable and profitable growth.

items.statement: Elevated newsprint prices, weaker rupee, and global supply chain uncertainties cited as concerns for Print margins going forward
items.quote: However, elevated newsprint prices, a weaker rupee, and global supply chain uncertainties are causes for concern going forward.

items.statement: No specific capex guidance given; focus on cost discipline and right-sizing organization driving employee cost reduction from INR 111 cr to INR 99 cr YoY
items.quote: We've been driving efficiency. I think that's something that we've been saying for the past sometime. We've been right-sizing the organization and that's basically what it is.

items.statement: Consolidated net cash INR 922 cr but sits in HMVL; HT Media and Digicontent are net debt companies; preferential issue only at those entities
items.quote: We have a very substantially healthy balance sheet position with net cash at INR 922 crores. But you have to understand that all that cash is parked in HMVL.

items.statement: Management expects traditional media (Radio, TV, Print) to remain subdued in FY27; Events business to grow exponentially; Digital (Gaana) targeting breakeven this year
items.quote: So we believe this year, the traditional mediums of Radio, TV, Print will remain subdued, the pure radio advertising. Events business will grow, exponentially has been growing across the board, and we continue to be bullish about it.

items.statement: Radio EBITDA margins historically 35-40%; Events EBITDA margins 25-30%; Gaana losses reduced 15% YoY to INR 8.3 cr, targeting breakeven
items.quote: So if you look at, our radio margins have always been in the range of 35% to 40%. Events have been in the range of 25% to 30% EBITDA margin. So you can look at in those lines as the profitability margin numbers.

items.statement: Radio advertising demand remains soft due to macro uncertainties and media fragmentation; Digital revenue grew 43.3% YoY to INR 31.1 cr (30.2% of total); Gaana revenue up 19% YoY to INR 21.4 cr
items.quote: The challenging conditions witnessed in FY26 extended into Q1 FY27 with advertiser demand remaining soft due to the uncertainties. This is affecting not only Radio segment, but the overall media industry.

items.statement: Radio inventory utilization down 8% but pricing improved ~4%; Gaana subscription price increased to INR 799 annual pack; cost rationalization via station networking and AI tools underway
items.quote: So inventory utilization has gone down by about 8%, but the price has improved by almost 4%.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Radio 56%, Digital 28%, Non-FCT/Events balance; Digital contribution up from 23% to 30.2% YoY; Gaana profitable subscriber mix ~70%
items.quote: So it's almost equal for us in terms of 56% Radio, 28% Digital and balance is non-FCT.

items.statement: Digital investment declined to INR 8.3 cr from INR 9.8 cr YoY; ongoing operational efficiency efforts using AI and broadcasting tools to reduce fixed cost base
items.quote: I'm happy to report that investment in Digital business declined to INR8.3 crores from INR9.8 crores in the same quarter last year, reflecting the results of our ongoing operational efforts.

items.statement: Some Events cancelled in Q1 due to artist travel disruptions from West Asia conflict; a few international concerts moved to Q2; Events business H2-heavy (35/65 split)
items.quote: There were a couple of international artist concerts we wanted to do, which are happening in quarter 2. But largely, sometimes it does happen that the events are planned for that month, and if that gets cancelled, then you lose the event.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflict (West Asia) causing event cancellations and artist travel disruptions; media fragmentation pressuring vanilla advertising across all traditional media; subscriber acquisition cost volatility in music streaming
items.quote: Performance was affected by the geopolitical conflict and related uncertainties, which led to our event cancellations, curtailed travel activities of artists and consequently lower business volumes during the quarter.

items.statement: Cash balance INR 390 cr as of June 30, 2026; buyback discussed at Board level but no decision announced; evaluating strategic initiatives
items.quote: The company continues to maintain a robust balance sheet with a cash balance of INR390 crores as of June 30, 2026.

items.statement: Three business verticals: Radio, Digital (Gaana), Events; experimenting with AI internally but sector focus remains media; no diversification plans outside media
items.quote: So Suresh, so far, we have concentrated on the Media business, but with new tech of AI and all, we do delve on that, and we keep experimenting on and do internal investments on usage of AI, but largely, our overall sector will remain media.

items.statement: Target Express Logistics EBITDA margin of 7.5% for FY27 and 10% over 3 years
items.quote: when we did this 3-year plan vision, which we shared with all of you, we had said it will be 7.5% on the Express margin so that we are looking at in this year. And if you see 10% is the target in that plan, so we are inching up towards that direction.

items.statement: Consolidated pre-Ind AS adjusted EBITDA margin target of 5-6% for FY27
items.quote: We are sticking to that plan. This year, the trajectory on this front is to be in the level of 5% to 6% and improve from there on.

items.statement: Aim to grow faster than logistics industry by a percentage point
items.quote: whatever logistics industry growth is, we will be at a percentage point above the logistics industry. That's the strive we have for growth.

items.statement: Express Logistics gross margin improved 100bps YoY to 26.3% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: If you see this quarter, both the yield effort and the volume growth has shored up the gross margin from the last year number of 25.3% to 26.3%. So there's a 1% improvement in the gross margin of Express business in this quarter.

items.statement: Express Logistics EBITDA margin at 6.2% in Q1 FY27, Consultative Logistics at 29.56%
items.quote: Express is at 6.2% and at CL, we are at Consultative Logistics, we are at 29.56%. So that's the breakup you're looking at, right?

items.statement: Express realization up 6.4% YoY; ~80% from service-driven escalation, ~20% from diesel pass-through
items.quote: the natural escalation is a larger pie, which would be, let's say, 80% and 20% would be around on the pass-through of diesel impact.

items.statement: Logistics industry expected to grow at low double-digits (1.2-1.5x GDP of 6-7%)
items.quote: the logistics industry by that factor will be anywhere in the low double-digit range. So that's what we estimate.

items.statement: Express KEA revenue share reclassified to ~60%, retail ~20%, balance strategic
items.quote: KEA that we account for here are at about 60% of our revenue, retail at about 20% and the balance is strategic.

items.statement: Consultative Logistics space reduced from 8.4M to 7.5M sq ft deliberately to cut white space cost
items.quote: 2 large warehouses we did action in terms of reducing the white space impact. So that was one deliberate attempt by us to reduce that white space as a cost.

items.statement: Other income INR14 crores includes INR8 crores lease closure gain, INR2 crores interest, INR4 crores liquidity/refunds
items.quote: One exceptional is the lease closure, which has happened in this quarter. So that's one INR8 crore amount, which is the other income component sitting here, plus we have received some income refunds and there's an interest component of INR2 crores.

items.statement: Express business 95% road, 5% air by volume
items.quote: About 95% of our business is road and about 5% is air.

items.statement: Oil production target of ~1 MMT per quarter going forward, implying ~4 MMT for FY27 and up to 4.2 MMT by FY29
items.quote: If everything remains ceteris paribus, then given everything going good and nothing adverse happens in the field, we expect that we will be reaching 1 MMT every quarter from now onwards.

items.statement: Gas production target of 3.8 BCM for FY28 with potential to reach 5 BCM by FY29 once pipeline infrastructure is complete
items.quote: Yes next year it will be 3.8 BCM. So now on an averaging we are shutting down some wells at least 30 wells we are always shutting down. When we will be opening all those well.

items.statement: FY27 total capex budget of INR 8,600 crores; Q1 FY27 actual spend of INR 3,050 crores
items.quote: Our total budget estimate for the whole year is as of now it is 8,600. It will go undergo some changes and revision during our next review. And actual expenditure for the previous year was INR13,026 crores.

items.statement: NRL expansion capex of INR 34,000-35,000 crores for refinery and INR 7,200-7,300 crores for PPU; INR 30,000 crores spent so far
items.quote: We have invested around INR30,000 crores so far. So we should be completing the refinery project around INR34,000 crores to INR35,000 crores and we should also be completing the PPU project by spending another INR7,200 crores or INR7,300 crores.

items.statement: Drilled 17 wells in Q1 FY27 (7 exploratory, 10 development); targeting 100 wells in FY27 (42 exploratory, 57 development)
items.quote: Like last year we drilled 74 wells and this year we are targeting 100 which includes onshore as well as offshore. So currently we are on track to achieve that big ambition of drilling, completing 100 wells.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin of 54%+ in Q1 FY27 vs 34%+ in Q1 FY26; NRL GRM of USD 35.95/bbl (USD 33/bbl normalized)
items.quote: We have also achieved the highest ever EBITDA during this quarter, which is 4,605 crores, as the margin is 54% plus as compared to 34% plus in the previous quarter of the last year.

items.statement: Crude oil realization USD 98.73/bbl in Q1 FY27 vs USD 66.20/bbl in Q1 FY26; Gas price USD 7.19/MMBtu vs USD 6.72/MMBtu
items.quote: The crude oil price realization was USD98.73 per barrel vis-a-vis USD66.20 per barrel as compared to the previous year. The natural gas price stood at USD7.19 per MMBtu in this quarter as compared to 6.72$ in the previous quarter of the last financial year.

items.statement: GST on royalty liability of ~INR 2,500 crores (principal) to be paid within 6 weeks; already provided for, no P&L impact
items.quote: So without interest it would be roughly about INR2,500 crores. So our undertaking to the court was that the court has given us six weeks time to settle this and we are trying to kind of make this payment as quickly as possible.

items.statement: Assam land tax case to be withdrawn by state government; currently shown as contingent liability with no financial impact
items.quote: So far whatever we have shown in our financials, we have shown them as contingent liability. So it has not impacted our financials at all. And in the days ahead as long as, I mean we'll have to wait till it is withdrawn by the state.

items.statement: Deepwater exploration campaign: first rig arriving Jun-Jul 2027, second by Mar 2028; govt to fund INR 800 cr for stratigraphic well and up to INR 675 cr/well for deepwater drilling
items.quote: The first rig is going to come in June-July 27 and the second rig is going to come by March 28. And that will kick start our deep water exploration campaign. And one well we are also going to drill next year in Mahanadi, but that is also going to be sponsored by the government, INR800 crores will be sponsored as part o

items.quote: So this will take about a month in Vijayapuram 1 for the testing to be complete. And then we will demobilize this rig, our current rig, semi-submersible rig that we have, because it has completed its contractual tenure. So the fourth well we are going to go in Andaman with a jack-up rig and this we are going to be dril

items.statement: Board approved preferential issue in HT Media and Digicontent to retire 30-50% of debt, improve EPS and credit rating; priced per SEBI formula at INR 24.7
items.quote: Once the preferential capital comes in, the money will be used to retire the debt. At least 30 % to 50% of the debt will be retired, which will definitely be accretive to the EPS and long-term interest coverage ratio, our credit rating and so on and so forth.

items.statement: Newsprint prices peaked at $650-700/metric ton, expected to plateau then decline; rupee at lifetime high adds cost pressure
items.quote: After that, it had come down very substantially. But after that, this is the highest peak that we have seen at about $650 to $700 a metric ton. We believe that the prices have peaked and should plateau at this level before they start coming down.

items.statement: Print EBITDA margin at 13% in Q1 FY27; management says use as baseline but margins depend on newsprint and FX
items.quote: So by and large, in your modelling, you can use that, but I told you what the imponderables are. So, let's say theoretically, if the dollar goes to 100 and the commodity goes to 700, then suddenly we'll have a margin dilution.

items.statement: Print ad revenue growth of 15% driven substantially by yield/pricing improvements; government ad rates increased in Nov 2025 after seven years
items.quote: So, a substantial part of that revenue growth of 15% is driven by our pricing . Of course, Government gave a price increase in November last year, but that was after seven years.

items.statement: Commercial print ad volumes held steady; government ad revenue grew on both volume and pricing
items.quote: We have seen commercial revenues holding from a volume perspective. We have had a benefit of yield improvement there. With respect to government revenues, we have a combination of both volume and pricing

items.statement: Digital revenue down 28% YoY as portfolio deliberately reset to leaner, profitable offerings; Digital EBITDA margin -12%
items.quote: Digital revenue moderated during the quarter as we deliberately reset the portfolio around leaner, more focused offerings with the intent of driving sustainable and profitable growth.

items.statement: No specific capex guidance given; cost discipline and right-sizing reduced consolidated employee cost from INR 111 cr to INR 99 cr YoY
items.quote: Well, we've been driving efficiency. I think that's something that we've been saying for the past sometime. We've been right-sizing the organization and that's basically what it is.

items.statement: Elevated newsprint prices, weaker rupee, and global supply chain uncertainties cited as concerns going forward
items.quote: However, elevated newsprint prices, a weaker rupee, and global supply chain uncertainties are causes for concern going forward.

items.statement: Radio revenue flat YoY; segment leaner after surrendering non-viable station licenses; Radio EBITDA negative INR 3 cr
items.quote: Radio revenue remained broadly steady year-on-year. The segment is now operating on a leaner and more sustainable footprint following the surrender of licenses for certain non-viable stations.

items.statement: No specific revenue or earnings guidance given; management hopeful of sustaining performance but cites imponderables
items.quote: We would not, as per usual practice, be giving any specific guidance on revenue or earnings projections.

items.statement: Management targets ~8% operating EBITDA margin for full year FY27, up from 7.3% in Q1, driven by commodity cost pass-through and better volumes in H2
items.quote: initially, at the beginning of this year, we had guided that we should be probably close to 8% kind of a margin for the whole year, at least at the operating level, which is this quarter about 7.3%.

items.statement: Expects close to 20%+ volume growth for full year FY27 on low base and market share gains, with potential to outperform industry by 4-5%
items.quote: we think that we should be having close to 20% plus kind of a volume growth for the full year

items.statement: FY27 capex of ~INR400 crore to complete compressor and refrigerator projects and consolidate plastic moulding operations at new Salarpur facility
items.quote: This year, the total capex that we have is about INR400 crores, which is going to actually be utilized in completing the ongoing projects of compressor and refrigerator.

items.statement: Washing machine capacity expanded to 3 million units annually with new 1.8M DMIC plant; targeting 70-80% utilization by FY28
items.quote: this new capacity, which is coming online will bring our total capacity to around 3 million. And we are hopeful that in next 1 or -- maybe by -- not by end of this year, maybe by the FY '28, we should have almost around 70% to 80% utilization

items.statement: Gross margin percentage softened YoY and QoQ due to commodity inflation and rupee depreciation; per-unit margins stable; expects normalization as cost pass-through improves in H2
items.quote: On a per unit basis, margin remained stable versus last year and commodity cost increases have been partially passed through to the customers.

items.statement: Commodity cost increases partially passed through; further price hikes expected from December quarter as copper >$14,000 and rupee ~95.5-96; RAC ASP up 10-12% in Q1
items.quote: we are hopeful that we'll be able to again pass -- go for a price increase going forward because today, the copper has crossed $14,000 and the rupee is also hovering around INR95.5 and INR96.

items.statement: RAC industry primary sales grew 10-15% YoY in Q1 with 10-12% ASP growth; secondary sales better than primary; channel inventory near normal at 4.5-5.5M units
items.quote: overall industry has done around 10% to 15% better, 15% better as compared to last year. And on the couple of that, if you combine that with around 10% to 12% value growth in the ASP

items.statement: No firm order book disclosed; AC season ending, fresh order book builds from Sep-Oct for Dec season; washing machine has volume commitments but not shared
items.quote: We do not share any order book numbers. And typically, the order book is not in terms of any firm commitment.

items.statement: Industry imports 50-60% of compressors; govt restricts imports to 25% of FY25 volumes until Mar 2027, then zero; potential supply tightness from Jan-Feb 2027 if demand strong
items.quote: at the industry level, I think we are still importing around 60% of our compressor requirements in India right now, around 50% to 60% right now.

items.statement: Geopolitical and supply chain risks remain; dependent on overseas suppliers for key components; demand uncertainty also a risk
items.quote: There can be a lot of geopolitical factors right now. See, we are living in such uncertain times. You don't know what will happen tomorrow.

items.statement: Net cash position with INR491 crore cash and modest debt; fixed asset turnover target >4x; AC revenue share to decline from 60-65% to 50-55% over 2-3 years
items.quote: On balance sheet, things are quite healthy. We are a net cash company now. Cash and bank balance stood at INR491.3 crores, and we have a modest debt at the end of 1Q 2027.

name: Multi Commodity Exchange of India Ltd

items.statement: Expects strong growth momentum at fundamental level to continue in FY27 despite high base from exceptional Q4 FY26
items.quote: So, we are expecting the growth momentum at the fundamental level to continue to be good. While the exceptional quarter on Q4 driven by many other factors holds the last year's numbers, we expect the numbers this year to be on a strong momentum as well.

items.statement: Total income grew 85% YoY to INR752 crore; revenue from operations grew 88% YoY to INR702 crore in Q1 FY27
items.quote: So, during the quarter, our total income increased by 85% to INR752 crores and revenue from operations grew to INR702 crores, which is an 88% growth.

items.statement: EBITDA more than doubled to INR544 crore with 72% EBITDA margin; PAT at INR413 crore in Q1 FY27
items.quote: EBITDA more than doubled to INR544 crores, and there is a good EBITDA margin of 72% with a PAT at INR413 crores.

items.statement: Traded client base doubled YoY to 13.72 lakh clients in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Our traded client base doubled from previous year to 13.72 lakh clients this quarter.

items.statement: Successfully launched Silver 100 Grams Futures contract in response to market demand; seeing good performance and adoption
items.quote: We've had a very successful launch of the Silver 100 Grams Futures contract. This was a demand from the market given the price of silver. In a quick response to market demand, the product was launched and has already seen a very good performance.

items.statement: 50+ AMCs now using MCX bullion price as reference for AUM calculations after regulatory directive
items.quote: We have worked very closely with the industry and have a number of AMCs, at least 50-plus AMCs, who are today using MCX bullion price as a reference for AUM calculations.

items.statement: Electricity futures Q1 ADT at INR37 crore with ~55% market share; open interest of 1,630 lots (>70% market share) across 3 months
items.quote: So, electricity futures Q1 ADT is about INR37 crores. We stand at, I think, about 55% or so from a market share standpoint when it comes to ADT. However, what we've done over the course of the year is really look at studying our market needs very carefully. And we have a strong reinforcement that our contract is very m

items.statement: Expects electricity derivatives-to-spot ratio to evolve to global market multiples over medium term; both hedgers and financial participants needed for depth
items.quote: We absolutely expect this to be reflective of what we see in global markets. So, we are in the really early phase of this journey. And like I said, all the lead indicators are looking strong. We have a strong feedback from market because any new product introduced also, we need to be really sure that despite having don

items.statement: Technology capacity well positioned: handled >3 billion transactions/day with capacity for >2x; continuing to invest in resilience and scale efficiently
items.quote: In fact, just in the last one year, we have very successfully handled large volume of transactions. We would have started the year at less than a billion. And when I say a year, I'm talking of maybe four quarters back, a billion transactions a day, and we've already handled more than 3 billion transactions a day with t

items.statement: Float income on margin money was INR30 crore in Q1 FY27
items.quote: That is around INR30 crores for this quarter.

items.statement: Management guides for 10-15% top-line growth across all segments for the year.
items.quote: We're looking at growth of, say, 10% to 15% on top line and it will be across all the segments.

items.statement: Hopeful to close FY27 with double-digit volume growth despite current disruptions.
items.quote: We're still positive in long term. And we're hopeful that for the year, we can still close out on double-digit growth.

items.statement: Indore ICD construction to accelerate after September; operational by 2028. Ankleshwar ICD EXIM operations to start by September 2026.
items.quote: Indore should be operational by 2028. Ankleshwar, they have received their initial customs permission, and we should be operational there for EXIM operations by September.

items.statement: Snowman Logistics to add ~24,000 pallets in FY27 with Pune and Patna facilities; similar additions planned for subsequent years.
items.quote: This year we'll see around 24,000 additional pallets, I mean, by end of this year. And subsequently, similar numbers is what we are planning for subsequent years.

items.statement: Rail EBITDA per TEU declined in Q1 due to adverse volume mix (lower imports, higher exports), port congestion, lower double stacking (39% vs 40-42%), higher empty running, and wage/fuel cost increases.
items.quote: On double stack, basically, we're at 39%. So, it has dipped a bit from last year where we were at like 40% to 42% depending on the quarter.

items.statement: Snowman achieved 5-7% average warehousing price hikes in Q1; further hikes expected at renewals due to labor and fuel cost increases.
items.quote: In terms of percentage, I cannot say right away, but in a range between 5% to 7% on an average is what we have got from most of the customers.

items.statement: Gateway passed on 35% Haryana minimum wage hike and fuel cost increases to customers with a time lag; impact more visible in Q2.
items.quote: Haryana had an increase by 35% in minimum wages. We've tried to pass it on to customers, but there is a time lag in that also. Fuel also, most of it, we've been able to pass on. So that impact will be more visible in Q2.

items.statement: June and July volumes similar to Q1 trend; July impacted by weather restrictions at ports. Market share intact but market degrown due to West Asia crisis.
items.quote: June was similar only. Even July is similar. We can't give specifics because this is a Q1 call and being listed, we have that restriction. But I mean, broadly, the trend remains the same.

items.statement: Ankleshwar ICD expected to ramp to ~5,000 TEUs/month within 3-4 years, adding direct EXIM volume and EBITDA.
items.quote: But we also estimate that, say, within 3, 4 years, we should be doing a similar number.

items.statement: West Asia crisis since April causing volume disruption; recovery timing uncertain. Double-digit growth dependent on crisis resolution.
items.quote: Right now, it's only dependent on this war situation. Once that clears up, then double digit will be easy to achieve for us.

items.statement: JNPT rail haulage 6 slabs higher than Mundra; special haulage charges discussed but nothing concrete. Shipping line decisions will drive volume shift.
items.quote: There is 6 slabs higher compared to Mundra. So, which makes it slightly expensive as far as the rail haulage is concerned. But again, so there has been request that if Indian railways can rationalize some of that haulage, especially on the JNPT. But that is a matter of question whether it is going to happen or not.

items.statement: MAT credit sufficient to maintain ~18.88% cash tax rate for 7-8 years; reported tax rate higher but cash outgo up only INR 1-2 crore YoY.
items.quote: We will be paying at the rate of 18.88% for at least 7, 8 years. So, we have a large amount of accumulated MAT credit, which we will be utilizing over the next 7, 8 years.

items.statement: CFS business not actively for sale after failed valuation attempt 1.5 years ago; open to deal if valuation improves.
items.quote: We undertook an exercise, but we didn't get the right valuation. This was about 1.5 years ago. And since then, we've not been actively looking because we reached about a net debt-zero position earlier in the year when we paid out the special dividend.

items.statement: Land bank ~475 acres across India, mostly freehold; Garhi Harsaru land estimated at INR 25-30 crore/acre but not assessed for market value regularly.
items.quote: Our overall land bank is about 475 acres across India in prime locations. Most of them -- some are industrial locations, some are port leases, but most of it is freehold.

items.statement: Maintain full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance of 75% YoY and consolidated EBITDA margin of 20-22%
items.quote: And we maintain that revenue guidance of 75% growth over the previous year and an EBITDA margin of 20% to 22% on a consol basis is what we maintain our guidance for the full year basis.

items.statement: Equipment supply share in order book increased to 59% as of July 2026, up from previous quarters
items.quote: As of July '26, the share of equipment supply in our order book stood at approximately 59% with the balance 41% being turnkey.

items.statement: 4X wind turbine prototype installation on track for August 2026, commercial launch by end of FY26
items.quote: We are on track to install the first prototype in the month of August with commercial launch expected by end of FY26.

items.statement: IRSL expanding transformer capacity to 4.9 MVA for 4X series, adding 8-20 MVA and 100+ MVA transformers, plus inverters and unit substations
items.quote: Our operational Jaipur transformer factory is gearing up to manufacture our next bigger capacity, which is 4.9 MVA transformers for our 4X series. We also plan to further increase our trafo manufacturing capacity, including medium-sized trafos between 8 to 20 MVA as well as large transformers, which is 100 MVA plus.

items.statement: Expect 8-10 GW annual wind capacity additions in India over next few years driven by RTC, FDRE, hybrid tenders
items.quote: We expect to see strong annual wind capacity additions ranging between 8 to 10 gigawatt over the next few years, driven by RTC, FDRE and hybrid capacity additions.

items.statement: INOX Green maintains FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR 600 crore on annualized basis post-consolidation from Q3/Q4
items.quote: INR600 crores is the annualized basis from Q3, Q4 onwards is what you can expect. Yes, there is an annual escalation as well, which is a natural business.

items.statement: INOX Green O&M portfolio targets 50% EBITDA margin on 4 GW legacy portfolio; acquired portfolios expected to have higher margins
items.quote: Generally, our guidance on the O&M business of Wind portfolio stands at 50% EBITDA margin. and that has been guidance.

items.statement: Only force majeure events beyond control (e.g., geopolitical crises) seen as risk to meeting 75% revenue guidance; equipment supply pivot reduces execution risk
items.quote: And I would say only force majeure, things which are beyond our control. I mean no one had an inkling about this Middle East crisis. So something like that. Otherwise, this pivot to move to equipment supply, honestly, we don't see a risk of not meeting our deliverables.

items.statement: MOU signed for 1.5 GW with INOX Clean Energy in June 2026; 500 MW firm orders signed, balance 1 GW to follow
items.quote: We are pleased to inform you that INOX Wind has signed an MOU for 1.5 gigawatt. I'll repeat again, 1.5 gigawatt with INOX Clean Energy in June, out of which firm orders have been signed for 500 megawatts so far.

items.statement: Received 200 MW LOA from NLC India in July 2026 via tender process; repeat order
items.quote: In another positive development in the first quarter, we have received an LOA for 200 megawatt from NLC India. This is a repeat order from NLC in the month of July through an extensive tendering process.

items.statement: NCLT approval received for Wind World India acquisition; formalities to complete in Q2 FY27, then financial consolidation
items.quote: We have received the approval from Hon'ble NCLT Ahmedabad for the acquisition of Wind World India Limited. The acquisition formalities are expected to be completed in quarter 2 FY27.

items.statement: Power evacuation infrastructure business demerged from INOX Green to IRSL effective August 1, 2026; IRSL to be listed post regulatory approvals
items.quote: Further, the demerger of the power evacuation infrastructure business from INOX Green into INOX Renewable Solution has been completed as on August 1, 2026, being the record date. IRSL would now be automatically listed on the stock exchange post receipt of regulatory approvals.

items.statement: ALMM compliance: 80-90% components indigenized; targeting 100% by end of calendar year for both 3X and 4X models
items.quote: Before end of the calendar year, we would be -- we hope that we are almost 100% on wind turbines. And I'm talking not only for our 3X model, but even for the 4X model.

items.statement: FY28 revenue growth of 25-30% year-on-year, targeting INR 1,000 crores revenue with 29-30% EBITDA margins
items.quote: I think we have developed a revenue model wherein we believe by 2030 we can easily reach INR1,500 crores revenue mark. So we are talking about doubling our revenues before end of FY30. So we will see a year-on-year growth of 25% to 30%.

items.statement: FY27 capex of INR 185-190 crores: INR 70 crores hormone plant, INR 50 crores oncology expansion, INR 25-30 crores bioequivalence, INR 20 crores working capital, INR 10-15 crores biosimilar R&D
items.quote: You can say INR70 crores probably in hormone, sir. INR50 crores will be in oncology. I think the bioequivalence will be roughly around INR25 crores to INR30 crores. Working capital will be INR20 crores. And then biosimilar R&D will roughly around INR 10 crores, INR15 crores. So we are looking at overall INR185 crores,

items.statement: Extended loan facility available but unutilized; current cash flows sufficient for FY27 capex
items.quote: So we have actually taken an extended loan. However, we have not utilized it. We have, we are considering if there is any disruption in the cash flow, we might use INR15 crores, INR20 crores, but as of now, there is no such utilization. So right now with the running cash flows we are able to make all these investments.

items.statement: Targets consistent 15% annual profit growth and 15%+ ROCE/ROE profile, aiming to be among top ~100 Indian companies with INR 500 cr+ PAT
items.quote: We want to drive SIS into that box of 100 companies in this country which deliver INR 500 crore plus in PAT and our material businesses with consistent year-after-year 15% growth in profits and 15% or greater return profile.

items.statement: India Security margins sustainable at 5.1%, targeting 5.5-6% range; FM margins at 5.5% targeting near 6%
items.quote: Our objective is to move from this range to 5.5%, 6% ballpark range in India.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA INR 207 crore (4.5% margin), up 36.2% YoY; India Security 5.1%, FM 5.5%, International Security 3.5%
items.quote: On a consol EBITDA level, we grew 36.2% year-on-year to INR 207 crore and a margin of 4.5%.

items.statement: Cash business IPO (DRHP filed) deferred due to market conditions and peer de-rating, waiting for opportune window
items.quote: We are waiting for a good time window. And in the IPO rush that we are witnessing right now, also given the fact that the peer comparables have witnessed significant de-rating, we are waiting on a more opportune time.

items.statement: Acquired 51% stake in Updater Services as treasury operation; remaining 49% to be acquired over next couple of years (anniversary 2028)
items.quote: No, we only have acquired 51% stake in the Company, and we still have to acquire 49% subsequently over the next couple of years. The anniversary for that '28.

items.statement: Australia minimum wage hike 4.75% passed through via rise-and-fall clauses with timing lag (invoicing/processing), not dependent on contract renewal
items.quote: When the minimum wage hike happens, our contracts have in-built rise and fall clauses, which basically means that we contractually have the right to pass through the higher wage cost of employees to the customer immediately.

items.statement: No exceptional labor shortage in India; seasonal April-June shortage normalizes by July as farm labor returns
items.quote: Nothing exceptional. I think every year, April through to June before the monsoon sets in, is a period where you witness shortages. And by about July when the farm labor returns to their blue-collar jobs, this subsides.

items.statement: Labor codes impact accretive at EBITDA and PAT levels over coming 3-4 quarters as contract negotiations progress
items.quote: You will see the impact over the coming 3, 4 quarters that it will be accretive both at the EBITDA and PAT levels as efforts are underway at multiple fronts in terms of contract negotiations, etc.

items.statement: Cumulative capital returned to shareholders will exceed INR 700 crore after current buyback completes (5 buybacks + 4 dividends since IPO)
items.quote: Once this program concludes, we would have cumulatively returned over INR 700 crore to the shareholders, thus keeping up with our track record of consistent capital return.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20% year-on-year reaffirmed
items.quote: Our guidance is 20% year -on-year, all right, and we are well on track to do that.

items.statement: FY27 order inflow target of INR4,500-5,000 crores reaffirmed with strong pipeline
items.quote: FY '27 order inflow target is between INR4,500 crores to INR5,000 crores.

items.statement: Order book at INR13,535 crores as of June 30, 2026 with 55% public, 45% private split
items.quote: Order book stood at INR13,535 crores as on 30th June 2026. Public sector accounts for 55%, while private sector accounts for 45% of the total order book.

items.statement: FY27 capex target increased to INR193 crores from INR165 crores; Q1 capex INR52.2 crores
items.quote: For the full year, the target is INR193 crores. The CapEx done in Q1 is INR79 -- sorry, INR52.2 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance 15.5-16% for FY27; Q1 margin 15.7% impacted by INR10 crore provision
items.quote: we have guided about 15.5% to 16% on EBITDA level margin

items.statement: INR10 crore additional provision in Q1 for nonferrous metal cost escalation not covered by indices; expect substantial reversal in Q3-Q4
items.quote: As a prudent measure, the company has, therefore, taken an additional provision of INR10 crores in the current quarter.

items.statement: Strong bid pipeline of INR22,000 crores public and INR5,000 crores private for Q2-Q3 FY27
items.quote: we have an identified bid pipeline of INR22,000 crores in the public side and approximately INR5,000 crores of targeted bid pipeline in the private sector for Q2 and Q3

items.statement: Factored 20 days NGT construction ban impact in North India; risk if AQI remains 400-500 extending to 40 days
items.quote: We have factored an average of 20 days' worth. Now if it goes to 40 days, everyone will suffer.

items.statement: Promoter pledge reduced from 85.5 lakh to 50 lakh shares; target full release by end FY27
items.quote: The promoter share pledge has been reduced from 85.5 lakh shares on an absolute basis as on 31st March 2026 to 50 lakh shares currently. The company targets for full release of the pledge by the end of the current financial year.

items.statement: Gross debt INR522 crores; net debt-free target in 8 quarters on track; working capital days to reduce 25-30 days in FY27
items.quote: The total gross debt is INR522 crores. I have given a commentary during the last conference call that on a yearly basis, it will reduce.

items.statement: Consolidated PBT growth guidance revised from mid-teens to double-digit for FY27; final guidance by end of Q2
items.quote: We had given a guidance of roughly around mid-teens. So again, I said, a lot will depend on the assessment we can take on the Crop Care business impact towards the second half. But I think one thing we're still pretty confident of is that we'll be able to target a double-digit growth still.

items.statement: Oil Palm FFB volume growth targeted at high single-digit to early double-digit CAGR over next 4-5 years
