items.quote: I would say we can look for a growth in FFB volume of high single digit to early double-digit growth. I'm being conservative on this. I'll be very honest because there can be some one-off here in this on the weather pattern sometimes. But yes, I believe we'll target double digit.

items.statement: Oil Palm capex of INR300-350 crores includes integrated complex and specialty fats refinery; all investments meet 16-18% IRR hurdle
items.quote: We have a tight filter on this very clearly. This is a high ROCE business for us. Nothing crosses our bridge broadly beyond -- until we are doing an IRR of around 16% to 18%, and this meets that bridge for us.

items.statement: Downstream value-added integration in Oil Palm expected to add ~200 bps to overall EBITDA profile when fully scaled
items.quote: We expect this downstream business when fully scaled up should add roughly around close to 200 bps to our overall EBITDA profile.

items.statement: Astec LifeSciences full-year revenue growth guidance raised from ~20% to >20% after Q1; CDMO mix expected at 50-52%
items.quote: In the last earnings call, we gave a revenue projections of around 20%. So now after Q1, we are confident that our growth will be now -- at least full year basis, it will be more than 20%.

items.statement: New Crop Care products Ashitaka and Takai together contributing 18-20% of Q1 sales in first season
items.quote: Happy to share that between Ashitaka and Takai put together in the first year itself or the first season itself right now, they will be contributing close to 18% to 20% of our Q1 sales.

items.statement: Crop Care EBIT margin expected to hold at 26-27% despite diversification into lower-margin in-licensed products
items.quote: I think we believe roughly despite it being a tough year, we believe we can still hold on to roughly around 26%, 27% kind of EBIT margin.

items.statement: Labour Code wage hike impact fully factored in; no additional provisioning expected
items.quote: Yes, we have factored in all the impact of the Labour Code already. So we do not expect any additional impact because of that.

items.statement: Bangladesh JV (ACI Godrej) returned to double-digit volume, revenue and PBT growth in Q1
items.quote: Our Bangladesh joint venture, ACI, Godrej Agrovet, also returned to a strong growth trajectory, delivering double-digit growth in volumes, revenue and PBT, supported by broad-based volume expansion and operating leverage.

items.statement: Oil Palm OER improved to 18.8% in Q1 FY27 vs 18.4% in Q1 FY26 despite adverse weather
items.quote: Our number last year was 18.4% in quarter 1, same quarter. And this year, that number is 18.8%.

items.statement: Synergy target of 10%-15% incremental EBITDA on FY24 proforma base (INR 150-200 crore) to be realized starting FY27
items.quote: We had said that about a year back that we hope to bring in 10%-15% incremental EBITDA on account of synergies, and we still stick to that.

items.statement: Plan to add over 4,170 beds in 3-4 years taking total capacity over 15,000 beds, with 53% brownfield expansion
items.quote: We have a clear roadmap to add over 4,170 beds over the next 3 to 4 years, taking our total capacity over 15,000 beds.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 saw 13% YoY patient volume growth to 2 million patients, blended occupancy up 510 bps to 64%, MVT revenue up 62% YoY
items.quote: We treated over 2 million patients in Q1, up 13% YoY, with blended occupancy expanding 510 bps YoY to 64%. This was supported by 62% YoY growth in Medical Value Travel (MVT) revenue.

items.statement: High-acuity specialties (Oncology, Neurology, Orthopaedics) grew >24% YoY; Robotics volumes up ~80%, Joint replacements up 39%, Transplants up 19% YoY
items.quote: Among CONGO specialties – Orthopaedics, Neurology and Oncology had an accelerated ramp -up during Q1FY27. All of these specialities grew in excess of 24% this quarter.

items.statement: Organic growth framework: 5%-6% volume growth and 7%-8% ARPP growth targeted to achieve 24%-25% EBITDA margin
items.quote: if I were to generate a 24%-25% of EBITDA margin in two to three year's time, we should be able to generate at organic level 5% -6% volume growth and maybe 7% -8% of the ARPP growth.

items.statement: ARPP IP grew 10% YoY driven by case-mix improvement from Centers of Excellence, high-end tertiary care, and robotic cases
items.quote: Growth in ARPP IP was well supported by Case-mix improvement led by the Centres of Excellence and High-end tertiary care including robotic cases.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth of 10-15% YoY expected without EU-GMP; FY28 growth of 30-35% if EU-GMP received and supplies start
items.quote: If we don't, let's say, if EU doesn't come or if you assume EU comes from FY28, we will still have a 10-15% growth in the FY27 year compared to the previous year.

items.statement: EBITDA margins for FY27 expected similar to FY26 if EU-GMP delayed; mid-teens EBITDA margin targeted post EU-GMP with revenue above INR 100 cr/quarter
items.quote: I think we would assume it to be similar to the last year, around that range.

items.statement: EU-GMP certification expected by end of Q3 FY27; revenue from EU supplies expected to start in Q4 FY27
items.quote: I think it will take about two to three months. So, by the end of the year, we should be ready to be in a position to supply to Europe. So maybe Q4, we can see some revenue starting to come in.

items.statement: NIP and OTF portfolio contributed 18% of Q1 FY27 revenue; 8-10 product MAs expected post EU-GMP
items.quote: Our new innovative product portfolio and oral insulin business returned to a normalized level of contribution during the quarter, accounting for approximately 18% of our revenue.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 3.7% impacted by one-time expenses (INR 1.82 cr) and higher employee costs; gross margin 55-58% range expected
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 34 million, translating into an EBITDA margin of 3.7%.

items.statement: Export business resilient at 84% of operating income; Middle East disruption impact seen in Q1 but regularizing
items.quote: Our export business remained resilient despite ongoing geopolitical uncertainties in certain regions, with exports contributing approximately 84% of our total operating income during the quarter.

items.statement: Australia TGA audit completed; CAPA submitted; certification expected in coming months; first product order received, supplies in 2-3 months
items.quote: We have received the final report, and we submitted the CAPA. Now the assessors are reviewing the CAPA. So, we expect the TGA certification also to come through in the coming months.

items.statement: US customers re-engaging after tariff uncertainty; Europe automotive components growing; domestic industrial bearing rings soft but automotive bearing rings strong
items.quote: The US market is coming back with the customers reengaging after a prolonged period of caution. Europe continues to fire on the back of our expanding automotive components presence there

items.statement: Management guides for 10-15% top-line growth across all segments for FY27
items.quote: We're looking at growth of, say, 10% to 15% on top line and it will be across all the segments.

items.statement: Hopeful to achieve double-digit volume growth for FY27 despite current war disruption
items.quote: We're still positive in long term. And we're hopeful that for the year, we can still close out on double-digit growth.

items.statement: Snowman Logistics adding ~24,000 pallets in FY27 with Pune and Patna facilities
items.quote: This year we'll see around 24,000 additional pallets, I mean, by end of this year.

items.statement: Snowman achieved 5-7% average pricing increase in warehousing; further hikes expected on renewals
items.quote: In terms of percentage, I cannot say right away, but in a range between 5% to 7% on an average is what we have got from most of the customers.

items.statement: Gateway passed on 35% Haryana minimum wage hike and fuel cost increases to customers with a time lag; impact more visible in Q2
items.quote: Haryana had an increase by 35% in minimum wages. We've tried to pass it on to customers, but there is a time lag in that also. Fuel also, most of it, we've been able to pass on. So that impact will be more visible in Q2.

items.statement: Double stacking dipped to 39% from 40-42% last year; import-export mix shift pressuring rail margins
items.quote: On double stack, basically, we're at 39%. So, it has dipped a bit from last year where we were at like 40% to 42% depending on the quarter.

items.statement: Ankleshwar ICD estimated to ramp to ~5,000 TEUs/month within 3-4 years; currently zero EXIM volume
items.quote: We also estimate that, say, within 3, 4 years, we should be doing a similar number.

items.statement: DFC JNPT connection complete but cargo shift will take months; Mundra/Pipavav congestion may drive some volume to JNPT
items.quote: Maybe it will take a couple of more months to see the cargo shifting towards JNPT. But now if we look at, after this West Asia crisis, wherein imports dried up in the months of April, May, there has been some improvement on the import side from June, July onwards.

items.statement: Cash tax rate to remain ~18.88% for 7-8 years due to large accumulated MAT credit
items.quote: We will be paying at the rate of 18.88% for at least 7, 8 years. So, we have a large amount of accumulated MAT credit, which we will be utilizing over the next 7, 8 years.

items.statement: CFS business not actively for sale after failed valuation attempt 1.5 years ago; open to deal if right valuation emerges
items.quote: We undertook an exercise, but we didn't get the right valuation. This was about 1.5 years ago. And since then, we've not been actively looking because we reached about a net debt-zero position earlier in the year when we paid out the special dividend.

items.statement: Net VNB margin improved 750 bps YoY to 22.9% in Q1 FY27 driven by mix shift to non-par savings and protection
items.quote: The net VNB margin has improved by 750 basis points on a year-on-year basis from 15.4% for the quarter ended 30 June '25 to 22.9% for the first quarter of the current year.

items.statement: Management expects VNB margin to improve further from Q1 levels and settle around industry average, targeting mid-20s by year-end
items.quote: In terms of VNB margin, we expect the margin to grow something more than where we currently are and settle something around the industry average.

items.statement: Non-par share of individual APE rose to 32.49% in Q1 FY27 from 30.34% YoY; non-par savings grew 59.24% and protection 43.59%
items.quote: Our non-par share of individual APE has grown to 32.49% for the quarter ended 30th June '26 as compared to 30.34% in the same period for the previous year.

items.statement: ULIP premium declined due to market volatility; expected to recover when markets normalize, but non-par growth to continue
items.quote: ULIP premium reduction is naturally a function of the market scenario when confidence in the market gets affected due to the high volatility in the market functioning.

items.statement: Individual new business premium grew 14.48% YoY to Rs 14,351 crore in Q1 FY27; total APE grew 8.22% to Rs 13,692 crore
items.quote: The individual new business premium income for quarter ended 30 June '26 was 14,351 crore rupees as compared to 12,536 crore rupees for the corresponding period last year, thereby registering a growth of 14.48% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Expense ratio increased 16 bps YoY to 10.63% due to loss of input tax credit after GST exemption on individual premiums
items.quote: While the GST has gone on the individual lines and the premium, the nonavailability of input tax credit has had an impact on the overall expense ratio.

items.statement: GST ITC loss impact of -1.9% on VNB margin assumptions expected to normalize after Q2 FY27 as YoY comparison base aligns
items.quote: Once the assumption change has been incorporated, I don't think it should have much of an impact in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: ASM (Available Solvency Margin) funds at book value of Rs 180,000 crore ring-fenced to support solvency and protection growth
items.quote: ASM funds is at 180,000 crores.

items.statement: Solvency ratio at 2.42% pre-dividend (2.32% post-dividend); will support protection growth but final level depends on regulatory changes
items.quote: If you take away the amount of dividend that was paid subsequent to this quarter, it will come down to 2.32%.

items.statement: Government completed 6.5% OFS in LIC, raising public float to 10% and achieving minimum public shareholding compliance
items.quote: Recently, the Government of India has sold 6.5% stake in LIC via an offer-for-sale, which has been well received by the market.

items.statement: Bancassurance new business premium grew 5.25% YoY to Rs 907 crore; bank channel declined 8.6% but alternate channels grew 27.3%
items.quote: Bancassurance and alternate channels, including micro insurance, collected new business premium income of 907.14 crore rupees for the quarter ended 30th June 2026 as compared to 861.92 crore rupees for the quarter ended June 30, 2025, registering a growth of 5.25% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Agent count declined 2.7% YoY to 1.45 million due to weeding out non-serious Bima Sakhi recruits; urban agent focus continues
items.quote: The number of agents reduction has been because of a good number of candidates who have taken up Bima Sakhi without fully understanding the requirement.

items.statement: Minimum sum assured increased from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 2 lakh in Oct 2024, driving higher average ticket size and margins
items.quote: The minimum sum assured has been increased from INR1 lakh to INR2 lakh.

items.statement: Segmental VNB margins: Par 19.4% (37.1% APE), Non-par individual 49.3%, Group 29.4% (45% APE)
items.quote: The proportion of par business, which is 37.1%, which gives a VNB margin of 19.4%. The proportion of non-par individual is INR1,678 crores, which gives a margin of 49.3%. And the group business is the third group, which is 45% on APE, which gives VNB margin of 29.4%.

items.statement: Targets 15%+ top-line growth for FY27 and mid-teens to high-teens growth trajectory
items.quote: we are getting very good response from our organized retailers seeing good growth and maintaining 15% plus growth overall this year. That's what overall target is.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin target of 13%-13.5% including PLI benefit
items.quote: So, from full year lens, we're targeting close to between 13%-13.5% margin. That's the target we are taking.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin aspiration of 15% over next 3 years
items.quote: 15% margin target is not for this year. It's long-term target that we want to be at 15% next 3 Years. That's a plan.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at ~13.5% vs 12.2% in Q4 FY26, up ~130 bps QoQ
items.quote: From EBITDA lens, this quarter, our EBITDA was close to 13.5% versus last quarter, our EBITDA was close to 12.2%. So there was good increase in EBITDA margin compared to last quarter.

items.statement: Two price hikes taken in last 4 months (April MRP increase + one more); no further hikes planned until after Diwali
items.quote: we have taken 2 price rise in the last 4 months and we are trying to maintain and trying to passing on the price to the consumer. We have taken one MRP increase in April, but, till now, we're not taking any MRP increase. And what we see that till Diwali, we will maintain this price what we're doing

items.statement: Quick commerce channel growing 100%+ YoY in Q1; growing in line with or faster than category on platform
items.quote: Our growth, if we look at in Quarter 1, is upwards of 100% in the q-com channel. Second thing, what you spoke about on the private label of their own brands. So this, any of the format, be it modern trade or q-com, where, you feel that the consumer or shopper footfalls are high, they tend to launch their own brands.

items.statement: PLI benefit of ~INR 50 Cr (150 bps EBITDA) ends this year; will take 1.5-2 years to offset via pricing/gross margin improvement
items.quote: from PLI lens, currently this year it should be contributing close to 150 basis points in overall EBITDA. So, what we're targeting, it will take it 50 to 75, based on improvement will take in pricing and gross margin. That's about it. It will take 1.5 to 2 Years to reach again at the original margin.

items.statement: Nepal JV plant construction underway; INR 15 Cr each partner; production start expected in 8-9 months
items.quote: from Nepal lens, we've done JV and within all the paperwork. Now, the plant construction is getting ready. So, both parties invest close to INR15 Crores each and by, I think in next 8 to 9 months, the plant will get started

items.statement: Maintain full-year FY27 revenue growth guidance of 75% YoY and consolidated EBITDA margin of 20-22%
items.quote: And we maintain that revenue guidance of 75% growth over the previous year and an EBITDA margin of 20% to 22% on a consol basis is what we maintain our guidance for the full year basis.

items.statement: Equipment supply share in third-party order book increased to ~59% as of July 2026
items.quote: As of July '26, the share of equipment supply in our order book stood at approximately 59% with the balance 41% being turnkey.

items.statement: Signed 1.5 GW MOU with INOX Clean Energy in June 2026; 500 MW firm orders signed, balance 1 GW to follow
items.quote: We are pleased to inform you that INOX Wind has signed an MOU for 1.5 gigawatt. I'll repeat again, 1.5 gigawatt with INOX Clean Energy in June, out of which firm orders have been signed for 500 megawatts so far.

items.statement: Received 200 MW LOA from NLC India in July 2026 via tender process
items.quote: In another positive development in the first quarter, we have received an LOA for 200 megawatt from NLC India. This is a repeat order from NLC in the month of July through an extensive tendering process.

items.statement: 4X wind turbine prototype installation on track for August 2026; commercial launch expected by end of FY26
items.quote: We are on track to install the first prototype in the month of August with commercial launch expected by end of FY26.

items.statement: INOX Green maintains 50% EBITDA margin guidance for wind O&M portfolio
items.quote: Generally, our guidance on the O&M business of Wind portfolio stands at 50% EBITDA margin. and that has been guidance.

items.statement: INOX Green maintains INR 600 crore annual EBITDA guidance for FY27 on consolidated basis post Wind World acquisition
items.quote: I think beyond whatever is there in the public domain or what we have guided for INR600 crores, we are sticking to that during the -- we are in the silent period.

items.statement: Expect 8-10 GW annual wind capacity additions in India over next few years driven by RTC, FDRE, hybrid tenders
items.quote: We expect to see strong annual wind capacity additions ranging between 8 to 10 gigawatt over the next few years, driven by RTC, FDRE and hybrid capacity additions.

items.statement: Only force majeure events (e.g., Middle East crisis) seen as risk to meeting 75% revenue guidance; equipment supply pivot reduces execution risk
items.quote: And I would say only force majeure, things which are beyond our control. I mean no one had an inkling about this Middle East crisis. So something like that. Otherwise, this pivot to move to equipment supply, honestly, we don't see a risk of not meeting our deliverables.

items.statement: Wind World India acquisition approved by NCLT Ahmedabad; formalities to complete in Q2 FY27, financial consolidation thereafter
items.quote: We have received the approval from honorable NCLT, Ahmedabad for the acquisition of Wind World India Limited. The acquisitions formalities are expected to be completed in Q2 FY27, post which the financial consolidation will take place.

items.statement: Demerger of power evacuation infrastructure from INOX Green to IRSL completed August 1, 2026; IRSL to be listed post regulatory approvals
items.quote: Further, the demerger of the power evacuation infrastructure business from INOX Green into INOX Renewable Solution has been completed as on August 1, 2026, being the record date. IRSL would now be automatically listed on the stock exchange post receipt of regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Targeting near 100% indigenization of wind turbine components by end of calendar year 2026 for both 3X and 4X models
items.quote: Before end of the calendar year, we would be -- we hope that we are almost 100% on wind turbines. And I'm talking not only for our 3X model, but even for the 4X model.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected a few percentage points above FY26's 21% YoY growth
items.quote: FY27 will see a top line increase, which is a few percentage points better than that.

items.statement: FY27 EBITDA margin expected to remain comfortably above 20%
items.quote: We are going to deliver FY27 also very comfortably over the 20% plus margin.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue expected in line with Q1 FY27
items.quote: Q2 looks very robust, and I think Q2 should be in line with Q1.

items.statement: Second half FY27 expected to be better than first half due to ag recovery
items.quote: Given that the ag industry recovery is going to happen in the second half, I think that's a fairly obvious and a fairly visible outcome.

items.statement: Capex requirement for organic business is 2.5%-3.5% of revenue
items.quote: Our capex requirements as a business are roughly about 2.5% to 3.5% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Warehouse sales at 56% in Q1 FY27 vs 50-52% in Q1 FY26, driving higher EBITDA margin
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, our warehousing sales was roughly at about 56%. And in Q1 FY26, I think it was roughly about 50% to 52%.

items.statement: Large ag at cyclical bottom in CY2026 with 15-16% decline, recovery expected CY2027/FY28
items.quote: In calendar year '26, it's expected to degrow by about 15%, 16%. So this is the trough and then the recovery will begin.

items.statement: Small ag recovery starting, meaningful volume recovery expected CY2027
items.quote: After 3 consecutive years of volume decline, we are beginning to see some recovery in unit volumes and the direction of growth is encouraging.

items.statement: Targets 20-25% revenue CAGR over next five years
items.quote: Our confidence is in the underlying growth opportunity remaining strong, and we continue to target a 20-25% revenue growth CAGR over the next five years.

items.statement: Guides FY27 revenue growth around 25% YoY with volume growth of 10-12%
items.quote: Our revenue growth will be around 25%. That's what is we expect.

items.statement: Guides FY27 EBITDA at INR 7-8 per SCM for next three quarters
items.quote: In FY27, in the next three quarters, we expect EBITDA to be in the line of INR 7-8 per SCM, operating EBITDA.

items.statement: Expects FY27 volume to reach 250 MMSCM, up from 224 MMSCM in FY26
items.quote: Last year, we clocked 224 MMSCM. We expect that it will be in the range of 250 MMSCM by this year end.

items.statement: Incurred INR 67 crore capex in Q1 FY27, cumulative capex ~INR 1,090 crore
items.quote: We have incurred CapEx of approximately INR 67 crore in three months quarter in FY27 this year, given FY27 this year, taking our cumulative CapEx to around INR 1,090 crore in that range.

items.statement: TNSTC committed 200+ buses for CNG conversion in Namakkal-Trichy, 80 already operational
items.quote: They are going to assure us more than 200 buses in near future.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 19%, PAT margin 10.5%, driven by favorable pricing and sourcing
items.quote: EBITDA, excluding other income, increased sharply to INR 62 crore, reflecting a growth of 139% YoY, with EBITDA margin expanding to 19% of profit after tax, which stood at INR 34 crore, which is up 140% YoY, with PAT margin improving to 10.5%.

items.statement: CNG volumes grew 22% YoY, commercial CNG up 75% YoY; CNG now 67% of total volume
items.quote: This was primarily driven by CNG volume that grew around 22% YoY and strong momentum on CNG commercial volume, which grew 75% YoY. This all has contributed 67% of the total volume during the quarter.

items.statement: Utilized INR 337 crore (68%) of INR 496 crore IPO net proceeds as of 30 June 2026; balance for Namakkal-Trichy CGD network
items.quote: We have utilized almost INR 337 crores out of the total net proceeds of INR 496 crores as on 30th June, 2026. This nearly represents 68% utilization. The balance amount is primarily a mark for the development of City Gas Distribution Network at Namakkal and Trichy GA.

items.statement: Revised AUM growth guidance to 20% for FY27 from previous guidance
items.quote: We have revised our guidance to 20%. We feel that with the momentum that we have in the quarter 1 and looking at the festive season approaching us and the way the liquidity is available to us and the demand that is there at the ground, we definitely feel that 20% is a growth that we can easily achieve.

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY27 at 12.3%-12.5%, confident of achieving upper end
items.quote: Our NIM guidance is around 12.5% on the upper spectrum and lower spectrum 12.3%. So we definitely believe that NIM will expand both on the side of the yield also as more and more of good portfolio becomes a part of the larger pool and the yield on the portfolio improves and collection also from the NPA improves.

items.statement: ROA guidance for FY27 at 3.3% upper spectrum, ROE at 18% upper spectrum
items.quote: ROA, we have guided for around 3.3% on the upper spectrum, and ROE of around 18% on the upper spectrum.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance revised lower, currently at 2.6% vs guided 2.7%-3.5% range
items.quote: We have given the guidance of around 2.7% to 3.5%. We are already below the lower spectrum of around 2.7%. We are already at 2.6% for the first quarter. And definitely, going forward, it will be improving in the coming quarters, so we have revised the guidance in terms of our credit cost.

items.statement: Targeting single-digit cost of funds by end of FY27, currently at 10.13%
items.quote: We feel that in the financial year, we should be able to come into single digits in terms of our cost of fund and availability of fund is already there.

items.statement: Branch network expansion planned to 1,740-1,750 branches in FY27 from current 1,670
items.quote: So we will be in the range of 1,750 to 1,740 branches. We are right now around 1,670 branches.

items.statement: Cost of funds reduced 14 bps to 10.13% in Q1 FY27, incremental borrowing cost at 9.8%
items.quote: In the quarter, we have reduced our cost of fund from 10.27% to 10.13%, 14 basis point reduction has already happened in the Q1 itself. And this is before the benefit of the rating upgrade.

items.statement: NIM expanded 50 bps YoY to 12% in Q1 FY27, further expansion expected in Q2
items.quote: Already, if you look at from a NIM perspective, as compared to the last financial year, the NIMs have improved. Last financial year, if you look at quarter 4 or the full year, we are flat. But if you look at from a quarter 1 perspective, there is a 50 bps of expansion already has happened.

items.statement: JLG lending rate increased from 23.5% to 24.85% at end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: On the price hike, we had increased the rate at the end of the quarter, so we had increased the rate by around from 23.5% to 24.85%.

items.statement: AUM mix at 76% JLG, 24% non-JLG; targeting 70-30 by FY27 end, long-term 55-45
items.quote: We had guided for this year at 75-25. We are already at 76-24. So this year, we will be around 70-30. And coming year, definitely, we will look at strategically where we want to be. But in a long-term scenario, AUM basis 50-45 but balance sheet basis, 60-40 will be there.

items.statement: Gold loan co-lending scaling at INR 100 crores/month, targeting INR 1,200 crores disbursement and INR 500 crores portfolio
items.quote: Our aim is to have around INR1,200 crores of disbursement and around INR500 crores of gold portfolio. We are likely to overachieve this number for sure.

items.statement: Assam flood exposure limited to lower Assam, natural calamity insurance covers all customers
items.quote: In Assam, the flood or this kind of a water problem is kind of an annual phenomenon, so one is that this is in upper Assam, we have no exposure to that state. We are at lower Assam, so our portfolio is not affected as of now entirely. And second aspect is we take natural calamity insurance for all our customers, so tha

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA breakeven expected in Q2 or Q3 FY27; Tritium EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27
items.quote: on a consolidated basis, the breakeven may be over the next 2 quarters itself. I can't specify whether quarter 2 or 3. But on a consolidated basis, it will be breakeven in quarter 2 and on Tritium level by quarter 4, '27.

items.statement: Tritium targets 3x revenue growth vs last year and EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27
items.quote: I'm sure that we will have 3x revenue growth compared to last year as well as EBITDA breakeven in quarter 4, '27.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at INR1,400+ crores as of 30 June 2026, a record high
items.quote: a consolidated book order of INR1,400 crores plus as on 30 of June, a record high sales and Tritium also looking up in terms of increased booking.

items.statement: EV charger order book near INR200 crores in India plus USD2 million exports; 180 DC chargers booked until Oct 2026
items.quote: today, we have an order book of almost INR200 crores for our AC/DC chargers in India, including exports of about USD2 million.

items.statement: Tritium bookings doubled to ~USD21 million in Q1 FY27 vs ~USD10 million prior quarters; revenue ~USD10.5 million
items.quote: the bookings are close to USD21 million this quarter, and you can see this is twice as big as the quarters before and the sales is roughly USD10.5 million.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin 29.1% in Q1 FY27, up 2% QoQ on better pricing and mix; down 3.6% YoY due to US input cost pressure
items.quote: Stand-alone gross margins for Q1 stood at 29.1%, which is 2% above the previous quarter, which is Q4 of last year on better pricing and customer mix in both the segments. On a year-on-year basis, gross margin was down by about 3.6%, primarily on account of the U.S.-led input cost pressure

items.statement: Large DC power system order margins offset by forex and commodity price rises; large volumes helped absorb some cost increases
items.quote: Some of these large orders, the margins were offset by a rise in forex and commodity prices. But due to large volumes, we were able to offset some of these cost increases.

items.statement: Supply chain disruptions in semiconductors, plastics, copper due to geopolitics impacting material availability and capacity utilization
items.quote: Some of the challenges today is not capacity, it's supply chain disruption. The geopolitical situation has caused supply chain disruption in semiconductors, anything plastic related, anything copper related has become very expensive.

items.statement: Tritium US factory capacity can service ~USD100 million revenue (2.5x current USD10 million quarterly run rate)
items.quote: I think the capacity there can service 2.5x of this revenue. So roughly, let's say, USD100 million, slightly more maybe. And we are doing 1/4 of that today.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of low to mid-teens for FY27 with 70-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion
items.quote: I would like to reiterate my confidence in Emcure to deliver low to mid -teen revenue growth in FY27. As I have said, we expect to see positive movement quarter after quarter, and as we discussed in the past we are committed to give 70 to 100 basis points of EBITDA margin expansion.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved 50 bps to 19.7% driven by operating leverage and cost control
items.quote: As far as EBITDA is concerned, it has grown by 25.8%, to INR 508 crore. Margin has improved to 19.7%, an expansion of 50 basis points reflecting productivity gains and operating leverage in this quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin guidance for FY27 revised to ~59% due to stronger international mix, down from earlier 60-61% target
items.quote: I think '27 will probably be around the 59%.

items.statement: India domestic business grew 10.2% YoY to INR 1,095 crore, returning to double-digit growth; expects acceleration from Q2 and faster than industry in H2
items.quote: On a year -on-year basis, it has grown by 10.2% to INR 1,095 crore, returning to double -digit growth compared with Q1 of previous year.

items.statement: International business grew 34.2% YoY to INR 1,485 crore; ROW up 44.8% driven by ARV, Europe up 32.8%, Canada up 24.6%
items.quote: The international business delivered very strong and robust growth during the quarter with revenue of INR 1,485 crore, a growth of 34.2%.

items.statement: ARV contributes ~2/3 of ROW revenue in Q1; full year expected at 50-55% ARV / 45-50% non-ARV
items.quote: So, about 2/3 of the business in ROW will be ARV in this quarter. But for the full year, we do expect we end up at about that 50%- 55% range.

items.statement: Net debt to increase by INR 450-500 crore in Q2 FY27 due to Mantra and Gennova minority stake payouts completed in July
items.quote: We have made these payments for acquisition of Mantra and also the Gennova minority stake. So that will take us by debt by close to around INR 450 crore to INR 500 crore.

items.statement: Acquired 12.05% minority stake in Gennova, making it 100% owned subsidiary; Samit Mehta appointed COO and CEO of Gennova
items.quote: The third important thing that has happened is we have just recently acquired 12.05% minority stake in Gennova, making it a 100% owned subsidiary of Emcure.

items.statement: R&D spend expected at 4-5% of revenue for full year FY27, up from 3.5% in Q1
items.quote: R&D, I for the full year will be between that 4% to 5% range. So, I think we continue to maintain that outlook.

items.statement: Domestic organic growth (ex-in-licensed) was 6-7% in Q1; price growth 4-5%, new launches 1-2%, rest volume; expects in-line with industry in Q2, faster in H2
items.quote: I think if I strip out the Sanofi OAD and the Roche, we'll probably be about 6%, 7% growth in the quarter.

items.statement: Liposomal Amphotericin B introduced in all European countries; order book across countries expected to ramp up with supplies
items.quote: It's pretty much in all the countries and there also, we are ramping up supplies. So , the order book across the different countries should also go up in line with the supplies.

items.statement: Net debt expected to reach ~INR 1,450 crore by end of Q2 FY27 from INR 1,103 crore in Q1; targets net cash by end of FY28
items.quote: by the end of next quarter, we should have a net debt of close to around INR 1,450 crore. From what today, I see at INR 1,560 crore.

items.statement: Gross margin decline driven by geography/product mix (higher exports, B2B model); procurement/COGS improvements ongoing but limited leverage
items.quote: I think broadly, it is due to the geography mix. We obviously continue to look for ways and means to improve some of the activities around procurement or COGS improvements. So that should continue as an ongoing basis.

items.statement: Reaffirmed mid-term revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and EBITDA margin range of 28-30% over a 3-5 year horizon
items.quote: We remain confident in our ability to sustain our longer-term revenue growth guidance of 15% to 20%, and the EBITDA range of 28% to 30%.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance maintained at INR 1,100-1,300 crores; FY28 guidance not yet provided
items.quote: So, we have given a FY27 capex guidance of INR1,100 crores to INR1,300 crores. That still stands. We haven't provided a guidance on fiscal '28.

items.statement: Peptide manufacturing facility at greenfield site near Hyderabad expected operational in 2028; total peptide spend by end of 2028 estimated < INR 300 crores
items.quote: Dhaval, it's probably going to be less than INR300 crores.

items.statement: 33 active commercial molecules and 14 in late phase; 6 late-phase molecules added in last 15 months, 5 from large pharma FTE engagements
items.quote: the underlying health of the CMC business continues to be strong with 33 active commercial molecules and 14 molecules in late phase

items.statement: Strong demand for integrated CRDMO services; seeing acceleration in scale and scope of big pharma relationships; 90%+ revenue from returning customers in FY25/FY26
items.quote: returning customers accounted for over 90% of our revenue in FY25 and FY26. We believe this is a strong reflection of customer satisfaction and the value we are creating for customers over the course of their programs.

items.statement: Expanding into peptides (GLP-1s, macrocyclic, PDCs, radiochemistry), XDCs (ADCs, PROTACs, oligonucleotides), and formulation (oral solids up to Phase 2); peptide commercial facility targeted 2028
items.quote: We are also expanding the scope of our peptides center of excellence support to both discovery and development teams with ability to deliver pilot quantities for clinical trials. In addition, we plan to break ground for a peptide manufacturing facility at our new greenfield site near Hyderabad, which is expected to be

items.statement: Formulation capabilities for oral solids up to Phase 2 expected operationally ready in ~6 months (within FY27); driven by China+1 strategy of pharma partners
items.quote: As of now, we're building small molecules, primarily oral solids of different forms up to phase 1 and phase 2. We have significant interest from multiple of our large pharma partners already who are working with on the chemistry side to be able to support them on their early clinical formulation.

items.statement: Business inherently lumpy quarter-to-quarter; management emphasizes viewing performance over 3-5 year horizon rather than quarterly fluctuations
items.quote: Given the inherent lumpiness in the industry and the way the business operates, we believe it is more appropriate to look at the direction of the business over a three-to-five-year period.

items.statement: Secured EcoVadis Platinum rating 2026, placing company in top 1% globally for sustainability performance
items.quote: I am also pleased to report that we secured the prestigious EcoVadis Platinum rating 2026, placing us among the top 1% of the companies assessed worldwide for sustainability performance.

items.statement: Boston and Manchester offshore facilities accretive and strategic; Boston discovery revenue growing at 30-35% CAGR over last 4-5 years; both act as feeders for India operations
items.quote: if you look at the discovery revenue it is probably in the last four, five years has grown at a CAGR of close around 30%-35%.

items.statement: Maintain FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20% year-on-year
items.quote: We maintain our guidance of 20% revenue growth for this year.

items.statement: Maintain FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of around 11% plus
items.quote: Accordingly, we remain committed to deliver healthy and sustainable profitability and maintain our EBITDA guidance of around 11% plus.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book at INR16,035 crores including L1 orders of INR400 crores as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: As of June 30th, 2026, our unexecuted order book was INR16,035 crores, including L1 orders of INR400 crores.

items.statement: Quoted tenders worth over INR20,000 crores expected to be declared in Q2 and Q3 FY27
items.quote: It is also noteworthy to note that we have quoted tenders worth more than INR20,000 crores, which will be declared in the coming quarter, that is Q2 and maybe part of Q3.

items.statement: Order intake guidance maintained at INR10,000+ crores for FY27
items.quote: And our overall order intake guidance remains the same. We will look at INR10,000 plus crores of new orders this year.

items.statement: Conductor brownfield expansion at existing plant expected to start in Q2 FY27 after approvals
items.quote: There are certain approvals required from the various approving authorities, and we are confident in Q2, we will start this.

items.statement: INR200 crores capex plan for tools and plants, 70% to be utilized in FY27 and balance in FY28
items.quote: So, this INR200 crores is predominantly for tools and plants to execute our projects, both in domestic and international, and it is going to be used in a staggered manner quarter-on-quarter. So, I would say 70-odd percent would be utilized this year and the balance will go to next year.

items.statement: Board approved proposal to raise up to INR600 crores via QIP or other eligible securities subject to approvals
items.quote: Further, subsequent to the quarter, Board has approved a proposal to raise up to INR600 crores through a qualified institutional placement, QIP, or other eligible securities, subject to the necessary shareholders and regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 11.7%, above the 11% guidance
items.quote: EBITDA stood at INR203 crores, resulting in a healthy EBITDA margin of 11.7%, which is more than the guidance of 11% given at the start of the year.

items.statement: Global electricity demand expected to nearly double by 2050; India plans 191,000 circuit km transmission addition by 2032
items.quote: Global electricity demand is expected nearly double by 2050, driven by electrification, renewable energy adoption, AI, data centers, and rising energy consumption.

items.statement: Acquired Gactel turnkey projects to add IDCT cooling tower solutions to existing NDCT offering
items.quote: With this acquisition, we expanded our offering in NDCT towers to include IDCT tower solutions, enabling us to serve wider range of customer requirements.

items.statement: Bangladesh order book nearly complete with only INR300 crores remaining to be executed in next 3 months
items.quote: Out of INR4,500 crores, only INR300 crores is left, which we will complete in the next 3 months.

items.statement: INR80 crores loan to related party Burberry to be repaid by September 2026 with interest
items.quote: It is INR80 crores loan, and it will be repaid before September 2026. That is the agreement.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR3,500-4,000 crores by FY30 reiterated
items.quote: Our objective remains unchanged: to build a stronger and more diversified and more profitable business while creating value for all stakeholders. We remain confident in our long-term growth roadmap and our aspiration of achieving revenue of INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores by FY'30.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth expected up to 10% YoY if situation stabilizes
items.quote: We believe that in terms of top line, we will do quite well and we will be back on track and we will be able to deliver a growth year-on-year in the range of maybe up to 10%.

items.statement: Full-year FY27 EBITDA margin improvement of ~50 bps targeted if price recovery succeeds
items.quote: If we do that, we will be able to for sure increase our overall EBITDA versus last year, probably by half a point, I would say it's something realistic but we will try for sure to do more than that.

items.statement: Domestic agriculture revenue grew 32% YoY in Q1 FY27; construction domestic grew 20% YoY
items.quote: In agri business there is 32% growth, Q1 versus Q1. On the construction business domestic, there is a 20% growth.

items.statement: Export volumes expected to normalize from Q2 FY27 after one-off logistics disruption in Q1
items.quote: Probably already from Q2, you will see that in terms of volumes we will be more or less back on track. This is kind of a one-off dip for this quarter.

items.statement: New paint shop construction started; portal axle and sub-assembly capacity commissioned; capacity expansion aligned to INR3,500-4,000 crore FY30 target
items.quote: Construction of our new paint shop facility commenced during the quarter, while additional investments in portal axle capacity and sub-assembly operations were successfully commissioned. These initiatives are aligned with long-term growth plans.

items.statement: Order book encouraging; capacity debottlenecking and expansion underway to meet demand
items.quote: We are seeing order book which is quite encouraging for us. So, for the capacity to meet the market demand, we are doing the debottlenecking and expansion of wherever we need capacities to meet the market demand in the direction towards INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: Engineering services assignments worth INR33 million completed in July 2026; discussions with another customer progressing
items.quote: Assignments worth approximately INR33 million that were under execution at quarter-end were completed in July 2026. Discussions with another prospective customer are also progressing, supporting further growth in this business.

items.statement: Export revenue split Q1 FY27: construction INR871M, agriculture INR424M, other INR357M
items.quote: Construction equipment in Q1 FY'27 was INR871 million and agriculture was INR424 million, and our other category was INR357 million.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin expected to increase 4-5% from solar plant commissioning in Q4 FY27
items.quote: with our capex of about INR60 crores with a 3-year payback, I think that itself will increase the margin to maybe translate into 4% to 5% increase in my view

items.statement: Invested INR60 crores in captive solar plant with battery storage for Pune hotels targeting Q4 FY27 commissioning
items.quote: We have now invested around INR60 crores in captive solar plant with battery storage for our Pune hotels targeting commissioning in Q4 FY27

items.statement: India EBITDA margin expanded to 36% from 35% YoY despite higher power and wage costs
items.quote: India EBITDA grew 16% to INR74 crores. And most importantly, our India margin expanded 36% from 35% even after absorbing higher power and wage costs during this quarter

items.statement: India RevPAR grew 20% YoY driven by 7% occupancy increase to 67% and 8% ADR growth in seasonally soft quarter
items.quote: Our occupancy grew to 67%, up about 7% is reflecting very, very strong demand both in Pune, Bengaluru, and Goa. Most importantly, the important point is we added occupancy and rate at the same time

items.statement: Maldives July tourist arrivals recovered to 2025 levels with only 27 disrupted flights vs 170+ previously
items.quote: July tourist arrivals have actually recovered to 2025 levels. And this is with only 27 disrupted flights. This indicates that travel disruption seems to be easing

items.statement: Maldives diesel prices reached 2.1x pre-war levels, driving INR19 crores fuel cost increase in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Diesel prices reached roughly 2.1x pre-war levels, driving a fuel and ancillary costs increase of around INR19 crores

items.statement: Raaya resort targeting 80% solar with battery backup by April 2027, saving $1.5M annually (2.5% of Maldives EBITDA)
items.quote: Raaya will be moving to about 80% of solar by April 2027. So, 1.2 megawatts will go up to almost 5 megawatts with additional capacity also in Conrad and Anantara. This will in absolute number, if I had to answer your question, will be about USD1.5 million saving every year

items.statement: Acquired Sahyadri Hills Ritz-Carlton Reserve (80 keys + 33 branded residences) for INR281 crores equity, targeting >12% yield-on-cost
items.quote: We have acquired it 100% at an equity consideration of around INR281 crores and enterprise value of around INR466 crores, targeting a yield-on-cost above 12%

items.statement: Maldives INR15 crores EBITDA impact from diesel spike expected to be offset in Q3 and Q4 peak seasons
items.quote: The INR15 crores impact will be negated in Q3 and Q4. And Raaya also has performed as per what we expected

items.statement: Sri Lanka Ritz-Carlton Reserve delayed to ~FY30 due to environmental permissions for 1.5km shoreline near Yala National Park
items.quote: What we are stuck right now is little bit on the front of permissions, because there's environmental sensitivity since we have about 1.5 Acres (correction: 1.5 kilometers) of shoreline, and one side is the Yala National Park. I think we are just on the verge of getting the completions and all the formalities past us. O

items.statement: Annuity business EBITDA flat at INR111 crores with 87% margin and 98% committed occupancy
items.quote: Our annuity business remains steadily high margin backbone of the group. Revenue grew 3% to INR128 crores, with EBITDA broadly flat at INR111 crores at 87% margin and committed occupancy holding at 98%

items.statement: Pune occupancy expected to stabilize in high 70s with 45M sq ft office space addition by 2030 driving 200-300 luxury room nights daily
items.quote: what we have in data is around 45 million square feet will be added in Pune by 2030, so this will feed into our hotel room nights to the existing 95 million square feet current office stock. So, in my view, this base scenario, we expect to add about 200 to 300 luxury and upper-upscale room nights on a daily basis, whic

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to normalize to 25-30% range in Q2-Q3 FY27 as raw material prices stabilize and price hikes flow through
items.quote: we expect EBITDA margins to gradually recover, and we are working towards stabilizing them in the 25% to 30% range during Q2 and Q3 of FY27.

items.statement: Industrial & fine chemicals vertical at Apiqo fully booked, expected to contribute Rs 120-150 crore of FY27 revenue
items.quote: Somewhere around 150 CR. Between 120 to 150.

items.statement: Anlon Biologics (peptides/biosimilars) construction to start within 2 months, revenue expected FY28 Q4; Anlon Medicare (surgical implants) revenue expected FY28 Q2
items.quote: by FY28 Q4 we'll start to generate the revenue and in Anlon Medicare at least by Q2 of FY28 we will start to generate the revenue.

items.statement: Plan to make Apiqo and Bizotic 100% subsidiaries via share swap by end of Q2 FY27
items.quote: we have already started to do the 100 making its 100% wholly own subsidiary by the way of share swapping. So that process is already going on. So, I think by end of the Q2 we'll complete it.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at Rs 3,200-3,400 crore; management confident of achieving target
items.quote: I strongly believe that we are on the right track to achieve the revenue guidance we have given in a range of Rs. 3,200 to 3,400 crore. I believe that we are absolutely on track and there are no concerns with respect to the business outlook as well as the execution capabilities.

items.statement: Executable order book stands at Rs 10,803 crore (Energy Rs 8,453 crore, Telecom Rs 2,350 crore) as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: As of 30th June, we have executable order book of Rs. 8,453 crore in energy and Rs. 2,350 crore in telecom ICT. Combined, our total executable order book at Rs. 10,803 crore.

items.statement: Energy:Telecom revenue mix expected to shift to 65:35 or 70:30 by FY27 end from current 80:20
items.quote: We estimate that this ratio should be between somewhere in the range of 65 :35 or 70: 30 when we close the financial year between energy and telecom.

items.statement: PAT margin guidance 10.5-11% for FY27; EPC margin 12-15%, BOO SPV IRR 12-13%, C&I BESS EBITDA margin 4-5% higher than grid-scale (13-15%)
items.quote: PAT margins we are trying to have about 10.5% to 11% for the mix of products and the projects.

items.statement: Strong BESS demand outlook; bidding for ~27 GWh tenders; NTPC Renewable Energy floated large tenders; C&I segment showing traction with thousands of units potential annually
items.quote: We also have the strong order pipeline and we are bidding for almost 27 GWh of tenders. Recently one or two customers, –such as NTPC Renewable Energy have floated big tenders, so we are hoping to get some good business out of that as well.

items.statement: BESS capacity expansion from 5 to 10 GWh by December 2026; third line (5 GWh) equipment arriving September 2026, installation Oct-Nov 2026
items.quote: Hopefully, by beginning of December, we would have 10 GWh operational facility, which would be the biggest operational plant in India by that time.

items.statement: Container manufacturing facility trial runs ongoing; batch production from next month; supplied 300+ containers; Q2 target 210 containers; 10 GWh = ~1,800 containers/year at 90% efficiency
items.quote: Basically, with 10 GWh our total production capacity will be 2,000 containers per year at a full efficiency. However, we always have to take some efficiency factor in terms of machine downtime and such other factors. Even if I take 90% efficiency, it will be about 1,800 containers in a year.

items.statement: Competitive intensity correcting: Maharashtra 4 GWh project cancelled, Punjab tender at better prices, NTPC tenders seeing 7-8 bidders vs 32-51 previously; only serious players remain
items.quote: There is a bit of correction in the bidding side. In the last six months till March, many people had bid aggressively. Though they are not from the energy sector or do not have background in this area.

items.statement: R&D center in Pune inaugurated 3 weeks ago led by Prof. Ogale with 8 PhD scientists; planning indigenous cell manufacturing in ~2 years; applied for 4 GWh PLI scheme (7-year duration)
items.quote: We have started a research center in Pune. It was inaugurated about three weeks ago and is led by Professor Ogale, who is also our Independent Director. A team of about eight experienced PhD holders scientists have joined the center.

items.statement: MEGMEET partnership for AI data center power solutions (Nvidia-approved) coupled with BESS; demo equipment preparation underway; concrete revenue plan expected next quarter
items.quote: We have tied up with them for providing those power solutions, coupled with our battery storage for all the new-age AI data centers in India. We already have started the work on the ground and there is a good amount of traction coming from the potential customers for these kinds of products.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia MOU signed; small container order executed in Q1; expecting export revenue ramp-up in subsequent quarters
items.quote: We have signed a MOU with a company in Saudi Arabia and we are also trying to explore the market in Saudi Arabia for the battery storage systems. We are actively exploring this opportunity and we expect this year we should have some portion of the revenue coming from the exports.

items.statement: Capex funded internally from private placement proceeds; seeking investors for BOO portfolio-level funding to accelerate developer projects
items.quote: Funded internally from our private say initial fundraising that we have done in terms of the private placement. We have funded using that amount.

items.statement: Operating cash flow negative due to telecom receivables (150 days NWC) vs energy (90-100 days); expect positive operating cash flow by March 2027 as energy contribution grows and telecom receivables ease
items.quote: By end of this financial year, we can expect that the cash flow from operation to significantly improve compared to the last financial year.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY27 is INR350-450 crore, indicative and subject to demand monitoring
items.quote: we are targeting to spend approx INR350 crores to INR450 crores for FY '27, which will support our double-digit top-line growth. Having said that, please be mindful that we are closely monitoring the economic environment across our key markets, and may pull in or pull-out capex based on the actual demand requirement.

items.statement: New ART plant in western India with ~INR70 crore investment announced due to >90% capacity utilization
items.quote: we've already announced one new plant for Advanced Ride Technologies, that should be in the western part of the country, with an investment of INR70 crores approximately.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 17.9% on VAR in Q1 FY27, down ~170bps YoY due to public company costs and non-indexed commodity inflation; partial recovery achieved
items.quote: EBITDA margins stood at 17.9% of VAR. While margins were impacted by significant commodity inflation, rupee depreciation, geopolitical supply chain disruptions, and incremental costs associated with operating as a listed public company, we were able to sustain strong profitability through disciplined execution, product

items.statement: Demand outlook positive through Q2 FY27; Indian OEMs predicting good demand; Middle East war a risk if deteriorates further
items.quote: the good news is where other regions in the world are struggling, India is still Indian OEMs are still predicting very good demand. Now, if the Middle East war continues on and on, there will be some impact, I think. I don't think it'll—the demand will keep continuing, but right now, it looks like through Q2 at least,

items.statement: DCx32 launched targeting A/B segment vehicles; DaVinci platform winning multiple programs across existing and 4 new customers; semi-active suspension in EVs
items.quote: we introduced DCx32, the latest addition to the DCx family, specifically targeting smaller A and B segment vehicles and significantly expanding our addressable market opportunity.

items.statement: Key risks: Middle East war driving non-indexed commodity inflation, US Section 232 tariffs on exhaust exports, Europe/US macro slowdown, Hyundai supply disruption (no impact)
items.quote: Yes, tariffs is a problem. The Trump administration levied additional tariffs on Section 232, which is the some of the exhaust parts that get exported from here. That affects other suppliers as well. So, it is a little bit of a downer, which makes the environment a bit tough for exports. But let's see, that's the situa

items.statement: Exports ~7% of revenue (70% intra-Tenneco, 30% third-party); export margins in line or better than domestic; royalty 2.5% of revenue net of intercompany sales
items.quote: in terms of the current quarter, our exports are slightly over 7% of the overall revenue.

items.statement: CAPT capacity utilization >80%; ART >90% driving new plant investment; cash conversion 50-60% of EBITDA; debt-free, capex funded internally
items.quote: for CAPT, it is upward of 80%. However, Advanced Ride Technologies, we are really working more than 90% of the capacity currently. And that's one of the reasons we've already announced one new plant for Advanced Ride Technologies

items.statement: Clean Air growth 9.6% YoY vs served market ~8-10% (ex-EV, ex-major Japanese OEM); market share gains in CV (58%) and off-highway (68%)
items.quote: Clean Air and Powertrain Solutions delivered VAR of INR6,626 million, representing growth of 9.6% year-on-year.

items.statement: Spark plug order won from largest PV OEM - strategic white space entry; value not disclosed yet; entry into Japanese OEM via CAFE 3 expected FY28-29
items.quote: One of the notable achievements during the quarter was securing a spark plug order from one of India's largest passenger vehicle OEMs. This win represents a strong entry into a new white space opportunity and demonstrates our ability to leverage long-standing customer relationships to expand our footprint.

items.statement: BS-VII/CAFE3 content per vehicle increase estimated at 1.2-1.5x vs 2-4x for BS-IV to BS-VI; Euro 7 POC successful with European truck OEM
items.quote: BS-VII, CAFE 3, it'll be more like X going to 1.3 x to 1.5x, something like that, I think, if you take the combination. But don't hold me on that, because it's still not sure how the BS-VII legislation will land.

items.statement: New product launches heavy through early CY27 to FY29 across DaVinci, semi-active, Clean Air programs; M&A/inorganic options being evaluated for excess cash deployment
items.quote: somewhere between, like, early calendar year '27 through '28 and through '29, so the next couple of years are going to be very heavy for new product launches across the board. So, we're quite excited about that, and that will automatically give us a pretty nice growth to look forward to.

items.statement: Segment I (Electro-Mechanical Projects & Commercial AC) FY27 margin outlook 6.5-7%
items.quote: As far as segment I is concerned, the margin outlook remains the same, 6.5% to 7%.

items.statement: Carried forward order book Rs 7,764 Cr as of June 30, 2026, up 13.5% YoY
items.quote: The carry forward order book as on June 30, 2026, grew by 13.5% to Rs.7,764 Crore as compared to RS.6,843 Crore as on June 30, 2025.

items.statement: Only 5% of 13% targeted cost increase passed on in Q1; balance 8% not passed on
items.quote: We entered the financial year with the hope that we will be able to pass on the commodity price and other input cost increase to the consumers. The total impact that we wanted to pass on was around 13%, what we could pass on was only 5%.

items.statement: Segment II Q1 EBIT margin 2.9% vs 5.8% YoY; Jan-Jun H1 margin ~7.1% vs 7.3% YoY
items.quote: In segment II, the revenue growth you will be seeing is around 13%, a significant drop in the EBIT margins by around 300 basis points from 5.8% in Q1FY26 to 2.9%.

items.statement: Segment I Q1 EBIT margin 6.8% vs 7.9% YoY, down 112 bps due to commodity prices and exchange rate
items.quote: If you specifically look at the segment I, you would have seen that we have grown more than 15.1% in terms of revenue and the margins were down by around 112 basis points, primarily due to input costs on commodity prices, the exchange rate.

items.statement: Net cash position Rs 900 Cr as of June 30, 2026, up from Rs 371 Cr YoY
items.quote: The quarter ended with a strong net cash position of RS.900 Crore as on June 30, 2026, as compared to a net cash position of RS.371 Crore as on June 30, 2025.

items.statement: International business targets additional USD 100 Mn export revenue per annum from FY28 (on top of ~USD 80-85 Mn in FY26)
items.quote: With product approvals in place for a few customers, we are looking to scale this business to generate additional export revenue of USD100 million per annum from FY28.

items.statement: Novelis long-term EBITDA per ton guidance of $600 remains unchanged
items.quote: Importantly, our long-term EBITDA per ton guidance of $600 remains unchanged.

items.statement: India downstream aluminium EBITDA per ton sustainable level around $250 for remaining FY27 quarters
items.quote: So I would say more around USD250 is a more sustainable number.

items.statement: Consolidated net debt-to-EBITDA to remain around 2x; India net debt-to-EBITDA not expected to materially change in FY27 due to high capex
items.quote: We remain disciplined in our capital allocation approach and committed to maintain net leverage at around 2x on a consol basis.

items.statement: Renewable energy capacity to reach 884 MW solar/wind/hydro and 125 MW RE RTC by end FY27
items.quote: With these additions, our renewable portfolio is expected to reach 884 megawatts of solar wind hydel capacity, along with 125 megawatts of RE RTC capacity by the end of FY27.

items.statement: Aditya Alumina refinery and first 180 pots of smelter expansion commissioning December 2027; second 180 pots December 2028
items.quote: The first, the 180 pots of Aditya smelter will come at exactly the same time as the refinery coming up. The expansion is in 2 phases, 180-180. The first 180 will come in December of '27. The next 180 will come in December of '28

items.statement: Aluminium hedging for FY27 at 29% commodity at $3,004/t and 18% currency at INR91.63/USD; FY28 hedging at 21% at $3,160/t targeting $3,200
items.quote: Our hedging positions in aluminum for the rest of FY27 stands at around 29% on the commodity at USD3,004 per ton and 18% in the currency at INR91.63 per USD.

items.statement: India upstream aluminium Q1 FY27 EBITDA record $2,331/t at 55% margin; downstream EBITDA $303/t
items.quote: This delivered an all-time high EBITDA of USD2,331 per ton this quarter. EBITDA margins were at a record 55% and continue to be amongst the best in the global industry.

items.statement: Novelis Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA $563/t up 30% YoY; run-rate cost savings $225M targeting $350-400M by FY28 exit
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA for the quarter stood at $516 million or $563 per ton, reflecting a 24% and 30% increase, respectively, year-on-year.

items.statement: Sulphuric acid prices elevated due to West Asia crisis; expect similar levels in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Well, they are staying elevated. So, I think it would be fair to say a similar number like Q1 for Q2.

items.statement: India aluminium cash cost up ~5% QoQ in Q1; expect another 5-6% increase in Q2 due to higher coal prices
items.quote: And quarter two, the coal prices in the northern region have gone up in the monsoon period. So, we are expecting maybe another 5% to 6% increase Q2 to Q1.

items.statement: India aluminium demand Q1 FY27 ~1.5 Mt, up 3% YoY; flat rolled products demand up >10% YoY
items.quote: We estimate aluminum demand in quarter 1 of FY27 at around 1.5 million tons representing growth of approximately 3% year-on-year.

items.statement: Brand royalty of 0.25% revenue capped at INR225 cr/year each for Hindalco and Novelis; below materiality threshold
items.quote: And it's capped at INR225 crores. And I think it's important to note for us this royalty amount is below what we say is our materiality threshhold.

items.statement: Organic capex of INR 1,800 crores planned for FY27 in India across forging, machining, heat treatment and ring rolling
items.quote: The overall capex will be in the INR1,800-odd crores range. This is the organic capex that we will do in India.

items.statement: Fundraise of up to INR 2,500 crores for growth capex in large engine, power gen, semiconductor components, aerospace and energetics plant in Andhra Pradesh
items.quote: And the fundraise of up to INR2,500 crores is basically for growth capex. And the instrument, etcetera, will be finalized in due course.

items.statement: Defense order book stands at INR 11,196 crores as of end of Q1 FY27
items.quote: The outstanding order book in defense now stands at INR11,196 crores as of end of the quarter.

items.statement: Defense business targeting steady-state annual margins of 22-23%
items.quote: But as we have mentioned, the margins on a steady state annual basis we are targeting in the 22% to 23% or so range.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin impacted by 160 bps due to energy, input cost and logistics escalation; recovery from customers ongoing
items.quote: The overall cost impact of these costs was about 160 basis points on our EBITDA margin and we continue to work on the recovery of these indirect cost increases with our customers.

items.statement: Strong business sentiment in North America driven by corporate capex in construction, mining, data centre and power systems; US mining economy restart announced
items.quote: We've had a strong business sentiment in North America driven by higher corporate capex which is boosting demand for construction, mining and data centre and power systems businesses.

items.statement: Asset turnover on new capex expected above 1.5x
items.quote: I think it will be above 1.5.

items.statement: Marine gas turbine generator order won for Kolkata class ships - largest naval order to date; multi-fuel turbines 1.25-25MW range; MRO tied up with Navy
items.quote: We won a large new order for marine gas turbine generators for the Kolkata class ships with the Ministry of Defence and the naval shipyards. This is the largest order we have won to date on naval systems

items.statement: Expect resilient 8% growth next quarter driven by festive demand, rural cash flows, infrastructure activity
items.quote: Next quarter, we expect a resilient 8% growth driven by festive demand, stronger rural cash flows and ongoing infrastructure activity.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 14% range; management confident of sustaining upward trend through operational excellence, localization, volume growth, productivity, favorable mix
items.quote: So overall, I would say we are on an upward trend, and we would say that we will sustain this.

items.statement: Domestic economy resilient in Q1 FY27; PV demand strong on SUV preference; HCV demand healthy despite diesel price hike; LCV robust on logistics and e-commerce; tractor resilient on farm cash flows; 2-wheeler robust on rural demand
items.quote: The domestic economy remained resilient in the first quarter of fiscal 2027. This stability was driven by robust private consumption and stable monetary policy from the Reserve Bank of India.

items.statement: Power Solutions outperformed market across passenger cars, commercial vehicles, tractors; 2-wheeler gained market share with new products to new OEMs; aftermarket highest ever monthly sales in June
items.quote: We've gained market share, yes. There are some new products introduced to new OEMs. So we've gained market share.

items.statement: Chassis Systems acquisition completed in July; consolidation underway; will publish consolidated results from next quarter; investor meet planned at Chakan, Pune in November
items.quote: Already starting next quarter, we will publish consolidated results, and you will start to see the impact of this.

items.statement: Monsoon variability, potential El Nino effect, geopolitical tensions remain key downside risks for next quarter growth
items.quote: However, monsoon variability, potential El Nino effect and geopolitical tensions remain key downside risks.

items.statement: Commodity prices saw strong increase over last several quarters but leveled off recently; environment volatile due to geopolitics, supply chain, logistics; impact contained but no guidance given
items.quote: We've seen pretty strong increase over the last several quarters, which has sort of leveled off a little bit at this point of time.

items.statement: TACO JV for e-axles has healthy order book from both sides; TSF JV for air systems starting customer discussions at IAA auto show in September; e-axle JV revenue expected by late next year
items.quote: We got into the JV only after we have a healthy order book from our side and from the TACO side. So we are doing quite good there.

items.statement: Export revenue currently at 8-8.5%; aim to continuously increase this over next couple of years on increasing trend
items.quote: We are probably at 8% now, if I'm not wrong, 8%, 8.5%. And we will continue to increase this moving forward.

items.statement: Growth drivers for next 3-5 years: volume growth across mobility portfolio, new product introductions, new technology introductions (CV ADAS from next year), premiumization of vehicles
items.quote: The first growth driver, as always, is volume, and we see significantly increasing volume growth in all our mobility portfolio over the next 3 to 5 years.

items.statement: No one-offs in employee cost or other expenses; margin improvement driven by operational excellence, localization, volume growth, productivity, product mix, worldwide purchasing organization
items.quote: No. To answer that, no, there are no one-offs.

items.statement: CAFE Phase 3 regulations from April and CV ADAS from October next year expected to boost Power Solutions growth further
items.quote: We also have the CV ADAS coming up in October of next year. So a lot of preparation going on towards that.

items.statement: Localization plans well on track and consistently increasing; will continue to increase localization content in coming quarters
items.quote: Our localization plans are well on track and consistently increasing localization content. And we will continue to go in this path and continue to increase our localization content.

items.statement: Management maintains sub-15% EBITDA margin guidance for FY27, citing volatility and uncertainty

items.statement: Yarn spreads increased from ~INR110 in Q4 FY26 to ~INR130 in Q1 FY27 and sustaining in Q2; driven by improved demand, capacity consolidation, and cotton price parity correction
items.quote: In the first quarter, I think in the last quarter of the last financial year, the spreads were in the range of about INR110. And now it is in the range of or INR130.

items.statement: Cotton prices up 8-10% in Q1 due to lower global production and logistics challenges; import duty removed; Indian cotton now at -1 to -2% vs Cotlook Index vs +5-7% previously
items.quote: Cotton prices increased during quarter 1 by about 8% to 10%, primarily driven by overall lower global production, global supply chain and logistics challenges due to West Asia war.

items.statement: Demand improved from both domestic and export markets; China cotton yarn imports rose from 90-100M kg in CY25 to 110-115M kg in CY26; India-UK FTA implemented, EU FTA expected to help
items.quote: The increased demand of cotton yarn in export market from China was one of the factors for a better demand scenario for the Indian spinners. The recently implemented India U.K. FTA is also expected to support India's exports.

items.statement: Knitted fabric utilization at 55-60% (vs pre-tariff 60-65%) due to US market uncertainties and frequent tariff changes; major presence in US impacted
items.quote: This is in the range of about 55% to 60% at this point of time. We have not yet reached the 65% level the usual utilization pre this US tariff regime used to be around 60% to 65%.

items.statement: No buyback planned; in growth phase deploying internal accruals and taking loans for capex
items.quote: I think at this point of time we are in a growth phase. We are deploying our capital for the growth purposes, internal accruals as well as we are also taking some loans as well.

items.statement: Blended power cost expected to be ~INR5.50/unit once full solar capacity (60% of requirement) is operational
items.quote: This should be once we have our complete capacity up and running, which would be constituting about 65% of our -- 60 to 60 -- about 60% of our overall requirements our blended cost should be in the range of about INR5.50.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 volumes achieved 16-29% of full-year FY27 guidance; FY27 mining guidance of 3.4 mt remains on track
items.quote: We remain on track to deliver our FY '27 guidance, with Q1 volume achieving between 16% to 29% of full year guidance.

items.statement: Pellet production guidance of 4.0 mt for FY27 likely to be slightly lower due to one plant shutdown since last 45 days
items.quote: Although we haven't revised, we are still evaluating but you can expect the volumes to be slightly on the lower side.

items.statement: CRM complex relocation to Maharashtra: INR1,100 crore capex (INR550 crore debt, balance internal accruals), commissioning by Dec 2027
items.quote: The project is now targeted to be, commissioned by December '27, with planned capex of INR1,100 crores to be funded through INR550 crores of debt and balance through internal accruals.

items.statement: Total remaining capex for FY27 and FY28 estimated at ~INR2,000 crore for CRM, BESS and mining projects
items.quote: Overall we envisage a CapEx of close to about INR2,000 crores for remaining FY'27 and entire FY'28.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 19.1%, PAT margin 12.7% in Q1 FY27; margin improvement expected from Q4 FY27 post beneficiation plant commissioning
items.quote: EBITDA and PAT margin stood at 19.1% and 12.7%, respectively. Except margin improvement, we expect margin improvement from Q4 FY '27, following commissioning of beneficiation plant.

items.statement: CRM complex margin expected to improve to 10-11% with Maharashtra incentives (vs earlier 7-8%)
items.quote: Yes, we should, Yes, exactly. We should touch 10%-11% with incentives.

items.statement: Beneficiation plant commissioning in Q3 FY27 to enable higher captive mining; market iron ore purchase to drop from 25-30% in Q3 to <10% in Q4, 100% captive by FY28
items.quote: Q3, you can say we'll still -- so we'll be running at pellet plant at full capacity. The purchase of market will be still about 25%-30%. And from Q4 gradually, it should come down below 10%, and finally in FY28, it should be 100% captive.

items.statement: Integrated steel plant (1 mt) kept in abeyance due to water allocation delays (6-8 months); treat as optional for medium-term; Vision 2030 revised excluding steel plant
items.quote: So, till the time we don't -- we don't get the water approval and all, so we really don't know when that's going to happen. So, better to keep it as an option now, the steel plant.

items.statement: Ari Dongri mining constrained by government land tree-cutting approval; approval expected by end Sep 2026, full ramp-up by Q4 FY27/Q1 FY28
items.quote: We are very hopeful we should get the desired approvals by end of September, and basis that from October onwards, we will get the land to start dumping.

items.statement: DR-grade pellet export plans for Middle East once 100% captive mining achieved in FY28; exported 2 vessels in Jun-Jul at ~INR9,000/t ex-plant
items.quote: No, we very much have plans to enter the DR market, which is mainly the Middle East. But that can only happen once we are able to feed 100% from our mines.

items.statement: Targeting 12-14% revenue CAGR but current traction suggests higher growth; high-teens FY27 growth feasible if macro conditions hold
items.quote: In terms of top line, we have been always saying that our CAGR would be in the range of 12% to 14%. But if you look at better years, we have done more than that. This year, if it continues to be more than that, definitely I think, as of now, it looks like it should be better than that number.

items.statement: Targeting 10-12% consolidated EBITDA margin by FY28; business inherently capable of 10-12% EBITDA margin now
items.quote: As we have guided earlier, our first aim is to really target between 10% to 12% by FY28. And we are heading very much in that direction. And of course, as and when there is a more opportunity coming up for improvement, will be in line with our capex plan, we'll keep intimating to you.

items.statement: Outlining capex commitment of INR200-250 crore for FY27 across geographies; detailed plan to be shared in coming months
items.quote: Further, we are in the process of outlining capex commitment of approximately INR200 to INR250 crores for FY27 across geographies. We'll update you on the detailed capex plan in coming months.

items.statement: Healthy order book with better capacity utilization in India vs last year; Bangladesh and Indonesia seeing healthy traction from existing and new customers
items.quote: At Pearl, we are having a healthy order book and have better utilization of capacity in India as compared to last year when we had the backdrop of the tariff pressure which had started around this time. Moving on to Bangladesh, here our business continues to grow. Again, we witnessed a healthy traction, both from the e

items.statement: US consumer behavior remains healthy despite geopolitical tensions; retailers gaining confidence from customer demand and tariff refunds, positive for order books
items.quote: On the brighter side, what we find is that despite all these war and inflation, the US consumer behaviour remained healthy.
