items.quote: Rishi, except for the Cell project that is now being completed, capex beyond that will be around ₹30-50 crore. You can use ₹50 crore as a target number.

items.statement: Signed first Mahashakti MoU with Axis Energy for 20 GWh over five to six years.
items.quote: This MoU is for 20 GWh over the next five to six years, and I feel confident that more demand pipeline will be announced as it develops.

items.statement: Service revenue roadmap targets approximately ₹400-500 crore by FY2027-28.
items.quote: As this base matures, service can increasingly develop into a recurring, high-margin revenue stream, with our roadmap targeting service revenue of approximately ₹400-500 crore by FY 2027-28.

items.statement: Most of Auto business will move to LFP; about 20% of portfolio remains NMC for high-performance products.
items.quote: Within Auto, about 20% of our portfolio will remain NMC-based for higher-performance and top-end products. Everything else will move to LFP.

items.statement: By end of this year most vehicles should be on own cells; no firm guidance.
items.quote: But, as an assumption, by the end of this year most of our vehicles should be on our own cells.

items.statement: Plans to scale Cell capacity from 6 GWh to 20 GWh in FY27, funded by separate equity at Cell company.
items.quote: At that point, we will aim to scale from 6 GWh to 20 GWh, but only by bringing equity into the Cell company.

items.statement: Completed ₹780 crore QIP, strengthening balance sheet and financial flexibility.
items.quote: The balance sheet strengthened during the quarter through the successful completion of a ₹780 crore QIP, giving us greater financial flexibility as we pursue the next phase of our growth.

items.statement: Dealership pivot expected to bring increased top-line growth over Q1 base, with meaningful scale before Diwali.
items.quote: I am confident that this will bring increased top-line growth over the Q1 base, and the best dealers working with the company can provide a strong uplift further ahead.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 34% YoY to INR2,508 cr; EBITDA and PAT grew 27% and 53% to INR759 cr and INR472 cr; margins steady at 30.3% and 18.8%
items.quote: Our total revenue has increased 34% year-on-year to INR2,508 crores. EBITDA and PAT have grown by 27% and 53% to INR759 crores and INR472 crores, respectively. The profitability margins have been largely steady at 30.3% and 18.8%, respectively.

items.statement: New orders of INR3,011 cr for cells and modules in Q1; total order book stands at INR15,000 cr including transformers
items.quote: We won new orders totalling INR3,011 crores for cells and modules, taking our total order book to INR15,000 crores, including transformers.

items.statement: Q1 capex was INR1,500 cr, with INR1,250 cr on solar (Seetharampur and Naidupeta) and INR250 cr on Transcon
items.quote: So the total capex in the quarter was about INR1,500 crores. Bulk of the capex was incurred on solar, on solar projects, basically both Seetharampur and Naidupeta. And then the remaining was incurred on Transcon, INR250 crores.

items.statement: Management expects to maintain EBITDA margins of 29-30% (+/- 100-150 bps) over next 2-3 years driven by backward integration, scale, and DCR mix shift
items.quote: we have consistently, you know, informed that the margins of 29%, 30%, plus-minus 100, 150 basis points, we will be maintaining. And this is because for a simple reason that our 7 gigawatt cell line is coming up, our transformer capacity is growing almost from 4 GVA to 16.25 GVA by FY28, we have ingot-wafer lines comin

items.statement: No concrete plan to raise primary capital in near future; enabling resolutions taken annually for flexibility in hyper-growth phase
items.quote: As we speak, I can confirm that there is no concrete plan to raise any primary capital in the near future.

items.statement: INR25 cr investment approved for further debottlenecking of bio-based specialty chemicals capacity, completion expected early FY28
items.quote: We have, therefore, decided to invest a further INR25 crores in debottlenecking our capacity to be able to further meet the growing demand for our bio-based specialty chemical business.

items.statement: Bio-based chemicals EBITDA margin expanded to 11.4% in Q1 FY27 from 8.9% YoY, driven by favorable product mix and debottlenecking benefits
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded to 11.4% from 8.9%, supported by favorable product mix and the benefits of the debottlenecking initiatives.

items.statement: DME pilot trials progressing as planned; final results expected by March 2027 to determine commercial scale-up
items.quote: The pilot trials are proceeding as planned. Final results of how the pilot trials have done will come latest by March of 2027.

items.statement: Sugar prices increased recently; ethanol prices from sugarcane juice unchanged for years; maize/grain feedstock adds cost flexibility
items.quote: The prices of sugar have increased in the past few weeks. The prices of ethanol from sugarcane juice have remained the same over the past few years.

items.statement: Full-year order inflow guidance of INR30,000 crores for FY27
items.quote: we remain confident of achieving our full-year order inflow guidance of INR30,000 crores

items.statement: Order book at INR43,290 crores end of Q1 FY27; orders booked YTD INR15,700 crores
items.quote: our order book stood at INR43,290 crores at the end of the quarter

items.statement: Capex guidance INR700-800 crores for FY27; INR600-650 crores for FY28
items.quote: for full year FY27, we are looking at INR700 crores to INR800 crores capex

items.statement: Overseas projects carry 200-300 bps higher margins than domestic projects
items.quote: the delta in, say, domestic versus overseas is around 200 to 300 basis points, which is higher in overseas market

items.statement: Bid pipeline INR1.5 lakh crores for next 9 months; INR3.96 lakh crores for next 2 years
items.quote: healthy bid pipeline of approximately INR1.5 lakh crores for the remaining 9 months of financial '27, and INR3.96 lakh crores for the next 2 years

items.statement: UP Jal Jeevan Mission payments remain stretched; receivables ~INR400 crores with minimal recovery
items.quote: Payment related issues in UP Jal Jeevan Mission is still continuing. We have received small amount of payment based on the completed portion of work

items.statement: Debt target: net debt around INR2,700-2,800 crores by March 2027; gross debt ~INR3,500 crores
items.quote: Net debt will be somewhere around INR2,700 to INR2,800 crores kind of a number

items.statement: Execution expected to significantly pick up from Q3 FY27; strong H2 anticipated
items.quote: we expect the execution to significantly pick up from Q3 onwards, and so, we'll have a very strong H2

items.statement: Q1 capex capitalized INR150 crores; CWIP similar to March level (~INR900 crores)
items.quote: capex in Q1, we have done close to INR150 crores capitalized, but then there is a sizable amount in CWIP

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 9.6% (INR263 crores) vs 13% (INR445 crores) YoY; lower due to reduced turnover
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR263 crores with an EBITDA margin of 9.6%

items.statement: ~11% of order book slow-moving (5.65% slow, 2% Bangladesh, 3% JJM); ~20% in initial phase
items.quote: roughly around 5.65% is slow-moving category, and Bangladesh orders constitute about 2%, and another about 3% constitutes Jal Jeevan Mission orders

items.statement: Other income expected ~INR400 crores for FY27 (arbitration interest, forex gains, miscellaneous)
items.quote: this year also, we'll be in the range of say, for the year somewhere around INR400 or so

items.statement: Expect H2 demand improvement; 60% of revenue typically in H2; too early for full-year volume call
items.quote: While Q2 is expected to remain seasonally soft, we expect customer sentiment and demand momentum to improve as we head into the second half of the year. As we highlighted previously, nearly 60% of our revenue is typically generated in H2.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 12.5%, down 70 bps YoY; Q2 margins challenging; target 13-15% corridor long-term
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter dropped by 70 basis points and came in at 12.5%.

items.statement: Evaluating another calibrated price hike after 2% increase in Q4 FY26; input costs rising on fuel and steel
items.quote: Following the price increases of about 2% that we took in Q4 FY26, we are also evaluating another price hike which will be implemented in a calibrated manner, with the timing and quantum to be determined based on the prevailing market environment.

items.statement: Industry registrations down 27% in Q1; AJAX volumes down 21%; market share rose to 75.1%
items.quote: The important thing, Raghu, what you would have noticed that the industry registrations in this quarter came down by 27% and AJAX was down 21%.

items.statement: UDAAN sold 121 units in Q1 FY27; ARGO 4000 launch planned in Q2 FY27; non-SLCM grew 6.4% YoY
items.quote: In the first quarter, I think we did some 121 numbers for UDAAN and I think that showed up the overall volume for the SLCM category as such to almost the same as last year in the first quarter.

items.statement: Multiple customer engagements progressing; expect meaningful wins over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We are actively pursuing multiple customer engagements and potential contracts, several of which are progressing well. We expect these efforts to start translating into meaningful business wins over the next two or three quarters.

items.statement: Non-SLCM target 10-15% YoY growth for FY27; exports targeting 30% CAGR over next 3 years
items.quote: We would be happy if we are able to drive the non-SLCM business on a lower base to a decent number of about 10% -15% growth over the previous year.

items.statement: State payment delays to contractors persist; Maharashtra and MP volumes down ~50%; geopolitical commodity cost pressure
items.quote: Contractors continue to experience delays in payments from some of the specific state governments, leading to cash flow constraints that dampen sentiments and reduce their appetite to place new orders and undertake fresh investments in equipment.

items.statement: Cash balance exceeds INR 1,100 crores as of June 2026; actively pursuing inorganic opportunities
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to be a key source of strength with cash balance exceeding INR1,100 crores as of June 2026, providing us with ample flexibility to pursue future growth opportunities, including inorganic opportunities.

items.statement: SAP ECC 6 to HANA migration costing INR 16 million in FY27; manufacturing streamlined under single leader

items.quote: Including the merged portfolio, areas sold stood at 46,000 square feet. Booking value was INR 108 crores and collections were INR 146 crores.

items.statement: Targets 30-35% EBITDA margins for new project acquisitions
items.quote: We have always had our EBITDA margins of 30-35% as a target for acquiring projects.

items.statement: QIP of INR 900 crores completed; net cash position with ~INR 200 crores acquisition capital available
items.quote: Following the successful QIP of INR 900 crores, we remain in a net cash position with approximately INR 200 crores of acquisition capital available for new acquisitions and a debt-free balance sheet.

items.statement: Merger timeline uncertain; depends on NCLT dates and processes, benches heavily loaded
items.quote: We are not sure about that because that depends on the NCLT's available dates and processes that NCLT follows. The benches are all heavily loaded with a lot of work.

items.statement: Merger to consolidate over 400 acres land, ongoing projects, and Futurex ready inventory; existing portfolio unsold GDV ~INR 8,000 crores
items.quote: The consolidation will bring over 400 acres of land, several ongoing projects and some ready inventory at Futurex into the company's portfolio. Friends, our existing portfolio has an estimated unsold GDV of approximately INR 8,000 crores.

items.statement: PTC sales vertical seeing huge demand from redevelopment projects in neighboring wards; presales expected in next few quarters
items.quote: And for redevelopment to become more viable, they require this PTC area. So especially in the newer deals, people are actually initially coming to us and seeking this area. So in the next few quarters, you might even see some presales from PTC area.

items.statement: Selective on redevelopment deals; avoids overpriced deals that risk project delays and financial imbalance
items.quote: Important thing to note here is when the offers are very high, we have seen so many of redevelopment projects that get stuck later on. So, it is a good idea to have a financially balanced approach even from the perspective of the occupants that if you seek very high amount and pricy deal, there is a chance that those d

items.statement: FY27 group revenue growth target 18-20% with EBITDA margin around 17.5%
items.quote: For FY27, we continue to continue to have a target group revenue target of about 18% to 20%, with margins being in the range of about 17-odd percent, a little bit maybe 17.5% because we're still working out the whole impact of the inflationary pressures.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR103 crores for FY27 across gaskets, forgings, heat shields
items.quote: Our planned capex is about INR103 crores for the year across gaskets, forgings, heat shields and to try and meet the demands of the OEM.

items.statement: Secured new orders from Kia, Cummins, Stellantis; Marelli order book ~INR500 crores over 5 years
items.quote: Some serious order book is coming our way, almost about INR500 crores for 5 years, INR100 crores per annum.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 17.6% under pressure from commodity inflation; expect recovery in coming quarters
items.quote: EBITDA at INR43 crores at a margin of 17.6%. Margins during the quarter witnessed temporary pressure on account of elevated commodity prices, particularly steel and aluminium as well as other inflation costs such as labour increases in some states.

items.statement: Expect to pass through commodity cost increases to OEMs in coming quarters
items.quote: But we are very positive that we will get these increases from the OEMs in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Export target 35% of revenue by FY28; forging division recovery expected with double-digit growth in Q2
items.quote: We are targeting to take our exports to 35% by FY28.

items.statement: Data centre gasket revenue potential INR30-40 crores annually, currently 5% of gasket business; target INR100 crores in 2-3 years
items.quote: We estimate the current revenue potential from this segment, so a little bit nominal can be about INR30 crores to INR40 crores annually.

items.statement: EV contribution 3.27% of total sales in Q1 FY27; target 5% in next 2 years
items.quote: First quarter, it is around 3.27% of this year. We expect in next 2 year it should go up 5%.

items.statement: Sustainable consolidated EBITDA margin around 17%
items.quote: Around 17%, you can assume.

items.statement: FY27 segment growth: Marelli JV 30-40%, forging 20%+, gasket 16-17%, TMR 18-20%
items.quote: First of all, it should be Marelli, okay, it will grow very fast in 30% to 40% growth will be there. And secondly, forging, it should be around 20% plus then gasket and similarly, TMR, both are same 18%, 20%.

items.statement: No EBITDA margin guidance given for FY27 due to market uncertainty
items.quote: No, I mean, with this kind of uncertainty in the market, I will not be in a position to give you a guidance on the EBITDA margin for the year.

items.statement: Cautiously optimistic on ad revenue recovery driven by improved market share, festive season, and West Asia conflict easing
items.quote: As I stated, Sameer, in my opening remarks, that we are cautiously optimistic that it will stabilize over the coming period, especially the fact that our market share has improved and the festive season is approaching. And thirdly, the West Asia war seems to be sorting itself out.

items.statement: ZEE5 revenue grew 58% YoY to INR 4,571 million in Q1 FY27 with EBITDA of INR 44 million
items.quote: Revenue grew 58% year -on-year in quarter 1 to INR 4,571 million. Further, we continue to invest for future growth by increasing our marketing spend in Bullet which has a huge potential in capturing the attention of new age consumers.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 4.1% in Q1 FY27 (EBITDA INR 789 million) impacted by ad revenue decline and higher sports marketing spend
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 789 million, impacted by operating deleverage due to Middle East crisis impacting the advertising revenue. As a result, EBITDA margins were at 4.1%.

items.statement: Linear TV price hikes expected at next NTO cycle in February 2025
items.quote: In terms of price hikes on the linear side, as you know, that we are regulated by NTO and as and when the next NTO cycle happens, which is, I think, February next year, we would be looking at price hikes there as well.

items.statement: Star arbitration final hearing completed in July 2026; outcome expected possibly in Q3 FY27
items.quote: Yes. So Mr. Doshi, the Star arbitration hearings were held in July, which we have disclosed. And now further procedural steps will follow, and we are looking at an outcome possibly in Q3 of this year.

items.statement: Fundraising timeline under regulatory review; company approached regulator and SAT for clarification on 12-month vs 18-month window
items.quote: So Abneesh, as far as the fundraising, we have already written to the regulator seeking clarification. And we have not received any response from there. We have also approached Securities Appellate Tribunal, and we have filed an appeal there.

items.statement: ZEE5 subscriber base more than doubled in Q1 FY27 post FIFA launch; renewal rates indicate sustainable growth beyond sports events
items.quote: So, on the B2C additions in the last quarter itself, we have more than doubled our subscriber base and a large part of that may be due to FIFA, but there is also a consumer base that comes in for non -sports is what I can say.

items.statement: Subscription revenue grew 16% YoY in Q1 FY27 driven by digital ARPU growth, subscriber additions, and linear price increases
items.quote: Moving to subscription revenues. It registered a 16% year-on-year growth, as Punit mentioned, primarily driven by a higher ARPU and growth in subscribers in our digital business and increased pricing in our linear business.

items.statement: Ad revenue declined 11% YoY in Q1 FY27 due to Middle East conflict impacting April-May; green shoots visible in June post FIFA rights acquisition
items.quote: Coming to advertising revenues. It declined by 11% year -on-year, largely due to the Middle East conflict severely impacting us during April and May as the advertisers remain very cautious.

items.statement: Music business not being demerged; internal transfer pricing ensures fair revenue allocation between ZEE5, linear and music segments
items.quote: We have thought about the demerger of the music business, but right now, there is no strategic reason for us to demerge the business outward. Therefore, we are not pursuing it unless some corporate action actually transpires.

items.statement: Expect high-teen revenue growth on base case over next 3-5 years
items.quote: on a base case basis, we want to grow on high-teen basis, I can say.

items.statement: Expanded fermentation capacity fully operational by end of August, running at full scale
items.quote: the manufacturing site starts full steam by the end of this month. So we have to basically commercialize everything that we produce.

items.statement: Hybrid power plant Phase 1 expected live in September, Phase 2 two months later, will significantly lower power cost and improve EBITDA margins
items.quote: We are expecting Phase 1 to go live in September. And then 2 months later, the second phase will start. And it should improve our EBITDA margins for sure, this will allow us to get power at a significantly lower price.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 22.1% YoY to INR43.8 cr driven by robust volume increase reflecting healthy demand
items.quote: Revenue from operations for Q1 FY27 stood at INR43.8 crores compared with INR35.9 crores in the corresponding quarter last year, an increase of 22.1% year -on-year. This growth came in from a robust increase in sales volumes, which reflects a healthy demand outlook for our products.

items.statement: Promoter share pledge (currently ~48%) expected to reduce significantly within 12-15 months
items.quote: I think within a year, it should be going down year to 15 months should be going down significantly.

items.statement: MicroBiopharm Japan brings 7-8 year capability leap in peptides, plasmids, precision fermentation, enzyme engineering, ADCs; 60% revenue from Japan, 40% global
items.quote: they have got peptides. They have plasmids, which essentially is a base to manufacture DNA, RNA, gene therapy, CAR-T. They have precision fermentation. They have enzyme engineering and capability that they are now building up is ADCs.

items.statement: Sanofi portfolio: 13 branded generic anti-TB/anti-infective brands across 55 countries; 3-year transition service agreement; plan to integrate GTBL API into supply chain for margin improvement
items.quote: After post-closing, there is a transition service agreement between us and Sanofi for 3 years, whereby in a step-by-step manner, all the transfers will take place.

items.statement: Expect revenue contribution from expanded capacity starting Q2 FY27, full impact in H2 FY27
items.quote: We should start seeing the output from the expanded capacity to a certain extent from this quarter and then finally in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Post-integration margins expected to be close to current GTBL standalone levels (~47.5% EBITDA margin)
items.quote: We would hope that once this integration is completed and once the stabilization is done, we would be -- we'll be close to where we are right now.

items.statement: Company expects consolidated topline to grow ~20% in FY27 with commensurate bottom-line growth; new businesses expected to grow ~60%
items.quote: The Company expects topline to grow by about 20% in FY26-27 on overall basis with commensurate increase in bottom-line. Further four new businesses are expected to grow about 60%.

items.statement: ROCE target of 15-20% over next 12-24 months from current ~11%
items.quote: We are now working to improve these ROCE over the next 12 to 24 months. We intend to take it to anywhere between 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Capex cycle largely complete after ₹1,200 Cr invested over last 3 years; focus now on leveraging assets and improving ROCE
items.quote: Capex cycle of the Company is largely complete. Now the focus will be to fully leverage the strategic capex done in last 3 years (₹1,200 Cr.).

items.statement: Rigid packaging (Plastech) targets ₹150-160 Cr revenue in FY27 and ₹200+ Cr next year; capacity expanding 50% with minimal capex
items.quote: This year we expect to grow from Rs. 100 crores of last year's revenue to Rs. 150 crores-Rs. 160 crores this year, and next year we would like to take this business to Rs. 200 plus crores.

items.statement: BOPP gross margin ₹30/kg in Q1 FY27 (incl. stock gain) vs ₹20/kg in Q4 FY26 and ₹23/kg in Q1 FY26; BOPET margin ₹9/kg vs ₹18/kg in Q4 FY26 and ₹13/kg in Q1 FY26
items.quote: BOPP gross margins was running at Rs 30/- per kg in June 2026Q vs Rs 20 per kg in March 2026Q and Rs 23/- per kg in June 2025Q. This includes stock gain as well which is non-repetitive. BOPET gross margin was running at Rs 9/- per kg in June 2026Q vs Rs 18/- per kg in March-26 quarter & Rs 13/- per kg in June-25 quarte

items.statement: Specialty film mix at 61% in Q1 (highest in 5 quarters); target to reach 70% and capability to go up to 85-90% without significant capex
items.quote: The current mix of 61% is anyways the highest that we have in the last five quarters. And as a company, our objective is to move it to 70%. So, any incremental capacity can always be allocated to specialty films.

items.statement: US subsidiary received ~USD 7 Mn refund in July 2026 post reversal of additional customs duty; not yet appropriated pending customer refunds
items.quote: Post reversal of additional custom duty imposed in FY 25-26 on imports from India into the USA, the US subsidiary received a refund of about USD 7 million in July-2026 which has not been appropriated pending finalization of customers' refunds there against.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR 1,310 crores, bifurcated rig-wise and year-wise in presentation
items.quote: The order book stands at INR1,310 crores, and we've also bifurcated the order book year-wise.

items.statement: Three rigs to be dehired in FY27; revenue to decline in H2 FY27 but EBITDA margin may increase as owned/high-rate rigs remain
items.quote: Yes, absolutely right. Because these three rigs will get dehired, they will go into refurbishment. No revenue will accrue till they get redeployed. So revenue will decline in the second half of this financial year.

items.statement: Refurbishment cost estimated at INR 90-110 crores per rig due to inflation in labor and material transit costs
items.quote: Considering the recent inflationary trend and the increase in labor cost and transit cost of materials, I think a figure between INR90 crores to INR110 crores would be a fair estimate per rig.

items.statement: New ONGC contract for Jindal Pioneer at fixed INR day rate of ~INR 45 lakhs, denominated in INR not USD
items.quote: It's at a fixed day rate of INR45 lakhs approximately. This contract was denominated in INR.

items.statement: Confident three dehiring rigs will be redeployed due to government's Samudra Manthan initiative boosting drilling activity
items.quote: However, going forward, we believe that the next three rigs, which are getting dehired, they should be rehired because of the Samudra Manthan exercise the Government of India has announced in the recent past.

items.statement: ONGC dispute pending in Supreme Court for 14-15 years; potential liability of INR 163 crores (INR 63 cr principal + interest/forex) if case lost, but assessed as remote
items.quote: There is a receivable of INR63 crores, the original receivable of INR63 crores. And then there is interest and forex appreciation on the said amount. The original receivable was denominated in USD. So, the total amount is close to INR163 crores.

items.statement: No acquisition plans currently; focusing on redeploying three dehiring rigs and conserving cash for their refurbishment
items.quote: As of now, we are not looking at any acquisitions right now. We are only looking at the ability to redeploy the 3 rigs, which are going to get dehired in the later part of this financial year.

items.statement: Day rates expected to improve for three redeploying rigs, but recent contract awarded at $47,800 vs bid of $62,000 due to customer willingness
items.quote: We had participated with a rate of $62,000, and we were pushed down to $47,800 approximately. I think more than our expectations, it is the willingness of our customers to pay the correct rate.

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer refurbishment to complete by first week of September 2026, deployment expected in October 2026
items.quote: We expect the refurbishment exercise to be completed by first week of September and deployment of this rig to take place in the month of October.

items.statement: Targeting 25% ROCE for FY27, with Q2 expected above 20% and full-year average around 25%
items.quote: ROCE for the year, I mean, our stated target is higher at around 30%, but we will definitely be over 20% for Q2, higher than that. For the year as an average, I think we said 25% that's at -- 25%, we can comment.

items.statement: Targeting 7% PBT margin over next 2-3 years, up from current 5.38%
items.quote: What we have guided to is over the next 3 years, reaching a PBT of 7%. We are right now at around 5% change, I think, 5.3, probably 5.38 I'm told is where we're at.

items.statement: Targeting debt-to-equity ratio of 0.7 by end of FY27
items.quote: We would consider any debt equity around 0.7 to be healthy. From an annualized point of view, by the end of the year, we are quite confident we will be able to get close to that number.

items.statement: Expecting double-digit revenue and profitability growth in Q2 FY27 sequentially
items.quote: I think you can look at -- I mean, if you sequential, I think, is what you mentioned. Q1 to Q2, you should expect growth. Yes, you should expect double-digit growth in revenue and profitability.

items.statement: PEB India order book at record INR 1,008 crores
items.quote: PEB India is at INR1,008 crores.

items.statement: PEB US (Ascent) order backlog crossed USD 100 million, a new peak
items.quote: PEB US has just crossed. I mean this is not a middle quarter as it is right now. We have crossed a USD100 million in order backlog for Ascent, which is our US sub.

items.statement: Boilers order book at record INR 150.75 crores
items.quote: Boilers again highest ever order backlog in over INR150.75 crores.

items.statement: PBT margin improved to 5.38% in Q1 FY27 from 4.77% YoY, driven by favorable mix shift
items.quote: On profitability and margins, PBT margin was at 5.38%, up from 4.77% last year. Mix moving in the right direction, higher-margin businesses, PEB U.S. and engineering services are growing faster and the group margin follows.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded to 43.85% from 42.56% YoY; contribution margin rose to 28.51% from 27.14%
items.quote: Gross margins have been expanded from 42.56% to 43.85% at a consolidated level, while the contribution margins has increased from 27.14% to 28.51%.

items.statement: Majority of steel price increases passed through in PEB; temporary 200bps margin dip in Q1 due to 1-2 month lag
items.quote: We were able to get the vast majority of the pass-through steel price increase pass-through, that did happen. Some I think there was a little bit of a bleed effect where it took some pain for us to get those increases.

items.statement: Legacy businesses (steel, railways) now ~25% of revenue, down from 35% a year ago; growth vectors are PEB India, PEB US, Boilers, BIW, Engineering Services
items.quote: Those legacy revenue streams currently contribute about 25% of our revenue. It used to be 35, a year ago it was 35, 33. It's reducing, quarter-on-quarter it reduces.

items.statement: Consolidated sales growth guidance raised to 15% for FY27 excluding Foskor and Awuko, up from prior 11-12% comparable guidance.
items.quote: Given our current order load and forecasts from customers, the growth could be 15% without the sales from Foskor and Awuko in both the periods.

items.statement: Consolidated Ceramics sales growth guidance raised to 23-25% for FY27 from prior 15-15.5%.
items.quote: We feel that this could go up to 23%-25%.

items.statement: Consolidated Abrasives sales growth guidance retained at 5.5-6% reported, 11-12% excluding Awuko for FY27.
items.quote: I retained the same guidance.

items.statement: Consolidated Electrominerals sales growth guidance retained at 8-9% excluding Foskor, could be 9-10% for FY27.
items.quote: This could be 9% to 10%. We retained the same guidance.

items.statement: Consolidated Abrasives margin guidance retained at 9.5-10% for FY27, excluding Awuko losses.
items.quote: Consolidated Abrasive margins were expected to be around 9.5% to 10% . In FY'26, the reported margin was 4.3%. However, if we exclude the Awuko loss, the comparable margin for FY'26 would be 7.9%. So, we retained the earlier guidance.

items.statement: Consolidated Ceramics margin guidance retained at 20.5-21% for FY27.
items.quote: Consolidated ceramic margins were expected to be 20.5% to 21%. We maintain our same guidance here.

items.statement: Consolidated Electrominerals margin guidance retained at 9-9.5% for FY27, excluding Foskor losses.
items.quote: Consolidated Electrominerals margins were expected to be 9% to 9.5%. In FY'26, the reported margin was 5.6%. However, if we exclude the loss of Foskor Zirconia and compare it, the FY'26 margin would be 9.1%. We retained the same guidance.

items.statement: Consolidated CAPEX guidance retained at INR 400 crores for FY27.
items.quote: We gave a guidance of INR 400 crores for the full year FY'27 and we keep the same guidance.

items.statement: Standalone Ceramics PBIT flat despite topline growth due to fuel, alumina cost increases and unabsorbed costs in new semicon and aerospace lines; expected to improve over next few quarters.
items.quote: PBIT of IC remained flat despite the topline going up. The reasons are cost increase in fuel, alumina, unabsorbed cost in new lines of semicon and aerospace and defence capacities. We expect this to improve over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Ceramics growth driven by Engineered Ceramics, Metallized Cylinders, and SOFC; Wear Ceramics seeing normal growth.
items.quote: It will be a combination of Engineered Ceramics, Metallized Cylinder, and as well as this, SOFC Ceramics.

items.statement: Rhodius Abrasives guidance maintained: ~5% sales growth in FY27 with small PAT loss.
items.quote: During the last call, we said Rhodius could grow by 5% in FY '27 and that there could be a small loss at the PAT level. We maintain the same guidance.

items.statement: Consolidated order backlog stood at INR618 crores as of June 2026 with Q1 FY27 order inflow of INR283 crores.
items.quote: As of June '26, our order backlog stood at approximately INR618 crores and we recorded an order inflow of INR283 crores.

items.statement: Penta Automation expected to grow 25-30% in FY27 and average 25-30% for next 2-3 years.
items.quote: Last year they did a turnover of, I believe, INR25 crores and going forward, this year we may be ending over almost 25% to 30% growth and for next two, three years, we are looking at an average growth of 25%-30% for Penta.

items.statement: Machine tool production capacity increased ~30% over last year; Quickmill expanding into Gulf, Mexico, South America.
items.quote: Based on the customer feedback and competitive benchmarking, our investment in capex is in machine tool divisions has started yielding results in terms of increasing production capacity around by around 30% over the last year.

items.statement: Absorbing part of raw material cost increases (copper, steel) and passing part to customers; focusing on productivity gains.
items.quote: For manufacturing space, of course, whatever the raw material cost increase comes up, like any other manufacturer, we are now trying to absorb part of it, trying to pass on to the customer, especially the copper, steel prices.

items.statement: Environmental Engineering secured INR52 crore order from SAEL Industries for solar cell facility pollution control system.
items.quote: Environmental Engineering division has secured a landmark order from SAEL Industries Limited for design, supply, installation, and commissioning of a pollution control system for their upcoming solar cell manufacturing facility in Jewar, Uttar Pradesh. This order is valued at around INR52 crores.

items.statement: Performance subject to no adverse impact from prolonged Middle East conflict or tariff-related headwinds.
items.quote: This is subject, of course, to not having any further adverse impact, if any, on the global and Indian economy in the event of a prolonged conflict in the Middle East and any tariff-related headwinds for the balance year.

items.statement: Bioconserve Renewable Envirotech outlook robust due to mandatory ZLD implementation; targeting pharma, food, chemical sectors after establishing in textile.
items.quote: Mandatory zero liquid discharge implementation in high pollution industries is creating sustained demand for advanced treatment systems. Outlook for Bioconserve Renewable Envirotech Private Limited remains robust.

items.statement: Currently 65-70% of factory power from solar; planning to augment remaining 30-40% capacity this fiscal.
items.quote: Right now, we have almost 65%-70% of the power commission solar power commissioned on our factory, and another 30%-40% of spare capacity available that we are definitely looking at augmenting that capacity by in this fiscal end.

items.statement: Quickmill recorded INR45 crore turnover in Q1 FY27; healthy pending orders to deliver consistent performance in upcoming quarters.
items.quote: Quickmill recorded a turnover of INR45 crores in FY27 quarter 1, and based on the pending orders as of Q1 end, Quickmill will be delivering a consistent performance in upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Q1 order intake INR11.4bn, down 30% YoY due to lower TBCB realization in Q4 FY26
items.quote: Coming to financial performance during the first quarter, we saw order book at INR11.4 billion, down 30% year-on-year compared to INR16.2 billion in the quarter ended June '26. The primary reason for the lower order intake was due to lower realization of TBCB in market in Q4 '25-'26.

items.statement: Order backlog INR209.3bn as of June 2026, down 2.5% QoQ, representing over 3 years of FY26 revenue
items.quote: Execution outpaced new orders because of which the order backlog moderated to INR209.3 billion as of June '26 versus INR214.6 billion as of March '26, down by 2.5% quarter-on-quarter. The order backlog stands at more than 3 years of our revenue for FY25, '26.

items.statement: Maintain full-year EBITDA margin guidance in mid-20s band for FY27
items.quote: So Amit, we maintain our guidance of mid-20s EBITDA for the year. There is no reason that we should deviate from that right now.

items.statement: Q1 gross margin 41.3% vs 45.3% FY26; 4% delta from lower export mix, commodity costs, and HV business ramp-up; 50% of gross margin impact offset at EBITDA level delivering 25.1% EBITDA
items.quote: Gross margins moderated to 41.3% from 48.4% a year ago and 47% in the last quarter. However, in our business, comparison with annual margin is a better reference point. So during financial year '25-'26, we achieved a gross margin of 45.3%. This quarter, gross margins are lower at 41.3%, representing a delta of 4%.

items.statement: INR10bn capacity expansion program announced in FY26 on track; INR29.3bn total cash including cash pool; INR13bn utilization plan (INR10bn capex + INR2.5bn dividend)
items.quote: Out of this cash balance, company has announced utilization plan of approximately INR13 billion, which includes INR10 billion of capacity expansion program announced in the last financial year and approximately INR2.5 billion of dividend in Q2, subject to the approval of shareholders.

items.statement: Domestic TBCB pipeline improving from June/July after soft Jan-Mar; expect market flat to 6-7% growth in FY27; base order flow guidance INR70-80bn/year maintained
items.quote: But we are seeing now the TBCB pipeline or decisions are getting much better. The last few months if you really look at June, July, the pipeline is much better than what it was in January to March.

items.statement: Transformer business has price escalation clauses (IEEMA formula) for commodity pass-through; non-transformer business builds in future commodity costs at tendering with 18-24 month execution lag
items.quote: In that scope, we get a price escalation. So all the commodities like CRGO steel, etcetera, there is a formula embedded in the contract with which we get the compensation. So that part of the business is not impacted.

items.statement: INR3,000cr RPT approval expiring at Sept AGM as customer put project on hold; INR1,300cr US data center RPT order delayed due to location/voltage changes; both not lost but timing uncertain
items.quote: So, Sameer, thanks for the question. So basically, the approval what we took for INR3,000 crores that project has been put under hold as of today by the customer. So, when the customer reinitiates that process, then at that point of time, we will again go back to the shareholders.

items.statement: Export orders 46% of Q1 intake (up from typical 30-33% revenue share); private customers 77% of backlog, central/PSU 21%, state utilities only 2%
items.quote: This export diversification, which now stands at 46% of our Q1 orders is a trend, we have been building forward and had flagged in our earlier calls.

items.statement: HVDC pipeline remains strong; first phase developer bids submitted, decision expected Aug/Sept; 1-2 more projects expected in upcoming NCT; meaningful HVDC revenue growth from FY29 onward
items.quote: The HVDC pipeline remains strong. Of course, the pace at which we would like it to come, it's slightly getting delayed, but it's not going away.

items.statement: Vallam project part capacity in Q1 FY27, balance by end FY27; capacity utilization mixed - some factories loaded, others have headroom; competitive advantage cited as technology, lean, localization
items.quote: I think part of the capacity we should be able to come up with in Q1 of '27, that is there, but the balance capacity will come, probably by end of '27.

items.statement: Maintains FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% and EBITDA margin guidance of 18-20%, tracking towards upper band of margin guidance
items.quote: As we said, we continue to maintain our revenue guidance of 15% and the upper side of the 18% to 20% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin expanded 175 bps YoY to 21.2% driven by operating leverage, product mix improvement, and US discount rollback
items.quote: EBITDA for Q1 FY27 stood at INR56 crores as compared to INR44.1 crores in last year corresponding quarter, growth of 27%. With EBITDA margin expanding by 175 basis points to 21.2% from last year 19.4%.

items.statement: Domestic sales grew 39.8% YoY to INR 56 crores in Q1; export from India operations grew 10.6% YoY; India volume growth 25% with 12% price realization growth
items.quote: Export from India operation grew by 10.6% in Q1 FY27 as compared to Q1 FY26 While domestic sales grew by 39.8% YOY. Our domestic sales outpaced our exports.

items.statement: Premiumization driving growth: India quartz sinks +31%, stainless sinks +60%, appliances +28%, faucets +45% YoY; faucet volumes +33.4% YoY, stainless steel volumes +16.3% YoY
items.quote: All the broad four categories, Quartz Sinks, Stainless Sinks, Appliances, and Faucets in India has grown 31%, 60%, 28%, 45%, respectively. We continue to see this momentum moving forward.

items.statement: Logistics disruptions causing container delays impacted Q1 dispatches; UK market remains modest but cautiously optimistic with new project channel customers
items.quote: There is a lot of disruption happening in the logistics side. So while we had a very strong order booking and I think we did well, we could not dispatch a lot of things because of the delay in containers.

items.statement: United Granite gross margins improved from 35% to 50% via 'cut less, make more' strategy with high-end exotic stone inventory investment of $1 million
items.quote: We invested in high exotic stones and marbles. And because the cost of the manufacturing is the same. So, we increase our inventory by $ 1 million to get a very high-end exotic Italian and stones. And I think that has turned around the corner where the margins have significantly improved. For example, I think it has go

items.statement: Factory running at serious stress - 7 days/week needed to meet order book; capacity expansion critical by March 2027 to sustain growth
items.quote: Because the kind of order booking what we have right now, my factory has to literally run now 7 days a week. So we are in a serious stress. We 100% have to see, that how fast can we expand our capacity and we will be doing our best.

items.statement: Management declined to provide specific FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance but expects quarter-on-quarter growth driven by strong tailwinds.
items.quote: we don't want to give any guidance as such. But what we can tell you is the tailwinds or growth drivers are very strong, and we are expected to show growth on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target is 30% over the next 2-3 years, up from 27% in Q1 FY27, driven by revenue growth and cost rationalization including renewable energy.
items.quote: our target is to take EBITDA margins up to 30% and it comes from both. I mean, higher revenue as well as cost. So, we are looking at various options to control or to rationalize our costs. One of it is moving to renewable energy for some of the properties.

items.statement: Capex for FY27 and FY28 will be limited to normal repair and maintenance; major capex for Mumbai/Pune refurbishment will be guided next quarter.
items.quote: just to give you guidance, it will be normal repair and maintenance CAPEX for next two years.

items.statement: Pipeline of ~400 keys across 6 hotels (Gwalior, Dehradun, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh, Mandvi) expected to open in 12-15 months.
items.quote: we are looking at around 400 keys addition, maybe next one year or 15 months from now. That is Gwalior, Dehradun, Dwarka, Nashik, Rishikesh and Mandvi Kutch.

items.statement: Domestic leisure and business travel demand remains strong; Q1 occupancy of 66% expected to continue improving through Q2-Q4 with business hotels targeting 75-80% occupancy.
items.quote: Q1 occupancy growth has shown good trend, and we expect this trend to continue for the remaining three quarters. Typically, business hotels cross more than 75-80% occupancy.

items.statement: Portfolio split between business hotels (Mumbai, Pune) and leisure destinations (Goa, Rishikesh, Bhavnagar); new supply focused on Tier-2/3 cities with industrial/tourism demand drivers.
items.quote: normally, these are two distinct hotels. I mean, business hotels, we don't get leisure business. If you look at our Mumbai or Pune, mostly it is business travel. There is no leisure. And there are identified, I mean, Goa, it is leisure. In Rishikesh, it will be leisure.

items.statement: RevPAR grew 18% (Orchid) and 17% (Lotus) in Q1 FY27; pricing strategy is dynamic, balancing ARR and occupancy based on micro-market demand.
items.quote: RevPAR for our two brands that is Orchid and Lotus grew 18% and 17% respectively in Q1 FY27. This is high teen RevPAR growth which is much higher than hospitality industry which they have shown in the current quarter.

items.statement: New hotel openings depend on third-party owners' capex and timelines; Dehradun delayed by ~6 months, Nashik delayed due to technical issues.
items.quote: Dehradun is delayed. There are challenges due to which they are delayed. That could be delayed by another six months. Nashik is going on. Work is going on. The target is to open before the main Kumbh.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 38-40 crore; balance sheet capacity to raise up to Rs 300 crore debt (3x forward EBITDA) to fund growth.
items.quote: Even if I take three times multiple of my forward EBITDA, we can raise debt comfortably up to INR 300 crore on the balance sheet.

items.statement: FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 10-11% for full year
items.quote: For the whole year, this will be dependent on the raw material prices, of course, but we are trying to maximize it. It may not be to the extent of what we have seen in the last financial year FY26 because of this first quarter. But yes, in the range of about 10% to 11%, if I have to make a guess.

items.statement: Q1 price hike ~5% taken monthly; further 8-9% expected; cumulative 11% in replacement
items.quote: In the first quarter, we took price increase of nearly about 5%. And going forward, we are expecting to take price increases in the range of about 8% to 9%.

items.statement: RM costs up ~20% QoQ in Q1; further 8-10% increase expected in Q2 from high-cost inventory
items.quote: And we are hoping that these raw material prices stabilize barring some increase of between 8 - 10% in our RM cost in next quarter as we have been noticing because of the higher cost inventory which we have accumulated.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin 6.8% vs 10.9% YoY; target to return to 11-13% range in H2 FY27
items.quote: We should be able to come back to the normal range of 11% to 13% in the second half.

items.statement: Rs 4,980 cr expansion for PCR & TBR at Chennai; ~7% capacity addition by FY28; TBR and PCR balancing at Banmore
items.quote: So, with our expansion plans worth Rs.4,980 crores, which will entail passenger and truck radial, we will be adding about 24%.

items.statement: FY27 net debt expected to increase Rs 500-700 cr for capex and working capital
items.quote: So broadly, we are expecting an increase of Rs.500-700 crores overall in this financial year.

items.statement: Domestic volumes grew 25% YoY in Q1 (OEM 42%, replacement strong); mid-single digit sequential growth
items.quote: Our domestic volumes which includes replacement and OEM, grew by 25% on a year-on-year basis from the corresponding quarter.

items.statement: PCR mix improving: 16-inch+ tyres now 35% of PCR volumes; consolidated mix: TBR 56%, PCR 27%, 2/3W 5%, others 12%
items.quote: In the PCR category, mix has been constantly improving, as we have mentioned earlier also. So, this is better now for 16-inch and above and these high rim sized tyres together make up 35% of total PCR sales volumes.

items.statement: Mexico operations hit by shipping disruptions, container shortage, China bead wire supply issues, IR slowdown; now resolved
items.quote: During the quarter, operations at JK Tornel, Mexico were impacted due to ongoing geopolitical disruptions resulting in constrained availability of key inputs. Furthermore, productivity enhancement negotiations with workers resulted in IR issues, which have since been resolved.

items.statement: EV tyre volumes grew double-digit QoQ; EV tyre life 5-10% shorter than ICE due to higher torque
items.quote: Because of the higher torque around 5% to 10%.

items.statement: India capacity utilization ~95% (TBR, 2/3W full; PCR 95%, non-truck bias 95%+); consolidated ~80%
items.quote: Our capacity utilization has been around 95% in the India and on consolidated basis it is around 80%.

items.statement: USMCA renewed for 10 years; favourable duty structure for Mexico exports to USA
items.quote: Yes, the USMCA agreement has been renewed for 10 years. And therefore, we are hoping that the relations between Mexico and USA in terms of the duty structure is going to be favourable towards Mexico.

items.statement: Management expects to sustain current EBITDA margin trajectory but will monitor commodity costs weekly; no formal 3-year CAGR forecast yet, will provide in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: We are in line for trying to carry on what we have delivered. And that is what the aspiration is, and that is what the plans and the discipline is there in order to ensure that we move ahead with a similar kind.

items.statement: Jammu alkaline battery plant commenced commercial production on May 29, 2026; plant & machinery investment INR 90-95 crores
items.quote: In Jammu, it will be around INR90 crores to INR95 crores will be our plant and machinery.

items.statement: Jammu plant expected to deliver 10% gross margin increment per SKU once fully stabilized; current alkaline share 6-7% of portfolio growing 50%+
items.quote: So, this is the first year like so we'll be stabilizing. And after a year and so when fully stabilized, we expect definitely a 10% margin up there.

items.statement: Lighting segment broke even in Q1 FY27; management expects it to hold through the year
items.quote: Yes. In quarter 1, we are broken even. Let's watch for it throughout the year. My sense is mostly it should hold.

items.statement: Management monitors zinc weekly; may take another round of price increases to manage commodity inflation
items.quote: I will not be very surprised if to manage the commodity inflation, we may have to do another round of price or margin corrections.

items.statement: Alkaline battery volume grew ~48% YoY; market share expanded to 18% in alkaline segment; carbon zinc volumes flat
items.quote: Our alkaline battery portfolio continued to be the key growth driver, delivering close to 48% volume growth during the quarter.

items.statement: Flashlight demand soft due to delayed monsoon; rechargeable flashlights grew >20% revenue; hybrid flashlight launched
items.quote: Our rechargeable flashlight portfolio remained a key growth driver, delivering over 20% revenue growth during the quarter.

items.statement: Lighting business grew 13.7%; price erosion stabilizing after 18-20 months; emergency LED bulbs and electrical accessories driving growth
items.quote: Our lighting business delivered an encouraging quarter, registering healthy 13.7% growth. The business benefited from strong demand across key product categories, while the pricing environment showed signs of stabilization after a prolonged period of price erosion.

items.statement: Alkaline target exit market share 25-30% in 2 years (from 18% currently); wires & MCBs targeting 2-3x growth to reach 1-2% market share
items.quote: My sense would be that we should be looking at anywhere between an exit share of 25% to 30% at the end of 2 years from now.

items.statement: GST incentive for Jammu plant (3x plant & machinery investment over 10 years) still pending approval; advanced discussions ongoing
items.quote: There is no movement has happened on our GST approval at this point of time, but we are in a very advanced stage of the discussion with the industries department.

items.statement: EPR compliance discussions ongoing with Ministry; operational and pricing framework challenges being addressed; no cost estimate yet
items.quote: With respect to the EPR compliance, there are some operational and with the pricing mechanism, there are some challenges for which we are working with the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change and the Pollution Control Board.

items.statement: No immediate fund infusion needed; company paying down debt ahead of schedule; Noida land sale partially executed, second plot closing shortly
items.quote: As of now, there is no such need of the extra fund. If you see the company is doing very well, we are paying ahead of time our debt.

items.statement: Company targets debt-free status (like-to-like) in 4-5 quarters; current debt ~INR 165 crores after INR 200+ crores Jammu investment
items.quote: If you ask me, we see shorter in the next maybe in the 4 to 5 quarters, the company should be having a positive and should be a like-to-like debt free.

items.statement: Management declined to provide volume or growth guidance for FY27, citing ongoing trials and technicalities; will reassess next quarter.
items.quote: We are not giving any guidance. What we are saying is, trials are going on, it is work in progress. We are getting decent responses, but there are technicalities which entail our team to engage more, give some more solutions. That process is going on. It may take a little longer time than what we had anticipated, so we

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance increased to INR350-400 crores from INR130 crores, driven by INR170-200 crores for new corporate house and INR50-100 crores for additional land acquisition.
items.quote: We are upping or increasing our capex guidance to now almost over about INR350 crores to INR400 crores because we've just recently contracted for a dedicated plot of land for our corporate house for which we will be able to -- we will be spending about INR170 crores to INR200 crores over this year mainly and something

items.statement: Chile high-chrome grinding media order (INR300 crores) supplying well at 3,000-3,500 tons per quarter; expected to continue.
items.quote: That that supply is going well. I think that is good fair point to remind that. I think that's going well. That is adding to I think about 3,000 tons. And as we speak, because there's a whole supply chain and invoicing, but between 3000 tons and 4,000 tons, 3,000, 3,500 tons -- per quarter. And that looks to be somethi

items.statement: Operating margin guidance maintained at 20-22%; Q1 EBITDA margin declined QoQ due to lower FX gains, unfavorable product mix, higher trial expenses and freight costs.
items.quote: I think our guidance continues at 20%. I don't think we're going doing a bridge for any margin that we do above that. 20% to 22% is our operating margin. I believe this quarter continues to remain above that.

items.statement: Realizations increased due to freight and raw material cost pass-through; freight currently $8,000-9,000/container but trending down; ferrochrome and scrap remain elevated.
items.quote: As the freight goes up, as the raw material prices go up, as we do the pass-through, the realizations will go up, other expenses will also go up, correct.

items.statement: Mining volumes flat QoQ; decline attributed to timing, product mix, and order execution cycles, not structural demand weakness.
items.quote: No, sir. As I said, see, we don't have a quarterly run rate kind of a tracking. It's annual. So, it's more of a timing issue, a product mix issue, an order execution cycle issue.

items.statement: Q1 product mix less favorable vs Q4 (fewer value-added castings), pressuring margins; NGDS solution sold only as integrated package with grinding media and liners, not standalone.
items.quote: Second is you would have seen major contributor is the product mix. So, in the past, we have said that in a given quarter, if the product mix is extremely favorable in terms of bigger castings going more, then the needle will move into a much better margin. So, in this quarter, that product mix has not been that great

items.statement: South America conversion trials ongoing with technical delays; no visibility on conversion timelines or volumes; Chinese competition in forged media but not in high-chrome; geopolitical shipping risks persist.
items.quote: Update is it's still work in progress, and we will wait for the final outcomes. It might take a little longer than anticipated because of certain technicalities, but it is work in progress. That's the short answer.

items.statement: No near-term plans for buyback or special dividend despite INR4,500-5,000 crores cash; board prefers to retain cash for potential opportunities during conversion phase.
items.quote: We are holding on to a little higher cash, I would say at least for a few more quarters, then we will definitely look at maybe what are the other options, what we should do, how do we should distribute, etcetera.

items.statement: Ghana and China overseas plant plans in slow mode; Ghana in government dialogue, China has small lab facility; no meaningful progress; India remains preferred manufacturing base.
items.quote: In Ghana, we've identified the location, we are now in dialogue with the government to make sure that all what we understand and what we need is available. In China, we have set up a small lab kind of a facility, we are now exploring the possibilities of what kind of, you know, infrastructure or investment we should ma

items.statement: Renewable hybrid solar-wind project (INR30-odd crores) recently operational; benefits expected in coming quarters.
items.quote: It is already implemented, I would believe. It has just become operational very recently, so I think in coming quarters, you should see.

items.statement: Capacity at 430,000-440,000 tons; current utilization ~60-65%; can scale to 300,000-350,000 tons on existing capacity; further brownfield/greenfield expansion planned.
items.quote: We are today about a 430, 000 tons -440,000 odd tons. Why? Because we have to make sure that as and when conversion happen, and when a customer is ready to place orders, I cannot run and say that I will set up a plant and then you come.

items.statement: Gross margins stable at 60-61%; management does not provide margin guidance; focuses on solution acceptance over quarterly metrics.
items.quote: Yes, yes, general in the range of around, you know, 60%, 61%, that is our consistent kind of a gross margin scenario. But, whether there should be an improvement or not, let us see. Let us wait and watch. We don't see, as you know, I don't give any guidance on the margin front.

items.statement: 99acres expected to become cash-generative during FY27 with healthy growth
items.quote: we believe 99acres is well positioned to sustain healthy growth while becoming cash-generative during FY27

items.statement: Job Hai revenue target to more than double from Rs.15 crores in FY26
items.quote: Last year we did about Rs.15 crores. We would like to more than double this year in Job Hai

items.statement: AI investments continue aggressively across infrastructure, talent, and tools
items.quote: We have invested across infrastructure, talent, and tools because we believe AI enhances the value for data products and marketplace positions

items.statement: AI-Rex live across 4,000+ enterprise customers with 10%+ conversion to paying
items.quote: As of the end of June, AI-Rex was live across more than 4,000 enterprise customers and recruitment firms, with over 10 % already converted into paying customers

items.statement: Talent Pulse serves 600+ paid customers across enterprise and SMB segments
items.quote: Our AI-powered Talent and Salary Intelligence Platform, Talent Pulse now serves more than 600 paid customers

items.statement: Jobseeker business EBITDA margin improved from 35-40% to 63% driven by AI offerings and self-serve model
items.quote: Our Jobseeker business used to have an EBITDA margin of 35-40%, and used to grow at 18-20%. For the last couple of quarters now, it's been growing at 35% and the EBITDA margins have improved to 63%

items.statement: AI-Rex priced at Rs.3,500 per mandate for companies and Rs.2,500 for consultants
items.quote: We are selling AI-Rex at rate card rate of Rs.3,500 per mandate to recruit to companies. We recently launched AI-Rex for consultants as well, which is at a lower price point

items.statement: Recruitment underlying billings growth estimated at 15% after adjusting for renewal timing
items.quote: Adjusting for these timing differences, we estimate the underlying billings growth in Q1 at around 15%

items.statement: GCC billing growth normalized at 15-17% after removing one-off renewal timing benefit
items.quote: If you normalize for that, then GCC broadly been growing at 15-17% and is around 17-18% of our overall distribution

items.statement: One-third of recruitment revenue growth from new offerings (AI-Rex, Talent Pulse, employer branding)
items.quote: we estimate that about a third of our growth was a result of our newer offerings, which we are pushing more aggressively in the market, like AI-Rex and Talent Pulse and so on

items.statement: Naukri 360 paid subscriber penetration doubled from 1.3% to 2.6% of MAUs over 6 quarters
items.quote: The paid subscribers as a percentage of monthly active users improved from 1.3% to 2.6% over the last six quarters

items.statement: Shiksha faces persistent AI-driven search headwinds; investing in domestic counselling and AI voicebots to offset
items.quote: We expect these headwinds to persist over the near term. To navigate this and sustain growth, Shiksha is investing in domestic counselling capabilities and AI-driven voicebots

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 9.7% vs 15.7% QoQ and 13.5% YoY due to planned phase-out costs and front-loaded AI investments
items.quote: Total EBITDA is at Rs. 116.3 crores, with a margin of 9.7%, as compared to 15.7% in the previous quarter, and 13.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Expect operating leverage to return as volumes normalize and AI investments commercialize, viewing current margin pressure as one-time absorption
items.quote: Consistent with what we have said in our prior quarters, we view this as a one-time cost and investment phase absorption, rather than any structural change in our earning power. And we expect operating leverage to return as volume normalizes and these investments commercialize.

items.statement: Intend to move growing share of contract value to outcome-linked and non-headcount commercial structures to turn AI productivity into margins
items.quote: First, the pricing shift – We intend to move a growing share of our contract value onto outcome-linked and non-headcount commercial structures. This is the single most important thing we are doing because it is what turns AI-driven productivity into our margins.

items.statement: Strong pipeline in Agentic AI, process automation, contact center, digital modernization and platform services with 19 new CX/digital logos and 8 HRO/payroll logos added in Q1
items.quote: We added 19 new logos across CX and digital services, and 8 clients in HRO and payroll processing. That is encouraging because it shows continued client confidence in our capabilities, even in a cautious demand environment.

items.statement: Every new deal closed recently has AI components enabled, with 20-30% of work using AI initially scaling to 60-70% as customers get comfortable
items.quote: Yes, we see every new deal that we have closed recently has AI components enabled in it. Either it is leading to running the operation and process using AI as at least 20% to 30% of the work, eventually scaling to almost 60% to 70% is what we foresee as the customers get more comfortable with AI performing the job.

items.statement: Funding growth initiatives including Project Ganga primarily through internal accruals with strong liquidity and comfortable gearing ratios
items.quote: Liquidity remains solid. Gearing ratios are comfortable and working capital metrics are stable. Collection discipline continues to hold, and we are funding our growth initiatives including Project Ganga primarily through internal accruals.

items.statement: New client ramp-up typically takes 6-8 months before meaningful revenue contribution, starting at $150K-$300K with training/onboarding costs in first 3 months
items.quote: Typically, once we add new clients, it takes around 6 to 8 months before you start seeing the benefits of that revenue and scale. Initially, it starts off as a small amount of work around $150,000 to $300,000 and then eventually it scales up.

items.statement: Macro uncertainties and client prudence may persist near-term as clients wait to see AI contributions before committing
items.quote: We remain cautiously optimistic with macro uncertainties and of course the client prudence where clients are waiting how AI is going to span out and what kind of contributions that is going to get in.

items.statement: DTV business faces significant industry-wide headwinds globally, mitigated through broadband bundling, IPTV rollout and cost optimization
items.quote: As you all know, there are significant headwinds impacting digital television or the linear TV business. And those are not just industry wide in India, but also pretty much globally.

items.statement: Project Ganga launched June 9 2026 targeting 2M households in UP over 2-3 years with 500 DSPs trained from 2000 applications as of Aug 4
items.quote: Over the next two to three years, Project Ganga, which as you know, is an acronym for Government Assisted Network for Growth and Advancement (GANGA), will look to connect over 2 million households with high-speed broadband.

items.statement: Broadband high-speed adoption (>100 Mbps) rose from 11% to 15% YoY on expanding subscriber base with entry plan uptake falling from 22% to 18%
items.quote: If you look at the shift in customer mix on Slide #16, pretty much high-speed adoption, which was barely in the low single digits, about a year and a half ago, already it's risen from about 11% last year, this time to 15% on an expanding subscriber base.

items.statement: Expects double-digit revenue growth for FY27 excluding Pril and FA; EBITDA margins under pressure in H1, H2 substantially better subject to demand and commodity stability
items.quote: For FY27, excluding the Pril business, we expect double -digit revenue growth. EBITDA margins are likely to remain under pressure during the year due to elevated crude -linked input costs, though H2 should be substantially better than H1, subject to demand momentum and commodity price stability.

items.statement: Total price increases ~4-4.5% since war start; 3% flowed in Q1, rest in Q2; Personal Care up 9-10%, Fabric Care ~5%, Dishwash competitive
items.quote: So overall, about 4%, you can say, 4%, 4.5% out of that, 3% has flown through quarter 1 and the remaining will be visible in quarter 2.

items.statement: Rural demand resilient; urban markets subdued due to higher household expenses and cautious sentiment; GT growth muted, MT/e-com/quick commerce strong
items.quote: Rural demand stayed relatively resilient, while urban markets after showing signs of recovery in the second half of FY26 remained subdued during the quarter.

items.statement: Fabric Care grew 14% value, 10% volume; Home Care +2.4% ex-Pril; Exo franchise mid-to-high single digit value, double-digit volume; Personal Care subdued, recovery expected
items.quote: Fabric Care maintained its strong momentum, delivering over 14% value growth and 10% volume growth during the quarter.

items.statement: Crude-linked input costs unlikely to correct immediately; higher cost inventory flows through Q2; meaningful benefit only from Oct if commodity prices stable; soap noodles rising from June
items.quote: In our assessment, raw material and packaging costs are unlikely to correct immediately even if crude prices remain moderate, as higher cost purchases and contracted inventories will continue to flow through Q2.

items.statement: Exo Liquid launched 3-4 months ago, ramping as per expectations; Maxo incense sticks launched July, priced at par with competition
items.quote: So, Percy, we have it's only been 3, 4 months that we have launched it. And from a launch perspective, it has done reasonably what as per expectation.

items.statement: Segment reporting realigned to 3 segments: Fabric Care, Home Care, Personal Care per Ind AS 108; comparative numbers restated
items.quote: From Q1 FY27, we have aligned our segment reporting with the way management reviews the business and allocates resources in accordance with the Ind AS 108.

items.statement: Pril exit effective 31 May 2026; matter before court, no specific cooling-off clause; Henkel recalled brand, did not renew agreement
items.quote: So as Henkel decided to recall the brand, and they decided not to renew the agreement. So, we did not manufacture, distribute, sell product beyond 31st April. There is no specific clause which requires them to wait for a certain period, but the matter is before the court.

items.statement: M&A: evaluated TTK assets but 2 divisions not aligned, 2 had significant overlap; continue to look at assets aggressively with stringent filters
items.quote: On the specific point that you raised about TTK business, yes, we had looked at the business, but the 4 divisions of the business, 2 of them were not aligned to our business strategy, and there was a significant overlap in the remaining 2. So, we did not take it forward.

items.statement: Endeavor to deliver double-digit revenue growth from current quarter; high single-digit volume growth expected through year
items.quote: See, our endeavor is to deliver double -digit revenue growth from current quarter itself. This is what we are aiming for. But of course, 3%, 4% price increase will be sitting over there. So high single digit is the volume growth that we are expecting throug h the year.

items.statement: Margin recovery gradual, not immediate in Q2/Q3; pace depends on commodity trends, demand recovery, pricing effectiveness; H2 better than H1 on growth and profitability
items.quote: Our margin recovery is expected to be gradual rather than immediately in quarter 2 or quarter 3. The pace of improvement will depend on commodity trends, demand recovery and the effectiveness of pricing actions. So that is how we are seeing, or we are anticipating that H2 of the current year should be better than H1 on

items.statement: Working capital hygiene: significant GT on advance payment; distributor stock 15-20 days; MT/e-com/quick commerce terms comparable
items.quote: We sell products, especially in general trade, we sell products on advanced payment basis. A significant portion of our ge neral trade business is on advanced payment basis. Even with modern trade, e -commerce, quick commerce, the payment terms are whatever payment terms we have agreed with our channel partners are com

items.statement: Expects sales numbers to increase quarter-on-quarter in FY27, with strong growth momentum continuing from Q1
items.quote: This year, even quarter 2 till date, we are seeing strong growth coming in. So that momentum is still continuing. And quarter-on-quarter, I think what we are expecting is the sales numbers to increase.

items.statement: Targets sustainable EBITDA margins of 12-13% long-term for automotive ancillary business; expects gradual improvement in Q2-Q3 as asset utilization improves and pending price claims settle
items.quote: If you talk about the automotive ancillaries, like us and so, because where we have the OEM customer where we need to be most cost competitive, 12% to 13% margins would be on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Raw material costs increased ~4% in Q1; passed on ~2% to customers; negotiating remaining 50% pass-through, expects settlement by end of Q2 or early Q3
items.quote: So approximately 4% of the raw material cost has gone up due to these increases. Out of that, we're able to pass on around 2% of the raw material prices to the customer. For the balance 50% price increases, we are in the discussion with the customer. And we are hopeful that by end of Q2 and the start of Q3, we will be

items.statement: FY27 capex focused on EPDM capability (3 new lines, 1 operational in Q2), toolroom expansion, and land near Sambhaji Nagar; funded partly by JV exit proceeds
items.quote: So investment would be in this financial year in 3 areas. One is the capability development in the EPDM product. Second, in the expansion of the toolroom and for the land requirement on the west area near Sambhaji Nagar.

items.statement: Aftermarket business grew 30% YoY in Q1 FY27; expects similar growth rate to continue; expanding distribution to 155 distributors and adding warehouse in West region
items.quote: Tanya, last year also this business grew by 30%. And this year also, we are expecting that this business will continue growing at that rate.

items.statement: Raw material inflation remains key near-term watch item; geopolitical developments, commodity volatility, and supply chain dynamics could impact operating environment
items.quote: However, raw material inflation remains an important near-term watch item across our businesses. While we have made progress in securing cost pass-through arrangements with customers, a portion of the recent cost increases is still under discussion.

items.statement: Received INR100 crores from JV exit; INR8 crores used for taxes; 25% retained for working capital; balance for strategic capex
items.quote: So on the sale proceeds, which we got from the exit of the JV, so around INR100 crores we got. So out of that, around INR8 crores has been utilized towards the payment of taxes. So out of that balance amount, 25% would be retained for the working capital requirements and rest would be used for the strategic capex requi

items.statement: Targets net debt-free status within 3 years
items.quote: So for the short-term side, our target is that in next 3 years at the net level, we would like to be debt free.

items.statement: Tooling business capacity utilization at 84%; received orders for 30 molds in Q1 with pipeline of 124 molds; targets 20% output increase this year
items.quote: Capacity utilization currently stands at 84%, indicating sustained demand and efficient utilization of available resources. During the quarter, we received orders for 30 molds, while maintaining a strong pipeline of 124 molds

items.statement: Battery business revenue grew 4x YoY in Q1 (low base); focus on minimizing losses; expects improvement from Q2 but remains concern
items.quote: We are hopeful that quarter 2 onwards, things may start get better, but it still remains a cause of concern for us.

items.statement: Technology partnership with Hutchinson for advanced body sealing systems; focus on glass run channel; targeting Indian market initially; expects clarity on revenue by end of FY27
items.quote: Through this partnership, PPAP will offer modern and advanced body sealing system solutions to all the customers in India, enabling access to global technologies and next-generation sealing solutions.

items.statement: Management expects Q2 to reflect similar growth trend as Q1; will revisit full-year guidance at mid-year
items.quote: We continue to be positive. We are committed to have quarter 2 reflect the similar trend. So I think this is what the focus is. items.quote: With this Busana partnership, we get to engage with more and more fashion customers, and we also get to benefit from the skill set that Busana brings in. Therefore, in our present manufacturing capacity, we should do upgrade to customer profile and the margin thereof.

items.quote: Net working capital reduced from 4 days at March 2026 to just 1 day at June 2026. This improvement, together with strong operating cash generation helped us reduce net debt from ₹105 crores to ₹29 crores, a reduction of 73% during the quarter.
