items.statement: Capex limited to maintenance and organic requirements; no expansion capex for new verticals
items.quote: We're keeping our capex limited to just maintenance and organic capex requirements, which is why I keep saying that all of these things are using our existing campus and infrastructure.

items.statement: US demand altered by tariff uncertainty and inflation; FTAs with UK/EU expected to help in medium term
items.quote: the tariff piece has stabilized and the FTA piece should offer some opportunities. But as I said, the domestic markets will also open up for us vis-a-vis our new product verticals

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 16% due to lower revenue, mix changes, and raw material inflation
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA came in at INR101 crores. The EBITDA margin came in at about 16%, again, primarily driven by slightly lower revenues, some tweaks in product mix and some inflationary headwinds on the raw material front.

items.statement: India to become largest or top-2 revenue jurisdiction in medium term via new verticals
items.quote: in the medium term, India will probably become the largest jurisdiction for the company going forward, if not the largest, amongst the top 2.

items.statement: No specific FY27 growth/margin guidance given; management says domestic demand positive, exports recovering, margins follow top line
items.quote: To give guidance is challenging in the current environment, there are so many factors out of control. But generally speaking, it is looking quite positive from where we sit today for the domestic as well as exports overall is alright, margins follow the top line typically.

items.quote: In FY27, we have about INR 100 crore budget and this does not include the separator. The separator spend will be over the course of the next 1.5 years. items.statement: Senior Living presales target of INR1,500 crores by FY29-30
items.quote: FY 29-30 target is actually to look at INR1,500 crores of presales from Senior Living itself.

items.quote: We have a total budget of deploying about INR800 crores in this financial year, including about INR180 crores that got deployed in the last quarter.

items.quote: The company recorded a booking value of INR358 crores during the quarter gone by, with 3.6 lakh square feet of area sold across 234 units.

items.statement: Target project-level gross margin ~30%, SG&A ~12%, PBT ~18%, PAT ~12-13%

items.statement: Anmol Phase 3 and Amarah Phase 1 blended gross margin in mid-20s%
items.quote: Blended across both those projects, we should be in the mid-20s.

items.statement: Average realization improved 37% YoY to INR9,923/sq ft in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Average realization also improved significantly to INR9,923 per square foot, representing a 37% year-on-year increase, driven by a favorable product mix and continued pricing resilience across our portfolio.

items.statement: NCD redemption of INR31.25 crores (25% of issue) in Q1 FY27; Vadgaon land partly funded via NCDs to landlords
items.quote: We also commenced the redemption of NCDs issued to ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund during the quarter, INR31.25 crores, representing 25% of the original issue was redeemed.

items.statement: Revised FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance to 14-16% from earlier 12-13%
items.quote: Overall growth percentage from 12% to 13% may become almost around 14% to 16% overall for the whole of the current financial year, yes.

items.statement: FY27 capex guided at INR 700-800 crores for capacity expansion in formulations, API, biotech
items.quote: So largely, I think almost around INR700 crores to INR800 crores in current year will go in the CapEx side itself.

items.statement: US business (Ipca+Unichem) expected to grow 15-17% annually over next few years
items.quote: Maybe around 15%, 16%, 17% kind of growth is possible, but currently looking at portfolio and other things.

items.statement: Management targets 15-20% revenue CAGR over next 3-5 years
items.quote: And the idea is that how we should grow between 15% to 20% CAGR in next 3 to 5 years. Management is committed for that number, and we are planning to do every bit in our scope to see that we achieve that growth.

items.statement: Annual EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 40-42%
items.quote: But annualized basis, 40% to 42% margins are sustainable.

items.statement: Seamec ANANT to resume ONGC IMR contract after ~1 month statutory formalities
items.quote: But due to some statutory formalities that we need to comply with, it may take almost like a month before it resumes its contract with ONGC. We will try to expedite this process as much as possible. But we are hopeful that it will start the operation within this quarter.

items.statement: Strong DSV demand expected for next 3-5 years, especially if Iran sanctions lift
items.quote: So for next 3 to 5 years, we remain quite bullish that DSVs are going to get a strong demand.

items.statement: Middle East (Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Abu Dhabi) identified as key growth markets
items.quote: Middle East as a whole is a very good opportunity. Saudi Arabia is a hotspot, then Qatar is a hotspot, then Abu Dhabi is also an hotspot. So there are a lot of opportunity in these 3 countries.

items.statement: Fleet contract mix: 35-40% short-term (EPC), balance mid-to-long term (IMR)
items.quote: See, around 35% to 40% contracts are short term and balance are on long-term. Basically, the EPC contracts that Naveenji mentioned are short term and IMR are generally mid- to long term.

items.statement: Samudra Manthan policy impact visible only after 3-5 years due to long gestation
items.quote: No, 2 years will be too short a time because it is going to take, as I told you, it is 3 to 5 years to get a visible impact for Seamec because oil exploration activity is a long gestation kind of activity.

items.statement: Gallant vessel sale expected to complete in September post shareholder approval
items.quote: So, post-shareholder approval, I don't think so there will be much formalities. And in the coming month, which is September, we should be able to complete.

items.statement: MOU with DG Shipping for INR 1,000 crore fleet growth over 2 years on track with ANANT acquisition
items.quote: So definitely, this is an MOU that we have signed knowing well our growth plans.

items.statement: Seamec Princess and Seamec III EPC contracts in advanced talks for post-monsoon deployment
items.quote: No, no, the talks are going on and it is at quite advanced stage. So once it is finalized, we will be filing with the exchange so that everybody is aware about the contracts.

items.statement: Seamec II charter ending August; evaluating redeployment for EPC work
items.quote: It will be completing its charter sometime in August end. And after that, we intend to use the vessel again for the EPC kind of work from -- instead of IMR work.

items.statement: FY27 branded alco-bev revenue growth guided at 60-70% YoY, with H2 as principal driver contributing 60-65% of annual branded revenue
items.quote: We expect our branded alco-bev business to grow approximately 60% to 70% for the full year, which is what we had indicated when we had done the Q4 call. With the second half expected to be the principal growth driver, in the last year it contributed nearly 60% to 65% of the annual branded alco-bev revenue.

items.statement: FY27 company-level revenue growth target of approximately 60% YoY
items.quote: At the company level we continue to target approximately 60% revenue growth year-on-year.

items.statement: FY27 company-level EBITDA margin guided at 23-24% range
items.quote: We remain confident in our ability to deliver a company-level EBITDA margin in the range of 23% to 24% for FY27, while continuing to invest behind our brands, new product launches, distribution capabilities, and international expansion.

items.statement: No large capex planned for FY27; only routine maintenance and upgrade capex as heavy capex cycle completed
items.quote: There is no large capex planned this year. Yes in the ordinary course the capex which goes into improving facilities and upgradation only that will be there. Mostly all the heavy capex has already been executed.

items.statement: Chhattisgarh distillery revenue guidance of Rs 300-400 crore for FY27 maintained despite delayed start
items.quote: We gave a guidance in Q4 where we said that between I think 300 crores to 400 crores would be the revenue from Chhattisgarh this year. And I think we are well on the road we will be able to achieve that guidance definitely.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved 30 bps YoY to 18.5%; full-year margin expected to reach 23-24% as H2 revenue scales and brand mix improves
items.quote: As we said earlier that our overall EBITDA margin in a full year basis will be on the same level or slightly better than the last year.

items.statement: Premium/super-premium/luxury portfolio grew 47.3% to Rs 82.3 crore, now 43.5% of distillery revenue vs 37.8% in Q1 FY26
items.quote: Our premium, super premium, and luxury portfolio grew 47.3% to 82 crores, raising its contribution to 43.5% of distillery revenue compared with 37.8% in Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Indri single malt growing 18-20% YoY with 87,000 filled barrels (1.6 crore litres) maturing, sufficient for multi-year growth
items.quote: For your question, we have 87,000 barrels of malt filled as on date. That is the largest in the country. And we do not see any constraints coming in from supply side.

items.statement: Camikara and Cashmir expected to grow triple-digit percentages in FY27 from small base, targeting 1 lakh+ cases each within 2-3 years
items.quote: Camikara and Cashmir this year are expecting, because see, the base is small, so they are going to see probably triple digit numbers grow.

items.statement: Ethanol policy uncertainty noted; Chhattisgarh ethanol sales dependent on government orders expected from Q2/Q3
items.quote: The reason for that is because see a lot of if you talk about ethanol the policy is very it's guided by the government and the thoughts right now. So you know to give a number there would be unfair because that's not in our control at all.

items.statement: Input cost pressures from grain and fuel prices affecting distillery margins; branded portfolio insulated due to premium pricing
items.quote: But if you see the distillery division there's been some cost pressures because of the war and internally as grain prices and fuel prices have been surging. So there has been some pressure been felt across the country because of that as well.

items.statement: Sugar division demerger scheme filed April 28, 2026; process progressing well
items.quote: We have given last quarter update that we have filed demerger of our sugar division, update on that the scheme was filed to stock exchange on 28th April 2026 and we are progressing well and so the process is continued.

items.statement: International expansion targeting 70% export / 30% domestic mix long-term; North America is largest export market currently
items.quote: So we ultimately want to have 70% export and 30% domestic. But that goal will is a few years away. But we are actively working on opening new geographies and as you understand the windows of each country start with the duty fees in the airports.

items.statement: Debt reduced by Rs 10 crore in Q1 FY27; no debt increase planned for FY27; significant debt reduction expected from FY28 as capex cycle completes
items.quote: So in this quarter we have reduced the debt by about 10 crores, but as you would understand that you know our growth trajectory continues, right? So we plan to not to increase the debt this year and all the cash from operation will be reinvested into growth and the gap.

items.statement: Defence revenue target for FY27 is INR300-350 crores with EBITDA margin of 30-35%
items.quote: In all, company aims to achieve INR300 crores to INR350 crores target this year with a marked EBITDA of 30% to 35%.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue growth guidance maintained at 15-20% for FY27
items.quote: We maintain our guidance that it should be 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Defence order book of INR307 crores (INR255 cr + INR52 cr) to be executed over 10 months and 3 months respectively
items.quote: Goodluck Defence and Aerospace Limited received an order of INR255 crores for 155 mm long-range, ready-to-fill empty shells to be executed over 10 months. In addition, it received an order of INR52 crores for 20,000 155 mm shell with execution over 3 months.

items.statement: Defence EBITDA margin guided at 30-35% range; Q1 FY27 Defence EBITDA margin was 38% on INR80 cr revenue
items.quote: Margins, it is a range bound. What is the 30% to 35% range bound margin should be there as we expect.

items.statement: Value-added products at ~60% of mix, targeting increase; hydraulic tube utilization at 60-65% in Q1, ramping up rapidly
items.quote: Value-added, we have almost 60% we are already there. And in the coming years, this will increase and the legacy business, it will get reduced due to the increase in the value-added business.

items.statement: Input cost risk high due to geopolitical volatility affecting petroleum products and logistics; West Asia crisis impacting operations
items.quote: Input cost risk is very high because war is going up and down. We never know when the war will start, when the war will stop. So all the petroleum products get volatile and the petroleum products are in every product.

items.statement: Defence expansion delayed 6-9 months due to financial closure; commercialization expected by Q4 FY28, taking capacity to ~350,000 shells/year
items.quote: Basically, it is a financial closure. Now the financial closure is being done nowadays. So as soon as the financial closure is over, we will start the ramping of the production as we had said. So that is why there is a delay due to the financial closure of the project.

items.statement: Defence IPO targeted within 18 months, subject to approvals
items.quote: We hope that 18 months from today, it should be the time. But however, again, it will depend on the approvals and the systems.

items.statement: Export growth 53% in Q1 FY27 from US and Europe; pipeline healthy but geopolitical uncertainty remains
items.quote: Was around 53% -- for this quarter, the pipeline of orders is pretty healthy for this quarter also. But again, geopolitical is a factor which should not be kept aside that we have to continuously monitor.

items.statement: Targets ~10% revenue growth in FY27 with significant H2 contribution; expects 15% growth in FY28
items.quote: Based on the visibility we have today, we remain confident of achieving approximately 10% revenue growth in FY27 with a significant portion of this growth expected to come through in the second half of the financial year.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins to remain in 13-14% range for FY27
items.quote: Current year estimates which is there is around 10% growth with EBITDA of 13%-14% with similar interest cost every quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated order book at Rs 14,636 cr as of June 30, 2026; expects execution over 3 years with book-to-bill ~3x
items.quote: As of June 30, FY26, our consolidated order book stood at Rs. 14,636 crores.

items.statement: May need Rs 100-200 cr additional working capital borrowings for execution acceleration; to be funded via internal accruals, asset monetization, project debt
items.quote: Plus, maybe some working capital borrowings of Rs. 100 crores – Rs. 200 crores may be needed in between.

items.statement: Targets Rs 150-200 cr non-core asset monetization in FY27; sold 27-acre Telangana land parcel for Rs 26 cr in Q1
items.quote: This year, target for non-core is between Rs. 150 crores to Rs. 200 crores. That we are fairly confident to achieve.

items.statement: Promoter pledge at 85-90%; expects 15-20% reduction in FY27; arbitration recoveries uncertain as PSUs pursue litigation
items.quote: Right now, if I am not mistaken, around 85% to 90% of the shares are pledged. So, we expect that to come down by at least 15%-20%.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Hydropower 68%, Irrigation 15%, Tunneling 13%, Roads/Urban 4%; order book mix similar at 62% Hydro, 17% Irrigation, 4% Tunneling, 17% Roads/Urban
items.quote: Revenue breakup sector-wise: Hydropower contributed to 68%, Irrigation 15%, Tunneling 13%, Roads, Urban Infrastructure and others 4%.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded: Long-term to A stable from A-, short-term to A1 from A2 in June 2026
items.quote: In June, our long-term credit rating was upgraded to A stable from A-, while our short-term rating was upgraded to A1 from A2.

items.statement: No exceptional items expected in FY27; prior year exceptionals from Vivaad-Se-Vishwas settlements and investment write-downs
items.quote: We don't anticipate exceptional items coming this year. That was mostly on account of last year for Vivaad-Se-Vishwas settlements and some write-down of investments.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM growth guidance of 25-30% for FY27
items.quote: Our expectation for growth of gold loan this year is around 30%, because some quarters are as per season, some quarters are off seasons. We expect that to be some between 25%-30%.

items.statement: Gold loan yield expected to stabilize around 18% with +/- 25 bps range
items.quote: We expect the yield to be somewhere around 18%. It may go down by 25 basis points or go up by 25 basis. Beyond that, we do not expect anything. It will be around 18%.

items.statement: Microfinance AUM to be contained below 10% of consolidated AUM
items.quote: I will tell at the group level, we want to contain microfinance at below 10% at a consolidated level.

items.statement: Plan to open 500 new branches in FY27 for gold loan business
items.quote: We have the plan to open around 500 branches now. We are at stream now already, progressing in that stream.

items.statement: Strong gold loan demand momentum continuing in July-August with customer and tonnage growth
items.quote: This first quarter, despite seasonally being slow, we had a good momentum, and we continue to build on that momentum in July and August as well, both from a customer perspective and from a tonnage perspective as well.

items.statement: Vehicle finance lending temporarily stopped; focus on collections with GNPA at 13.3%
items.quote: We have temporarily stopped the vehicle lending, vehicle finance. We are focusing on collection. Our collections are improving because of the improved focus.

items.statement: New MD & CEO Ashish Singh to join by January 1, 2027 with 25 years retail banking experience
items.quote: Mr. Ashish Singh has been appointed as the MD and CEO and expected to join by January 1st of 2027. He is a seasoned banker with over 25 years of experience in the retail banking space.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR 1 per share declared for Q1 FY27
items.quote: The Board has declared an interim dividend of INR1 for this quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated capital adequacy ratio at 21.29%; net worth INR 16,552 crores as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: Our capital position is strong and company is well capitalized with a capital adequacy ratio of 21.29%. The company's consolidated net worth stands at INR16,552 crores as of June 30, 2026.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 sales volume grew 3%, value grew 24%; EBITDA margin expanded 360 bps to 11.6%; expects mid-single-digit volume growth and to maintain or improve 11%+ EBITDA margin for FY27
items.quote: We maintain that the EBITDA margins delivered in this quarter would be maintained, and we are trying to better our EBITDA margins, which we have delivered in last quarter and on this quarter.

items.statement: Announced 9+ million sqm greenfield plant in South with INR 220 crore outlay, operational by Q3/Q4 FY28; plus INR 55 crore for balancing equipment across plants by Q3 FY27; total FY27 capex ~INR 275 crore, 65-70% internally funded
items.quote: So from now to '27 end, we have already looked at approximately INR275 crores outlay, which includes the INR220 crores plant plus balancing equipment in various other plants and some more balancing equipment in the Bathware, sanitaryware plant.

items.statement: Standalone capacity utilization rose from 72% to 83% YoY; JVs swung from INR 10 cr loss to INR 3 cr profit in Q1; targets 12%+ EBITDA margin
items.quote: My margins really have not gone up because of pricing. My margins have gone up because of operational efficiency that we are producing 100% in our own plants and also our JV losses have come down.

items.statement: Implemented 16-17% average price hike in Q1 to pass through gas cost increases; blended natural gas cost ~INR 68/scm (North INR 68-69, South/Morbi mid-70s); gas prices still rising marginally in July-August
items.quote: We took a price hike of -- you can take an average of about 16%, 17%.

items.statement: May-June demand decent; July resilient despite rains; expects mid-single-digit volume growth for FY27; channel inventory lean due to gas price volatility
items.quote: Demand is looking good. Let's not forget that in the last 30 months, prices had reduced also by 15%, 16%. So that's been the price increase. So from that point of view, because of that scenario, it's been well accepted in the market. And demand seems to be absolutely good.

items.statement: Adding 4-5 million sqm capacity via balancing equipment in Bahadurgarh, Gujarat, Morbi, South by Q3/Q4 FY27, focused on value-added products; project sales to rise 3-4% from current 17-19% of revenue
items.quote: All put together, we will be adding another 4 million to 5 million for the mid -- this will be ready from mid-quarter 3 and would be completely in place in quarter 4. This would add, not only capacity, but also will add value-added mix.

items.statement: Morbi exports down 50-60% from peak due to geopolitics/freight; expected to persist this quarter; domestic dumping risk low due to high gas costs
items.quote: The only negative in the quarter has been from a Morbi perspective is exports has been down due to geopolitical reasons, the export is down a good 50%, 60% from the peak.

items.statement: Current revenue run-rate ~INR 3,700 crore at today's prices with existing capacity; balancing equipment could add ~INR 300 crore; new South plant adds INR 350 crore potential revenue from FY28
items.quote: Approximately INR3,700 crores, yes, more or less, give or take, INR50 crores at today's price.

items.statement: Working capital days improved from 17 to 12 days; receivables and inventory reduced; Somany Max JV loss narrowed from INR 7 cr to ~INR 1 cr YoY
items.quote: Working capital days also have come down from 17 to 12 days.

items.statement: Targeting >15% YoY top-line growth to ~INR1,350 cr in FY27
items.quote: We are targeting a top line growth of more than 15% year-on-year, resulting into about INR1,350 crores for this financial year, maintaining a healthy bottom line.

items.statement: FY28 revenue target ~INR1,600 cr (+/- INR50 cr)
items.quote: Next year, you're looking at about INR1,600 crores plus/minus INR50 crores.

items.statement: Standalone order book INR2,156 cr (66% defense, 34% space/met/hydro) as of Q1 FY27 end
items.quote: Our stand-alone order book as of quarter end stands at INR2,156 crores, providing strong visibility for the upcoming period. Around 66% of this order book is from defense and the rest that is 34% is from space, metrology and hydrology sectors.

items.statement: Consolidated order book INR2,849 cr including INR244 cr service orders
items.quote: Our consolidated order book stands at INR2,849 crores, which includes service orders of about INR244 crores, which are typically more accretive to margins.

items.statement: Secured INR2,205 cr order from HAL for Uttam Radar subsystems in July 2026
items.quote: In the month of July, we secured a significant order worth about INR2,205 crores from Hindustan Aeronautics Limited for procurement of critical subsystems for Uttam Radar.

items.statement: Total order book ~INR4,300 cr as on date after HAL order
items.quote: So with this major win, our total order book sells to a record-breaking of INR4,300 crores as on date.

items.statement: Expect INR1,600 cr new order inflows in FY27 (excl. HAL order)
items.quote: M.V.R. confirms that we will see at least INR1,600 crores being added this year. And we may improve that number by the way, over the next few quarters.

items.statement: Order intake visibility INR8,000-9,000 cr over next 3-4 years for execution over 5-6 years
items.quote: Our order intake over the next 3 to 4 years, I think should be in the region of at least INR8,000 crores to INR9,000 crores to be executed over the next 5 to 6 years.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected similar to FY26 with positive delta
items.quote: Definitely, definitely, the margins are going to be similar to last year. You can expect a delta increase on that -- positive increase in that margins.

items.statement: Invested in automated process engineering workflows and advanced infrastructure for large-scale execution
items.quote: To support this rapidly growing volume and complexity of work, we have invested steadily in automated process engineering workflows and advanced infrastructure.

items.statement: Space & Weather division to be spun off as separate listed entity effective April 1, 2027
items.quote: The company shall operate as an independent entity from April 1, 2027, is our expectation.

items.statement: Supply chain stretch risk highlighted; beefing up purchase dept to mitigate
items.quote: So we've got to make sure that our supply chains remain intact and stuff comes in within the defined time lines.

items.statement: Sustained government focus on meteorological budgets expected due to climate change
items.quote: So given all these things combined, I think there should be and there ought to be and from indications are, there will be a sustained focus on meteorological budgets.

items.statement: Revised FY27 revenue guidance to INR 2,200-2,300 crore with EBITDA margin of 10-11% (INR 220-230 crore EBITDA), down from prior INR 2,000-2,400 crore revenue and INR 250-280 crore EBITDA guidance.
items.quote: So basically, what we are guiding is INR2,200 crores to INR2,300 crores top line and EBITDA margin in the range of 10% to 11%. So, it will be in that range between INR220 crores, INR230 crores kind of EBITDA.

items.statement: Expects normalized EBITDA margins of 12-14% in FY28 once raw material pressures ease and capacity utilization improves.
items.quote: In fiscal '28, I think it's in the region of 12% to 14% is what we can look at.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin collapsed to 4% from 45% in Q4 FY26 due to raw material cost spikes, freight increases, and inability to fully pass on costs.
items.quote: You would have seen the details of our financial statements and you would have seen that our margins, which were plus 45% last quarter, has come down to 4%, and that's what has percolated down to our EBITDA for the quarter.

items.statement: Specialty Ingredients segment EBITDA margin was 6.35% in Q1 FY27; expects improvement to >10% normalized as raw material costs stabilize and price pass-through improves.
items.quote: The EBITDA is 6.35% here. Predominantly, it has come down basically because of raw material prices being high.

items.statement: Aroma (vanillin) segment EBITDA negative INR 4-4.5 crore in Q1 FY27 due to low capacity utilization (25%) during ethyl vanillin ramp-up; expects positive EBITDA in Q2 FY27 and 7% EBITDA margin at $13/kg pricing with 3,000 tons annual volume
items.quote: As the capacity utilization crosses 70%, 80% in the subsequent quarters, we will absorb almost all the fixed costs. And on a yearly basis, it's come down to that. This is a cutoff in a quarter where the expenditures are for the full capacity, but the utilization is hardly 25%.

items.statement: Revised FY27 vanillin production guidance down to ~3,000 tons from 3,600-4,000 tons due to slower ethyl vanillin ramp-up and 4 campaign changeovers costing ~4 months production time.
items.quote: So basically, we had guided for 3,600 to 4,000 and now we are saying 3,000 -- around 3,000. The change is basically in our ethyl vanillin run. The ramp-up we took was slower than what we had anticipated purely because we wanted to get the quality standards to be absolutely undoubtable.

items.statement: Raw material cost pressures persist due to geopolitical conflict (Red Sea/Hormuz Strait); expects elevated prices for at least 3 months; able to pass on ~50% of cost increases in blends in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: In Q2, it will remain with us because I don't see so much of a difference in raw material prices because with the war situation and the conflict, it keeps moving in directions which we don't understand sometimes.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced to INR 640 crore from INR 670 crore (Mar 2026); may need INR 100-200 crore additional credit lines in FY27 for working capital; targeting to secure lines in 1-1.5 months.
items.quote: We will try to use the internal cash, but it looks like as the year progresses, we may have to go and go and take credit lines from the market in the range of INR100 crores to INR200 crores plus.

items.statement: Working capital cycle elongated to ~100 days due to Red Sea shipping rerouting and slower customer collections; using supplier/dealer financing which adds 1-1.5% to raw material costs.
items.quote: Working capital remains a bit of a concern because of the elongated working capital cycles. As you know, with the Hormuz Strait and the Red Sea issues, we have to now ship it across the South Africa, and that has increased the working capital needs.

items.statement: Vanillin channel inventories cleared globally; U.S./Europe demand gap of 5,000-6,000 tons identified due to antidumping duties; demand pickup confirmed with F&F majors for quarterly/annual contracts.
items.quote: Those are dried out. There is no overhang of any channel stock, either Chinese or pre antidumping duty on now. So, there is no channel stocks in any of the country.

items.statement: CFS Europe liquidated (no further cash burn); China entity liquidation underway with INR 10-20 crore expenditure in Q2 FY27; Brazil fire insurance claim settled at INR 400 crore with 20% haircut.
items.quote: China is in the process of liquidation. We have been telling it that this will happen this year, and we will have around INR10 million to INR20 million of expenditure, which we'll be incurring during this quarter.

items.statement: Expect positive sales growth from Q2 FY27 as monsoon improves and agriculture activity normalizes
items.quote: Difficult to give the number, but we should be positive and that positive impact should be visible from Q2 itself, I believe.

items.statement: Target to double company size in 4-5 years through product mix, technical manufacturing and international business
items.quote: The idea is to double ourselves. In the past, we used to double in 3 to 4 years. Now I believe that we should be able to double in 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Sotanala project total investment ~INR200 crores (INR50 crores formulation, INR150 crores technical), INR70 crores spent so far
items.quote: It will be a project total investment. These total investment will go roughly about INR200 crores, out of which I think about INR50 crores will be going in the formulations and INR150 crores will be for the technical. And the total investment made so far is to the tune of about INR70 crores.

items.statement: Annual capex to normalize to INR30-40 crores maintenance after current investment cycle ends
items.quote: Once the current projects are completed, we expect annual capex to normalize around INR30 crores to INR40 crores of maintenance capex, allowing us to increasingly focus on utilization, cash generation and returns.

items.statement: Target to increase premium product contribution to 70% of B2C sales in next 3-4 years
items.quote: five years back when we started this exercise when the contribution from the premium product was 48%. Now we have reached to 60-plus percentage already and the target is to reach to 70% in next three years to four years time.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 240bps to 31.6% in Q1 FY27 despite 12% revenue decline, driven by premium mix and 2% price increase
items.quote: I just told actually that there was a 13% decline in the volume and there was 2% rise in the prices. So, this price rise can be due to the focus on the specialty products and some advantage due to inventory also you can say

items.statement: Sales returns expected but reduced to at least half of prior year's INR200 crores due to cautious placement strategy
items.quote: I think that we should be able to reduce the sales return numbers to at least half what was there in the previous year.

items.statement: Crude/petroleum-linked raw material costs pressured margins; calibrated pricing, better mix and differentiated products used to offset
items.quote: On the operating side, crude and petroleum-linked raw material costs remain an area of pressure during the quarter, impacting parts of crop protection value chain. We continue to address this through calibrated pricing, better product mix and increasing contribution from the differentiated products while remaining comp

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at minimum 50% for FY27
items.quote: So I think revenue guidance remains the same. It will be at least 50%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin to be maintained despite aggressive store expansion
items.quote: And we will try to maintain the EBITDA margins even after opening so much new area.

items.statement: SSSG guidance for FY27 at 8-10%
items.quote: And the guidance for SSSG has always been 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Per store capex increased 10% to INR 1.2-1.22 crores from INR 1.1 crores
items.quote: So earlier, the capex used to be about INR1.1 crores. So I think it is up because of the prices rising, it has moved up to INR1.2 crores, INR1.22 crores.

items.statement: On track to open 170-200 stores in FY27, 56 net stores added in Q1
items.quote: Yes, we are on track to open 170 to 200 stores this year.

items.statement: 4-5% garment cost increase from Q3 FY27 due to raw material inflation, to be passed to consumers
items.quote: So I think we'll start seeing that impact from the third quarter onwards, and it will be an increase of about, I would say, 4% to 5% increase in the overall garment cost, which we'll have to pass on to the consumer.

items.statement: Demand inelastic in value fashion; kids wear 25% of sales ensures recurring need
items.quote: We think we are selling necessity to the consumers. And for example, kids wear is 25% of our sales. So you have to buy new clothes for your kids every year.

items.statement: Full price sales 90% in Q1 (down from 92% due to Adhik Maas), volume growth 56%

items.statement: Morbi industrial gas pricing at INR 78/scm vs propane at INR 65/scm; non-Morbi industrial at INR 70/scm
items.quote: Ours is close to 78 Rs/scm and propane is close to 65 Rs/scm.

items.statement: Gas sourcing mix: 20% term contracts, 12.5% domestic gas, 67.5% spot; of term, ~20% Henry Hub linked
items.quote: On an overall level, we are doing close to 20% on term contract basis. Domestic gas is close to 12.5% and the rest is spot.

items.statement: Non-Morbi industrial volumes at 2.2 mmscmd; target 3 mmscmd in 1.5-2 years as infrastructure completes in DNH, Ahmedabad rural, Dahej, Kutch, Thane
items.quote: As we expect LNG prices to become stable maybe in a year from now, we expect these volumes to be at least 3 mmscmd by 1.5 years to 2 years from now.

items.statement: GSPL Transmission listing delayed to early September due to SEBI exemption process for listing without public issue
items.quote: We expect this towards early September.

items.statement: Blended revenue growth of 30-35% YoY targeted for next 3 years driven by new brands, vintage business, and capacity expansion
items.quote: So a blended growth of somewhere around 35% to 30% for the next 3 years is kind of on the charts and it's going to be a combination of all the new brands and our existing ones, plus the increase in the capacities that we are building currently at our own facility.

items.statement: GX domestic business expected to grow 25-35% YoY for next 5 years from INR100-110 crore base
items.quote: We expect 25% to 35% growth in this business year-on-year, even for the next 5 years, we don't anticipate any hiccup because we are at a very small base.

items.statement: Capex of INR30-40 crore planned for FY27 and similar for FY28, targeting INR35-45 crore per year for next 2 years
items.quote: We have a plan of about INR30 crores to INR40 crores of CapEx in this financial year from now. From onwards, maybe the same plan for the next year as well, about INR30 crores to INR40 crores.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR800 crore for FY27, on track to overachieve; INR1,000 crore not committed
items.quote: This year, our target was somewhere around INR800 crores. I think we are in line to achieve that. We will cross that hopefully. INR1,000 crores, I do not want to comment.

items.statement: EBIT margin improvement to 12-13% expected over next 12 quarters (3 years), not within 15-18 months
items.quote: But we are on line that within the next, say, 12 quarters, we should be probably near that number.

items.statement: Pet care targeting 40-50% YoY growth for next 3-4 years from INR40-45 crore base, with cat food launch by Q4 FY27 and diagnostics expansion
items.quote: So overall, we are looking, again, at 40% to 50% growth in those numbers for the next 3, 4 years. We have a very small base of INR40 crores, INR45 crores overall with this.

items.statement: Inventory days targeted to reduce from ~135-140 to ~120 within 4 quarters, stabilizing at 110-125 days due to SKU complexity and hypergrowth phase
items.quote: We are looking at around 140, 135 days of inventory. Hopefully, within the next 4 quarters, it will come to around 120 days. It will always hover between 110 to 125 days because of the nature of the business and the number of SKUs that we have.

items.statement: Working capital at INR170-175 crore (50% cash) at INR850 crore run rate; absolute working capital will rise with revenue but comfortable with internal cash flows and improving credit rating (BBB to BBB+)
items.quote: We have a working capital of somewhere around INR170 crores, INR175 crores, which is not a high working capital for a company our size. We also have a lot of debtors. We have a good stock, and we have almost 50% of our working capital as cash on hand.

items.statement: Wagr.in pet parenting platform in beta with 1,500-2,000 products, 1,500 pharmacies onboarded; full launch with marketing campaigns expected within 90 days
items.quote: I think within the next, say, 90 days, you will see campaigns coming out, partnership with various key players in the industry coming up and a lot of exciting things coming up.

items.statement: Functional foods targeting INR18-24 crore revenue in FY27; adding 42 variants, cat biscuits in 6-7 months, strong doctor-recommended pull
items.quote: Our functional foods this year, we are looking at around INR18 crores to INR24 crores to sell only functional foods, but that will also include what we are doing right now as a product basket.

items.statement: Pet care capacity expansion underway with new plants for functional foods; OEM manufacturing for other companies planned
items.quote: We are planning to be INR100 crore say within 3 years from launching or within 3.5 years from launching our plants that we are building right now for increasing functional food capacity. That itself, we are going to also start OEM for those for other companies as well.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guardrail set at ~15% of gross revenue; core business to remain profitable while incremental accruals reinvested in AI
items.quote: The guardrails that you can establish is about 15%. That's like a guardrail, if you ask me. We always want to have guardrails, which is we never want to go below that certain amount

items.statement: AI infrastructure investment front-loaded in FY27; selective smaller data center capacity, no large-scale capex; focus on SLMs and application layers
items.quote: Our cost base remains front-loaded as we invest in AI infrastructure, international expansion and our new financial services capabilities. We are, therefore, not building for a short-term margin spike

items.statement: RediffPay UPI platform exiting CUG this month; RediffOne evolving into enterprise operating platform; PayCentral agentic payment platform launched on Google Agent Payments Protocol
items.quote: RediffPay is progressing well as our UPI-based consumer payments platform. It will be out of CUG this month and into production. RediffOne is evolving into an operating platform for businesses

items.statement: Transaction processing volume grew 74% YoY to INR 1,479 billion in Q1 FY27 with strength across utility, government, retail, B2B, hospitality
items.quote: Our transaction processing volume for the quarter grew 74% year-on-year to INR 1,479 billion with continued strength across utility payments, government payments, retail, B2B and hospitality

items.statement: UPI MDR monetization bill passed Lok Sabha, awaits Rajya Sabha and Presidential approval; expected to be positive for both CCAvenue and RediffPay but quantum uncertain
items.quote: It still awaits Rajya Sabha and still awaits President's approval and then the gazette and then we will know what kind of pricing and monetization that NPCI and RBI is allowing to be done

items.statement: Strategic investments approved: up to 2.5% in RatnaFin Capital (RBI NBFC) and up to 7% in Online PSB Loans (digital credit platform); asset-light credit distribution model
items.quote: We have progressed well in proposed investments of up to 2.5% in RatnaFin Capital, which is an RBI registered NBFC with a very strong SME lending franchisee. We also approved a strategic investment of up to 7% in online PSB loans

items.statement: Enterprise AI (SLM/PrivateGPT) revenue impact expected in 9-18 months; targeting financial institutions and critical operations with data sovereignty needs
items.quote: In terms of impact to our business is concerned, I think it's about anywhere from 9 to 18 months out, where you'll have -- you'll start seeing some good impact, we believe

items.statement: Rediff IPO timeline unchanged by corporate actions; Rediff to house consumer payments (RediffPay), enterprise platform (RediffOne), and streaming content (RediffTV)
items.quote: We don't see any impact of the corporate action on the filing of Rediff. They are 2 separate events. The corporate action is, to remind you, just increasing the face value of the share from INR 1 to INR10

items.statement: Meaningful AI/platform revenue contribution expected from Q3/Q4 FY27; international expansion focus on UAE, Saudi, and US markets
items.quote: So we expect that -- I mean, we are investing quite a bit in that area and some meaningful results should start showing up in Q3 time frame. So you can expect that maybe some movement will start in the Q3, Q4 time frame

items.statement: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance maintained at INR 2,000 crores with growth weighted to H2
items.quote: Based on current customer discussions, our receipt order visibility, expected capacity ramp-up and planned utilization levels, we remain confident of achieving our previously stated consolidating revenue guidance of INR 2,000 crores for FY27.

items.statement: Garment division EBITDA margin guided above 15% for full year including Sri Lanka
items.quote: See, with respect to margins, we have already guided for a consolidated like garment division that is between Young Brand and S.P. Apparels put together, we will be anywhere above 15% for the whole year. Even including Sri Lanka business, we should be 15% EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Standalone adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 17.5% in Q1 FY27 vs 15.2% YoY
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margins improved to 17.5% compared to 15.2% Q1 FY26.

items.statement: Garment division Q1 EBITDA margin 17.6% driven by better efficiency and product mix change
items.quote: The margins is purely with respect to the improved efficiency because there is a change in the product mix.

items.statement: Sri Lanka operations at 85-90% utilization, revenue INR 25 cr in Q1, targeting INR 150-200 cr by March
items.quote: Roughly anywhere between INR 150 crores to INR 200 crores of revenue, which will sit in the books of S.P. Apparels only.

items.statement: Dividend of INR 3/share approved; stock split proposed from FV INR 10 to INR 2
items.quote: I'm pleased to inform our shareholders that the Board has approved a dividend of INR 3 per share for the year and has also proposed a stock split of the company's equity shares from a face value of INR 10 per share to INR 2 per share.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 3,200 crore as of 7th August 2026, with metering and systems accounting for over 96% of total orders.
items.quote: Our order book stands at 3,200 CRS as on 7th August 26 with metering and systems accounting for more than 96% of the total orders.

items.statement: EBITDA margin moderated to 12.26% in Q1 FY27 due to input cost volatility in metals and industrial plastics from geopolitical disruptions and changing revenue mix.
items.quote: On profitability, EBITDA grew during the quarter although EBITDA margins moderated to 12.26%.

items.statement: Price increases initiated in wire & cable and lighting to pass on higher input costs; pass-through occurs with a time lag.
items.quote: Plus the prices are the price increases are also getting passed on to the consumer. So like we've just had couple of increases in the wire and cable.

items.statement: C&I segment (wire & cable, switchgear, lighting) expects high double-digit growth over next 12-18 months driven by volume scale and channel expansion.
items.quote: when you look at consumer and industrial there I would say the next 12 to 18 months will be very strong the the cable and wire segment has been we've been growing well well above the in fact the volume growths are far exceeding even the value enhancements.

items.statement: Smart metering provides strong revenue visibility for next 3-5 years with 7 crore meters installed so far out of 25 crore target; execution pace depends on AMISP rollout.
items.quote: if you look at smart metering they have a you know a a strong visibility. If you look at this year Next year, the next 3 to 5 years seem to be a strong visibility.

items.statement: Developing data center-specific cables with international certifications; target launch by May-June 2027 (Q1 FY28).
items.quote: hopefully by May-June of next year we should be having those kind of cables with the international certifications what are required.

items.statement: Geopolitical conflicts (West Asia) driving metal and crude-linked plastic cost inflation; 40% minimum wage hike in Haryana (May 2026) increased manpower costs.
items.quote: there has been almost a 40% increase in the minimum wages by the Hana government in May. So and since most of our manufacturing is there so that has also added to the cost on this.

items.statement: Backward integration efforts underway for smart meter components (relays, critical electronics) under government Make in India push; no manufacturing setup yet but technology work in progress.
items.quote: we have also been making efforts conscious efforts to ensure that these are to be made in India. So I think you will hear from us as we because these are long These are highly technical products.

items.statement: Middle East utility recently approved HPL's metering products; export push leveraging India scale and certifications (DECA lab, IEC compliance) for 55+ countries.
items.quote: one of the the utilities in Middle East has just approved our metering. This is very recent. Already we are now moving to the international markets thanks to the scale and technology what we are using in India.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 515 cr (+35% YoY), highest ever Q1; EBITDA Rs 63 cr (+9% YoY), PAT Rs 19 cr; C&I revenue Rs 278 cr (+55% YoY, 54% of total).
items.quote: Revenue from operations grew 35% year-on-year to 515 crores. Our highest ever first quarter revenue and remained above 500 cr level despite Q1 typically being a seasonally light Quarter.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit EBITDA margin on consolidated basis, dependent on geopolitical situation and overseas demand
items.quote: See consol business, we are trying to achieve double-digit EBITDA margin, and it all depends on how the geopolitical situation stand and overseas demand stand with us. But we'll be back again for sure on this.

items.statement: Mag carbon brick and casting flux new lines can add INR150-200 crores revenue at peak capacity
items.quote: What I said that in past, we have spoken about the addition of two new product lines, mag carbon brick and casting flux, we can add around INR150 crores to INR200 crores on account of these two new product lines at the peak level.

items.statement: Price increases implemented across customers and product categories to offset input cost inflation; benefits to flow through progressively
items.quote: To mitigate these pressures, we have implemented appropriate price increase across customers and product categories. However, given the nature of our business, there is typically a time lag in passing on cost increases with some of the elevated costs being absorbed in near term. We expect the benefits of pricing action

items.statement: Employee cost at ~10% of standalone revenue; management expects to maintain at this level and not exceed
items.quote: If you compare with this quarter 4 number, which is around INR24 crores, there is an increase. If you compare this with quarter 1 FY26, this is at the similar level. So 10%, obviously, this is 10% of overall revenue. And we are trying to manage this, and we do not expect this to go beyond this.

items.statement: Monocon expanding into foundry industry and new geographies including Australia and Saudi Arabia; positive feedback from Mexico and USA markets
items.quote: Also, we are trying to get into the foundry industry, again, primarily with refractories in the similar family and nature of application. And in terms of geographies, it is all spread over. See, Monocon has operations in U.K., China. And we have as you have seen, we have opened an office or company in Australia. Now re

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target 11-13% and EBITDA margin 11.5-12.5%
items.quote: So, for the revenue growth, it would be somewhere between 11% to 13%. That is the kind of growth we are looking forward to during this fiscal. And at EBITDA level, it would be somewhere between 11.5% to 12.5%.

items.statement: Price hike of 4-5% taken in Q1 FY27; no further hikes planned as cotton/yarn prices stabilized
items.quote: So, till date, we have taken just 4% to 5% of price hike. And no other price hike is in picture right now. And the yarn prices and the cotton market is also stagnant, and they are stabilized right now.

items.statement: Targeting double-digit volume growth for FY27 after Q1 volume decline of 1.6%
items.quote: Yes. So, that is our internal target as well. So, we are very hopeful and aggressive towards the fact that in the next three quarters coming ahead, we will be, overall at a company level, we will close this particular fiscal with a double-digit growth, which will be a combination of volume plus value growth.

items.statement: Force NXT grew 7% volume in Q1 but value declined due to innerwear mix shift; premium brands growing 20-25% CAGR
items.quote: In Q1, we did 7% kind of a volume growth, although there has been a value degrowth because the innerwear traction was more than the athleisure.

items.statement: No major capex commitment in near term; focus on free cash flow and debt reduction
items.quote: Given that we have no major capital expenditure commitment in the near term, our capital allocation strategy remains clear. We stay focused on improving free cash flow generation and reducing debt.

items.statement: Thermal season bookings from July conferences show strong trajectory for FY27
items.quote: The conferences that we do in the month of July, pan-India basis and the booking that we got for the thermals is really, it shows the trajectory for this year as well.

items.statement: Not entering new states for Project Lakshya due to market intensity; existing states may face 5-6 month disruption during rollout
items.quote: So, see, given the overall intensity that is going in the market and the external factors that is not letting us to enter new states basically. So, actually, whenever you implement project Lakshya, that states or that area get disturbed for around 5 to 6 months.

items.statement: Targeting zero net debt by FY28; repaid INR 86 crore in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Yes, already we repaid around INR 86 crores in this quarter only. And we are on the target that by FY '28, we reduce our company into the net debt, zero debt policy.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle targeted to improve 6-7 days in FY27 and 15-18 days over 3 years
items.quote: So, for this particular fiscal, we have targeted that around 6 to 7 days improvement we will see as compared to March 26. And over 3 years' time period, it would be a total of somewhere between 15 to 18 days reduction in the overall working capital cycle.

items.statement: Quick commerce channel grew 59.4% value and 15.1% volume YoY, now 5% of revenue
items.quote: The quick commerce channel sustained its strong growth trajectory, recording 59.4% value growth and 15.1% volume growth year-on-year, with its contribution to revenue increasing to 5% in Q1 FY '27 from 3.1% in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: Southern region grew 22.9% value and 7.3% volume YoY, now 8.9% of revenue
items.quote: The southern region delivered 22.9% value growth and 7.3% volume growth on a year-on-year basis, taking its contribution to our overall business to 8.9% in Q1 FY '27 from 7.2% in Q1 FY '26.

items.statement: G.O.A.T JV revenue grew 21% YoY to INR 16.44 crore in Q1 with 13.8% PAT margin; targeting INR 65-75 crore revenue in FY27
items.quote: So, last year, we closed this JV company at around INR 50 crores revenue. And this year, we are in line that we will be able to do INR 65 crores. So, our plan is INR 75 crores and yes, we are in track.

items.statement: Ad spend capped at INR 100 crore annually; expected to moderate to 5% of revenue in FY27 from 5.5% in FY26
items.quote: With our annual advertisement expense capped at INR 100 crores, we expect ad spend as a percentage of revenue to moderate over the coming quarters, it aiding profitability.

items.statement: Management guides for sustained 20%+ organic revenue growth and aims for 10x revenue in ~5 years via organic + M&A
items.quote: if the analysts are modeling us at 20% growth, they should derive confidence from the fact that 95% of business is actually growing at 25%+

items.statement: Internal plans pegged at 25% growth; combined entity post-M&A to maintain 20%+ growth and be EPS-accretive
items.quote: internally they are pegged at 25% growth and we are convinced and seeing the right kind of momentum on the ground to realistically peg ourselves internally on that

items.statement: Q1 FY2027 revenue INR 7.47B, up 20.4% YoY and 3.1% QoQ; highest ever quarterly revenue
items.quote: we delivered revenues of INR 7.47 billion, a growth of 20.4% y-o-y

items.statement: EBITDA margin stable at 22.4% QoQ; PAT margin improved to 16.6% (+60bps QoQ); expect better margin expansion in Developed Markets this FY
items.quote: EBITDA margins also improved from 22.3% to 22.4% q-o-q

items.statement: Average CPCU rate above INR 60; currency-adjusted pass-through to advertisers slightly compressed margins short-term
items.quote: average CPCU rate, which is now above INR 60, but on a currency-adjusted basis, we are actually passing some of the benefit to advertisers

items.statement: Festive quarter demand environment encouraging across key markets; 95% of revenue grew >25% YoY adjusted for RMG/Fintech headwinds
items.quote: As we look ahead to the upcoming festive quarter, we remain encouraged by the demand environment across our key markets

items.statement: Direct advertiser revenue share rose to 79% in Q1 from 74% in FY2026; 100% of business has direct advertiser tech integration
items.quote: direct customer contributed around 79% of the revenue, which was around 74% for the entire FY2026

items.statement: Bobble investment (INR 136 cr) under insolvency; impairment testing deferred pending NCLT appeal outcome
items.quote: impairment would be tested once the appeal is decided in NCLT

items.statement: Larger M&A due diligence underway with third-party advisors; target close by early 2027; funding already raised
items.quote: We aim to close the larger M&A by early 2027 and the identified targets shall accelerate our expansion across Developed Markets

items.statement: AdColony asset acquisition provides strategic SDK, brand trust, and publisher goodwill in Developed Markets without major new cost
items.quote: AdColony, powered by Affle, will have unique differentiations in the way we will unlock value for the ecosystem

items.statement: OCF/PAT conversion 41% in Q1 due to front-loaded FY2026 collections; expected to normalize to 80-85% by Q3
items.quote: You had an up-fronting of the cash flows. This will get normalized when we go into Q2 and Q3. You will see about 80%-85% OCF to PAT ratio by Q3

items.statement: Revenue target of INR3,000 crore by FY30, with INR2,000 crore organic and INR1,000 crore inorganic
items.quote: Our goal is to do about INR2,000 crore from our organic business. The INR1,000 crore inorganic part is something that we are still working on.

items.statement: Bharat Seats revenue target revised to INR3,500 crore by 2030
items.quote: That should be about INR3,500 crore for Bharat Seats by 2030.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR650 crore, to be realized incrementally till 2030
items.quote: The INR650 crore order book should come incrementally till 2030.

items.statement: Annual capex of INR40-50 crore planned for next couple of years
items.quote: The capex should be about INR40 crore to INR50 crore for the next couple of years annually.

items.statement: New products include sunshades (started), seat inserts, seat latch, seatbelt reminder system, ambient lighting (from 2028)
items.quote: In addition to that, we are also going to set up a plant for seat insert, so that is going to be there. There is going to be seat latch and there is going to be a new plant for seatbelt reminder system. In addition to that, there are some new ambient lighting orders that we have received, but that is a smaller part of

items.statement: NDR South plant (Anantapur) to start production in 10-15 days, revenue potential INR70-80 crore at full capacity
items.quote: The revenue potential for that plant is about INR70 crore to INR80 crore, subject to how the model performs.

items.statement: NDR Hayashi JV to continue losses for several quarters until break-even at INR100-150 crore revenue
items.quote: So, we will continue to have losses for some quarters until we touch a break-even point for sales.

items.statement: No customer pressure to reduce selling prices; cost increases offset by operational efficiencies
items.quote: We are not facing any pressure from customers to reduce selling price. We have actually been able to set off our cost increases with operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Bidding for business from Toyota and Kia; non-Maruti revenue ramp-up expected in 2-3 years
items.quote: Maruti is being our core client, we are bidding for business from Toyota and we are bidding for new business with Kia. In addition to that, we are continuously working with the other two OEMs.

items.statement: Aurangabad plant setup contingent on winning Toyota business; Toyota plant delayed to CY29
items.quote: We have got the land at the moment. We are still acquiring business from Toyota. Once we acquire the business, that is when we will look to set up the plant.

items.statement: Non-seat products expected at similar margins; new product ROCEs slightly lower but overall ROCE stable
items.quote: Non-seat should be at similar margins.

items.statement: Marketing, R&D, and hiring expenses to continue as company grows aggressively
items.quote: These expenses will tend to continue as we are trying to grow aggressively. In addition to that, we have also hired some people for our growth.

items.statement: Asset turnover on INR150 crore combined capex expected at approximately 4x
items.quote: So, it should be approximately 4x.

items.statement: Revenue from new strategic manufacturing agreement expected to start from calendar year 2029 with potential of USD90-100 million annually
items.quote: Once all products are commercialized, revenue potential is expected to be approximately USD90 million to USD100 million. Technology transfer activities are planned for completion within 2 years with revenues expected to commence from calendar year 2029.

items.statement: Commercial opportunities and meaningful revenue from China liposomal product in-licensing expected from FY30
items.quote: Given the development time lines involved, we expect commercial opportunities and meaningful revenue contribution to start from FY30, creating another important long-term growth driver for the company.

items.statement: New high-capacity ampoule line at Fontenay facility expected to enter production in early 2027 adding ~30 million ampoules annual capacity
items.quote: This new line is expected to enter production in early 2027 and will add approximately 30 million ampoules of annual capacity for enhancing efficiency, competitiveness and growth potential for the site.

items.statement: Secured multiple new CDMO contracts in Q1 FY27 including a new GLP-1 collaboration
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured multiple new CDMO contracts, including a new GLP-1 collaboration and expanded our pipeline across complex injectables, peptides and drug delivery platforms.

items.statement: Executed strategic manufacturing and supply agreement with leading global pharma for 55 SKUs across 3 sites
items.quote: The current agreement covers 55 SKUs to be manufactured across the 3 sites with scope of adding more products soon.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin at 65% driven by favorable product mix, CDMO contribution, operational efficiencies and procurement initiatives
items.quote: Overall gross margin for the quarter stood at 65%, reflecting the benefits of a favorable product mix, increasing contribution from CDMO projects, improved operational efficiencies and procurement initiatives.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin at 28% with reported EBITDA of INR4,930 million
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA for this quarter stood at INR5,102 million with margins of 28%, while profit after tax was INR3,170 million, reflecting a healthy growth of 47% year-on-year with PAT margin of 18%.

items.statement: US market revenue grew 32% YoY to INR9,810 million driven by recent CDMO launches and volume expansion
items.quote: The United States continues to be our largest market and delivered another strong quarter. Revenues for the quarter stood at INR9,810 million, reflecting a growth of 32% year-on-year.

items.statement: Rest of world revenue flat at INR3,039 million impacted by Saudi Arabia supply disruptions and delayed NUPCO tenders
items.quote: In the rest of the world markets, revenues for the quarter stood at INR3,039 million, broadly in line with the corresponding period last year. While demand across several key markets remain healthy, revenues in the quarter were impacted by supply disruptions in Saudi Arabia.

items.statement: Launched 4 products in US during Q1 FY27; MVI and Dalbavancin ramping up as expected
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched 4 products in the U.S. In Europe and other regulatory markets, revenues for the quarter stood at INR4,488 million, reflecting a growth of 11% year-on-year.

items.statement: Saudi Arabia supply disruptions and delayed NUPCO tender awards impacted rest of world revenue in Q1 FY27
items.quote: While demand across several key markets remain healthy, revenues in the quarter were impacted by supply disruptions in Saudi Arabia, one of our important markets. The award of NUPCO tenders has been delayed, and we expect the results to be announced shortly.

items.statement: Actively progressing multiple brownfield and greenfield expansion initiatives across manufacturing network to support growth
items.quote: Building on our recently announced capex program, we are actively progressing multiple brownfield and greenfield expansion initiatives across our manufacturing network.

items.statement: Targets ~20% revenue CAGR over next 4 years with new CDMO contract; FY27 constant currency growth ~15% achievable, potential upside if bag line approved by Q3
items.quote: But as of now, with this new contract in place, we are looking at 20% -- around 20% growth next 4 years.

items.statement: Targets consolidated EBITDA margin of 30% near term and 35% in 3-4 years as CDMO contracts scale
items.quote: So today, we are at 28% consol EBITDA percent. So near term, we're working towards 30% and we'll see midterm to long term. Ultimately, always we look like a profitable company. We wanted to be a profitable company, hitting those 35% EBITDA.

items.statement: Announced INR2,000 crore capex program; Q1 FY27 spend INR1,132 million; FY27 capex guided at ~INR550 crore with priority on isolator line (INR165 cr) and Neuland API block
items.quote: So this year, we are going to spend about INR550 crores capex. And this will scale up as and when we start building the brownfield, which we already announced earlier.

items.statement: Strategic manufacturing agreement with specialty pharma global company: USD90-100M peak revenue potential, tech transfer starts Sep 2026, first filings in 24 months, commercial launch from CY29 ramping to CY30
items.quote: And the revenues will ramp up from '29 because the filings will start happening from next year. And as soon as the products get approved, especially the U.S. ones are an easier one because it's a CB-30 format. So then it started getting launched in CY29. So it will -- the ramp-up will happen from '29 to '30.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin 65%, adjusted EBITDA margin 28% (up from 25% YoY) driven by CDMO mix, operating leverage, productivity and cost optimization
items.quote: Adjusted for non-cash ESOP expense of INR172 million, adjusted EBITDA stood at INR5,102 million, reflecting an adjusted EBITDA margin of 28%, up from 25% in the corresponding quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: New GLP-1 CDMO contract signed for semaglutide and tirzepatide (US/EU); revenue contribution minimal until FY30-31, mainly tech-transfer fees in near term
items.quote: Very limited. We have not assumed too much of that because the major volume will come from the U.S. when it goes in FY30, '31. So we're not considered much in the next few years other than the tech-transfer fees what we get for transferring.

items.statement: Cenexi Q1 impacted by heat wave delaying quality releases; expects Q2 better than last year as delayed shipments shift forward
items.quote: It really -- I would say it will be better than last year, for sure. Some -- because some releases couldn't happen last quarter because of the heat wave. The impact was more on the quality release. So that will help a better next quarter over the last year, yes.

items.statement: R&D expenditure INR772M (4% of revenue) in Q1 FY27, up 16% YoY, focused on complex injectables, peptides, depot, drug delivery and liposomal products
items.quote: R&D expenditure for the quarter stood at INR772 million, representing approximately 4% of consolidated revenue, an increase from INR723 million in the previous quarter and INR664 million in QI FY26, demonstrating a 16% year-on-year increase.

items.statement: Launched 4 molecules in Q1 including MVI (CGT exclusivity), Dalbavancin, Sugammadex; MVI has limited competition due to manufacturing complexity
items.quote: So the products what we launched, we have launched MVI, multivitamin. We launched Dalba. We also launched the Sugammadex. And the MVI, we have CGT exclusivity. So we don't see competition coming in soon. It's a very difficult product to make.

items.statement: Bag line and ophthalmic capacity constraints may limit FY27 growth to 15% constant currency unless FDA approves bag line by Aug-Sep
items.quote: But we're also looking at a couple of lines like the bag line and ophthalmic products we have tight capacity constraints. Bag line, we're expecting an approval in the third quarter. If it happens as planned, then probably we can cross 15%.

items.statement: Net cash surplus of INR32,939M as of June 30, 2026; cash & equivalents INR35,466M; minimal external debt
items.quote: With healthy cash in hand, we are a net cash surplus company with a net cash position of INR32,939 million.

items.statement: Cenexi targets double-digit EBITDA margin by end of year, up from current 4%
items.quote: So by the end of the year, we want to get into double-digit EBITDA.

items.statement: Cenexi EBITDA margin currently at 4%, improved from 2% last year
items.quote: The profitability is in the same trend like what we said is 4% EBITDA.

items.statement: Base business (ex-Cenexi) grew 24% YoY; US grew 32% YoY; constant currency growth ~19-20%
items.quote: So the base business has grown by 24%.

items.statement: All projections and guidance given on constant currency basis
items.quote: For projection, we take constant currency only. For FX movement, we cannot predict. So all our projection or guidance, what we are giving is the basis of constant currency.

items.statement: Launched MVI (multivitamin with CGT exclusivity), Dalba, and Sugammadex this quarter
items.quote: So the products what we launched, we have launched MVI, multivitamin. We launched Dalba. We also launched the Sugammadex.

items.statement: Liposomal in-licensing product for China (approved via EU RLD) with USD3B market potential in 3 years; rights for US/EU secured
items.quote: It's a USD3 billion product, estimated USD3 billion in the next 3 years. Currently, it's USD1.6 billion globally and U.S. about USD600 million, USD700 million. And so we got rights for U.S. and EU.

items.statement: US injectable market growing 3-4%; Gland growing faster due to new launches and cost advantage
items.quote: If you look at the entire market is growing probably 3% - 4%. But then you have to see which are the products where we don't have and what is our base and what products we actually never launched.

items.statement: Major complex ANDA opportunities (microsphere products) are post-FY29; timing uncertain
items.quote: It's post '29. Some of the big products, especially on the microsphere products, there are a couple of big ones, which is post '29.

items.statement: US revenue run-rate ~USD110-120M; expects growth above market rate from new launches and share gains
items.quote: It's a bit more than USD100 million. It's about USD110 million, USD120 million.

items.statement: Dr Reddy's biologics partnership generating INR50-60 cr/year; slow ramp-up expected in next 1-2 years
items.quote: Currently, it's a normal business, I would say, it's generating around INR50 crores, INR60 crores a year, and probably it will slowly ramp up a bit in next year or two.

items.statement: Profit share revenue ~9% of quarter revenue
items.quote: Profit share is about 9%.

items.statement: Expects to return to historical EBITDA margin trend of 20-22% in FY27, with BMC contract starting Q3 and Atkoli capex reimbursement in Q4 providing margin uplift
items.quote: So, the internal threshold should be to go back to our historical margin trend, but yes, it can be a plus or minus a quarter here and there.

items.statement: Existing portfolio provides 6-9% growth from tipping fee escalation; new contracts add 10-15% incremental growth, though revenue recognition is staggered over 2-3 quarters
items.quote: So our existing portfolio gives us a scope of anywhere between 6% to 9% depending upon the tipping fee escalation that gets registered and clocked in. The new businesses, new scope of additional growth will give us around 10% to 15% additional growth coming from that.

items.statement: Secured ₹243 crore, 5-year contract from Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority for 16 electric road sweepers with 2-year extension option; expected to start Q3 FY27, contribute ~₹46 crore in first year
items.quote: We secured a new contract from the Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority for the procurement and comprehensive O&M of electrical mechanical road sweeping machines, which is across Greater Noida East zone. This is a ₹ 243 crores project over 5 years with a further 2-year extension option. Expected to commence i

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin compressed to 16.8% from 24.4% YoY due to ₹10 crore deferred disposal costs, 18% employee cost increase (34% of revenue), and higher vehicle hiring costs; viewed as transitional
items.quote: The EBITDA came in at ₹ 45 crores, which is down 27% year-on-year and 33% sequentially with EBITDA margin at 16.8% compared to 24.4% in Q1 FY26 and 22.8% in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: Labour cost spike to 34% of revenue (vs historical 30-31%) due to Maharashtra DA rate revision and Labour Code changes; expects normalization over next 3 quarters as escalations kick in
items.quote: If you look at the labour cost as a percentage of revenue, historically, it has been in the range of around 30% to 31%. This time it spiked to 34%, which is an aberration for us. So normally in the next 3 quarters, I think it will be normalized to those levels and then the margin expansion will step in.

items.statement: WtE plant at PCMC to restart by first week of October after safety certification; fixed cost of ₹2.5-3 crore/month during shutdown; full revenue stream from second week of October
items.quote: The WtE plant is expected back by first week of October. During this period, the fixed cost incurred would be in the range of around ₹2.5 crores to ₹3 crore per month for us. So that's like around ₹7 crore will be sitting on our books of accounts. The revenue will start technically from first week or second week of Oct

items.statement: Expects ₹22-24 crore impairment charge from monsoon damage to WtE assets (treated as exceptional item); insurance recovery may offset part; details in Q2 results
items.quote: Based on our current assessment, we expect an impairment charge in the range of around ₹ 22 crores to ₹ 24 crores, which we will treat as an exceptional extraordinary item separate from our core operating performance.

items.statement: Targeting 50-50 revenue split between Collection & Transportation and Processing/WtE (currently ~62% C&T); BMC contract (1,500 TPD from Q3) and Atkoli project (600-800 TPD from Q4) to drive processing growth
items.quote: We used to be essentially 70% Collection and Transportation and 30% of processing. We are actually moving towards 50-50 kind of portfolio, and that's our target.

items.statement: C&D waste plant at BMC now operating at 600-650 TPD (near 600 TPD capacity) after policy mandating builder compliance; achieving industry-leading 96% recycling rate
items.quote: Now we are getting close to 600 to 650 tons per day, and we have a capacity of 600 tons per day, plus or minus 10% that we can process. So, I think that plant has started giving better financial results.

items.statement: Evaluating Compressed Biogas (CBG) projects as part of integrated waste management (wet fraction to CBG, dry to WtE); not viable standalone but strategic for future municipal contracts
items.quote: We have evaluated and we are indeed looking at CGB project, but it's a part of the integrated waste project. What it means is that the city is responsible for sending 1,000 tons of waste. And while the waste-energy plant will take care of the dry fraction, the wet fraction will be sent to the CBG plant.

items.statement: Gross debt ₹435 crore (long-term ~₹300 crore, short-term ~₹135 crore); net debt ₹324 crore; net D/E 0.4x; weighted average cost of debt ~10.1%, expected to trend lower post-refinancing
items.quote: On the balance sheet, as of June 2026, gross debt stood at approximately ₹435 crores with cash and bank balances of around ₹111 crores, translating to a net debt of approximately ₹324 crores and a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.4x.

items.statement: Management expects sustainable revenue growth of at least 15% YoY going forward, with 20-22% looking doable if new products scale successfully.
items.quote: So, moving forward, I believe that our growth level should be at least that or more because now we have larger facilities, a stronger company, much larger product line and a lot of new products to offer as well.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 growth exceeded 15%; management believes FY27 could achieve 15%+ growth if demand recovery sustains.
items.quote: For now, it looks like we could with our Quarter 1 having exceeded 15% growth, and it looks like the demand is recovering well, and we are growing strongly.

items.statement: Total pending capex (capital advances + CWIP) ~INR 180 cr; to be completed by Q2-Q3 FY27. No major new capex planned beyond maintenance (~INR 20-25 cr/yr).
items.quote: Currently, in our balance sheet, total capital advances lying is around INR 20 crores and CWIP is around INR 160 crores. So, our major objective is to complete this whole pending CAPEX. Apart from that, some maintenance CAPEX will only fall in place.

items.statement: Peak revenue potential from 4-year capex plan estimated at INR 750-800 cr (incremental ~INR 400 cr on fixed asset turnover of 0.8x).
items.quote: I would say more like INR 750 crores, what I discussed in our calls earlier. INR 750 crores to INR 800 crores, not INR 900 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 margins hit by 25-50% raw material cost spike; partial price hikes taken in domestic market (full benefit with 1-quarter lag); near-zero hikes in exports.
items.quote: Our key input costs have gone up anywhere in the range of 25% to 50%, putting pressure on gross margins.

items.statement: Domestic demand recovery seen as sustainable; market back to late single-digit growth (8-9% pre-COVID levels).
items.quote: I believe we are almost there to the late single digits where the domestic market traditionally grew at pre-COVID levels.

items.statement: New product portfolio (incl. cell culture) expected to contribute INR 65-70 cr in FY28; Panchla & Amta to contribute 20-25% of standalone revenue in FY28.
items.quote: We could expect from my entire portfolio of new products, approximately INR 65 crores to INR 70 crores in the next year is what we expect from our entire new portfolio.

items.statement: Export business recovered 29% YoY in Q1; customer inquiries and order pipelines recovering with healthy conversion; white-labeling seen as key export growth driver.
items.quote: Our export business from India saw a healthy recovery, growing 29% in the first quarter. Customer inquiries and order pipelines have recovered with healthy momentum, with increasing inquiry levels translating into healthy order conversions.
