items.quote: What's interesting is that the development of these opportunities is coming all together. So, the opportunity also therefore presents challenges in terms of execution bandwidth. And that is what continues to preoccupy us.

items.statement: Export revenue ~Rs 23 cr in Q1 (annualized ~Rs 92 cr); all exclusive contracts; 16% of geographic mix; building structural export engine beyond transactional
items.quote: In absolute terms, the export has grown, I think it is almost Rs. 34 crores and for the quarter, it is around Rs. 23 crores. If you annualize it, you can see it is Rs. 92 crores.

items.statement: Opened FY27 with order book over INR300 cr; delivered >20% in Q1, remaining INR256.8 cr to be executed by Q3
items.quote: We entered FY27 with an opening order book of more than INR300 crores, and our priority for the year is conversion of the opening order book into revenue. We delivered more than 20% of the same in the first quarter.

items.statement: Plan to execute remaining order book of INR256.8 cr by Q3 FY27 per customer timelines
items.quote: We plan to execute and deliver this order book by Q3.

items.statement: No major capex plan beyond ongoing product development; can scale to 3 shifts in existing facility
items.quote: Right now, we do not have a capex plan other than our regular product developmental efforts that will continue in pushing the boundaries for our continued programs that are already there.

items.statement: Raised INR500 cr via QIP; received LoI for up to INR151 cr low-cost long-term debt for YETI under RDI scheme
items.quote: We completed a qualified institutional placement raising INR500 crores with participation from marquee domestic and global institutional investors.

items.statement: INR20,000 cr fast-track drone procurement pipeline from Indian Army; one RFP live, others expected H2 FY27; DAC cleared INR52,000 cr including kamikaze and naval UAS
items.quote: Public reports of INR20,000 crores of drone procurement under the fast-track procurement route from the Indian Army are now seeing the light of the day with one opportunity in the RFP stage, others remain in the approval pipeline with the expectation of RFPs in the second half of the year.

items.statement: Revenue procurement limits for field commanders nearly doubled via revised delegation of financial powers; expect acceleration in Q3-Q4
items.quote: We are also getting positive signals from the field, and we believe that this development would accelerate procurement activities in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Q1 revenue mix 60% defense / 40% civil vs typical 70/30; defense has higher margin due to EW resilience requirement
items.quote: Today, because EW resilience is a necessity on the defence side, that business has more margin contribution than the civil business, which is not delivering an EW resilient product.

items.statement: Supply chain pressure on thermal cameras and electronic components causing timeline delays; not currently impacting customer delivery commitments
items.quote: Due to the current ongoing geopolitical conflicts, there is a pressure on the supply chain of thermal cameras and the electronic supply chain also is seeing a certain pressure where the timeline delays are happening.

items.statement: YETI middle-mile logistics UAV completed tethered hover test; designed for 6,500m takeoff altitude, 200kg payload; only platform with this capability
items.quote: YETI, in my opinion, is the only platform in the world from whatever we have searched that is designed to take off at 6,500 meters takeoff altitude.

items.statement: Q6 V2 GEO received DGCA Type Certification; 6 platforms now type certified; enables GIS, mapping, urban planning, digital twin use cases
items.quote: Our Q6 V2 GEO received DGCA Type Certification, opening up advanced GIS use cases across large-scale mapping, urban planning and digital twin applications. Six of our UAV platforms are now type certified by DGCA.

items.statement: Advancing combat capabilities: air-launched effects, fuel-hybrid ZOLT, loitering munitions, long-range strike platforms with partners; targeting upcoming large defense opportunities
items.quote: In Q1, we made significant progress in the development of combat drone capabilities like air-launched effects and fuel-hybrid long-endurance capability for ZOLT. We are also in advanced stages of developing combat capabilities like long-range strike platforms and loitering munitions along with our partners.

items.statement: Deployed fleet crossed 1 million customer missions; drone takes off every 2 minutes globally; operates in extreme altitudes, temperatures, EW environments
items.quote: I'm elated to share that during the quarter; our deployed fleet crossed the milestone of 1 million customer missions. Across our fleet today an ideaForge drone takes off somewhere in the world every 2 minutes.

items.statement: US operations: focusing on JV operationalization and Blue sUAS certification; exploring USD30M+ defense programs; international NFR orders from partners in Europe, Middle East, South America, Africa
items.quote: In fact, I feel that at least one of the programs that is live right now is about a USD30 million program, where they have many players who will be participating.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth guidance retained at 20%+ (implying >INR10,000 cr vs FY26 INR8,430 cr); will revisit after Q3
items.quote: We remain focused on achieving 20%+ value growth for the financial year, building the Senco brand across the country, reaching more customers and expanding through both owned and franchise stores, with a geographical focus on East and North India.

items.statement: Added 3 COCO, 4 franchise, 1 Sennes store in Q1; 12-15 more stores planned for rest of FY27, majority franchise, focused on East and North India
items.quote: In terms of new stores added during the quarter, we added 3 company-owned, company-operated stores, 4 franchise stores and 1 Sennes showroom focused on lab-grown diamonds. The company remains on track to open another 12 to 15 stores during the remainder of the financial year, and these are very much in the pipeline.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 7% (INR213 cr) vs guided sustainable 7.5%-7.8%; impacted by gold price fall, discounting, old gold exchange; customs duty gain ~INR12-15 cr
items.quote: As noted in our comments, this quarter's margins were affected by the fall in gold prices, competitive intensity and discounting, partly offset by the customs-duty impact. That is the broader context in which the 7% EBITDA margin should be viewed.

items.statement: Q1 FY26 reported 10.1% EBITDA included 1.5-2% inventory gains; adjusted PAT ~INR70-75 cr vs Q1 FY27 PAT INR101 cr
items.quote: Q1 last year benefited from a price rise, and we clarified at the time that although the reported EBITDA margin was 10.1%, our sustainable EBITDA margin was between 7.5% and 7.8%.

items.statement: Customs duty increase benefit estimated at INR12-15 cr in Q1 (45 days impact); further benefit expected over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: We estimate that the customs-duty gain in Q1 was around INR12-15 crores. This benefit will be partly offset by customer schemes, discounts and other promotional measures, but INR12-15 crores is the estimated gross range for the quarter.

items.statement: July-August tracking ~25% YoY growth, 8-10% above May-June run rate; Q2 seasonally softer, focus on inventory build for festive season
items.quote: As we move through July and August, we are seeing a substantial improvement in consumer sentiment and in customers' inclination to buy jewellery and prepare for their festive and wedding requirements.

items.statement: Hedging maintained at ~50% under Board policy due to volatility; intend to move toward 75-80% as conditions stabilise; GML availability constrained in Mar-Apr, now normalised
items.quote: Our hedging strategy is guided by the Board-approved policy. At present, we are maintaining hedging at approximately 50% because the last financial year saw extreme volatility. We need to balance liquidity risk with the risk of gold-price movements.

items.statement: Other expenses rose to INR195 cr (from ~INR80 cr) on store renovations, customer schemes, brand building; management says this run rate will not continue and will subside in upcoming quarters
items.quote: Exactly. This run rate will not continue, and we expect it to subside in the upcoming quarters.

items.statement: Inventory days at ~152; improved stock turnover by end of Q1; will build inventory again from September for festive season
items.quote: Inventory days are currently around 152, as stated in the presentation. We will continue to work on improving this further.

items.statement: Sennes (lab-grown diamond, perfume, leather) and Dubai subsidiary in start-up phase, weighed on consolidated PAT (3.3% margin)
items.quote: However, the Sennes brand is still in its start-up phase and is developing its lab-grown diamond, perfume and leather-bag businesses. Any new brand takes time. Sennes Fashion Limited and the Dubai entity therefore partly affected consolidated PAT, which was nevertheless at a margin of 3.3%.

items.statement: Launched Aham men's jewellery collection combining titanium with gold/diamonds, priced INR20,000-1 lakh; among first in industry with titanium jewellery
items.quote: I can proudly say that, consistent with Senco's focus on innovation, we are among the first in the industry to launch titanium jewellery. While gold and diamonds are incorporated in the jewellery and contribute to margins, the addition of titanium keeps the overall price range affordable. The range starts at about INR2

name: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth to exceed FY26's 37% YoY; EBITDA margin target upwards of 24%; ARPOB growth 9-10% YoY
items.quote: I think we have said that last year, we grew 37% Y-o-Y. As you can clearly see this year, we will easily surpass that growth even the EBITDA is concerned. I think the company is on track close to upwards of 24% EBITDA margin for the full FY27 is concerned. And I think similar is the ARPOB growth and the PAT parameters.

items.statement: ARPOB growth guided at 9-10% YoY for FY27
items.quote: I think 9% to 10% is the right estimation to be taken.

items.statement: Capex per bed for next 1,800 beds estimated at INR 75-80 lakhs; Gurugram at ~INR 1 crore per bed
items.quote: I think the capex per bed should be around INR75 lakhs to INR80 lakhs capex per bed, which includes the greenfield, the brownfield, the acquisitions.

items.statement: Bed capacity target of 5,000 beds to be achieved in ~2.5 years (earlier than 3-year target); 3,200 beds already announced/under construction
items.quote: I think it should be even less than three years. So, we did mention last time around three years, so as we also mentioned that we will be surpassing that target much earlier as 3200-bed capacity is already visible and it's already announced.

items.statement: New hospitals (Faridabad Sec 20, Model Town) to reach 15-20% EBITDA within 15-18 months post-breakeven; mature units at 25-27%
items.quote: Both these 2 hospitals, from here, we are targeting, let's say, around 15 months, once they get breakeven, the EBITDA there could be somewhere around 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Room rent capping recommendation viewed as non-material risk; government historically supports private sector; past price caps (stents, implants) absorbed
items.quote: So far, we have always seen that government, in fact, has always supported the growth of private hospitals. In fact, for the first time after a lot of years, CGHS's rates were also revised. So, we feel in the past, government has always backed the private sector as well.

items.statement: Occupancy at mature Noida/Jhansi hospitals at 90%+; Greater Noida 74%, Noida Extension 56% with improvement expected; new hospitals ramping volumes
items.quote: Our existing hospital occupancy reached approximately 75% as inpatient volume improved 15% year-over-year. As far as hospital-wise occupancy is concerned, Noida and Jhansi-Orchha Hospital achieved 90% plus occupancy.

items.statement: Oncology contributing ~10% of group revenue; adding LINAC at Faridabad Sec 20 and New Delhi to strengthen oncology; surgical mix improving in new hospitals
items.quote: Oncology has already started contributing close to 10% to the group's revenue with only one LINAC machine currently at Noida Extension Hospital. We are in the process of adding another LINAC at our Faridabad Sector 20 hospital soon, followed by the New Delhi facility.

items.statement: PAT margin pressure from higher depreciation and interest cost due to recent capex (Gurugram, oncology machines); pressure to ease as capex slows
items.quote: I think it's because we have done certain high capex over last few months as far as the acquisition of Gurgaon and the construction is going on. Also, we have recently ordered for oncology machines for both Faridabad and Model Town. So, a lot of capex has been done in this quarter and a bit of bank debt increasing sinc

items.statement: Debt increased from INR 210 Cr to ~INR 300 Cr (INR 80 Cr for acquisition); future capex funded via internal accruals and debt; comfortable with 2x TTM EBITDA leverage
items.quote: If you see that we have a debt in our books in March of nearly around INR210 crores which is now being increased to around INR300 crores. Basically, it has increased because we have partly taken the acquisition fund from the debts around INR80 crores.

items.statement: Model Town Hospital EBITDA breakeven expected between Q3-Q4 FY27; Faridabad Sec 20 achieved breakeven in Q1 FY27 (9 months)
items.quote: Model town, we are expecting it to break even, somewhere around, between Q3, Q4 this year, so that will also reduce the drag on EBITDA.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion at Greater Noida and Noida Extension (450 beds) to start coming live in 15-18 months; Gurugram (250 beds) live by Q1 FY28
items.quote: We feel, as mentioned earlier in the fall, somewhere around 15 to 18 months in the capacity will start coming live for the Brownfield capacity expansion.

items.statement: EBITDA per TEU expected to remain around INR 2,400 level going forward
items.quote: Going forward, we expect EBITDA per TEU to remain around INR2,400 level.

items.statement: Target EBITDA per TEU of INR 2,750 in 3-year plan including Farukhnagar ICD
items.quote: In our 3 years plan, we have targeted EBITDA per TEU of INR2,750. That's including Farukhnagar project.

items.statement: Endeavor to maintain EBITDA per TEU in range of INR 2,400 to INR 2,500
items.quote: We will endeavor to maintain profitability, EBITDA per TEU numbers in the range of INR2,400 to INR2,500 per TEU.

items.statement: Total capex plan of INR 400 crores over 3 years (Plan 2030), with INR 100 crores in FY27
items.quote: Close to INR100 crores of that capex we should incur in the current financial year, '26-27.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved from 17% to 22%+ over 2-3 years; expect to maintain current profitability levels
items.quote: We expect the profitability numbers to hover around the current level because as you know, the market is very competitive.

items.statement: Revenue per TEU increased from INR 11,000-11,500 to INR 13,000; 50% yield management, 50% operational efficiencies
items.quote: Now that is something which we have been able to push at INR13,000 per TEU in the current financial quarter.

items.statement: Container volumes grew 7% YoY in Q1 FY27; India trade fundamentals remain strong despite global uncertainty
items.quote: Our container volumes grew 7% year-on-year, demonstrating the resilience of our business model.

items.statement: Higher share of transhipment containers and upward rate revisions drove Q1 profitability improvement
items.quote: The improvement in profitability came on the back of operational efficiencies supported by technology improvements and by higher share of transhipment containers volume plus upward rate revisions at various locations.

items.statement: No dividend payout planned currently; prioritizing capex for growth projects over shareholder returns
items.quote: As of now, because considering the plans which we are having, we are staying away from declaring dividend at this point of time.

items.statement: myCFS app adoption at 70-80% monthly usage among CHAs; automates 70% of import workflow
items.quote: We have seen an adoption rate ranging monthly usage rate ranging between 70% and 80% amongst the CHA community.

items.statement: Farukhnagar ICD to handle 20-25% domestic and 75-80% EXIM rail volumes
items.quote: The volumes that this terminal will handle will be in the range of 20% to 25% domestic and about 75% to 80% EXIM.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target ~15% and EBITDA margin upwards of 10%
items.quote: For financial year 27, our objective remains to deliver approximately 15% revenue growth and EBITDA margins on upwards of 10%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 11-12% for FY27
items.quote: Our target this year is to achieve 11 -12%, more than 10%.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization expected to reach 70-75% by year end
items.quote: Overall, it will be around 70-75%.

items.statement: Kutch new facility investment Rs 20-25 crore for 10,000 IBC units/month, commissioning by March 2027
items.quote: We are investing approximately 20 to 25 crore in a new facility with a capacity of 10,000 IBC units per month, which is expected to be commissioned by March 2027.

items.statement: Kutch plant revenue potential Rs 50 crore initially, up to Rs 100 crore at full capacity
items.quote: It is a 100 crore business, but we are going by 50 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton increased to Rs 16,380 in Q1 FY27 vs Rs 11,252 in Q1 FY26 and Rs 15,053 in Q4 FY26
items.quote: EBITDA per ton increased to approximately 16 ,380 in Q 1 FY26 compared with 11 ,252 in Q1 FY26 and 15 ,053 in Q4FY26.

items.statement: Gross margin compressed to 23% in Q1 FY27 as raw material costs rose with price increases
items.quote: Gross profit rose 19% year -on-basis, but gross margin compressed a little to 23% as raw material costs rose in step with price increase.

items.statement: Gross margin expected to return to 26-27% as polymer prices normalize
items.quote: So we should have this understanding that this year also we will match the number of 26-27% in gross profit.

items.statement: Polymer drum selling price at Rs 193/kg in Q1 FY27 vs Rs 138/kg in Q4 FY26; expects price to settle at Rs 140/kg in 5-6 months
items.quote: In the last quarter, our selling price was Rs.138 in March. This time, my selling price of polymer drums is Rs.193 per kg. The selling price has increased by Rs.55.

items.statement: Raw material cost pass-through maintained; EBITDA per ton resilient despite volume decline
items.quote: This clearly demonstrates that despite the temporary volume impact, our pricing, product mix, and operating efficiency are supporting profitability at the unit level.

items.statement: Export volumes impacted by Middle East war and freight costs; expects recovery next quarter as rates normalize
items.quote: In the middle east, due to the war, freight cost has grown significantly, so there is a problem in export, we are not able to export. For this, it is growing by 2 -4% this quarter. And the growth that was supposed to happen has not happened, so everything should match from the next quarter.

items.statement: Wada facility contributed Rs 43 crore (19% of revenue) in Q1 FY27, operating above 70% utilization, targeting 80%
items.quote: Our WADA facility is in full swing now across HDPE, IBCs, and MS Drums, and is already operating above 70% utilization. We expect it to reach 80% during this year. The facility contributed approximately 43 crore or 19% of revenue from operations in this quarter, Q1 FY27.

items.statement: Reiterated FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15% year-on-year
items.quote: Despite the prevailing geopolitical uncertainty and the challenges arising from West Asia situation, we remain confident in the underlying demand environment and reiterate our FY27 revenue growth guidance of 15%.

items.statement: Placed order for fourth stainless steel bottle manufacturing line; commissioning expected by Q4 FY27, increasing capacity by 30-35%
items.quote: The order for the fourth next-generation manufacturing line has recently been placed and its commissioning is expected by Q4 '27. The new line is expected to increase our manufacturing capacity by approximately 35%.

items.statement: Incurred INR43.42 crores capex in Q1 FY27, including INR33.25 crores for Valsad factory building
items.quote: During Q1, the company incurred a total capital expenditure of INR43.42 crores, of which INR33.25 crores was capitalized towards the factory building in Valsad facility.

items.statement: Implemented selective price increases across all three segments and rationalized trade schemes/discounts to protect margins
items.quote: We have also taken proactive measures to protect margins, including rationalizing schemes and discounts and implementing selective price increases across all our three segments of businesses: Writing Instrument, Creatives, and Steel Bottle and Houseware business.

items.statement: Pen segment expected to grow at high single-digit; Creative and Steel Bottles at ~40% growth for FY27
items.quote: As far as category-wise is concerned, as we had always mentioned that it's going to be high single digit in Writing Instruments for us, the growth. Creative and Steel Bottles will, of course, higher number digits, like about almost 40%.

items.statement: Marketing spend guided at 8-10% of revenue for full year FY27
items.quote: Marketing investment during the quarter was approximately 8.5% of revenue, which is in line with our full year guidance of 8% to 10% through FY27.

items.statement: Targeting mid-single-digit same-store revenue growth for FY27
items.quote: we are looking to increase the same-store revenue in the mid-single-digit numbers. That's what we are aiming to do for this year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 gross margin at 61.6%, EBITDA margin at 21.2%, PAT margin at 1.8%
items.quote: Gross profit stood at INR77.2 crores with a GP margin of 61.6% for the quarter. EBITDA stood at INR26.6 crores. Our EBITDA margin stood at 21.2%. Profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR2.3 crores. Our PAT margin stood at 1.8% for the quarter.

items.statement: Near-term demand visibility uneven; discretionary spending soft but positive signals from renovated stores
items.quote: While near-term demand visibility may remain uneven, we believe Mufti 2.0 is building a stronger foundation for the brand's next phase of growth.

items.statement: Unable to extrapolate growth numbers for next couple of years; transformation impact longer-drawn
items.quote: for the next 2-odd years, it's going to be very difficult for us to say what exactly the numbers will pan out.

items.statement: Inventory days expected to reduce; no inventory write-offs in company history
items.quote: there should be some reduction in the inventory days. That is always the endeavour to.

items.statement: Industry AC growth expected ~20% in FY27; EPACK aims to surpass industry growth; SDA/LDA growing faster than RAC; no specific company revenue guidance given
items.quote: For AC, we are very confident that this year, the industry is expected to grow at around 20%. So we would definitely surpass the industry growth as we have done it in Q1. items.quote: Net cash stood at ₹7,100 crore as of June 30th, against ₹7,500 crore at March-end and this is after the ₹1,473 crore dividend payout during the quarter. Auto ROCE continued to be strong at 68% on a trailing twelve-month basis, against 72% for FY26.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 revenue target of Rs 750 crore and EBITDA margin around 17%
items.quote: Let me close my remarks by recreating our guidance of Rs. 750 crores in revenue for FY '27 at an EBITDA margin of around 17%.

items.statement: Q1 revenue of Rs 182 crore represents ~24% of FY27 target, ahead of 45:55 H1:H2 split
items.quote: The 1st Quarter therefore represents approximately 24% of our full-year revenue target of Rs. 750 crores. That is ahead of where the 1st Quarter needs to be, given our guidance that the year splits 45:55 between the two halves.

items.statement: Saicriti facility at Gummadidala on track for April 2027 completion, adds 154.66M units injectable capacity (47% more than original plan)
items.quote: This proposed route delivers approximately 154.66 million units of injectable capacity against approximately 105 million units under the original upgradation plan. That is roughly 47% more capacity on a larger and long-lived asset, at an unchanged CAPEX outlet from the company and with the completion extended only abou

items.statement: Australian facility physical completion targeted January 2027, TGA inspection by March 2027, Phase 1 manufacturing from April 2027
items.quote: Construction is on schedule with physical completion targeted for January 2027. The TGA licensing inspection anticipated by 31st March 2027 and Phase 1 manufacturing expected from April 2027.

items.statement: Contracts have 90-120 day lag for price revisions; recovery of raw material cost increases partial, full benefit expected in Q2 FY27
items.quote: Our contracts carry a window of 90-120 days between a price revision being notified and being realized. That lag is now beginning to unwind in our favor. The recovery of raw material cost increases remain partial at this stage, and we expect full further benefit to flow across the contract book through the 2nd Quarter.

items.statement: Noumed holds 5 exclusive long-term contracts and 10 exclusive supply molecule contracts covering 526 SKUs with 5+ year terms
items.quote: Today, we hold 5 exclusive long-term contracts and we hold 10 exclusive supply molecule contracts, covering 526 SKUs. The typical terms are 5 years and more.

items.statement: Peak debt expected in FY27 with de-leveraging from FY28; gross debt/equity comfortable at 0.6x; Saicriti project debt at subsidiary level
items.quote: FY '27 is expected to be a peak year of debt growth for the existing business as we complete the ongoing CAPEX and Acquisition Program with de-leveraging from FY '28 as these assets begin to contribute to earnings and cash flows. Even at peak debt, the gross debt to equity ratio is comfortably placed at 0.6 times.

items.statement: Prathyak Labs acquisition brings 65-person R&D team (28 scientists), 150 SKUs across 86 molecules in complex injectables (lyophilised, liposomal, nano, oncology)
items.quote: Prathyak operates an established research and development center at the Genome Valley in Hyderabad with 3 years of operating history, 65 personnel including 28 research scientists and a pipeline of 150 SKUs across 86 molecules with proven capability in lyophilised, liposomal and nano-based complex injectables and in on

items.statement: US subsidiary incorporation approved for preliminary market entry evaluation; no timeline or strategy finalized
items.quote: The Board also has approved the incorporation of the subsidiary in the United States to be held as a step-down subsidiary through Sai Parenterals PTE Singapore. The entity is being created to support the company's evaluation of an entry into the United States market. This evaluation is at a preliminary stage.

items.statement: Guided FY27 revenue growth of 20-25%, similar to FY26 trajectory
items.quote: So this year we will be keeping a same growth trajectory what we have posted last year, around 20% to 25% growth range we will be trying to keep.

items.statement: Current order book of INR100 crores executable in Q2 and partly Q3 FY27
items.quote: Yeah, so like I said, the current order book stands at INR100 crores.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR25-30 crores over 1-1.5 years for Nashik premix facility redevelopment, 70% debt-funded
items.quote: So overall capex -- so as you are aware that one strategic, there is a demolition happening at our Nashik factory for our premix facility, and it is redeveloping with the new infrastructure, for that we will be incurring a capex roughly around INR25 crores to INR30 crores in the coming one year or maybe one and a half

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 11.3% in Q1 FY27 from 13.8% in Q1 FY26 due to raw material cost increases from West Asia crisis
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin stood at 11.3% during the quarter compared with 13.8% in Q1 FY '26. The movement in EBITDA margin needs to be viewed in the context of the business and the product mix during the quarter, along with the investments being made to support our next phase of the growth.

items.statement: MRP increased 10-15% on select branded products to pass through raw material cost increases, impact visible from Q2
items.quote: Approx 10 % to 15% we have increased our MRP. So that will see a impact in the Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Strong order book of INR100 crores supports Q2 FY27; historically Q3-Q4 are stronger quarters due to seasonality
items.quote: No, in fact our Q2 is very strongly supported by a strong order book of around INR100 crores. Okay. So there is definitely no sign of a slowdown in the quarter two.

items.statement: Branded segment grew 28% YoY, now ~30% of revenue; target 35% in next couple of years
items.quote: So in the next couple of years we expect that to go to that 35% mark.

items.statement: Capacity utilization improved to 47% blended in Q1 FY27 from ~30% last year; Nashik at 55-60%, Chennai 25-30%, Tuticorin 35-40%
items.quote: So overall, capacity-wise we have seen a volume growth this quarter, which representing around 47% of total capacity utilization at this stage.

items.statement: West Asia crisis increased freight costs and critical raw material prices (whey proteins), impacting gross margin by >3%
items.quote: The major reason is the West Asia crisis where we have seen few of our critical raw materials in our segments in premix as well as branded has seen a rise in the cost.

items.statement: ESG order pipeline of INR75-100 crores for FY27 from national governments and UN agencies
items.quote: Right. So we will be looking at around INR75 crores to INR100 crores. For the year. Yeah.

items.statement: Volume growth of 25-40% YoY in Q1 FY27 across premix and branded segments; price hikes not main driver
items.quote: So overall, if you see the volume mix, the volume has grown roughly around 25% to 40% for this quarter.

items.statement: Field force increased >50% YoY to expand into Tier 2/3 cities; operating leverage expected by Q3 FY27
items.quote: More than 50% of our field force have increased compared to last year Q1. And we see this as an investment which has impacted the bottom line at this moment, but definitely it will add value in the next coming quarters.

items.statement: International growth driven by Central Asia and Africa; targeting Europe and North America expansion
items.quote: Yeah, so we are looking at a good growth in areas like Central Asia and also Africa. And going forward we are also looking for newer geographies which include Europe and North America.

items.statement: Management will not provide formal forward-looking revenue or profitability guidance due to structural uncertainties in approvals, government tenders, and global volatility.
items.quote: We intend to stick to a policy of not providing formal, forward-looking guidance.

items.statement: EBITDA margin for FY27 expected to be similar to FY25-FY26 blended levels (~27%), with less dramatic quarterly volatility than seen in FY26.
items.quote: If you look at '25 and '26, I think there would be reasonable guides for, I mean, we should expect very similar numbers in '27 for EBITDA as a percentage.

items.statement: No significant capex planned for core business in FY27-FY28; only maintenance capex of 5-10% of gross block annually, plus potential debottlenecking if large orders materialize.
items.quote: For maintenance capex, I mean, you can look at, I think at any point in time, it will be a few percentage points, that is required. So, one can say that between 5% to 10% of your gross block at any point in time you can assume is a maintenance capex that you have to keep doing.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue of INR247.2 cr driven significantly by ready parachute contract execution; Q4 FY26 was anomaly due to pulled-forward US exports and parachute shipments.
items.quote: This growth was primarily driven by execution of our ready parachute contracts which scaled meaningfully during the quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 31% (up 900bps YoY) due to richer product mix including parachute contracts; sequential decline from 41% in Q4 FY26 due to lower operating leverage off elevated base.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR75.9 crores at a margin of approximately 31%. Year on year basis, this represents a margin expansion of roughly 900 basis points from the 22% in Q1 FY26, driven by a richer higher margin product mix including the ready parachute contracts.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization 55-60%; large capex came fully online last year, management hopes for full utilization but business growth depends on approvals.
items.quote: However, on utilization, I would be I would say we are currently between I would say 55% to 60% utilization. We did a very large capex, that sort of came fully online last year.

items.statement: Management does not disclose executable order book; orders exist in stages (POs, LOIs, projections) making parsing difficult. FY27 expected to be steady growth year with moderate volatility.
items.quote: At any point in time, sir, we have orders that are in various stages. One is where we have received formal POs, then the second is where we have LOIs, and then the third is where we have projections. It becomes difficult for us to sort of parse these numbers and be able to sir, exactly tell you which of these will get

items.statement: Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in FY27; receivables normalized after Q4 FY26 anomaly.
items.quote: I think it will be positive sir. It is positive only, sir. Yes, sir.

items.statement: Parachute systems executed under licensing agreement with technology partner, not own IP.
items.quote: Yes, they are, so it's under a licensing agreement. That's right. With one of our technology partners, sir.

items.statement: Outdoor & Lifestyle segment capacity not a constraint; growth driven by progressive brand approvals and seasonal volume ramps; brand projections strong but subject to material changes.
items.quote: The outdoor and lifestyle business, I mean, capacity at this point of time is not really a constraint for us. It's progressive product approvals, that brand by brand, customer by customer, we continue to get approvals.

items.statement: Company operates 7 manufacturing facilities (6 Gujarat, 1 UP) with full vertical integration; 1000+ fabric SKUs; 2000+ employees; exports growing.
items.quote: We operate seven manufacturing facilities, six in Gujarat and one in UP, spanning the full value chain from preparatory and weaving through dyeing, printing, finishing, coating, lamination, and fabrication of certain specialized products.

items.statement: Aim to reach 2 million tons LPG distribution volume in coming years, targeting 50% growth rate
items.quote: We have always had aim to reach 2 million tons in distribution in coming times ahead.

items.statement: JNPA Port: executing ~318,100 cbm liquid, 77,236 MT LPG, bottling plant 35k MT/yr at ~INR1,675 crore; Phase 1 (100k cbm) Q3 FY27
items.quote: executing a major expansion of approximately 318,100 cubic meters of additional liquid storage, 77,236 metric tons of LPG capacity and an LPG bottling plant with 35,000 metric tons of annual capacity with a total capital outlay of roughly INR1,675 crores

items.statement: JNPA Board approved 52,000 MT refrigerated double-walled steel LPG tank
items.quote: the Board of Directors in its recent meeting has approved the development of a 52,000 metric ton refrigerated double-walled steel LPG tank at JNPA

items.statement: Targeting gearing ratio ~0.6; funding $5B capex via balanced mix of equity, internal accruals, debt; Aegis Vopak self-funded via equity dilution
items.quote: We'll pursue this growth with disciplined funding through balanced mix of equity, internal accruals and debt, targeting a gearing ratio of approximately 0.6

items.statement: CPG division targets quarterly breakeven in 4-5 quarters via margin-accretive model
items.quote: In terms of a quarterly breakeven for this business, we are working towards another 4 or 5 quarters. We should have a quarterly breakeven on this business.

items.statement: Nutra EBITDA margin steady state expected at 12-15% once scale normalizes
items.quote: From an EBITDA margin perspective, steady state is likely between 12% and 15%.

items.statement: Jaggery plant in Karnataka to commission in 6 months, will more than double capacity
items.quote: The plant will be commissioned in 6 months' time. It is coming up in Karnataka. It will more than double our current jaggery capacity.

items.statement: Jaggery turnover from both plants expected near Rs 100 crore once fully running
items.quote: Once we have both plants running, we should be able to do closer to Rs. 100 crores in terms of turnover, just from both of these plants.

items.statement: Sugar prices moved above Rs 45-46/kg; may correct once crushing starts
items.quote: In the current month, sugar prices have moved well north of Rs. 45-Rs.46 per kg. We will need to wait and see if these hold. Perhaps once crushing starts, it is very likely that there may be some correction.

items.statement: TN/AP cane availability declining; expect flat to 5% drop in crush this season
items.quote: In the current year, yes, probably there is going to be a flat or about a 5% drop in these geographies.

items.statement: Employee cost rose due to VSS at legacy plants; more VSS planned to reduce fixed costs
items.quote: They have gone up because of VSS which we have done. A lot of our legacy plants we are offering VSS. You will see more of that. This is being done with a longer term interest in mind. And overall bringing the fixed cost position down.

items.statement: Ethanol-sugar mix optimized dynamically; 582 KLPD ethanol capacity (120 KLPD grain); OMC commitments limit switching
items.quote: 582 KLPD is our capacity, which is roughly about Rs. 18 crore liters, out of which about 120 KLPD is our grain capacity. In terms of switching between ethanol and sugar that is an evaluated call we have to take depending on the margin profit.

items.statement: CPG shift to value-added products (jaggery, brown sugar) and distribution expansion driving margin pool growth despite revenue decline
items.quote: Yes, value mix shifting more towards value-added. I think you have seen that shift play out in Quarter 1. We will see more of that play out. I think adding new products, jaggery, brown sugar, etc., is a big area of focus.

items.statement: JLR targets 10% revenue growth per annum with significant focus on US market
items.quote: So we are setting a goal of 10% revenue growth per annum and focusing on the US market for a significant part of that.

items.statement: JLR aims to save $1.7 billion on ex-works cost, warranty, and fixed cost base
items.quote: On costs, our focus is the ex-works cost of our cars, warranty, and our fixed cost base. And our intent is to save $1.7 billion in this space.

items.statement: TMPV targets higher double-digit volume growth in FY27, maintaining ~2x industry growth pace
items.quote: We would like to keep that kind of momentum going forward. So, I would definitely be targeting higher double-digit growths in FY 27.

items.statement: TMPV capex at Rs 1,300 Cr in Q1; will step up for next growth phase per Investor Day guidance
items.quote: Our Capex at Rs. 1,300 Cr for the quarter, this is still tracking last year's trends, but we will see it step-up as we execute our next phase of growth in line with our Investor Day guidance.

items.statement: JLR Q1 EBIT margin 2.8%; VME rose to 7.1% driven by China luxury taxes and US market normalization
items.quote: VME in the second big column is significantly higher. It's now at 7.1%. China is the most difficult market year-over-year for us given economic and retailer stress and also the effect of the new luxury taxes that came into force after Q1 last year.

items.statement: TMPV took cumulative 1% price increase (0.5% each in April and July); will take further calibrated increases through year
items.quote: We have already taken a 1% cumulative price increase across April and July and while we will be taking calibrated increases through the rest of the year...

items.statement: TMPV accelerating cost reduction initiatives; achieved 1.5% benefit in Q1, expecting incremental gains in Q2
items.quote: We are also having strong cost reduction programs that we are accelerating. We had a 2% benefit YoY. In Q1 itself, we had 1.5%. We'll get incrementally more this quarter.

items.statement: Revenue growth momentum expected to continue for 3-4 quarters; freight rates rising is positive for freight forwarding
items.quote: I would not put any number, but this growth momentum would continue for coming quarters, three to four quarters, which we have seen in first quarter also.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 275 bps YoY to 9.34% in Q1 FY27; further improvement expected from technology and cost rationalization
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin also improved to 9.34% from 6.59%, effective increase of 275 basis points.

items.statement: Warehousing gross margin is 15-20%; contribution expected to grow from 15% to 17-18% by year-end and ~20% eventually
items.quote: But on absolute margin if you talk about it is 15 % to 16% gross margin at which we operate in the warehousing business, 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Volume growth 6-7% YoY in Q1; rest of 18.4% revenue growth from freight rate increases due to geopolitical volatility
items.quote: If you see the number of shipment, the shipment growth is around 6% to 7% as compared to last year. And rest of the growth has been happen from the freight rates.

items.statement: Asset-light model to continue; investments primarily in technology (AI-based application launched July 1) and selective leased warehousing
items.quote: Whatever the investment will happen will happen primarily means as of now it's primarily focusing on asset-light model only.

items.statement: Ocean export freight rates rising; air freight benefiting from cargo shifting from ocean; this incremental profitability expected to continue 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Incremental profitability in our industry is in ocean exports, if the ocean exports right now going up because the freight rates are going up.

items.statement: Freight rate growth sustainability may not be long-term; volume growth essential for India's export economy
items.quote: The freight growth sustainability may not be very long term. So our growth has been a mix of 6 %, 7% growth in the volume growth and another growth is the freight rate growth.

items.statement: DSO improved from 72 days to 56-57 days; working capital discipline supporting operating profitability
items.quote: At one point of time our DSO or collection cycle increased to almost 72 days, which has come down now to 57 day, 56 days.

items.statement: AI-based application launched July 1 automating 42,000 annual shipments; reducing paperwork, TAT, and manpower costs
items.quote: We have almost we have done 40,000 shipments last year, 42,000 shipments. So we created 42,000 files manually. Now we are basically automating this entire process.

items.statement: Targeting 20% revenue growth for FY27; Q1 achieved 18% growth
items.quote: So the 20%, as I said, that is definitely what we are working towards. And Q1 has been at 18% growth, as far as revenue is concerned.

items.statement: Engineering capex ~INR400 crores for stamping capacity in Gujarat, Gurgaon, Bangalore; land acquired in Gujarat
items.quote: We are investing in Stamping capacity enhancement in Gujarat, in Gurgaon and in Bangalore. So in these 3 places, we -- as you might be knowing, we have acquired land in Gujarat for EV project and Stamping project.

items.statement: Full-year capex for Engineering division guided at INR110 crores
items.quote: The capex is about INR110 crores.

items.statement: Engineering division has LOI from Tata for ~INR150 crores battery project; project on hold pending Tata Group decision
items.quote: We had bagged LOI from Tata, which is about INR150-odd crores. But you might have seen that yesterday, in the newspaper, news related to Tata, Agratas and others, there are issues.

items.statement: Home Appliances PBDIT margin target: early double digits (10%+); Q1 FY27 PBDIT margin 5.79% vs 5.34% YoY
items.quote: So PBDIT should be early double digit in my opinion.

items.statement: Gross margin down ~160 bps YoY due to commodity/forex; cost initiatives offsetting at PBDIT level
items.quote: Our gross margin is down by about 160 basis points because of the material cost increase.

items.statement: AC volume growth 6-8% YoY in Q1 (industry ~20%+); disadvantaged by new energy ratings making products 10-15% costlier; focusing on higher-capacity models
items.quote: The new rating, as you might realize, is about 10% to 15% more expensive than the market. And therefore, we did not have the advantage of the older-rated products with a price advantage in the market.

items.statement: Targeting 50-60% AUM growth for FY27
items.quote: We have committed, that 50 % to 60% of AUM growth at the start of this financial year, we'll continue to, we are continuing to pursue that.

items.statement: Targeting debt-to-equity of 4-4.5x for FY27 with 15-20% co-lending share
items.quote: Our targeted range is about where the industry is right now, which is at 4x and beyond that, we will also have participation in terms of co -lending. Our idea of having a co -lending proportion of at least 15% to 20% by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Investing in compliance software and team for middle-layer NBFC and RBI regulations
items.quote: We got head of compliance as well as a whole team under the compliance set, as well as we are investing in software to ensure that we are fully compliant for both, middle layer regulation as well as new RBI compliance regulations.

items.statement: Yields stable at 20%, targeting 20-20.5%; cost of funds to decline with rating upgrade and co-lending; opex/AUM to fall with scale
items.quote: The yields have been stable at 20%. These yields will not go down, they trying to increase these yields. You can assume that it will it will stabilize somewhere around 20% or 20.5%.

items.statement: Targeting steady-state ROA of 3-3.5% and ROE of 18% over medium term
items.quote: If you ask us ROA, ROE guidance for the next five years, we ideally would want to be at a 3 %, 3.5% ROA and a 18% ROE kind of a number. That's what we are targeting.

items.statement: Gold price correction reduces ticket sizes and industry growth; new branch expansion offsets impact for small NBFC
items.quote: If you look at historically, whenever the gold prices are corrected or subdued, the gold loan industry did not grow to that extent. It has an industry-wide direct correlation.

items.statement: Implemented RBI-mandated segregation of consumption loans (tiered LTV 75-85%) and income-generating loans (board-approved policy)
items.quote: In terms of LTV, that is where the major changes have happened, wherein RBI wanted to segregate clearly between consumption loan and income generating loan. That we have implemented.

items.statement: Gross NPA 0.54%, Net NPA 0.48%; conservative LTV and collateral management protect portfolio despite gold price volatility
items.quote: Our NPAs have been pretty much stable, pretty much under control. It is at 0.54% gross NPA and 0.48% net NPA.

items.statement: Branch network grew 42% YoY to 118; target avg AUM/branch Rs 12-13 cr; new branch breakeven at Rs 5-6 cr in 12-18 months
items.quote: Our branch network has increased from 83 count to 118 branches as of 30th June, which is a 42% increase.

items.statement: Expanding organically to adjacent states (e.g., Odisha) after saturating current four southern states
items.quote: We will continue to do that and then we will cater to adjacent states. Just to give an example, we are already there till Visakhapatnam border. The next best location is Orissa.

items.statement: Capital sufficient for FY27 growth: Rs 350 cr net worth + Rs 100 cr cash + co-lending + Rs 30 cr promoter warrants can support AUM to Rs 1,900-2,000 cr
items.quote: On a Rs. 1,270 crores, we are almost adding Rs. 700 crores which will again take us to Rs. 1,900 crores to Rs. 2000 crores kind of an AUM.

items.statement: Current cost of borrowing 11-11.5%, opex 6-7%; spread 100-200 bps pre-tax; NIM expansion from yield increase, cost decline, opex leverage
items.quote: Our average cost of funds or cost of borrowing to say is about 11 % to 11.5%, that's the range with an opex cost of about average 6% to 7%.

items.statement: No major regulatory changes expected for gold loans in next 12-24 months; RBI framework already implemented
items.quote: I think whatever they had to give, they have given already.

items.statement: MEL Phase 2 thermal plant full commissioning delayed to Q2 FY28 (June-July 2027) due to logistical delays from global conflict
items.quote: So, what that has done is it has moved the commissioning by a couple of months to probably Q2 of FY27-28. We are looking around the June-July timeframe.

items.statement: 100 MW solar plant to be commissioned by end of September 2026
items.quote: Solar plant is set to be commissioned by the end of September.

items.statement: MEL Phase 2 project cost INR400 million (INR300 million debt, INR100 million equity), no change in debt profile
items.quote: The project cost is INR400 million, out of which INR300 million is debt and INR100 is equity. So, that remains constant.

items.statement: Zambia energy sustainable EBITDA margin 45-50% at consolidated level
items.quote: Around like 45% to 50% is the EBITDA.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expected 35-40% after intersegment eliminations
items.quote: And when it comes to consolidated EBITDA, it will be between 35% to 40%.

items.statement: Metals business margins expected stable to slightly higher, no downward trend seen through FY27
items.quote: We could probably either see stability in terms of where we are today or if not, a slight increase. But I don't see a downward trend, at least until the end of the financial year.

items.statement: Actively investigating renewable opportunities (solar, wind, battery storage) in India and internationally; monitoring SMR nuclear technology
items.quote: We, as a company, are looking seriously at the renewable space, and not just solar. We're looking at solar. We're looking at wind. We're looking with a combination of both of them with battery storage.

items.statement: Nava Limited owns 100% of Nava Global (ultimate owner of Zambia assets); no spin-off/IPO plans disclosed
items.quote: The ultimate owner, yes, is Nava because it owns 100% of Nava Global.

items.statement: Revenue target raised to over INR3,200 crores for FY27, with confidence to surpass INR3,250 crores
items.quote: We are confident we will be surpassing this and we will be achieving a revenue more than INR3,200 crores in FY 2027.

items.statement: Quarterly revenue trajectory: Q2 ~INR840 crores, Q3 ~INR850 crores, Q4 ~INR900 crores
items.quote: We'll be crossing INR840 crores for Q2. And the total comes to about INR3,250 crores plus. And Q3, we'll be crossing INR850 crores and then Q4 is about INR900 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 4.6% in Q1 FY27; expect progressive improvement from Q3 as air freight ceases and price settlements realized
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR34.8 crores, translating into an EBITDA margin of 4.6%.

items.statement: Target full-year EBITDA margin of 12% for FY27, confident of achieving despite near-term pressures
items.quote: Our target -- we had mentioned last year that we -- our target should be around 12%. We will be achieving the 12% target.

items.statement: Raw material settlement lag impacted Q1 by ~INR10 crores; aluminum prices up 57% YoY (INR222 to INR349/kg)
items.quote: The settlement lag resulted in an estimated impact of approximately INR10 crores during the quarter.

items.statement: One customer agreed to pay ~50% of air freight costs incurred; negotiations ongoing with others
items.quote: And in fact, one of the customers has agreed to pay us a freight and which would be accounted for as and when we get it. And that's almost 50% of whatever will be already incurred.

items.statement: Capex focused on completing 54 launch programs; minimal new investments for 1 year, then stabilize before larger projects
items.quote: We are making investments there, but we are also curbing the investments. And -- but having said that, after this, I think for 1 year, we are going to invest only wherever absolutely necessary.

items.statement: 55 new programs in launch phase (28 launched, in ramp-up); long-term programs for Toyota, Ford, BMW with 7-8 year life, single-source, highly profitable
items.quote: There are around 55 new programs in launch phase, out of which 28 programs already launched and are in ramp-up phase. These are long-term programs for Toyota, Ford and BMW with program life of more than 7 to 8 years.

items.statement: July revenue ~INR300 crores, indicating strong demand momentum continuing into Q2
items.quote: Like I mentioned that in the month of July, we have done almost INR300 crores, and we are heading for plus...

items.statement: Shipping route disruptions increased ocean freight transit from 5 to 9 weeks, causing air freight dependency; geopolitical risk (Iran/West Asia) could prolong
items.quote: disruption in global shipping routes due to increase in ocean freight transit time from 5 weeks to 9 weeks, which led to greater resilience on the air shipments to maintain supply continuity.

items.statement: FY27 revenue growth target of 15-20% YoY, driven mainly by exports as domestic facility ramps up
items.quote: So right now for the current year, our target is to have a growth of around 15 % to 20%.

items.statement: By 2030, domestic business expected to reach ~50% of total revenue, implying ~INR550-600 cr total revenue
items.quote: As I said on by 2030, we are expecting 50% of our revenue to be domestic. At current rate we are at around INR280 crores in exports. So a rough calculation you can make based on this that it would be around, you know, INR550 crores to INR600 crores.

items.statement: Five-year vision: revenue more than double current levels
items.quote: And in five years down the line, we look forward for a revenue which would be more than double of what it is right now.

items.statement: New Andheri facility: 5,360 sq ft, 125-150 kg/year capacity, adds 50-60% to overall capacity
items.quote: The facility covers approximately 5,360 square feet and has an estimated manufacturing capacity of around 125 kg to 150 kg of jewellery per annum. This is expected to increase our overall manufacturing capacity by approximately 50% to 60%.

items.statement: New facility revenue potential INR250-300 cr at peak capacity; FY27 contribution only INR15-20 cr as samples/pitching phase
items.quote: So we expect all this put together, it should be around a INR250 crores to INR300 crores kind of a revenue generation capacity.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 10.14% from 7.35%; export margins sustainable, domestic margins initially tighter but expected to converge over time
items.quote: EBITDA margin improved from 7.35% to 10.14%.

items.statement: Lab-grown diamond jewellery <5-7% of revenue currently; major push planned in domestic B2C and US exports
