items.statement: Catering margins traditionally between 10% to 12%; proof-of-concept impact of INR4 crore to die down by Q3; one-time HR cost of INR20 crore booked in Q1 will not repeat
items.quote: So this is one, and proof of concept will slowly die down. There are two trains I think they will finish by September and the remaining two trains will finish by November. So that way it will help and the catering margin traditionally have been between 10 % to 12%. So we will try to maintain that.

items.statement: 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains expected in FY27 or next year; license fee calibrated at INR6 crore per train totalling ~INR120 crore
items.quote: But whenever there is a passenger growth, the trains, normally there may be around 20 Vande Bharat sleeper trains introduced in this financial year or the period of next one year. So, the license fee of this can be calibrated to around INR6 crores per train to INR120 crores.

items.statement: Internet ticketing EBITDA margin 80.33% in Q1 FY27 vs 84.12% YoY; decline due to NGET infra refresh (~INR150 crore), INR10 crore maintenance, upcoming active-active disaster recovery at Secunderabad
items.quote: Normally, it remains between 80% to 85%, so it is, like you have seen, it is around 80% this time. These are some of the reasons which I would like to share with you.

items.statement: Rail Neer margin fell from 14% to 10% YoY due to ~30% resin cost increase (petroleum/West Asia crisis); material cost rose INR55 cr to INR61 cr
items.quote: Due to the increase of petroleum product due to West Asia crisis, the material cost increased from INR55 crores to INR61 crores. There was a dip of INR6 crores. You have seen that the margin has gone from 15 to 11.

items.statement: E-catering meals grew from 1.05 lakh/day to 1.69 lakh/day; e-catering revenue rose from INR16 cr to INR22 cr; election specials revenue jumped from INR5 cr to INR41 cr
items.quote: E-catering is another growing segment which has grown to around INR1.05 lakh meals from '25 to '26 to INR1.69 lakh meals in financial '26-'27. And e-catering revenue has grown by INR6 crores from INR16 crores to INR22 crores.

items.statement: Vande Bharat catering via empanelled service providers (limited tender); 81 Vande Bharats currently served by IRCTC; shift to sleeper Vande Bharat will increase catering lead and capacity
items.quote: In Vande Bharat also we have got empanelled service providers, for which we float a limited tender and then we give it out as far as the catering is concerned.

items.statement: AGEasy expected to reach contribution breakeven by Q4 FY27 (January 2027) and EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27
items.quote: As we look ahead, we remain committed to profitability. As I said, AGEasy perhaps by January or last quarter of this year will be in that zone.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue trajectory to continue growing substantially in FY27 while EBITDA losses get contained as no new beds are being added
items.quote: This trajectory will continue for FY27 in terms of revenue going up substantially and EBITDA losses getting contained because now we are not adding any new beds at this point of time.

items.statement: Antara Noida Phase I: 340 units offered possession in June 2026, INR169 crores demand raised, ~75% collected as of August 2026
items.quote: We raised a demand of about INR169 crores with the offers of possession. INR30-odd crores were collected within June, but the rest has now come, most of it in July and August. As on date, approximately 75% of total dues have been collected.

items.statement: Antara Noida Phase II approval next focus; current prices INR16,000-18,000+ vs Phase I average INR7,000-10,000
items.quote: the rates have moved significantly up, and they are in the range of INR16,000, INR18,000 plus. So hopefully, when we launch Phase II, we should be able to realize the profits as well.

items.statement: Dehradun expansion: <150 units on new land parcel, potential sales value INR850-900 crores
items.quote: We have found a small piece of land. It might be just less than 150 units. But given the sales price we are commanding, the sales value will be again INR850 crores to INR900 crores.

items.statement: Gurgaon E361 sales velocity recovered: 27 units in Q1 FY27, 34 units in July 2026, similar trend in August
items.quote: while we sold only 27 units in Q1 FY27, in the month of July alone, we sold about 34 units and a similar trend continues in August. So we have caught up.

items.statement: Care Homes: 4 of 8 homes achieved highest ever ARPOB of INR7,000+ in June 2026; 3 of 4 show significant contribution margin improvement
items.quote: Happy to also report that 4 of our Care Homes achieved an ever highest ARPOB, which is average revenue per occupied bed day of INR7,000 plus in June '26.

items.statement: Blended ARPOB expected near INR7,500 as occupancy rises across Care Homes
items.quote: It should be near INR7,500.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 revenue grew 22% YoY to INR 2,355M; like-to-like projects grew 12% YoY
items.quote: Our revenue grew approximately 22% year-on-year in Q1. More importantly, our like-to-like projects grew approximately 12%.

items.statement: Retail business (RPL) expected to turn EBITDA positive by Q2 FY27
items.quote: by Q2, we expect RPL to also be EBITDA positive. And from there on, it will continue it's upward journey.

items.statement: Retail revenue contribution target 10-15% of total revenue by end of FY27
items.quote: Our contribution what we are looking to target this financial year is to be in the range of 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Awarded Himachal Pradesh CT project for 34 CT scans across state, predominantly cash-paying, 10-year visibility
items.quote: Krsnaa has recently been awarded the Himachal Pradesh CT project for 34 CT scans across the entire state. This is Krsnaa Diagnostics Limited August 14, 2026 Page 3 of 18 particularly significant for us because Himachal Pradesh is where Krsnaa began its PPP journey almost 12 years ago with just 12 centers.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin 25% vs 27% YoY; compression due to upfront costs of new projects (4,000 manpower in Rajasthan) while like-to-like margins stable
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR588 million with an EBITDA margin of 25% against 27% in Q1 FY26. As guided in our previous call, this quarter did carry an element of upfront cost, largely around 4,000 manpower onboarded in Rajasthan logistics across collection center ahead of full revenue realization from the projec

items.statement: Retail revenue grew 64% YoY to INR 193M (9% of group revenue); network expanded to 4,000+ touchpoints across 7 states
items.quote: Our retail revenue for the Q1 FY27 stood at INR193 million against revenue of INR118 million in quarter 1 FY'26, growing at impressive year-on-year growth rate of 64% and contributed approximately 9% of overall group revenue.

items.statement: Promoter warrant infusion for capex on projects and potential acquisitions
items.quote: Two reasons. One is, of course, the funds will be utilized for certain capital expenditure for projects and certain acquisitions that we have in mind, and that was the reason why the funds have been raised.

items.statement: Fees to hospitals expense rose to INR 41 crore in Q1 due to Rajasthan project partner revenue-sharing arrangements
items.quote: the actual increase is on account of Rajasthan project. So for a project like Rajasthan or even other PPP projects, we have certain partners that we work in these remote locations. And there's a certain revenue share amount that goes to these partners.

items.statement: FY27 guidance unchanged; confident of achieving full-year targets backed by strong launch lineup and project completion visibility
items.quote: Our guidance remains unchanged. We remain confident of achieving our full year guidance. The confidence is primarily underpinned by the strong launch lineup and the project completion visibility.

items.statement: FY27 sales value guidance INR 3,300-3,500 crores (40-50% growth); collections guidance INR 2,100-2,200 crores (26-30% growth)
items.quote: In our FY27 outlook, we have given a sales value growth of almost 40% to 50%, up to INR3,300 crores to INR 3,500 crores, whereas the corresponding collection figure is much muted at a 26% to 30% growth of INR2,100 crores to INR2,200 crores.

items.statement: FY27 PBT margin expected 8-9%; FY28 PBT margin target ~10%
items.quote: So, this year, we might be in the 8% to 9%. And as I said earlier in the past, we would have at least a 20% growth in our revenue recognition and therefore, from last year.

items.statement: FY28 EBITDA margin target 22-24%
items.quote: What I would like to say is, our EBITDA margin should be in the range of about 22% to 24% by FY28.

items.statement: FY28 mission: sales value ~INR 5,000 crores, revenue ~INR 2,500 crores, PBT ~INR 250 crores
items.quote: We are on track towards achieving our FY28 mission. The current pipeline provides substantial visibility for this objective.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity may rise temporarily in FY27 but long-term comfort zone 0.5x; gross debt INR 651 crores, net debt INR 432 crores as of June
items.quote: So, if I look at our overall gearing, it will go up. It would most likely go up during FY 27. The gearing can rise temporarily, because as you know, as we are pursuing aggressive growth and trying to lock more project pipeline, understandably, either equity or debt has to come in, not only the cash from operation.

items.statement: Current pipeline 33.7 msf (16 msf ongoing + 17.7 msf upcoming) with GDV ~INR 13,530 crores; additional 7.3 msf (GDV >INR 6,000 crores) likely in 3-6 months; target to nearly double upcoming pipeline in 18-24 months
items.quote: We currently have approximately 16 million square feet of ongoing projects and 17.7 million square feet of the upcoming projects, Giving us a total current pipeline of 33.7 million square feet. The ongoing portfolio has 2.9 million square feet of unsold area with unsold GDV of approximately INR1,970 crores. The upcomin

items.statement: Q1 margins muted due to ~40% revenue from low-margin legacy Kolkata projects; margins expected to improve in H2 as higher-margin products complete
items.quote: The muted margins are largely product mix driven rather than structure, with around 40% from relatively lower margin legacy projects from Kolkata. Margins are expected to improve in H2 and higher-margin product reaches completion.

items.statement: Sustenance sales prices rising 4-5% annually; launch prices set per micro-market competition; no large post-COVID style 10-15% jumps expected
items.quote: On the pricing side, I don't see a big jump in price. I just want to clarify. So like the post-COVID, we saw like 10%, 15% annual increase. That may not happen. On an average, we are seeing roughly about 4%, 5% increase in selling price.

items.statement: Underlying demand strong across Bangalore, Chennai, Pune, Kolkata; mid-market end-use demand resilient; conversion rates stable; no material slowdown in housing loan applications
items.quote: We are not seeing on ground where customers are backtracking. We haven't seen the conversion rate going down in a material way. Therefore, we are of the belief and even my industry checks with housing loan companies, they are not seeing any slowdown in application momentum.

items.statement: Strategy: premiumization (Chennai premium launch Shriram Stellar 20% sold in launch weekend) and product diversification (Kolkata plotted development 55% sold in 30 days); mid-market ASP up from ~INR 5,000 to ~INR 7,600-7,700/sqft
items.quote: With Shriram Stellar, we have entered Chennai's premium residential segment with our premium offering. Around 20% of the project was sold during the first weekend of the launch, validating the product positioning with our brand distinct.

items.statement: Launch calendar back-ended (Q3/Q4) creating collection timing gap; Kolkata 2.3 msf apartment approvals to be phased; Pune Manjari launch dependent on local approvals; gearing may rise temporarily
items.quote: Since they are all Q3, Q4 launches, they will not translate exactly into the same amount of collections. And so this year, based on the progress of current ongoing projects and the timing of launches of our five or six launches that we are targeting in Q3 and Q4, we expect the collection to be in the range of about INR

items.statement: H2 handover pipeline: >2,900 units with INR 1,560 crores revenue potential; 410 units (INR 400 cr) ready now, 400+ units (INR 160 cr) targeting OC in Q2, 2,100+ units (INR 1,000 cr) targeting OC in H2
items.quote: Overall, more than 2,900 units representing over INR1,560 crores of revenue potential are scheduled for handover and revenue recognition during the balance of the year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27: highest ever Q1 sales INR 484 crores (0.85 msf, +10% YoY); collections INR 365 crores (+8% YoY); 690 units handed over; free cash flow before new investment INR 135 crores; net free cash flow INR 47 crores; cash balance INR 219 cro
items.quote: We achieved our highest ever Q1 sales of INR 484 crores with sales volume of 0.85 million square feet. Collections were INR 365 crores, supported by execution and handovers.

items.statement: Expect full year FY27 EBITDA margins broadly in line with FY26
items.quote: As shared earlier, we expect full year EBITDA margins to be broadly in line with last year.

items.statement: Confident of delivering clear step-up in FY27 full year growth given strong Q1 start
items.quote: Looking ahead, given the strong start in Q1, we are confident of delivering a clear step-up in our FY27 full year growth.

items.statement: FY30 ambition remains 2x revenue from FY25 and 3x EBITDA in same period
items.quote: Our ambition of 2x revenue from FY25 to FY30 and 3x EBITDA in the same period remains the North Star for us, and we remain confident of delivering that.

items.statement: ESOP expense expected in range of INR25-26 crores for FY27
items.quote: We expect ESOP to be in the range of INR25 crores to INR26 crores. We should be in that range.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin at 10.5%, down 46 bps YoY due to gross margin moderation and higher growth investments
items.quote: On the profitability front, adjusted EBITDA margin came in at 10.5%, a decline of 46 basis points year-on-year, primarily due to a moderation in gross margins and our planned and deliberately higher growth investments.

items.statement: Gross margin at 58.4% in Q1 FY27, down 131 bps YoY due to higher commodity costs and adverse currency
items.quote: Gross margins for the quarter stood at 58.4%, lower by 131 basis points year-on-year, reflecting the impact of higher commodity costs and adverse currency movements.

items.statement: AMC price increases of 3-12% implemented, led to some deferral in renewals but expect normalization over time
items.quote: The price increase, the band was roughly between 3% to 12%.

items.statement: Product price hikes taken at start of Q1, peers followed with lag; now at price equilibrium with competitors
items.quote: The price increase that we took, our peers followed albeit with a lag with almost similar price increases. Though like I said, there was a lag and of roughly a 30-day period when we had pricing ahead of the others. But now as things stand today, there is again price equilibrium versus competitors.

items.statement: No further consumer price hikes planned currently; bias towards not disturbing growth momentum, will drive efficiencies instead
items.quote: At this point in time, we are going to be more measured as far as consumer price increase is concerned because we see a very, very strong tailwind as far as growth is concerned and our bias will be towards not disturbing that.

items.statement: Service AMC bookings softer due to price hike deferral; expect Q2 service revenue growth similar to Q1, visibility beyond depends on bookings and filter business scale-up
items.quote: Given that there is a relative softness that we've seen and these are initial signs that we've seen as far as AMC bookings are concerned, that impact would play out towards the later part of the year.

items.statement: A&SP spends to increase ahead of revenue growth in FY27, focused on in-store presence and consumer finance adoption
items.quote: At an overall year level, we do expect our A&SP spends to be ahead of revenue growth. So that is something that we are planning for.

items.statement: Launched 4-year filter life products (Glow 4X, Ritz Pro 4X) 45 days ago, first in market, met with very positive response
items.quote: More recently, about 45 days ago, we were the first in the country to launch water purifiers with a four-year life. We launched two products in e-commerce, Glow 4X and Ritz Pro 4X with stainless steel, priced at roughly INR22,000 and INR25,000 respectively. And they've met with a very, very positive response.

items.statement: Management expects to reach EBITDA breakeven by next year (FY28).
items.quote: So I would say that by next year, we will actually come to the breakeven thing, okay?

items.statement: Management reiterates prior commitment to EBITDA breakeven by H2 FY28.
items.quote: Presently, I would say that I would stick to what we have committed last time. If it happens earlier, for sure, we will also announce the same.

items.statement: Railway lounge capex ranges from INR 1.5 crore to INR 5-6 crore per lounge depending on size and location.
items.quote: So it depends from INR1.5 crores going up to maybe INR5 crores to INR6 crores is the capex investment right now.

items.statement: Railway lounge opportunity estimated at INR 500 crores over next 5 years driven by government railway modernization.
items.quote: And this INR500 crores in the next 5 years is very much possible considering that kind of investment.

items.statement: Non-airport lounge services contributed ~33% of revenue in Q1 FY27, a significant diversification milestone.
items.quote: Our non -airport lounge services contributed approximately 33% of the top line during the quarter.

items.statement: Global lounge margins currently similar to legacy domestic lounge margins; expected to improve as volumes scale.
items.quote: Presently, you would not see a better margin compared to what it was earlier. But eventually, I would say that, yes, the margins would get better for Global.

items.statement: Revenue drop in Q1 FY27 driven by sharp decline in Middle East outbound traffic due to war.
items.quote: The drop is drastically because of the war which is happening. So yes, internationally, the traffic is down, and that is one of the biggest reasons that why there is a drop in the revenue.

items.statement: India credit card transaction value expected to grow from ~INR 21 trillion in FY25 to ~INR 54 trillion in FY30 (CAGR ~21%).
items.quote: India's credit card transaction value is expected to grow from approximately 21 trillion in FY 25 to 54 trillion in FY 30, representing a CAGR of around 21%.

items.statement: Signed 3 large APAC banking clients (Singapore, Indonesia) with programs going live in Q2 FY27.
items.quote: We have a very large (card) network in Singapore, where we have already signed up and our program would be going live hopefully by end of this month or early next month. Our second one is in Indonesia, one of the largest bank in Indonesia. Also, we have also gone live there.

items.statement: No current plans for promoter stake increase or strategic investor fundraising; focus remains on business execution.
items.quote: Presently, I think there is no such plans in the promoter group because presently, I think the focus is completely on how to bring the business back into where we were.

items.statement: Cash increased to INR 193.3 crores (from INR 149 crores) due to ~INR 40+ crores collections from receivables.
items.quote: There has been significant efforts in terms of collections. So you are right, there has been like collection of nearly INR40-plus crores, which is there from different customers.

items.statement: No further Minimum Guarantee (MMG) payments expected going forward; gross margins should turn positive.
items.quote: However, going forward, like there will be no such payment. So anyways, you will see positive margins.

items.statement: Employee costs (including ESOPs) expected to remain at current quarter run-rate; full-year ESOP impact only INR 14 lakhs.
items.quote: So if we talk about on a full year basis, the impact of those ESOPs which are issued is only INR14 lakhs. So that is not at all impacting. So if you see basically the variance that is appearing if you are comparing the current quarter number, so these will be more or less equivalent to what we have been doing in the pr

items.statement: Expect normalized demand trajectory through later part of FY27 after GST-related lumpiness last year
items.quote: While these dynamics are largely behind us, we expect a more normalized and consistent demand trajectory through the later part of the year.

items.statement: Capex guided at ~INR50 crore for FY27, Q1 spend below proportionate share
items.quote: Our capex, which we had guided in the last year closing at around INR50 crores. We are as of now in line. The first quarter, we have spent less than the proportionate share.

items.statement: Premium and mass segments growing faster than luxury segment in recent months post GST cuts
items.quote: Due to various macro factors and post the GST cuts, we have seen that the premium and mass segments have grown faster than the luxury segment over the last few months.

items.statement: Syros EV receiving healthy order bookings across India, new Sorento launch expected in September
items.quote: The recently launched Syros EV has also received a very healthy order bookings across India. The new Sorento is expected to be launched in September.

items.statement: Signed industry-first MoU with ChargeZone for EV charging revenue share and customer wallet credits
items.quote: We have signed an MoU with ChargeZone, one of India's leading EV charging networks. Under this partnership, our EV customers will receive wallet credit redeemable at ChargeZone's charging locations, while we will earn a share of charging revenue from onboarded customers.

items.statement: Mercedes average selling price increased to ~INR79 lakh in Q1 FY27 from INR73 lakh in Q4 FY26
items.quote: We have seen this reflecting in our average selling price, which has increased to approximately INR79 lakh in Q1 FY27, which is up from INR73 lakh in Q4 FY26.

items.statement: EBITDA to CFO conversion ~95% (0.95x) maintained, similar to last 2 years
items.quote: Cash flow last year, it was 0.95%. We will be around that only.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 900-950 crore, implying ~50% YoY growth from FY26
items.quote: And the whole year revenue, we are looking at the same at par revenue, which was in FY'2024-2025, that is of the order of Rs. 900 crores to Rs. 950 crores.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue expected 30-35% higher than Q1; Q3/Q4 growth >50% QoQ
items.quote: If in percentage terms we were to explain Q2 would be about 30% to 35% higher than Q1 and thereafter you will see a growth of more than 50% quarter-to-quarter.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target ~25% and PAT margin ~15% for FY27
items.quote: No sir. We are confident that we would be achieving those numbers because the work that we currently have in our order book is of similar margins and was built by keeping those numbers in mind.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 2,329 crore as of July 2026
items.quote: It is Rs. 2329 crores as of now.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 order inflow Rs 317 crore; Q2 FY27 to date Rs 158 crore; L1 on Banaras project >Rs 100 crore
items.quote: As far as the 1st Quarter is concerned, we converted these bids to work orders of about Rs. 317 crores. And after that also, till date, in the 2nd Quarter, we have received a work order of about Rs. 158 crores. And we are L1 for a project in Banaras of about excess of Rs. 100 crores.

items.statement: No capex plans for FY27 as of now
items.quote: As far as any CAPEX plans are concerned there is no such CAPEX plan as of yet.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin 17.9% (Rs 28.14 cr on Rs 157.24 cr); PAT margin 9.9%
items.quote: EBITDA stands at Rs. 28.14 crores with an increase of about 31.62%. And PAT stands at Rs. 15.49 crores with an increase of about 1.28%.

items.statement: Bidding in Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka; pipeline Rs 2,500-3,000 crore in Delhi & Maharashtra
items.quote: We are bidding in Bihar and Madhya Pradesh. And any projects that we see, we are exploring some projects in Maharashtra and Karnataka also.

items.statement: Execution risk from monsoon (Q2), election restrictions (Kolkata), government payment delays stretching working capital
items.quote: In this rainy season again, we will increase with Q1 but not to the extent we are intending. Not by the amount of 50%, but 30%, 35% we will increase.

items.statement: Working capital cycle ~120 days; delays in government payments create cash flow pressure
items.quote: For working capital, definitely once work is stopped due to whatsoever reason, then payment from the government is delayed. And payment from the government is delayed, it hampers the work again.

items.statement: Revenue concentration: ~42% from Uttar Pradesh, ~61% from Uttarakhand in recent quarters (overlap likely due to consolidated vs standalone)
items.quote: As far as the current numbers are concerned about , so the revenue is about 42% from Uttar Pradesh and about 61% from Uttarakhand as far as these quarters are concerned.

items.statement: Kolkata sewerage project execution to ramp from Q3 FY27; Q2 still weak due to project nature
items.quote: I think that will only be achieved from Quarter 3. Because it is a sewerage network project. So, in Quarter 2 also, that revenue cannot be achieved in sewer line projects. But Q3 and Q4 numbers with regard to the Kolkata project would be much better than what you are anticipating.

items.statement: No guidance issued for FY27; management expects to provide guidance next quarter as market stabilizes
items.quote: See, we haven't given any guidance for the current year, Sonal. And at this point as well, we are not really issuing a guidance for the current year. We will evolve and as the market stabilizes, we should hopefully be coming out with the guidance next quarter.

items.statement: Expect EBITDA margins to return to 20%+ in H2 FY27 and progress to 30% range over mid-term as MICE recovers, air margins stabilize, and corporate travel scales
items.quote: we will see margins come back very quickly to the 20-plus percent mark first. And as the business continues to scale, we do feel confident that we'll get back to that 30% aspiration in the mid term. So my sense at this point based on what trending we are seeing is that in the second half of the year, we should start be

items.statement: Q2 FY27 margins expected to improve marginally but remain range-bound; meaningful improvement seen in H2 FY27
items.quote: I think there is a little bit of improvement on account of MICE, but for the second element, which is the capacity still continues to be coming back only gradually. So I think we'll see a marginal improvement to -- if MICE continues this momentum, hopefully, we might see some more tangible improvement, but largely rema

items.statement: MICE operates at 40%+ operating margin vs 15-20% for other businesses; contributes 20-25% of annual profitability; lumpy quarterly nature requires year-on-year view
items.quote: MICE will account for anywhere between 20% to maybe -- on an annual basis, 20%, you might have quarters where it tends to be closer to 25%, but that's about it. It's not that more than 50% of the business would come from MICE.

items.statement: Corporate restructuring (Yatra India merger with parent) ongoing across India, Singapore, Cyprus, Cayman, SEC; no fixed timeline given regulatory complexity
items.quote: having seen how regulators in different markets behave, it's very hard to give an exact timeline on that.

items.statement: Full-year EBITDA margin expansion of 150-200 bps expected vs prior year, above the 100-150 bps annual target
items.quote: this a year where we will clearly do better than that, at least 150 basis points – 200 basis points is what we see us doing you know over last and this year.

items.statement: Calibrated price increases taken end of Q1 to offset packaging cost inflation from crude oil; real gross margin impact expected in Q2
items.quote: we've actually taken calibrated price increases towards the end of Q1, we'll be able to offset any such inflationary impact on our procurement perspective.

items.statement: Focus categories contribution rose to ~85% of revenue in Q1 FY27
items.quote: Now the contribution of focus categories has also increased to almost 85%, in Q1FY '27.

items.statement: Launched FIKN, India's first elixir-based fine fragrance brand with patented design; clinically tested 12-hour stay
items.quote: We finally have launched a brand called FIKN. It's India's first elixir-based brand, which is the highest dosed and the strongest form of perfume that we have brought to India.

items.statement: BTM Ventures (Reginald) ARR grew ~100% post-acquisition to INR 150 cr; expanded to Maharashtra, new category, new channels
items.quote: BTM Ventures, which we acquired in January, it continues to do well. It has reached an ARR of INR150 crores in the last quarter. Since we acquired, we've actually grown it almost 100%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR 8,200-8,300 crores implying 20-25% growth over FY26 INR 6,400 crores
items.quote: This year, we were looking at touching approximately INR8,200 crores, INR8,300 crores. So we'll see close to about 20%, 25% growth.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin expected to reach 4.3-4.4% for FY27, below earlier 5% target due to CV mix shift
items.quote: We would still be in the region of about 4.3%, 4.4% overall for the -- I mean, when we go to Q3, Q4.

items.statement: Acquired businesses expected to achieve sustainable PAT profitability from Q2 FY27 onwards
items.quote: As guided during our previous call, we expect the acquired business to achieve sustainable profitability at the PAT level from Q2 onwards.

items.statement: PV service volume growth of 6-7% expected from Q2 FY27 onwards after Honda divestment impact removed
items.quote: Q2 onwards, we'll see a growth. I wouldn't say 15% growth, which we have guided, but we'll show -- we'll be having a growth of about 6% to 7% in terms of volumes.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 reported EBITDA margin 3.8% vs 2.9% YoY; adjusted EBITDA INR 62 crores up 82% YoY
items.quote: reported EBITDA increased approximately 87% Y-o-Y to INR71.5 crores, with EBITDA margins improving to 3.8% from 2.9% in Q1 last year.

items.statement: PV segment EBITDA margin currently ~4%, expected to inch up from Q2 with Maruti growth and Audi contribution
items.quote: currently, we are at around 4% in terms of PV EBITDA as such. So that should keep inching forward in Q2, Q3 and Q4 with Audi also coming in line.

items.statement: CV EBITDA margin ~3.6-3.7% due to high ticket size (~INR 17 lakh) dragging blended margin lower
items.quote: our CV EBITDA percentage because of the CV ticket size, the ticket size of CVs would be about INR16,00,000 on an average. Our EBITDA margins because of that is about 3.6% to 3.7%

items.statement: CV tipper segment seeing low to negative growth due to construction slowdown; other CV segments holding well

items.quote: Cash and bank balances as on 30th June stood at ₹8.12 crores against the borrowings of ₹6.74 crores and our consolidated debt-to-equity ratio remains comfortably at approximately 0.04 times.

items.statement: New hub breakeven historically achieved in 3 months (guided 6 months); mature hub annual cycles estimated at 30 (Tier 2) to 50 (metro).
items.quote: The breakeven usually comes, like we say six months, but historically it has always come in three months. So that is what we've been doing. And in the first three months our centres have break even wherever we have opened them in the past.

items.statement: Flagship Janakpuri centre growing ~30% YoY; Patna centre relocated to Kankarbagh medical hub; Srinagar seasonal with winter strength; Ludhiana expanding spokes in Punjab.
items.quote: So our Janakpuri center has been growing roughly 30% year-on-year and is still growing. You know, Delhi is such a huge market and it is still growing at 30% year-on-year.

items.statement: Aggressive pan-India marketing push for SiD and ERICA in Q1 was a one-time expense impacting margins; expected to drive differentiation and rewards through rest of FY27.
items.quote: This margin decline is mainly because of just one heavy marketing push that we did. This was a one-time marketing push which contributed to this difference. And this was done to basically market SiD and ERICA aggressively throughout the country.

items.statement: Management reaffirmed medium-term pre-sales target of Rs 15,000 crores over three years
items.quote: We are absolutely confident of our long-term guidance that we have given. We are all aiming towards that. We are building up our BD pipeline and also showing up on phase launches. We are very confident that we will be able to achieve that.

items.statement: FY27 business development target of Rs 10,000-15,000 crores GDV
items.quote: On an annual basis, I have guided you in the range over Rs. 10,000 crores to Rs. 15,000 crores is what we are aiming to do in this financial year.

items.statement: FY27 construction cost guidance revised to Rs 1,200-1,300 crores from earlier Rs 1,000 crores
items.quote: Yes, around Rs. 1,200-Rs. 1,300 crores will be the overall construction cost for the current financial year.

items.statement: Business development pipeline of over Rs 60,000 crores GDV across NCR, Mumbai, Pune, Bangalore
items.quote: We have more than about term sheets and advanced deals worth about more than Rs. 60,000 crores in the pipeline. These are reasonably split between NCR, Mumbai, Pune, and Bangalore.

items.statement: Redevelopment project margins expected at 25-30%
items.quote: Around 25%-30% is what we expect. It is a very high margin, very high, very premium location.

items.statement: Birla Niyaara Tower-1 margins expected at 40%+
items.quote: Margins are very healthy. I do not want to disclose now, but here the margins are in the range of about (+40%).

items.statement: Price increases implemented; Niyaara cancellations rebooked at Rs 4 crores higher per apartment
items.quote: For example, at Niyaara we had four cancellations, but two of them we have booked at much higher prices with at least about Rs. 4 crores more per apartment.

items.statement: Premium housing demand strong in Mumbai, NCR, Bangalore; MMR leading volumes
items.quote: In Mumbai premium housing demand continues to be very stable, strong, growing, both in price terms and volume terms. So, we are pretty confident that we are betting on the right market.

items.statement: Focus on large formats and premium segments; Niyaara Tower C launch price estimated Rs 100,000-120,000 per sq ft on carpet
items.quote: It is too early to talk about a launch price, but tentatively it will be in the range of about Rs. 100,000 to Rs. 120,000 per square foot.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to virtually zero after Century Pulp & Paper divestment; collection efficiency at 98%
items.quote: Our net debt, as I mentioned earlier, is virtually zero. So, in that sense, we do not have much debt remaining.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 collections robust at Rs 713 crores, up 31% YoY
items.quote: Collection remained robust at Rs. 713 crores, registering 31% of Y-o-Y increase overall, from Rs. 445 crores in Q1 FY 2026.

items.statement: Birla Taranya achieved Rs 1,000+ crores booking value within 3 months of RERA approval
items.quote: Birla Taranya delivered an especially strong start. Within just first 3 months of receiving RERA approval, the project achieved booking value of over Rs. 1,000 crores, demonstrating strong customer acceptance and robust underlying demand.

items.statement: INR250 crores investment program over 2-3 years: SIOP capacity expansion from 30k to 45k tpa (Phase 1: +7k tpa by Q4 FY28) and captive power plant at Sahupuram by Q4 FY28
items.quote: Yesterday, we announced the first step in what we envisage as DCW's next 5-year growth journey, a INR250 crores investment program over the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals EBITDA grew ~20% YoY; margins ~35-36% on SIOP, CPVC margins dynamic due to PVC/CPVC spread volatility
items.quote: I think the margins would be somewhere around 35%, 36% and has been stable ever since we have been communicating that.

items.statement: Domestic demand resilient supported by infrastructure, housing, water management, manufacturing; SIOP demand healthy across construction, infrastructure, paints & coatings
items.quote: Domestic demand, however, remained reasonably resilient, supported by infrastructure, housing, water management and manufacturing activity.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals revenue grew 38% YoY to 33% of total revenue; CPVC volumes up 59% YoY; increasing value-added contribution supporting portfolio through weak Basic Chemicals quarter
items.quote: Revenue from operations grew 14% year-on-year, led by 38% growth in Specialty Chemicals.

items.statement: PVC business hit by West Asia crisis: VCM supply disruption, elevated VCM prices, temporary import duty suspension; Basic Chemicals EBITDA negative INR14 crores; PVC contribution swing ~INR50-55 crores QoQ
items.quote: We have a guesstimate of maybe a swing from a sequential basis of around INR50 crores, INR55 crores on the PVC business.

items.statement: Legacy long-term debt to be fully repaid in FY27; target effectively net debt free by end FY27; will borrow slightly more than repayments (~INR135 crores) for capex, maintaining 5-10% of revenue as cash
items.quote: We expect our legacy long-term debt to fully be repaid during this year. Before incremental borrowings for new growth projects, we remain on track to become effectively net debt free by the end of FY27.

items.statement: CEO transition: Sudarshan Ganapathy appointed CEO to lead next growth phase; targeting minimum 20% incremental ROCE on new investments
items.quote: We are targeting a minimum incremental ROCE of 20% on our new investments. We are not pursuing growth for the sake of growth.

items.statement: INR 8,000 crore revenue target by CY30 remains the north star, driven by organic growth (JVD, Volteron) and external acquisitions
items.quote: The INR8,000 crores target, it's not only a target for the complete organization and the management team, but this is the north stars we are following every night to find our way to success.

items.statement: Consolidated order book stands at INR 4,500 crore as of June 2026, up from INR 1,200 crore secured in Q2 CY26
items.quote: We secured order worth approximately INR1,200 crores. With these wins, our total order book as of June 2026 stands at approximately INR4,500 crores.

items.statement: Standalone order book is INR 2,200 crore (half of consolidated)
items.quote: So, the consolidated is around INR4,500 crores and the standalone is half of it. Yes, INR2,200 crores yes.

items.statement: CY25 consolidated revenue guidance of ~INR 2,000 crore may not be fully met but should not be far off including US entity
items.quote: I think you will see a significant improvement in the revenue generation. In the second half and I think, okay, we may not be at 2,000, but I think we should not be very far if at all we include the U.S. in that.

items.statement: JVD technology commercializable; advanced discussions to close first JVD project in Asia this year; Volteron still in R&D phase
items.quote: JVD is already commercializable, and we have very advanced discussion to close one project hopefully this year for JVD in Asia.

items.statement: Potential JVD order size in range of EUR 50-100 million
items.quote: The order that we are looking at is in the range of EUR50 million to EUR100 million.

items.statement: Strong pipeline for new orders across India, Asia, Europe and USA; order wins expected before year-end
items.quote: The pipeline for new orders is still very interesting. We have a possibility for new orders in different regions that we are active on.

items.statement: One-time consolidation costs (transaction, forex, legal, audit, compliance) to stop from H2 CY26; parent company agreed to share-based payment instead of cash
items.quote: Many of these costs will actually stop incurring. We will stop incurring from the second half of the year. So that will be a significant saving.

items.statement: JVD offers significant customer savings vs hot-dip galvanizing: at least INR 1,000/ton, up to 20x for automotive/advanced high-strength steels
items.quote: So, I would say in terms of savings for the customer, we are talking about cases where it is at least INR1,000 saving and it can go up to 20x this figure based on the case.

items.quote: So for delivering B-80 program, we will have to rely on debt. 2e are in the process of raising debt. By the quarter four of by November, December of next year, 2027, our cash flows will be sufficient to fund our growth for B-15

items.statement: B-80 crude inventory liquidation ongoing; 15% sold at INR 4-6 cr loss; targeting full clearance by Oct-Nov 2026
items.quote: We have reversed the sale, as Allen said, in March, April of this year, and we agreed to sell it to third parties. items.statement: Q1 FY27 standalone revenue INR 117.5 cr, net revenue INR 107.6 cr; PBT INR 12.54 cr; consolidated revenue INR 124 cr, net INR 114.17 cr, PBT INR 6.5 cr
items.quote: During the current quarter, the company recorded standalone revenues from operations of INR117.5 crores compared with negative of INR194 crores in the previous quarter. After accounting for profit petroleum and revenue share of INR9.83 crores, the net revenue stands at INR107.6.

items.statement: Crude realization improved to $95.5/bbl from $70.8/bbl QoQ; blended gas realization $12/MMBtu vs $9.8/MMBtu; B-80 gas $16.5/MMBtu, Dirok $12.5/MMBtu
items.quote: The average realization of crude and condensate improved significantly to about $95.5 a barrel, compared with approximately $70.8 per barrel in the previous quarter on a standalone basis. In addition, the average gas price realization improved to $12 MMBTU, compared with 9.8 MMBTU in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Kharsang production doubled to 17,400 BOE from 12,300 BOE; 5-6 workovers done, 23 more wells identified; 2nd 9-well phase rig award imminent
items.quote: Even from an operational perspective, the production from Kharsang has been most encouraging, where production increased from approximately 12,300 barrels of oil to 17,400 BOE.

items.statement: B-80 workover risk: subsea wells need rig for re-perforation; 2P reserves 26 MMBOE with 1.5-2 MMBOE produced; PY-1 drilling contingent on gas sales agreement
items.quote: We believe our 2P reserves are still there, 26 million, of which 1.5-2 million has been produced so far. So there are reserves to be produced. So we are giving it our best shot, we are planning properly, and we hope that we will be able to minimize the risk.

items.statement: Kharsang gas pipeline: 24 km route survey tender closing; 6-8 months for right-of-way, 6-8 months construction; target Dec 2027 completion
items.quote: All going well, we believe in six to eight months, we should be able to get the right of way. If we get the right of use for the way -- for the pipeline route, then it is another six to eight months, it's just a 24 kilometer pipeline to lay. If it were to be an ideal situation, we would believe that by the end of next

items.statement: Cambay assets: 20-30% production increase expected from belt technology at Balol and debottlenecking at Palej; sucker rod pumps ordered
items.quote: Then we have also debottlenecked our Palej facility to be able to increase production by using thermionic heaters and those kind of things. So overall, 20% to 30% increase in production we will see going forward, although we have already seen a 5% to 6% increase in the last quarter.

items.statement: B-80 FSO crude sale planned for Oct 2026 post-monsoon; 120,000-150,000 barrels via smaller tankers to avoid demurrage
items.quote: In October, we'll sell. In October, we'll have sufficient volumes for a small tanker to be able to take it and we'll be able to sell, but that would be around 120,000 to 130,000 barrel of crude we'll be able to sell in October.

items.statement: IGL Spirits targets EBITDA above INR500 crore for FY27 and aims to become debt-free from FY28, targeting EBITDA above INR1,000 crore in 4-5 years
items.quote: All of this naturally gives us a very encouraging outlook for FY27 and we expect to deliver an EBITDA in excess of INR500 crores.

items.statement: Chemicals business aspires to reach INR2,500 crore revenue and INR400 crore EBITDA in 4-5 years, with gross margins approaching 30% by 2030
items.quote: The aspiration that we are looking at is to deliver an EBITDA of about INR400 crores and a business which is approximately INR2,500 crores in the next four to five years.

items.statement: Ennature Bio Pharma aspires to achieve INR130-150 crore EBITDA over the next 4-5 years
items.quote: In terms of our aspiration for EBITDA, I think over the next four or five years, we are aspiring to do a INR130 crores to INR150 crores EBITDA.

items.statement: Chemicals business expects minimal capex of INR5-20 crore in FY27, with no major plant investment for next 2 years
items.quote: So, there may be incremental capex, but we are talking about perhaps INR5 - 10 crores, maybe INR15 crores, INR20 crores based on the plans that we have right now.

items.statement: IGL Spirits Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 22.9% (+207 bps YoY) for Spirits and 10.8% (+250 bps) for Bio-Fuel
items.quote: Spirits business had a net revenue of INR371 crores with an EBITDA margin of about 22.9%, which is an improvement of 207 bps.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 15.0% in Q1 FY27 from 14.3% in Q1 FY26, continuing multi-year margin expansion trend
items.quote: EBITDA margin is 15.0% versus 14.3% in the Q1 last year.

items.statement: IMFL volume grew 55% YoY to 1.4M cases in Q1 FY27; Prestige & Above segment doubled to 0.5M cases; mass premium grew faster than premium
items.quote: We have grown 26% year-on-year in terms of net revenue, doing 1.4 million cases, which is a 55% growth over last year.

items.statement: IMFL industry growing at 4-5% CAGR; IGL Spirits expects healthy double-digit volume growth in FY28 driven by new launches and geographic expansion
items.quote: The outlook for next year, we expect to continue to grow in healthy double digits.

items.statement: War-related disruptions: crude spike and freight volatility (5-20x) created both tailwinds (bio-EO competitiveness) and headwinds (propylene oxide shortage, Middle East/US export collapse)
items.quote: The war has impacted us in multiple ways, some good, some not so good. So, it is both a combination of headwinds and tailwinds for us.

items.statement: Bio-based EO pricing reached parity or slight discount to Reliance's petro-EO for several months, boosting specialty chemical offtake and glycol penetration
items.quote: We were either similar to Reliance's prices or slightly lower, which meant that we had greater off-take for specialty chemicals and greater penetration for some of the glycols.

items.statement: Thiocolchicoside sales grew 26% QoQ supported by strong order pipeline and improved price realization; nicotine sales doubled QoQ driven by European customer conversions
items.quote: Thiocolchicoside sales registered a robust growth of 26% over the prior quarter, previous quarter, supported by a strong order pipeline, improved price realization.

items.statement: NCLT approved demerger scheme on July 17, 2026; effective date pending; will create three entities: IGL (chemicals), IGL Spirits (spirits + biofuel), Ennature Bio Pharma (nutraceuticals + biopolymers)
items.quote: NCLT has now sanctioned the scheme of arrangement on 17th of July 2026, and upon effectiveness, the Spirits, Bio-Fuel, and Bio Pharma undertaking transfer to dedicated resulting companies.

items.statement: Chemicals NSU segment aspires to reach INR150+ crore revenue in FY27 and INR600-700 crore in 4-5 years with modular capex approach
items.quote: We aspire to be INR150 crores plus in this year. And we aspire that in 4 or 5 years, we see this business to be possibly INR600 crores to INR700 crores business.

items.statement: IGL Spirits targets doubling IMFL volumes in FY27 vs FY26 (3.4M cases) through deeper penetration in UP, Uttarakhand, Delhi and new brand launches
items.quote: When I look at the volume, we are looking at doubling our volume from what we delivered last year.

items.statement: Management expects VNB growth to outpace APE growth in FY27, implying margin expansion.
items.quote: We do intend to grow VNB at a faster clip than the APE growth.

items.statement: VNB margin expanded to 23.2% in Q1 FY27 from 20.3% in Q1 FY26, driving 33% VNB growth.
items.quote: Our VNB margin expanded from 20.3% in Q1 of FY26 to 23.2% in Q1 FY27, driving a robust 33% growth in the value of new business or VNB.

items.statement: Margin uplift driven ~70% by favorable yield curve and ~30% by protection mix and operating leverage; GST impact largely behind.
items.quote: Now, in this 3% approximate increase, you can say 30% is linked to mix around protection and some bit of operating leverage and around 70%, you can say is the yield curve, which actually has also helped offset the GST impact.

items.statement: Policyholder operating expense ratio improved 185 bps YoY to 16% of GWP; opex grew only 7% vs 19% GWP growth.
items.quote: Policyholder operating expense as a percentage of GWP has improved by 185 basis points year -on-year to touch 16%, driven by focused productivity enhancement initiatives. Despite a healthy business growth, policyholder operating expense increased by only 7% during the quarter.

items.statement: Axis Bank infused INR 381 crore for 0.98% stake (now 19.99%), raising solvency to 198%; MFSL has enabling QIP approval (INR 1,600 cr) valid till May 2027 but no immediate need.
items.quote: We achieved a key milestone during the quarter with the completion of Axis Bank's acquisition of an additional 0.98% stake in Axis Max Life Insurance through an equity infusion of INR381 crore, increasing its shareholding to 19.99%... The infusion enhanced our financial strength, raising our solvency ratio to a robust

items.statement: Solvency at 198% (regulatory min 150%), internal risk threshold ~180%; can sustain 2-3 quarters without fresh capital; sub-debt of ~INR 480-490 cr redeemed July 31, will be re-raised.
items.quote: Our solvency is, as, as you are aware, the regulatory threshold of the solvency is 150 %. 198% is fairly well above the regulatory minima and also above our internal thresholds that we derive from a risk principal perspective.

items.statement: Persistency: 13-month at 83%; longer tenure (37/49/61 month) improving on premium and policy count basis; NPS improved to 63 (touchpoint 65, relationship 61).
items.quote: Our 13 -month premium persistency stood at 83%. Additionally, longer tenure persistency metrics, including 37th month, 49th month and 61st month persistency, continued to improve on both premium and number of policy bases.

items.statement: Offline proprietary APE grew 9% impacted by voluntary policy cancellations for quality; excluding that, growth robust; advisor recruitment up, top advisor premium +28%, FLS productivity +7%.
items.quote: On offline proprietary, to be very honest, I mean it is a small quarter and there were certain one -offs related to certain specific very consciously thought through cancellation that we had to undertake, which actually impacted the numbers.

items.statement: Dynamic repricing based on yield curve; June curve ~50bps lower at long end vs March may unwind some Q1 yield benefit in Q2, but operating leverage and mix to support VNB>APE growth.
items.quote: Your observation is correct. You are saying that at the end of the June, the curve has moved, which could take away not the entire, but some benefits that were available in the first quarter from a yield curve perspective.

items.statement: Online proprietary diversified: ~45% of Q1 sales outside largest aggregator (up from 38% YoY); D2C engine strong with good customer quality from Tier 2/3 markets.
items.quote: Actually, only, almost 45% of the sales in quarter one were outside this large aggregator. This number was 38% in the last year quarter one. So this number has clearly grown.

items.statement: Revenue, EBITDA and PAT growth guidance of more than 25% YoY for FY27
items.quote: The company is maintaining its guidance of an increase in turnover of more than 25% compared to the corresponding period in the last financial year.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR5,100 crores with INR1,251 crores legacy projects and balance at 10%+ margins
items.quote: Our order book today stands at approximately INR5,100 crores, providing healthy medium-term revenue visibility. items.statement: Order intake guidance of more than INR5,000 crores for FY27, with INR1,293 crores booked in Q1 and INR212 crores L1
items.quote: The company is hopeful of surpassing its guidance of more than INR5,000 crores in order intake in the current financial year, against which we have taken INR1,293 crores order in Q1 and are L1 in INR 212 crores of orders.

items.statement: BESS manufacturing facility 2.5 GW phase ready, expansion to 5 GW and 600 container units by H1 FY28 with INR236 crores total capex fully financed
items.quote: We expect the capacity enhancement from 2.5 gigawatt to 5 gigawatt along with the container facility expansion to be completed in the first half of FY 2028, along with the order for the associate facility, which addresses a market potential of 208 gigawatt by 2030.

items.statement: BESS revenue target of INR200-300 crores in Q4 FY27 from NTPC order subject to design approvals by December
items.quote: So if everything goes right, then we can expect 200 crores to 300 crores of BESS order execution into this financial year.

items.statement: New orders only accepted at 10%+ EBITDA margins; Q1 FY27 EBITDA margin improved to 10% from 9% YoY
items.quote: As a strategy, at this moment, we don't take any order less than 10%. So it is always more than 10%.

items.statement: Price variation clauses in all contracts to neutralize currency, steel and lithium price fluctuations
items.quote: As a strategy, we have made it very clear that we will keep a PV (price variation) clause in all our contracts. Our expertise is in execution, and that is where we will continue to focus and take calls. Everything else, whether it's a steel price increase, a dollar/currency increase, or a lithium price increase, all of

items.statement: Legacy debt of INR375 crores backed by INR678 crores arbitration award; targeting INR300 crores NARCL repayment in FY27
items.quote: We are targeting few arbitration award also into this financial year that will further reduce our liability to the NARCL. So we are expecting roughly around INR300 crores of left this NARCL payment after the completion into this financial year.

items.statement: Pipeline of 134 upcoming projects worth INR98,725 crores across 11 states, 80%+ in irrigation and water supply
items.quote: On the water and power front, we track a pipeline of about 134 upcoming projects, worth close to INR98,725 crores across 11 states, with irrigation and water supply making up over 80% of this value.

items.statement: Credit facility enhanced from INR505 crores to INR860 crores from PSU bank plus INR300 crores surety bond line
items.quote: We have also enhanced our credit facility of INR505 crores to INR860 crores from reputed PSU bank, the documentation of which is under process and approx INR300 crores surety bond line, ensuring adequate liquidity.

items.statement: Promoters infused INR400 crores over 3 years; net worth doubled from INR500 crores to over INR1,000 crores; debt-to-equity improved from 1.1x to 0.4x
items.quote: Our promoters have infused approx INR400 crores during the last 3 years, helping our net worth double from approximately INR500 crores to over INR1,000 crores, while our debt-to-equity ratio has improved from 1.1x to 0.4x now.

items.statement: Legacy orders of INR1,251 crores to be executed mostly in FY27 and FY28
items.quote: This will be executed this year and next year, most of the legacy order will be executed.

items.statement: BESS plant revenue potential: INR2,000-2,500 crores at 2.5 GW, INR4,500-5,000 crores at 5 GW capacity
items.quote: Basically, if it is a 2.5 gigawatt, it is -- revenue guidance will be between 2,000 crores to 2,500 crores. If it is a 5 gigawatt, it is roughly around 4,500 crores to 5,000.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance INR7,800-8,000 crore, 23-27% growth
items.quote: Revenue, we should do between INR7,800 crores to INR8,000 crores, which is a growth of 23% to 27%.

items.quote: The quarter also saw our order bookings of US$339 million, taking our order backlog to a record ever of approximately US$950 million, up 83% year-on-year.

items.statement: Plans to onboard nearly 2,000 professionals to support execution at scale
items.quote: We continue to hire and train talent at scale with plans to onboard nearly 2,000 professionals, ensuring that we have the resources required to support our customers' long-term growth plans.

items.statement: Strong demand across AI-led digital infrastructure, data centers, enterprise networking, managed services, cybersecurity
items.quote: We continue to see strong customer spending across AI-led digital infrastructure, data centers, enterprise networking, managed services and cybersecurity, giving us confidence in the sustainability of our growth pipeline.

items.statement: Non-hyperscale enterprise growing at modest double-digit ~10%; data center hyperscale driving 25% blended growth
items.quote: The non-hyperscale enterprise will grow at modest double-digit 10% odd. Combining, we are putting at 25% odd at this time.

items.statement: Operating cash flow to EBITDA conversion expected to improve meaningfully in FY27 vs FY26
items.quote: For FY27, we expect our operating cash flow to EBITDA conversion to improve meaningfully over FY26, supported by disciplined working capital management.

items.statement: Tax rate expected 10-15% for FY27 and FY28 due to carryforward losses; regularizing to ~20% thereafter
items.quote: For FY27 and FY28, I'm expecting it to be in the range between 10% to 15% and after that, it should regularize to around 20% type of levels.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 highest ever quarterly revenue INR1,719 crore, up 24% YoY; EBITDA INR160 crore, up 38% YoY; PAT INR56 crore, up 18% YoY
items.quote: Quarter one of FY27 was one of our strongest quarters as we reported highest ever revenue of INR1,719 crores, representing a 24% year-on-year growth. EBITDA increased to INR160 crores, up 38% year-on-year, while profit after-tax grew to INR56 crores, an increase of 18%.

items.statement: Aspires to improve UCP EBIT margins towards 7%+ over next 8 quarters, driven by cost optimization, scale benefits, and past capex investments
items.quote: So whether there's a room for improvement going forward over a long period of time over the next 8 quarters or so, the answer is certainly yes, actually because that eventually, we've had margins of upward of 7% in these quarters earlier.

items.statement: Segment B (Electromechanical Projects) carryover order book at Rs 6,345 crores as of June 30, 2026, providing revenue visibility
items.quote: As of 30th June 2026, the total carryover order book value for segment B stood at Rs. 6,345 crores, providing revenue visibility and underpinning the Company's confidence in the long-term prospects.

items.statement: UCP EBIT margin improved to 5.3% in Q1 FY27 from 3.7% in Q1 FY26 despite 10-12% cost inflation; near-full cost pass-through achieved
items.quote: Segment A margins improved significantly compared with the previous year despite commodity inflation and currency depreciation. These pressures were partially mitigated through progressive price increases and comprehensive cost optimization program.

items.statement: Total cost inflation 10-12% (7-8% from BEE table change, 4-5% from commodities/freight/FX); passed on nearly all to market, holding only 1-2% if any
items.quote: All that added up to another sort of 4% to 5%. And so overall, all put together, 10% to 12% was the cost, and we have also passed on very close to that number into the market, maybe a percentage or 2 lesser, if at all.

items.statement: RAC industry primary volume growth estimated at 20-22% in Q1 FY27; Voltas volumes grew 45% YoY, gaining share from 15.9% to 17.3%
items.quote: My sense is the primary increase would be anywhere between 20% to 22% in volume terms and maybe around 25% to 26% in value terms, maybe the industry growth.

items.statement: RAC mix steady at ~75% in-house / 25% OEM for Split ACs; Window ACs (10% of sales) fully outsourced; no shift expected
items.quote: In the Split AC bucket, we will have that 75-25 kind of mix. That will continue.

items.statement: Segment B margins soft in Q1 due to execution challenges and calibrated order booking; recovery expected from Q3 FY27 as shorter-gestation private sector projects ramp up
