items.quote: Yes, we are expecting approx. ₹100-130 odd crores in these two products. Not the entire ₹200 crores in year one. Gradually it will increase.

items.statement: Export sales target of ₹750 crore in FY27 with 45% from CDMO business
items.quote: The total export sales which we are expecting this year is ₹750 crores. And out of ₹750 crores, approx. 45% would be through the CDMO business.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin of 18%, potentially rising to 21-22% with sales growth
items.quote: Yes, yes, 18% is fully sustainable and we plan if the sales we are able to increase quarter-on-quarter they might go up to 21 to 22%.

items.statement: FY30 revenue target of minimum ₹1500 crore and net profit of approx ₹200+ crore
items.quote: FY30 is very long way to go, but yes, we would look for a revenue of minimum ₹1500 crores of a revenue and maybe a net profit of approx ₹200 plus.

items.statement: ₹250 crore capex over 2.5 years for warehouse, capacity enhancement, and Jammu facility upgrade
items.quote: That ₹250 crores will be deployed in capex over a period of 2.5 years approx.

items.statement: Additional ₹50-75 crore capex for two new CDMO customers, generating ₹150+ crore revenue
items.quote: See, the capex should be between the tune of ₹50 to 75 crores. And the revenue should be 150 plus.

items.statement: Export business gross margins at approximately 55%
items.quote: In the export business, we are enjoying approx. 55% margins. Gross margins.

items.statement: CDMO product selection requires minimum 50-55% gross margins
items.quote: So while selecting the products first point is very clear to us, it should have a minimum 50% of gross margins. That is the starting point, minimum 50 to 55%.

items.statement: Dossier filings target of 2500+ by Q4 FY27 from 2100+ currently
items.quote: We should be 400 plus. So from 2100 to 2500 is where we will reach by Q4 of this year.

items.statement: No plans to divest 7.8% stake in Synthimed this year; tag-along rights exist for future exit
items.quote: Currently there is no plans for divestment this year. This year the budgeted EBITDA of Synthimed is approx. ₹ 750-odd crores and we had gone through their first quarter results, and they are on track on achieving those numbers.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR3,104 crores with multi-year engagements and recurring revenue components
items.quote: As on date, our order book stands at approximately INR3,104 crores, providing strong visibility for future execution.

items.statement: Bidding pipeline at INR6,650 crores across data center, cloud, networking, workplace solutions, and managed services
items.quote: In addition, our bidding pipeline stood at approximately INR6,650 crores across data center and cloud, networking, workplace solutions, and managed services.

items.statement: Revenue normalization expected progressively over coming quarters; confident of maintaining long-term growth momentum
items.quote: We are very confident that based on the current visibility, the deliveries are expected to normalize progressively and we are confident of converting this order book into revenue over the coming quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement driven by better business mix, disciplined execution, and higher value-added services; trend expected to continue but may fluctuate quarterly
items.quote: The improvement in margins was primarily driven by a better business mix, disciplined execution, and higher contribution from value added infrastructure and managed services segments.

items.statement: Strong demand across all segments including AI infrastructure, data center modernization, cyber security, and managed services
items.quote: The demand continues to remain strong across all the segments there.

items.statement: Price escalation risk mitigated through back-to-back OEM support and contracted pricing; DaaS contracts repriced at fresh rates for new orders
items.quote: In a typical project once a customer order is finalized, it is finalized along with in tandem with the OEM there. So, at that time we have the OEM backing and the prices are already loaded in.

items.statement: Revenue impact in Q1 due to extended OEM lead times for AI infrastructure components (GPUs, memory, high-performance servers)
items.quote: The primary reason for this temporary decline is due to the extended delivery lead-times on certain orders due to OEM and supply chain lead-time issues which have deferred execution and revenue recognition during the quarter.

items.statement: Major wins: RBI INR750 cr private cloud, NPCI INR267 cr data center augmentation, CBI INR125 cr AI-ready infrastructure, J&K Bank INR25 cr ERP
items.quote: We secured a INR750 crores mandate from the Reserve Bank of India for private cloud infrastructure, a INR267 crores project from NPCI for the data center augmentation, a INR125 crores mandate from CBI involving AI-ready infrastructure and containerization platforms, and a INR25 crores ERP implementation engagement from

items.statement: Order book execution timeline: 18-24 months average, ranging from immediate to 5 years
items.quote: If you want to put a number to it, I would say you know 18 months to 24 months average time for the order execution there, but overall some of these are immediately executable to around five years.

items.statement: Competition intensifying at larger deal sizes (INR750 cr vs previous INR350 cr max); now competing with Tier-1 and global SIs
items.quote: Earlier our highest order was around INR350 crores. Now today we have a single largest order of INR750 crores. So obviously our qualification and the type of projects that we can successfully bid in has also... that trajectory has also changed. So we are able to participate in much larger projects there, and there the

items.statement: Participating in hyperscaler/co-lo data center wave with global large data center players in India, though margin profile lower than end-customer engagements
items.quote: We are working with some global large data center players in India with whom we are working there and working in that journey there. So yes, we are definitely looking at that segment.

items.statement: Targeting ROCE of 20%+ within next one year once ICONIQA stabilizes
items.quote: Of course, we are targeting an ROCE of 20% plus, okay, and which will happen in next couple of one year or so, once we have established -- once ICONIQA gets stabilized itself

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to ~30.7% from 30% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA grew faster than revenue, rising 39 % year-on-year to approximately INR modestly to approximately 33 cr which is Ebitda margin expanding modestly to approximately 30.7% from 30 %.

items.statement: Q1 occupancy 70% in JLO hotels, 60.8% in managed/franchise; ADR grew to INR 6,233 (JLO) and INR 4,300 (managed)
items.quote: as far as the occupancies are concerned, we are at 70% in our JLO hotels and at 60% odd, 60.8% at our -- all the managed and franchisee portfolio. And as far as the ADR is concerned, last year we were at an ADR of 5,488. This year, we are at an ADR of 6,233 in our JLO hotels. And in managed hotel, our last year ADR in

items.statement: Realization up 21% YoY to INR14,256/sqft driven by pricing increases and higher-value product mix
items.quote: Our realization though increased to INR14,256 per square foot, a strong 21% year-over-year improvement, driven by disciplined pricing increases in our existing projects and a positive shift in our product mix towards higher-value homes.

items.statement: Real Estate EBITDA margin improved to 21% from 12% YoY; improvement expected to sustain through FY27
items.quote: The operating impact of 5% to 6% in improvement in contribution margin itself will mostly be retained right through the year. But obviously, it will again depend on the mix as and when the revenue recognition comes through, but the improvement should be seen.

items.statement: Morgan Heights relaunch delayed due to SEIAA environmental clearance revocation; matter in High Court
items.quote: Our planned relaunch of Brigade Morgan Heights highlighted last quarter was impacted by the project's environmental clearance being revoked by SEIAA. We have refunded affected homebuyers. Our position remains that the project land does not fall within the Pallikaranai marshland.

items.statement: Commercial rentals achieving 10-15% mark-to-market increases on new leases
items.quote: The good news is that we are able to increase our rentals. So we are able to get that mark-to-market increase of at least 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Kochi hotel rebranding to Courtyard by Marriott expected to drive 15-20% ADR increase
items.quote: And because of the rebranding, we can expect at least a 15% to 20% increase in ADR.

items.statement: Hyderabad Neopolis 2 and Whitefield-Hoskote launches advanced to Q3 FY27 from Q4
items.quote: The Hyderabad launch, we are planning to advance that. I think it's looking quite likely to come much earlier than Q4. Definitely Q3, if not sooner. And the Whitefield Hoskote launch as well is looking like a Q3 launch for Bangalore.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR2,200-2,300 cr with 8-9% EBITDA; FY28 target INR3,000+ cr with 11-12% EBITDA
items.quote: This year, we are targeting somewhere around, you can say, INR2,200 crores to INR2,300 crores of revenue with EBITDA of around 8% to 9% this year. And next year should be the good year. We are thinking they try to cross INR3,000 crores plus with EBITDA of around 11% to 12%.

items.statement: Order book INR8,667 cr (excl. new HAM/mining); INR15,234 cr incl. new HAM and mining; 38% roads, 11% irrigation, 6% pipeline, 45% mining
items.quote: As on 30th June 2026, the company total order book stands at INR8,667 crores. This order book does not include the recently won 2 HAM project and mining project. Including the HAM project and the mining project, the company's total order book stands at INR15,234 crores.

items.statement: FY27 capex INR350-400 cr (mainly mining); Q1 capex INR14 cr; Kusmunda mining needs INR500-600 cr equipment; Banhardih needs INR300-400 cr
items.quote: FY27, we are planning somewhere around INR350 crores to INR400 crores basically mining capex will be more capex. So including that, it will be around INR350 crores to INR400 crores

items.statement: NHAI FY27 plan: 54 projects, 2,444 km, INR1.8 lakh cr; Railway capex INR2.93 lakh cr; AP railway allocation INR10,134 cr; Metro/urban mobility pipeline growing
items.quote: NHAI has also outlined a revised FY27 plan to award 54 highways and expressway project covering through 2,444 kilometers worth of combined INR1 .8lakh crores across 13 states so that the near -term awarding environment remains measured.

items.statement: Asset monetization: Sold 2 HAM SPVs to Indus Infra Trust; Ramagiri invested INR83 cr, got INR227 cr; Palani invested INR64 cr, got INR295 cr (incl INR90 cr EPC claim)
items.quote: In KNR Ramagiri, the company has invested INR83 crores in SPV through equity and subordinate debt and received a total consideration of INR227 crores from the purchaser. And for KNR Palani, the company has invested INR64 crores in SPV through equity and subordinate debt and received a consideration of INR295 crores, in

items.statement: Battery storage: Early stage, bids went badly, cautious approach due to dollar/price risk; No revenue guidance
items.quote: Sir, battery storage, initially, we tried some bids. They went ver y bad actually. So, right now, I think we are just preparing some bids, but I'm not very sure of winning a contract because the way things are moving here in India, they are very wrong actually.

items.statement: Domino's household penetration low: 6-7M Indians eat pizza monthly, only 3 occasions per 1,000 meals; massive category growth headroom; focus on growing frequency beyond 3 occasions
items.quote: what are we saying that there are 6 million -7 million Indians who are eating pizza every month, right? So that's a very low number. And even in those 6 million - 7 million out of 1,000 meals they will eat in a year, they will eat it 3 in those 1,000 occasions

items.statement: Targets same growth pace as last two years with healthy margins; may invest margin for growth if ROI favorable
items.quote: Our overall financial year basis target remains the same to continue the same pace of growth that we have demonstrated over the last two years.

items.statement: Positive consumer sentiment seen in August; expects festive demand in Q3/Q4 to improve price elasticity ROI
items.quote: If I am looking at Q2 generally, we are seeing positive consumer sentiment in August, and we hope that this will continue for the rest of the year.

items.statement: Women's wear emerging as growth pillar; targets 2-3x revenue in a year; Dockers license to contribute meaningfully in coming quarters
items.quote: We believe that in the future, women's wear could easily be at least 2x, if not 3x of our revenue in about a year's time, 3x of the current revenue in a year's time, considering the current pace.

items.statement: Wholesale/B2B2C channel now ~40% of Thomas Scott brand revenue (~INR 10 cr in Q1); margin neutral at EBITDA level
items.quote: Wholesale basis revenue now accounts for approximately 40% of the total revenue of Thomas Scott brands, highlighting the growing penetration of our best-selling styles across the aggregator-led route within the marketplaces.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacities fully occupied; adding capacity incrementally; CapEx not high, focused on operational needs like worker training and line efficiency
items.quote: Our manufacturing capacities are fully occupied. So, we largely have to produce in capital capacities, rent out or pay job work and kind of utilize other capacities of other factories.

items.statement: Fire incident last year led to elevated working capital debt; insurance claim of ~INR 21 cr under process; expects debt normalization and interest cost reduction upon settlement
items.quote: We had a fire incident last year where we had about Rs. 21 crore worth of stock covered by insurance fully. Against that, we had to take an elevated level of working capital loans to finance the inventory.

items.statement: Own website contribution increasing due to AI-oriented tech upgrades; sees potential as major future channel
items.quote: Our own website contribution has increased over the last few months, largely driven by certain technology-related uplifts that we have done on our own website and making it an AI oriented website.

items.statement: Offline stores EBITDA positive but ROCE lower than online; capital deployment focused online; selective store expansion may accelerate next financial year
items.quote: Stores have been growing consistently and they are EBITDA positive. But generally, when we look at our return on capital employed, we find better opportunities in what we are doing within the scope of online at the moment.

items.statement: Manufacturing mix steady at ~50% in-house, 35-40% job work, 5% trading; core fast fashion speed (15-45 days) requires in-house control
items.quote: We are looking at about 50% in-house, 40%, 35% odd outsource and 5% outright where we just buy out the goods and trade on it. So, that would largely be consistent.

items.statement: Customer acquisition cost typically 4-6% of GMV; higher in Q1 due to marketing spend but offset by higher price points
items.quote: Typically our customer acquisition costs are about 4% to 5%, sometimes 6% of the GMV basis and then the reductions are there. This quarter it would have been a little higher, much higher actually.

items.statement: Trade receivables decreased in Q1 despite higher revenue; insurance receivable claim in final stages, small exception item INR 3-4 lakhs recorded
items.quote: Our trade receivables have decreased this quarter. We have not disclosed it as it is not required as a part of a Q1 disclosure, but it has gone down with higher revenue level over last year.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 order intake of INR 915 crore is the highest ever quarterly order booking; sequential growth in double digits
items.quote: The order is what you see here is the number is INR915 crores. The good part here, the INR 915 crores is the highest ever quarter we booked order in any of the quarter.

items.statement: Order backlog grew ~33% to over INR 2,100 crore entering Q2 FY27
items.quote: Very good news that we still have very strong backlog, which is growth is close to 33% and around INR 2,100 crores plus backlog we are going entering into the Q2.

items.statement: Gross margin dipped due to commodity inflation (copper, transformer wire) impacting legacy orders booked before December with fixed prices
items.quote: When we said legacy orders means the orders which booked before December last year, and these all contracts has a price which we offer to the customer is kind of a firm price because the revision period was somewhere close to 6 months.

items.statement: Negative operating leverage in Q1 due to 5% sales growth vs higher fixed cost inflation (salary increments, 8-10% cost inflation, FX impact)
items.quote: Largely because of operating it started from Q1 and we will hopefully even out throughout the year.

items.statement: Price hike actions initiated timely on standard products; recovery varies by product due to different commodity composition
items.quote: We have initiated the price hike action right at the time when we started witnessing it. And that's the reason why I would not like to comment upon how the competition is doing.

items.statement: Price variation clauses cover only 20-25% of backlog (large projects >6-12 months); mandatory PV clauses now in new contracts but not enforceable in government tenders
items.quote: Historically, I think we -- given this heads up that on price variation clause in the contract, it's in the range of 20%, 25%, not more than that.

items.statement: Capex programs in Baroda (MV factory, transformer factory) and new Kolkata plant on track; staggered completions through CY27 and CY28 with ramp-up thereafter
items.quote: There are many things which are going to happen in calendar year '27. There are a few which is going to get over by '28 and thereafter a ramp-up plan.

items.statement: Healthy opportunity pipeline across emerging segments (data centers, semiconductors) and core Power & Grid; >20% of order book from emerging segments
items.quote: More than 1/5 of what is coming is on this new emerging segment is what we hold in our order bank.

items.statement: Emerging segments (data centers, semiconductors) driving higher project scope with installation/commissioning; transactional mix stable
items.quote: Emerging segments is coming with the higher scope, including installation and commissioning. So from supply, we are also getting into the larger the project execution cycle.

items.statement: Rupee depreciated ~8% YTD; commodity prices (copper, aluminum, steel, labor) rising; FX impact on import costs (10-15% of COGS) partially hedged by exports (10-12% of revenue)
items.quote: At the same time, there are certain headwinds, which all of us are facing and so is our company is also facing is the devaluation of rupee, which has gone down. And also it's about 8% is where the rupee has depreciated since the time we started this year.

items.statement: Confident on full-year FY27 delivery; pricing actions and execution plans initiated; balance 3 quarters expected to be good
items.quote: I'm confident that moving forward, the year, which are balance 3 quarters will be good for us.

items.statement: Export revenue 10-12% of total; Kolkata plant capex aimed at export growth but still in ramp-up phase; no medium-term export % target given
items.quote: Today, our export revenue is in the range of 10% to 12% in the revenue. And you know that the capex we invested in Kolkata largely will cater the export market, which is just starting.

items.statement: Strong macro tailwinds: GDP 6.5-7% for 4 years; per capita electricity consumption to reach 1,800-2,000 kWh by 2030; data center capacity 1.6 to 8 GW by 2030; EV penetration 8% to 30%; Vande Bharat trains 160 to 800
items.quote: Data center capacities, as you know, is going to grow up from 1.6 to about 8 gigawatts by 2030, if not more.

items.statement: Legacy fixed-price orders (pre-December) across Power & Grid segments compressing margins; cannot enforce price variation in government/EPC tenders
items.quote: So while we've taken an action, we can't enforce the price variation in all the government tenders backed by EPC and others. So that's -- we have a challenge there.

items.statement: Target overall growth of roughly 10%, with foreign growth expected to be more pronounced than domestic.
items.quote: In terms of growth, we have set a target of roughly about 10%. It varies for domestic and foreign. In foreign, we would expect a more pronounced growth than the domestic market.

items.statement: Domestic combined ratio target set at 103%, foreign combined ratio target at 95% over next 2-3 years.
items.quote: And we would like to have combined ratio target for domestic book at something like 103 and the foreign book at 95 in line with the global markets.

items.statement: Medium-term goal to achieve 60/40 domestic/international premium mix, long-term aspiration remains 50/50.
items.quote: What we are presently targeting with a medium-term in view is 60/40. But again, our goal will be 60/40, but as I said that domestic market outgrows the global market, so it will be a tough job.

items.statement: Life reinsurance portfolio requires evaluation over a full cycle; reserve strengthening previously impacted results, not an experiment but backed by actuarial analysis.
items.quote: I would suggest that life portfolio needs to be watched over a period of couple of years, because ultimately it continues to remain competitive and one has to watch a particular segment over a cycle rather than a couple of years.

items.statement: Investment book at INR 157,800 crores market value (INR 120,000 crores book value); allocation 73.4% fixed income, ~17% equity, ~8.7% money market.
items.quote: Market value as told is INR157,800 crores. That includes only equity, which is around INR58,000 crores, because debt is kept at cost only in ours as it is held to maturity.

items.statement: Solvency ratio improved to 4.32x as of June 30, 2026 from 3.85x a year ago; management expects gradual decline as growth resumes.
items.quote: Solvency ratio improved to 4.32 as on June 30, 2026, as compared to 3.85 as on June 30, 2025.

items.statement: Credit rating upgrade to 'A' from 'A-' expected in 4-5 years, contingent on IFRS/RBC implementation and business performance.
items.quote: If things go all right, probably one can expect in a period of, say, something like 4 to 5 years.

items.statement: Foreign premium target of INR 18,000 crores (historical peak) unlikely in 2 years due to softening rates; may take 3-4 years with focus on ROE over volume.
items.quote: Maybe not in a couple of years because of the significant softening trends, the same exposure is coming at a lesser premium. But maybe not in 2 years, maybe 3 or 4 years.

items.statement: Consolidated profit lower due to subsidiary losses: South Africa INR 287 crores loss, Moscow INR 29 crores loss in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: South Africa, we have shown INR287 crores loss during this quarter, and Moscow some INR29 crores loss from the subsidiary. That has resulted into the lower figure compared to last year in consolidated operating profit.

items.statement: Management guided for double-digit EBIT margin growth on standalone basis after steel price recovery
items.quote: we have given guidance, we will be able to grow EBIT margin in the double digit. And post the price recovery, we are confident that double digit margin improvement will keep happening in the future also.

items.statement: Rs.250 Crores already infused in Q4 FY26; another Rs.250 Crores planned in Q3 FY27; total guidance Rs.750 Crores over time
items.quote: we have already infused Rs.250 crores in the last quarter, maybe basically Q4 of the last financial year and we anticipate maybe in Q3, we will infuse another Rs.250 Crores. We are given a guidance of total put together about Rs.750 Crores infusion will happen over a period of time.

items.statement: Engineering volume grew 17% in Q1; demand bullish for next 1-2 quarters; exports up double-digit at 14% of revenue
items.quote: So volume grew about 17%.

items.statement: HCV tipper order book 20-25 units; port deployments at Welspun Anjar (22 trucks), Vizag, Chennai, Wonder Cement (Tuna/Dahej ports)
items.quote: As far as the existing tippers are concerned, we have sold about 20-25 numbers of tippers and the initial feedback is positive. Also, keeping in view the order book, which we have for some of the other products, where we have a confirmed order book

items.statement: Cycle business margin expansion in Q1; targeting at least 200 bps improvement for full year FY27
items.quote: we are hopeful, like we shared maybe at least another 2 basis point in the cycle business, we will be able to improve margin for overall year in the current financial year.

items.statement: L3 autos partially seeded in UP/Bihar for testing; full launch decision pending feedback
items.quote: we have introduced L3 products in quarter one, but in the select markets of UP and Bihar, we are testing those particular vehicles in these market and basis on the feedback that we get from these markets, we will take a call forward on L3 as a product.

items.statement: Maintained FY27 volume growth guidance at 6-8% and raised EBITDA per metric ton guidance to INR 24,000-25,000 from INR 19,000-21,000
items.quote: As regards to our guidance for the full year, we maintain our volume guidance at 6% to 8% for the full-year FY26-27, but I, however, increased the range of the EBITDA per metric ton guidance from the current INR 19,000 to INR 21,000 per metric ton to INR 24,000 to INR 25,000 per metric ton.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 EBITDA reached INR 252.5 crore, up from INR 135.1 crore YoY; EBITDA per MT improved to INR 35,458 from INR 20,009
items.quote: For quarter one, I'm pleased to inform you all that the EBITDA stood at INR 252.5 crores compared to INR 135.1 crores in Q1 FY26, while EBITDA per metric ton improved to INR 35,458 per metric ton from approximately INR 20,009 per metric ton in the corresponding period last year.

items.statement: Expect healthy demand through coming quarters driven by India festive season and improving international momentum, but monitoring West Asia geopolitical risks
items.quote: As we look ahead, demand indicators remain encouraging across many of our key markets. With the upcoming festive season in India and improving momentum across several international markets, we expect demand to remain healthy through the coming quarters.

items.statement: Geopolitical developments in West Asia creating feedstock volatility, longer transit times, port congestion and elevated freight costs requiring close monitoring
items.quote: While supply side pressures have started easing towards the end of June, the situation remains fluid and recent geopolitical developments have once again introduced volatility across commodity and the logistics markets. Longer transit times, port congestion and elevated freight costs continue to be the areas that requi

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of INR 150 crore, similar to last year, with some front-loaded capacity already commissioned
items.quote: We talked about capex guidance. So I think this year, we will be at about an additional listing of about INR 150 crores.

items.statement: Specialty Care mix improved, contributing positively to EBITDA per MT growth; new products SimpliX, Galaxy Hearth Biosurf, Everbond gaining traction
items.quote: Specialty Care mix has improved, contributing positively to growth in EBITDA per metric ton, moving us steadily towards objective of improving the quality of our earnings through a richer and more differentiated product mix.

items.statement: Fatty alcohol prices expected to move sideways between INR 2,600-2,800 per kg; no significant jumps or corrections anticipated
items.quote: We do see that there should be some steady state in the prices of fatty alcohol, because it's currently at about INR 2,700, INR 2,800 ship India. We do see that it should move sideways between INR 2,600 to INR 2,800.

items.statement: EPC project in Mexico progressing as planned, on track for commercialization within 12 months; EPC service income recognized in Q1
items.quote: I'm also pleased with the progress being made with our EPC project in Mexico. The project continues to progress as planned, contributing EPC service income during the quarter, and we remain on track for commercialization over the next 12 months.

items.statement: India volumes grew 11% YoY led by double-digit performance segment growth; Tier 1 customer demand recovered; non-Tier 1 and D2C grew near double-digit
items.quote: India, our primary engine grew by an impressive 11% led by double-digit growth in performance segment and high single-digit growth in specialty products. More importantly, we witnessed a recovery in Tier 1 customer demand and the return of positive growth momentum in businesses that have been impacted by reformulations

items.statement: Reformulation risk remains if petrochemical prices fall significantly while oleochemical prices stay elevated; currently balance is favorable
items.quote: I would say that, yes, if the petrochemical prices come down significantly and the alcohol prices remain elevated, like as of today, when we see the balance, we do see that the balance is not significantly concerning, for the reformulation to get aggravated.

items.statement: No acquisition planned in AMET region; focus on debottlenecking and diversifying portfolio to other countries
items.quote: AMET market very clearly, we have already done our capex. We obviously will be -- any capexes that we'll be doing there will be more in terms of certain debottlenecking exercises we'll do investments. There is no acquisition we are planning in AMET for sure.

items.statement: New product pipeline targeting >5% of revenue and contribution margins by 2030; some launches expected next quarter
items.quote: And we do look at all new products, -- this thing is by 2030, they should contribute to almost greater than 5% of our total revenue and our contribution margins.

items.statement: Inorganic growth evaluation ongoing with strict criteria; significant work underway but no announcement yet; will not pursue deals for fear of missing out
items.quote: Yes. So this is something that we are progressing well in terms of the way that we are evaluating, mandate with regard to what can be the targets. but we need to get the right fit. we are very clear that we will not do anything that doesn't meet the criteria that we have set, because anything that we do has to be in li

items.statement: Management aims to sustain double-digit revenue growth over the long term, averaging out quarterly volatility.
items.quote: we have been saying for the past few investor calls that what we have been aiming at to sustain a double-digit growth

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 69.05% in Q1 FY27, up ~3% YoY; management expects margins to remain around current levels but acknowledges pressure at higher volumes.
items.quote: EBITDA percentage of total income was 69.05%, also nearly 3% higher than the corresponding period of FY26

items.statement: Scrap sales contribute 50-55% of e-commerce revenue; mineral blocks and coal auctions are the next largest contributors.
items.quote: almost about 50% to 55% of our e-commerce revenue is coming from scrap sale over the past many years

items.statement: Asset-light strategy maintained; no major capex planned. New verticals (TReDS, EPR, Travel, Coal Exchange) leverage existing digital infrastructure.
items.quote: We also took a decision to remain an asset-light company. So, apart from scaling up existing e-commerce business by aggressively expanding our client footprint, we decided to venture into a limited number of new verticals

items.statement: Coal India linkage auctions (NRS) first batch underway; sector-wise auctions to follow. Critical mineral block allocations (7th tranche) completed.
items.quote: we have won the contract with Coal India for coal linkage auctions. So, the first batch of auctions for the same is underway right now and it is expected to be extended to other sectors

items.statement: MMRPL JV turned profitable in Q1 FY27 driven by higher ELV feedstock from EPR norms and OEM/government incentives; positive outlook expected to continue.
items.quote: For the first time in quite a few number of sequential reporting periods, the venture has shown a positive PAT. This has largely been driven by significantly higher feedstock inflows

items.statement: EPR certificate exchange platform ready but awaiting government notification; no minimum volume guarantee; revenue potential speculative until operational.
items.quote: As on date, everything is happening completely in the dark. Nobody knows as to how many certificates are getting transacted, what is the value of the certificates

items.quote: We effectively are seeing a situation where the demand from the Western Hemisphere, which is largely U.S. and Latin America, is ramping up.

items.statement: Clove supply disrupted by Madagascar floods and port closure (~30 days); shipping challenges persist but material flowing from May
items.quote: there was a major cyclone resulting into flood-like situation in the cultivation areas in Madagascar. As a result of which, the incoming raw material shipments were significantly delayed because even their port in Toamasina was shut down, I believe for a period of close to 30 days.

items.statement: Brazil subsidiary approved to expand distribution reach in Latin America for essential oils, aromatic and specialty chemicals
items.quote: The company has approved the incorporation of a Brazil subsidiary, representing another step towards expanding our distribution reach in Latin America and creating a dedicated platform for our essential oils, aromatic chemicals, and specialty chemicals.

items.statement: Currency depreciation not a tactical advantage due to import-processing-export model and hedging of foreign contracts
items.quote: it is not really a tactical advantage nor is it a disadvantage for us because we import, we hedge our foreign contracts in terms of what the export realization is and then we subsequently export it out.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 capex INR7.36bn, of which INR5.88bn deployed at Sri City plant; capitalization expected from H2 FY27
items.quote: On the capital expenditure, for the quarter, we land up at INR7.36 billion of out of which INR5.88 billion was deployed at Sri City. We expect capitalization to begin from the second half of this fiscal year as the aircon compressor and room air conditioner lines come on stream.

items.statement: EBITDA margin 12.5% in Q1 FY27, up 110bps YoY and 80bps QoQ; driven by premium mix, calibrated price hikes, operating leverage
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR9.04 billion as compared to INR7.16 billion, a growth of 26.2% with an EBITDA margin of 12.5% as compared to 11.4% in Q1 FY26, an improvement of 110 bps points year-on-year.

items.statement: Calibrated price increases taken across selected categories absorbed input cost inflation without impacting demand; further hikes only if input costs require
items.quote: On the price side, we have already taken a calibrated increase, and which has absorbed well in the market, and further action would only follow if input costs require, but however the cost and the sourcing efficiency will always be the first preference.

items.statement: Broad-based double-digit growth across all categories in Q1; TV and washing machines expected to drive H2 growth; ACs and refrigerators to benefit from premiumization and replacement demand
items.quote: We see demand remaining very healthy across both Home Appliances and Home Entertainment in this financial year. What gives us the confidence that Q1 has already demonstrated that we can deliver a very strong growth even challenging external environment.

items.statement: Premium and Essential series both growing strongly; 55-inch+ TVs grew ~53% YoY and now ~50% of TV revenue; Essential series sold >500k units in Jan-Jun 2026
items.quote: In our product portfolio, 55-inch and above segment has grown roughly around 53% in quarter one. And now our 55-inch plus segment is contributing around 50% of our overall business.

items.statement: B2B segment delivered strong Q1 growth; Information Display LED signages hit highest ever quarterly sales; 36% market share; confident of 20% CAGR trajectory
items.quote: In information display panels, our LED signages recorded its highest ever quarterly sale in the Q1. And with continuous inflow of government and corporate orders, we have also achieved 36% market share in this business.

items.statement: Government imposed quantitative restrictions on compressor imports (60% reciprocating, 70% rotary); LG benefits from local compressor capacity (1mn at Greater Noida, +2mn at Sri City)
items.quote: In this year, 8th of May, the Government of India, they introduced quantitative restriction on the import of compressors. So import of compressors are restricted against the financial year 2024-2025 up to 60% for the reciprocating compressors which we use for refrigerators and around 70% for the rotary compressor which

items.statement: No external borrowing needed; Sri City INR5,000cr investment funded from internal accruals; cash balance INR57.07bn as of June 30, 2026
items.quote: Preserving our internal accruals to fund this investment entirely without any external debt is a conscious and deliberate decision that we believe is in the best long-term interest of our shareholders.

items.statement: Localization rate 55.2% in FY26; targeting 65% over next 3-4 years; Sri City plant to accelerate localization and act as export hub
items.quote: Our localization rates for the last full year was at 55.2%. And we are continuing focus on further improving this in current year as well. Over the past years, we have consistently improved our localization rate by 2% to 3% every year and we expect this to maintain trajectory going forward. Our target to reach the loca

items.statement: Data center cooling seen as long-term B2B opportunity; mid-scale segment already revenue-generating; hyper-scale at preliminary evaluation stage; not a key FY27 driver
items.quote: From a materiality standpoint, this is not a key driver for us in FY27 outlook, but yes, it aligns well with our long-term B2B growth strategy.

items.statement: Dividend payout deferred to fund Sri City capex; management commits to review dividend plans as investment progresses and cash generation strengthens
items.quote: We would like to assure our shareholders that this is not a permanent position. As our Sri City investment progresses in a phased manner and our cash generation strengthens further through revenue growth and margin improvement, we definitely plan to review our dividend plans.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guided at INR840 crore (granite INR720 crore, quartz INR100-120 crore) vs FY26 INR645 crore
items.quote: FY27 we will be close to -- we are estimating around INR840 crores against past year's number of INR645 crores.

items.statement: Granite EBITDA margin expected in same range as prior years (50-100 bps variance) unless diesel price impact
items.quote: Granite-wise, we will be achieving whatever we have recorded in the last few years. It will be more or less in the same lines. Except unless we have diesel price impact. We will be we will be like maybe a 50 bps to 100 bps kind of a range, we will be in the same lines as last years.

items.statement: Quartz Phase 2 capex ~INR125 crore split over FY27 and FY28; INR60-70 crore outflow in Q2-Q3 FY27
items.quote: Capex on quartz would be approximately INR125 crores.

items.statement: Sri Lanka project plant build capex ~INR120 crore
items.quote: Sri Lankan project for plant building it's around INR120 crores.

items.statement: Granite demand strong with 35% YoY revenue growth; pricing improved; diesel cost volatility main concern
items.quote: Demand is good, you can see from the numbers we have 35% topline growth. I think if you remove the quartz part, we are still above 30. So I think the demand-wise is good, the pricing-wise we have had a better realization.

items.statement: Quartz sales mix: 65% engineered stone, 35% solar
items.quote: Around 60% to 65% engineered stone, balance solar. I think 65-35 is a reasonable assumption.

items.statement: Quartz production ramp: Q2 FY27 ~20,000 tons/month, Q3 FY27 10,000-12,000 tons/month, Q4 FY27 >15,000 tons/month; FY27 quartz revenue INR100-120 crore
items.quote: This quarter we are looking at around 20,000 and the next quarter by the end of this quarter, we will be able to touch a run rate of 10,000. So next quarter, you can do 10,000 to 12,000. I think Q4, we will be exceeding 15,000. That's the plan.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin FY27 ~26-27%; FY28 expected ~29-30% as quartz scales
items.quote: EBITDA would be close to 30%, little above 30%. And overall blended EBITDA might be around 29%, 30%.

items.statement: Granite order book supports 10-12% volume growth in FY27; Q4 historically 30-38% of annual revenue due to Chinese New Year
items.quote: I think last year it was 35% of the overall year revenue. So that is also historically constant for us. So this year also I think it will be not be any different.

items.statement: Diesel cost volatility key risk; electrification of fleet and solar back-integration underway to reduce exposure
items.quote: The biggest lever in this is the volume growth, right revenue growth. So if if revenue growth is able to absorb most of the other costs, fixed costs and I think that revenue growth we will be able to meet, we feel as of now.

items.statement: MoU signed with Indonesia's PERMINAS for rare earths (ionic clays, heavy & light); JV formation expected this quarter; first production in 12-15 months post-JV
items.quote: Now this MoU will be translated into an agreement to form a JV along with them and I think you will find developments on that during this quarter which we will update you in the next meeting.

items.statement: Sri Lanka policy finalized; license expected this quarter; ground breaking ~October; plant build 12-15 months; revenue from FY29
items.quote: I think we will can start internally timelines we can start breaking the ground somewhere in October. So I think from that point of time, we should look at 12 to 15 months for the plant build-out and start operations.

items.statement: Kerala JV stalled awaiting new government MD appointment; progress expected next quarter
items.quote: We are hoping that once the new MD and new team comes in place, we will start progressing that and in continuation to that. Now, a timeline on that we frankly cannot estimate, because government thing.

items.statement: Intent to keep operating costs flat in USD terms over coming couple of years; only INR cost changes from currency translation
items.quote: So in dollar terms, our intent would be to keep the employee expenses and the admin expenses flat over the coming couple of years. That would be the intent.

items.statement: Gross profit per unit (yield) at current levels considered sustainable; incremental volume growth directly multiplies gross profit; EBITDA margin % not relevant due to freight pass-through
items.quote: In terms of the gross profit per unit of volume, we believe that the current levels can be sustained. So any incremental growth that you would see in volumes would be a direct multiplier on the gross profit.

items.statement: Sequential volume improvement across trade lanes: LCL and air up ~5% QoQ, FCL up ~1% QoQ; half of growth from market, half from outperformance
items.quote: As an outcome of that, we have seen incremental volumes in both LCL and air of the magnitude of about 5%, while on the FCL, we have seen a quarter-on-quarter growth rate of about 1%.

items.statement: Freight rates elevated due to capacity constraints from geopolitical disruptions; higher rates improve container utilization and FCL margins, boosting absolute gross profit despite pass-through nature
items.quote: The capacity on the carrier side has been somewhat more constrained with all these disruptions. And as an outcome of that, the freight rates prevailing over the last few months have been on the higher side.

items.statement: LCL is highest margin, lowest working capital business with 14.5% global market share; FCL <1% share but higher growth potential from low base; air sits in middle
items.quote: In the addressable market globally we hold about 14.5% market share in LCL. In FCL that number is not even 1%.

items.statement: Business is extremely asset-light; capex investments are tiny fraction of P&L; most depreciation is non-cash from goodwill and acquisitions
items.quote: As a business, it's an extremely asset-light business with hardly any capital assets owned or even the capex investments are a tiny fraction of the company's P&L.

items.statement: No near-term acquisition plans; strategy is organic growth through hiring teams for new markets/products; present in all relevant markets and products
items.quote: At least in the near term, the strategy is to grow by investing in people and not buying businesses.

items.statement: Maintain FY27 revenue growth guidance of 30% and 100% EBITDA improvement
items.quote: To add on here, the annual guidance was 30% revenue improvement and 100% EBITDA improvement remains the same.

items.statement: Offline business targeting near profitability in FY27 with steady-state margin of 13-15%
items.quote: Our clear path to profitability of a steady state of 13% to 15% will largely come in from an ARPU play and improving the outcomes.

items.statement: Online margins improving from 27% in FY26 with further expansion expected in FY27 as new categories break even
items.quote: Last fiscal year we witnessed around 27% margins. items.statement: Offline Vidyapeeth centers from FY23-24 cohort already delivering 13-15% margins
items.quote: The steady-state margin is 13% to 15% which we are delivering in our '23-'24 centers.

items.statement: NEET exam cycle shift delayed enrollments by 5-7 weeks; offline growth would have been 22-25% vs reported 14%
items.quote: The offline revenue growth that has been witnessed to the tunes of 14% for this quarter y-o-y would have been to the tunes of 22% to 25% had the NEET examination cycle would have sort of been over by 4th of May.

items.statement: Online K-12 enrollments grew 41% YoY to 0.78M; revenue up 88% to INR105 cr
items.quote: It has grown by 40% - 41% enrollment-wise from 0.55 million to 0.78 million. Revenue-wise, it has grown by 88% year-on-year from INR56 crores to INR105 crores.

items.statement: NEET PG enrollments up ~50%, collections up 100% YoY
items.quote: This year we have seen NEET PG enrollments growing approximately by 50% and the collection are growing by 100% in NEET PG.

items.statement: Vernacular enrollments and revenue up 1.7x; state board enrollments and revenue doubled
items.quote: Vernacular, which is a vision to make a pan-India brand, we have 1.7x jump in our enrollments and revenue in vernacular categories. K-12, Alakh already spoke about, like 41% jump in enrollment and 88% jump in our revenue. Along with that, our state board, which is a huge, huge TAM, the enrollments are doubled, so does

items.statement: Online revenue grew 33% YoY; offline grew 16% YoY; online now 33% of total revenue mix
items.quote: Revenue from online grew 33% year-over-year and offline and other businesses grew at 16%.

items.statement: Offline expansion opportunistic and limited; new center planning to be decided over next 2 quarters
items.quote: Our approach to offline expansion will be opportunistic and limited to geographies that fit into our cohort economics. Accordingly, new centers planning would probably get decided over the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: Treasury at INR5,600 cr including INR2,000 cr IPO proceeds; capital allocation focused on online content/categories organic and inorganic
items.quote: As of June 30, our treasury is INR5,600 crores, including IPO proceeds of INR2,000 crores. Like I mentioned last time, our capital allocation will largely be towards new online content and categories, both organic and inorganic.

items.statement: Divesting Finzy Fintech; received interest and signed 2 non-binding term sheets; expect completion in a quarter
items.quote: Along with the capital allocation, we have decided to divest Finzy Fintech and we have already received couple of interest and signed 2 non-binding term sheets. So, probably in a quarter timeline we will be able to achieve this divestment.

items.statement: Pathshala centers reduced from 84 to 70 due to conversion to Vidyapeeth format; zero closures
items.quote: So, zero Pathshala has been closed. Actually those Pathshalas were converted into Vidyapeeth.

items.statement: Gross margin expected in 67%-69% range for FY27; Q3 seasonally strong
items.quote: I would try to kind of keep it in the 67% to 69% zipcode, right, like at least for this year and see where it goes.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin 11.5%, up from 5% YoY and 1.2pp sequentially despite salary increments
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA rose to INR50 crores with a 11.5% margin and PAT was INR34 crores with a 7.5% margin.

items.statement: Trailing 12-month net revenue retention (NRR) reached 125% in Q1 FY27
items.quote: We saw our trailing 12-month net retention, NRR going up to 125%.

items.statement: 10 active AI pilots; major U.S. news network selected Newspulse for AI-first newsroom transformation
items.quote: We have more than 10 active pilots across different customers. And more importantly, we had a major U.S. news network that selected Amagi's Newspulse to transform themselves into an AI-first newsroom.

items.statement: Generated $282K monthly run-rate cloud cost savings in Q1, reinvested into AI initiatives
items.quote: In Q1, we generated about $282,000 of monthly run rate savings in gross margin cloud cost optimization that we've reinvested into the AI-related initiatives.

items.statement: Target adjusted EBITDA breakeven for full year FY27 with profitability expected in H2 FY27
items.quote: We also indicated that we'll try really hard for the entire year to be adjusted EBITDA breakeven in the current year. We also indicated in the last call that given the seasonality in the business, some of this profitability should come in the second half of the current financial year.

items.statement: Expect corporate overheads to decline to 7-8% of revenue over next 4-5 years from current 22%
items.quote: Our corporate overheads continue to reduce and we expect over the next four to five years for it to come below to 7-8%.

items.statement: Service EBITDA margin expanded to ~13% in Q1 FY27 from ~10% in Q1 FY26, driven by renewal book growth and operating leverage
items.quote: In Q1 FY27, service EBITDA has grown at nearly 90% to reach INR 39 crores for the quarter. This is approximately 13% of our quarterly revenues.

items.statement: Renewal service EBITDA is 2.5-3x higher than new business service EBITDA due to lower CAC and better insurer terms
items.quote: Renewal from a service EBITDA point of view, if I were to compare renewal service EBITDA to new service EBITDA, renewal service EBITDA is about 2.5 times to 3 times higher than the new service EBITDA.

items.statement: Platform premium grew 49% YoY to INR 1,205 crores in Q1 FY27, with strong growth across motor, health (45%+) and life (60%+)
items.quote: Platform premium for the quarter was INR 1,205 crores, which has grown by 49% YoY.

items.statement: Renewal revenue share increased to 22% of total revenue in Q1 FY27 from 19% in Q1 FY26, growing 66% YoY
items.quote: Renewal revenue last year was 19%. This year, it has gone up to 22% in Q1.

items.statement: Active digital partners (P3M) grew 30-32% YoY to ~90,791, with total DP base at 690,000+ after recruiting 32,000+ in Q1
items.quote: Our P3M Active base, meaning rolling 90-day active, were just above 90,000 active digital partners for the quarter, which was a growth of about 30% YoY.

items.statement: DP attrition stable: 28-30% in first 24 months, then 2-3% annually, with ~65% retention at year 5-6
items.quote: Basically, over the years, we know that in the first 18 months, there is a learning curve. And you see some attrition of about 28 -30% in the first 24 months. Then the attrition rate drops to 2-3% where basically 95% of the people after 18 months retain on the platform.

items.statement: Claims servicing handled INR 26+ crores in Q1 with 1.5 lakh+ service requests, building trust and differentiation
items.quote: During Q1, we helped policyholders settle claims amounting to more than INR 26 crores, there would have been some complexity delay or rejection. We handled around 1.5 lakh plus unique servicing requests during this quarter.

items.statement: Management expects 35% top-line and EBITDA growth in FY27 vs FY26, with similar growth continuing in FY28 and FY29
items.quote: I think we're expecting 35% growth in our top line in this financial year. And similarly, EBITDA also, we'll see the same growth coming up in this financial year as compared to last financial year.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margin of 14%+ seen as achievable for FY27, with potential for better if geopolitical conditions remain favorable
items.quote: As of now, what we can perceive that, that will happen. But if things remain as good as they are currently and no untoward incident happens on the geopolitical front, we'll give you better results than this.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 normalized EBITDA margin 15.5% (up 480bps YoY); overseas ops contributed 91% of incremental EBITDA; management confident margins sustainable for next 3 years
items.quote: Normalized EBITDA post adjustment of Rs. 825 million on forex derivative transactions reached Rs. 8,373 million, which is 78% growth year-on-year, expanded to 15.5%. Our overseas operations contributed around 91% of the Rs. 4,410 million incremental EBITDA.

items.statement: BOPP prices up 25-32%, BOPET up 30-35% since Feb 2026 due to West Asia crisis; raw material costs rising but less than finished goods; pricing seen as stable at current levels while crisis persists
items.quote: BOPP prices have gone up by 25%, and BOPET prices have gone up by almost 30%-35% from, to be specific from February '26 level to now, it is 25-32% higher on BOPP and BOPET rate is around 30-35% higher.

items.statement: Strategic shift to value-added products driving margin expansion; 60-70% of future capex to value-added verticals (Aseptic, WPP, recycling); Aseptic expected to rebound from Q3 with Egypt plant adding ~2B packs in FY27
items.quote: We are moving from normal films to value-added products, which can give us a better realization, so those are being done very aggressively now. From Q3 onwards, you see Aseptic coming back on track.

items.statement: West Asia crisis (Bab-el-Mandeb) creating supply chain disruptions but UFlex's derisked multi-geography model (local-for-local) mitigates impact; duty-free Aseptic imports from Indonesia pressuring India volumes
items.quote: We are running a derisked model now. India caters to mostly India demands and other areas cater to other areas demand. Somebody who is dependent on Indian export only will have a difficulty in supplying the material. But we have all across geographies and are fully integrated.

items.statement: Revenue growth expected around 20% for FY27, higher than previous 12% guidance
items.quote: See, 27% is obviously very good growth, but we expect the revenue growth to be in the range close to 20%, right, much better than the 12% guidance we had given earlier, around 20% something.

items.statement: Capex of INR 170-180 crore planned for FY27, part of INR 500 crore total capex largely completing by FY28
items.quote: it's largely this year, we are expecting to have a capex of about INR170 - 180 crores at least in the current financial year.

items.statement: INR 500 crore total capex largely completing by FY28, with some spillover possible to FY29
items.quote: Largely, if you look at FY basis, largely it would be over by FY28. Maybe some part could spill down to FY29, but largely it will be over by FY28.

items.statement: Commodity inflation pass-through to OEMs is work in progress with 1-2 quarter lag; exact numbers not disclosed
items.quote: On price and commodity inflation, if you see our OEM contracts usually have a clause around the commodity inflation linked to the index in which we keep working along with the OEMs. And even currently, it's the work in progress for the recent round of commodity inflation.

items.statement: Vehicle aftermarket volumes slightly declined; focus on protecting margins and recovering volumes in next 5 months
items.quote: So vehicle aftermarket business has a certain different set of challenges. So far, it's kind of plateau or a small decline in our revenue. The next 5 months, we have some different strategy to cover up or recover our volume.

items.quote: our OEM basically, it contributes about 62%, as you have seen it, out of which our 2-wheeler is about 54%, passenger vehicle is around 31% and commercial vehicle is about 15%.

items.quote: we have got a very good wheel-end business from one of the customers which we were working since last couple of years after so many audits. items.statement: EV bearing programs in development phase, full production ramp-up expected mid-2027 with revenue visibility in 2028
items.quote: These are the businesses that will come on stream during 2028, more precisely towards the last quarter of the calendar year, 2028.

items.statement: Sales to SKF Industrial not a growth priority; expected to decline over next few years as capacity shifts to automotive
items.quote: as far as the volume is concerned, as Shailesh mentioned, it's not a priority for growth. This is something which over the next few years is expected to come down. And we focus that capacity towards serving our automotive customers.

items.quote: Now our all the 3 plants have been achieved more than 98% renewable energy sourcing. items.statement: Commodity cost pressures to peak in Q2, with softening expected from Q3 and turnaround in Q4
items.period: Q2 FY27, Q3 FY27, Q4 FY27
items.quote: Respite from that we think will come in Q3 and Q4 only. So it will be a challenging quarter, but then we are accelerating a few things internally

items.statement: Price increase of 1.2-1.25% taken in Q1; additional hikes in July (MHCV >1%, LCV >2%) and more planned before quarter end
items.quote: Price increase during the quarter was about 1.2% - 1.25%. That also helped us in negating the commodity cost increases

items.quote: Despite record revenues, the EBITDA was flat at INR970 crores as compared to same quarter last year. EBITDA margin was 10.1%, 100 basis points lower on Y-o-Y basis

items.statement: Capex outlook increased to INR 900-1,000 crore range for FY27, up from historical INR 400-500 crore; expected to rise further over next 2-3 years
items.quote: We were generally doing about INR400 crores, INR500 crores. And in last 2 years, we are in the range of INR900 crores to 1,000 crores

items.statement: MHCV industry growth expected at high single digit for full year FY27; LCV outlook slightly better; Q2 growth to be much better than Q1's 13-14%
items.quote: even if we take a conservative outlook for the second half of the year, let us say, October, November onwards, we still believe that the industry has potential to grow by high single digit

items.quote: Switch Mobility has a healthy order book of 2,100 e-buses. During the quarter, Switch Mobility delivered 225 electric buses and close to 300 electric light commercial vehicles

items.statement: Key risks: elevated commodity prices (steel, natural rubber), regulatory burden (potential BS7 by 2031-32), competitive intensity in MAV segment
items.quote: We remain mindful of the key risks, particularly the elevated commodity prices, but shall continue to put all efforts to achieve better price realization and mix

items.quote: we have about GBP 50 million debt, which is there, and we don't want to incur interest cost. So, we are trying to pay another GBP 25 million by this year, and we will pay another GBP 25 million by next year

items.statement: Net cash position strengthened to INR 2,252 crore (up INR 1,431 crore YoY); HLF AUM grew 20% to INR 60,310 crore; HHF AUM grew 13% to INR 16,157 crore; both maintain net NPA at 2.1%
items.quote: We had net cash of INR2,252 crores at the end of the year, an increase of more than INR1,431 crores on a Y-o-Y basis

items.statement: Expect INR900 crore profit repatriation from St. Regis Dubai in FY27; INR142.58 crore received in Q1, balance on track
items.quote: we have in the current quarter received AED55 million, which in Indian rupee terms translates to INR142.58 crores. And we had projected that we will receive up to INR900 crores in the current financial year. And I should say that we are on track to receive the balance amount.

items.statement: Expect INR258 crore loan repayment from Zuari Agro Chemicals in Q2 FY27
items.quote: we are expecting, as I mentioned earlier, the entire INR258 crores outstanding debt to be repaid to us in the current quarter.

items.statement: Simon India executed INR30 crore projects in Q1 with INR70 crore under execution; West Asia crisis deferring capex
items.quote: during the quarter we executed projects worth about INR30 crores with approximately INR70 crores worth of orders currently under execution. The ongoing crisis in West Asia has resulted in deferred capex across sectors

items.statement: Sugar prices up 10% in past month to record highs; UP prices INR4,860-4,920/quintal; festival demand expected to support realizations
items.quote: Indian sugar prices have risen 10% over the past month to record highs. Prices in Uttar Pradesh are currently at INR4,860 to INR4,920 per quintal, with Maharashtra also registering reasonably high prices. With festival demand expected to gather pace, the pricing environment is expected to support sugar realizations.

items.statement: Ethanol realizations static at INR60.70/liter, weighing on margins; expect government price revision soon
items.quote: As regards our ethanol business, the realization, the prices continue to be static and therefore they weigh on the margins. However, we remain optimistic about the sector's outlook and expect the government to consider a price revision in the near term.

items.quote: Despite the improvement in sugar volumes and realizations, margins remained somewhat under pressure, substantially due to about 8% increase in the SAP, which was INR30 per quintal for the last season, as well as somewhat lower recovery from ethanol

items.statement: UP ethanol import/export pass fee exposure INR507 lakh not provided for; confident law cannot be applied retrospectively

items.statement: Raw material pressure (copper, aluminium, compressor imports) easing; price increases requested from customers to average out over next couple of quarters
items.quote: We hope that now the pricing is a little more stable. And over the next couple of quarters, I mean, we hope that the price increase that we are requesting our customers and also the market will effectively even out or average out.

items.statement: FY27 revenue mix: AC 55-60%, Compressor ~15%, EMS ~10%, Commercial Refrigeration ~10%, Components/Washing Machine ~5%
items.quote: AC will remain at around 60%, 55% to 60% of the overall revenue. EMS will stay at about 10% in terms of the overall contribution. Commercial refrigeration will be at par, at about 10%. The component washing machine and other businesses should contribute about 5% of the overall revenue. And compressor will move up to ab

items.statement: PLI benefits expiring in 2027 (~1% EBITDA impact); negotiating pass-through with customers over next 12 months

items.statement: Peak revenue potential of INR 3,500-4,000 crores with ongoing expansions (AC INR 2,000 cr, Compressor INR 750 cr, Others INR 400-500 cr)
items.quote: With the ongoing expansion that we are doing, which we conclude till in the next 12 months, we are looking at a peak revenue of about INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores.

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY27 consolidated revenue growth guidance of 40% despite Q1 at 28% YoY
items.quote: Our guidance was 40% on a consolidated basis, and we are not moving away from that guidance as yet.

items.statement: Stand-alone revenue growth guidance for FY27 maintained at 25% range
items.quote: So it is about 18% is the growth on a stand-alone basis and which we had projected that overall, it would be about in the 25% range is what we had projected for the stand-alone, and we still stand by that guidance

items.statement: Q1 FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin at 8.2% vs 10.1% YoY; expects improvement as DICE revenue kicks in from Q2
items.quote: Our consolidated EBITDA margin is about 8.2%. And what we see is in the coming months, we will come to know more closely as the revenue from DICE also kicks in.

items.statement: Long-term EBITDA margin target of 14-15% over 5-7 years; current volatility due to acquisitions and capitalization policy changes
items.quote: And what we have guided that 14% to 15% margin is over a period of 5 to 7 years. The measures which we are taking today are basically to moving the trajectory towards that margin

items.statement: Moderating capitalization policy; expensed ~INR6 crores of product development costs in Q1; will expense more than capitalize over time
items.quote: What we did was that particular cost which we did, which was about -- roughly about INR6-odd crores is what we have gone and expensed it completely. And the policy is going to be that we expense more than we capitalize over a period of time.

items.quote: The contract novation of around 85-plus clients is underway, and we should complete by the end of Q2 FY27.

items.statement: DICE revenue expected INR15-16 crores in FY27 (vs INR12 crores last year); 90%+ gross margins; full impact from FY28
items.quote: Sir, last year, they had done about INR12-odd crores, okay? And we expect that at least we are able to achieve anywhere between INR15 crores to INR16 crores this year, okay?

items.statement: Zagg.Money annualized card acquisition run rate increased 2.3x to 84,000 cards; launched Twin co-brand card with PNB and live with AU Small Finance Bank on Visa/RuPay
items.quote: Now I'm happy to announce that we have increased the annualized run rate by almost 2.3x to now reach around 84,000 cards in a short span of time.

items.statement: Save business seeing strong growth from new income tax regulations; 73% of new users from existing corporates upselling; marquee wins include Radisson, SCA, Avighna, Slice SFB, Bikaji, Bureau Veritas, Nuvama
items.quote: While the focus has been on new client acquisition, around 73% of the new user onboarded came from our existing corporates, where we were able to upsell new wallets and add new users.

items.statement: Zoyer business rolling out to 2,000 stores of large retail chain with 17,000 more pending; new wins include Diesel Fashion, Mokobara, AppsForBharat, CBM Retail; DICE clients Hindalco, Bajel, Dezerv, Navi billing from Q2
items.quote: We have already onboarded about 2,000 stores with an impending rollout of the balance 17,000-odd stores in the coming months.

items.statement: Propel signed Saint Gobain, Supreme Pipes, Phoenix India; fleet business 43% transaction growth YoY, 5.8% value growth to INR100 cr annualized spend; signed 5-year HPCL aggregator agreement for Driver Track Plus
items.quote: We have seen a remarkable 43% increase in the total transactions, along with a resounding 5.8% increase in transaction value, which has reached an annualized spend rate of INR100 crores as of today.

items.statement: Program fee growth slowed to 10% YoY by design to optimize cash flow and capitalization; moving customers from banks with longer working capital cycles
items.quote: On the program fee side, we have taken a very conscious call overall itself the business, sir, we've taken a very conscious call to optimize for both cash flow and to work on controlling or calibrating our capitalization.

items.statement: Strategic investment of INR8 crores in Unobanc (moneyHOP) with AD Category-2 license for cross-border payments; aligns with Save and Zoyer products
items.quote: We have made a strategic investment of around INR8 crores in Unobanc Private Limited, which operates under the brand of moneyHOP.

items.statement: Opening ADGM subsidiary in Abu Dhabi in Q2 FY27; DICE acquisition validates UAE product-market fit; will enter with Save, Zoyer, Propel stack
items.quote: Now we are in the process of opening a subsidiary in ADGM, Abu Dhabi Global Markets International Financial Center and Free Economic Zone within this quarter, which is Q2 FY27.

items.statement: Remaining commercial capex Rs 1,500-1,800 cr fully tied up with equity and debt sanctioned
items.quote: The remaining capital which we need to deploy on these assets is amount in the range of Rs. 1,500-Rs. 1,800 crores and which would be, which is completely tied up as we speak

items.quote: At Estate 105 Noida, driven by the strong response to the project, we have revised the development mix to a residential portfolio, enhancing our project GDV to Rs. 6,000 crores, with Phase-2 of this plan in FY '27 as a launch

items.quote: Sector 59 on Golf Course Extension Road, it has a development potential of 1.3 million square feet, with a GDV potential of more than Rs. 3,500 crores, and we are expected to launch in Q3 of FY '27

items.statement: Target annual rental income ~Rs 700 cr at peak occupancy; target 1 msf new commercial BD annually
items.quote: As our under-construction pipeline progresses, we expect to achieve our annual rental income of approximately Rs. 700 crores at peak occupancy. We will also continue to target 1 million square feet of new business development

items.statement: Expect high single-digit ARR growth in upcoming quarters driven by BRICS Summit, wedding season, and conferences
items.quote: So, we can expect definitely high single digit ARR growth as we go forward.

items.statement: Target 140 Flurys outlets by end of FY27, adding 29 outlets from current 111
items.quote: We plan to add 29 outlets from here on to end the year at about 140 outlets by the end of the year.

items.statement: FY27 capex estimated at Rs.200-250 crores; total 4-5 year capex plan of Rs.1,500 crores net of EM Bypass funding
items.quote: Within this year there could be around Rs. 200 crores - Rs. 250 crore of the CAPEX requirement.

items.statement: 33 of 69 service apartments sold at EM Bypass Kolkata; Rs.21 crores received, Rs.70-80 crores expected in FY27
items.quote: 33 of the 69 apartments available for sale have been sold in our EM Bypass Hotel and Residential project at Kolkata. This will lead to improved cash flow of Rs.70 to Rs.80 crores during the course of the year, of which Rs.21 crores is already received.

items.statement: Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin at 28.12%; PAT margin ~7% due to higher finance costs and deferred tax
items.quote: EBITDA stood at Rs.47 crores up 3% year-on-year with EBITDA margin at 28.12%.

items.statement: Domestic travel resilient; 40 wedding dates Nov-Mar, BRICS Summit, Aero Show, Bharat Mobility Expo to drive demand
items.quote: There are about 40 wedding dates during the course from now to March'27, Aero Show at Bangalore and the Bharat Mobility Expo among others.

items.quote: Food and Beverage remain an important part of our overall hospitality ecosystem, contributing approximately 43% of total revenue during the quarter.

items.statement: West Asia crisis and flat domestic air traffic pressured Q1 ADR; international air traffic into India declined ~10%
items.quote: International air traffic into India during this course of this quarter has declined by almost 10%.

items.statement: EM Bypass sales to generate Rs.300-325 crores over 4 years, funding hotel development; net debt/EBITDA at 0.70
items.quote: We expect to have sale of Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 325 crores which is our share in this mixed-use development. And the same amount of money is going to be used for the development of the hotel at EM Bypass.

items.statement: Portfolio to grow from 42 hotels (2,677 keys) to 3,149 keys by end FY27 via 12-hotel pipeline (472 keys); target 6,719 keys by 2030
items.quote: We now have a pipeline of 12 hotels comprising of 472 keys for this year. These additions are expected to take our portfolio from the current 42 hotels with 2,677 keys to 3,149 keys by the end of FY27.

items.quote: The acquisition of the Malabar House in Fort Kochi is currently in progress. The property comprises of 17 keys on approximately half an acre of land and this acquisition is expected to be completed by October-November of 2026.

items.statement: Pune FSI increased from 2.5 lakh to 6.7 lakh sq ft; plan 2.5 lakh for hotel, 4+ lakh for residential development
items.quote: At Pune, the FSI available to us on our land has changed from 2.5 lakh square feet to 6.7 lakh square feet.

items.statement: Tax rate to drop from ~40% to 30-35% from Q2 FY27 under new tax regime, improving PAT
items.quote: Our tax rate from next quarter will go down from 35 to 25% as we are coming under new regime. So, this time it does have a 40% tax rate but in future in Q2, Q3, Q4 our tax rate is going to come down to around 30% to 35%.

items.statement: SAP S4 HANA Finance implementation completed to strengthen controls and reporting as portfolio scales
items.quote: During the quarter, we completed the implementation of SAP S4 HANA for Finance.

items.quote: 20% is something we were expecting, 20 -25% to happen in the entire year, but it is already translated and the other products have not even contributed.

items.statement: Strong domestic demand across all products; infrastructure and power push driving growth; export orders rejected due to full galvanizing capacity
items.quote: This year, market looks very good domestically as the global situation is very unpredictable. The freight charges are quite high. Most of the steel manufacturers are concentrating on their domestic sales, which is why we are seeing a lot of growth domestically.

items.quote: We are not able to take a lot of orders that come from export because again that will occupy our galvanizing. Most of the orders are galvanizing pipe. So, our galvanizing capacity in Bombay where we do our exports is already full.

For example, we're expecting that we'll increase our sales by 1,000 ton

items.statement: Uniware expected to grow over 15% YoY from Q4 FY27 onwards
